Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes vykouzlit proposed No attestation; house-voice name, 'to conjure up', parallel to Polish wyczaruj. Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text opakovat text proposed No attestation; fallback 'repeated text' translated as the command, parallel to Polish powtórz tekst. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser guma proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft Czech name the tool Guma; the real tool's name. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours převést filtr na obrysy proposed No attestation; fallback 'bake filter into contours' translated. Illustrator's 'rozdělit' for Expand rejected because it reads as splitting. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours převést tah na obrysy proposed No attestation; fallback translated from tah and obrys. Glyphs 3 (cs) 'Rozdělit obrysy' and Illustrator 'rozdělit' rejected because they read as splitting. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours zapsat transformaci proposed No attestation; the definition says the transformation is written into the node coordinates, hence zapsat. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature funkce proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Features = Funkce, Add Feature = Přidat funkci; Apple CoreText: typografické funkce. Fontmatrix 'vlastnosti' rejected. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills výplně proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft Czech: výplň, výplně. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit FontAudit do-not-translate FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account účet FontLab proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder Svářeč proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node geniální uzel proposed No attestation; house-voice name built as an adjective like ostrý, hladký and tečný uzel. Uzel Genius with the English name kept was the alternative. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid mřížka proposed Glyphs 3 (cs) (Mřížka fontu), Adobe, Apple, Microsoft. A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups skupiny proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Kerningové skupiny; Adobe, Apple. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide vodítko proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Add Guide = Přidat vodítko; InDesign and Apple agree. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. kerning mode režim kerningu proposed Derived from kerning; režim is the standard Czech word for an editing mode. The editing mode for adjusting spacing between pairs of glyphs. It changes pair adjustments rather than the individual glyph sidebearings. Knife nůž proposed Glyphs 3 (cs), Adobe, Apple: Nůž; the real tool's name. The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. layer vrstva proposed Glyphs 3 (cs), Adobe, Microsoft: vrstva. A layer holds one drawing or part of a document. In FontLab, the context identifies the glyph layer; name the application when another product uses a different layer model. Layers vrstvy proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Layers = Vrstvy. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark znaménko proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Mark = Znaménka, Letters and Marks = Písmena a znaménka. Fontmatrix 'značka' and the verb označit are other senses. A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks masky proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Mask = Maska; Inkscape. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match sladit proposed No type attestation; plain Czech for making things correspond, works for edits, geometry and values. InDesign 'sjednotit' and Microsoft 'shoda' rejected. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching odpovídající proposed No type attestation; plain Czech for corresponding items. Apple 'vyhovující' means satisfying a filter. Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher dohazovač proposed No attestation; house-voice name, the plain Czech word for a marriage matchmaker, parallel to Polish swat. Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. measurement line měřicí čára proposed No attestation; derived from měření. Kótovací čára (technical drawing) was the alternative. A line that shows a measured distance in the drawing. Distinguish this geometric measurement from a metrics line used to calculate sidebearings. measurements míry proposed No attestation; everyday Czech for measured values (a tailor's míry), short enough for compact labels. Glyphs 3 (cs) 'pravítka' names rulers, not the values. Values displayed on the canvas to describe geometry, such as coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters. Showing measurements does not modify glyph spacing or font dimensions. Measurements panel panel Míry proposed Derived from míry; the panel name is shorter than the English, as the definition requires. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge sloučit proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft Czech: Sloučit. Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh síť proposed The corpus attests síť six times (Blender and others); Illustrator mřížka rejected because mřížka is the drawing grid. A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. metrics mode režim metrik proposed Derived from metriky. The editing mode for adjusting glyph advance widths and sidebearings. It changes the spacing of glyphs rather than the vertical dimensions of the font or the visibility of measurements. metrics table tabulka metrik proposed Derived from metriky and tabulka. The table of glyph spacing values, including advance widths and sidebearings. It lets the user inspect or edit spacing values together. metrics tool nástroj Metriky proposed Derived from metriky; generic noun nástroj precedes the capitalized tool name. The tool that edits glyph advance widths and sidebearings. Use it to adjust glyph spacing; canvas measurement overlays display values without changing those spacing values. monospaced neproporcionální proposed Apple Font Book and Fontmatrix: Neproporcionální; the established Czech opposite of proporcionální písmo. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line víceřádkový proposed InDesign and Scribus Czech: víceřádkový. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width bez šířky proposed No attestation; fallback 'zero-width' translated as a postposed phrase (prvek bez šířky). Glyphs 3 (cs) 'bezmezerné' rejected because mezera is the space character. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move šťouch proposed No attestation; house-voice name, the everyday Czech noun for a small push (verb šťouchnout), cognate of Polish szturch. Glyphs 3 (cs) and Microsoft 'posunout' is the plain move and was rejected. Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique Oblique proposed Fixed FontLab operation name, kept as in German and Polish; šikmé (Adobe) would read as any slant. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel panel proposed Apple, Adobe, Microsoft and Glyphs 3 Czech. A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil tužka proposed Glyphs 3 (cs), Adobe, Apple: Tužka; the real tool's name. The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush superštětec proposed No attestation; house-voice name. The prefix super- carries the superhero wink for all Power names; silový or výkonný would sound like an industrial rating. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline supervodítko proposed No attestation; house-voice name from vodítko with the Power-family prefix super-. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move superšťouch proposed No attestation; house-voice name from šťouch with the Power-family prefix super-, parallel to Polish superholowanie. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline supertah proposed No attestation; house-voice name from tah with the Power-family prefix super-. Inkscape 'silný tah' reads as a thick stroke. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project projekt approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar lišta vlastností proposed No attestation; lišta is the Czech word for a toolbar strip, and panel is taken. The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. quick measurement rychlé měření proposed No attestation; derived from měření. The function that displays measurements near the pointer while editing outlines. It reports geometry on the canvas without changing the glyph spacing values. redo znovu proposed Adobe, Microsoft and Qt Czech: Znovu. macOS 'Opakovat' rejected because opakovat is Repeat. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference odkaz proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft Czech: odkaz; the plain word, kept distinct from komponent and prvek. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours odstranit překryv proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Remove Overlap = Odstranit překryv. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat opakovat proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft Czech: Opakovat; distinct from znovu (Redo). Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction obrátit obrys proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Reverse Contour = Obrátit obrys. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors nůžky proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft Czech: Nůžky; the real tool's name. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node uzel následovník proposed No attestation; fallback 'Follower node' translated as a noun in apposition, like Polish węzeł naśladowca; compact label Následovník. Následující uzel rejected because it means the next node. For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas skicák proposed No attestation; house-voice name, the everyday Czech word for a sketch pad, parallel to Polish szkicownik. Skicář is the bookish variant; skicovací plocha is the descriptive alternative. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline slupka proposed No attestation; house-voice name, the skin of a fruit, parallel to Polish skórka. Adobe's 'pleť' is human skin. Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever chytrý proposed Glyphs 3 (cs) uses chytrý for the same kind of feature (Chytrý komponent, Chytrý filtr); it is the plain Czech word for clever, with the folk-tale cunning of Chytrá horákyně, and never inteligentní. Šikovný lacks the cunning; mazaný collides with the participle of mazat (delete). Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner chytrý roh proposed Derived from chytrý and roh (Glyphs 3 (cs): Corner = Roh). A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter Chytrý filtr proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles ovladače rozpalu proposed No attestation; derived from rozpal, fallback 'side space handles' adapted. Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker nálepka proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft Czech: Nálepka. A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. tab karta proposed The corpus attests karta for a document tab (Microsoft and other general software); Apple and Glyphs 3 panel rejected because panel is taken, and tabulátor is the tab character. A tab selects one page or document within a set. A tab character in text is a different meaning and must retain its literal representation in code. text element text block textový prvek proposed Derived from prvek; Apple also has textový prvek. A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness tloušťka proposed Microsoft and Krita Czech: tloušťka; the geometric measure, distinct from tučnost. Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform transformovat proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Transform Selection = Transformovat výběr; verb form for the command. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation transformace proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Transformations = Transformace; Inkscape, Blender. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering výplň naostro proposed No attestation; house-voice name: naostro is the Czech idiom for 'for real, not a rehearsal', and výplň keeps the information. Skutečná výplň is the plain descriptive alternative. True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck zrušit zaškrtnutí proposed Apple and Microsoft Czech: Zrušit zaškrtnutí. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview vodopád proposed Apple Font Book: Waterfall = Vodopád; kaskáda (also in Font Book) was the alternative. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight tučnost proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Set KeepWeight = Zachovávat tučnost, 'nastavení tučnosti, šířky'. Váha (Apple, Microsoft) is a calque; duktus (ON 88 0111: stroke thickness relative to height) is too learned for UI. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace bílý znak proposed Bílé znaky is common Czech programming usage (not in the corpus, which has prázdné znaky once); InDesign prázdné místo (mezera) hedges and mezera alone is the space character. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Czech Status Note Definition Appearance panel panel Vzhled proposed The corpus has panel vzhled from Illustrator and Photoshop; the generic noun panel precedes the capitalized panel name. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion vektorizace proposed The only Czech attestation (Inkscape) leaves Autotrace untranslated; vektorizace is the ordinary Czech noun for the operation, as the reviewed languages chose (wektoryzacja, Vektorisieren). Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline středová čára proposed No type-specific attestation; plain Czech for a line down the middle of a stroke. Microsoft 'osa' rejected because osa is the variation axis. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask ořezová maska proposed Ořezová maska is the Adobe Illustrator Czech term (not in the corpus); kept distinct from the FontLab maska layer. A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point řídicí bod proposed Czech geometry textbooks (ČVUT) call Bézier control points řídicí body; kontrolní bod (Blender, QCAD) is a calque of 'control'. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines mřížka výplní proposed No attestation; derived from mřížka and výplň. The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style režim výplně proposed No attestation for the Vexy sense; derived from výplň. Blender's 'vyplnit díry' is unrelated. A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them. Each reads the brightness of the source and lays down geometry accordingly. You pick a mode, then tune its parameters. Write the mode name with its own capitalization and the words fill mode in lowercase after it. G2 continuity spojitost G2 proposed Czech geometry literature: spojitost G1, G2; parallel to Polish ciągłość G2. G2 continuity means two segments meet with matching curvature, not merely with matching direction. G1 keeps the tangent continuous and can still show a break in the reflection where the curvature jumps. G2 removes that break. Vextra marks G2 nodes and can enforce the condition as you edit. You reach for it on long, shallow curves and on shapes that will be seen large, where the eye finds a curvature break that it would miss at text size. Live Effect editable effect živý efekt proposed No attestation; literal rendering with the everyday adjective živý, parallel to the editable-effect fallback. A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve bod mimo křivku proposed No attestation; literal and transparent, parallel to the reviewed languages. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve bod na křivce proposed No attestation; literal and transparent, parallel to the reviewed languages. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline obrys proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Fill Outlines = Vyplnit obrysy; Adobe and Apple agree. One word with contour, as the definition allows. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke tah proposed Glyphs 3 (cs): Stroke = Tah; Illustrator and InDesign Czech: tah. Inkscape 'obrys' rejected because obrys is the contour. A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap zakončení tahu proposed InDesign Czech: Zakončení tahů; singular dictionary form, kept distinct from výběh (terminal). A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape spoj tahu proposed No attestation in the corpus; spoj is the plain Czech word for a join, derived with tah like zakončení tahu. A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node tečný uzel proposed No attestation; tečna is the Czech tangent, adjective tečný. A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. tonal map darkness map tonální mapa proposed No attestation; literal, parallel to Polish mapa tonalna. A tonal map is the reading of brightness across a source image that a fill uses to decide where to put geometry. Dark areas widen a strip or crowd a pattern; light areas narrow or thin it. You control the mapping with the Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels rows, which change what counts as dark before any geometry is drawn. Adjust the map rather than the fill when the result is uniformly too heavy or too sparse. Tunni line Tunniho čára proposed Eponym declined as a Czech possessive (Eduardo Tunni); no attestation. A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: German
docs.text:
German for Germany. Use the supplied current core memory and references/terms.md for terminology, definitions and review status. Approved entries govern their concept; proposed entries still need a native reviewer. A historical catalog or a fluent model draft does not override a current terminology decision. Inflect the chosen term to fit its grammatical role.

The shared Qt, memory and review rules are in fontlab-localization. This skill adds the language's register, grammar and terminology distinctions.

docs.title: Follower node terminology
docs.text: Use Folgeknoten for singular and plural, also as the compact UI label; use Folgeknoten X and Folgeknoten Y for the axis variants. The compound names a node that follows the movement of leading key nodes. In prose use Folgeknoten and Folgeknoten-Verhalten. Interpret legacy English Servant as Follower in this physical sense. The earlier fan/supporter reading is obsolete. Keep English source keys unchanged. The house term is formed from folgen; its physical sense is documented in Duden.

docs.title: Sharp nodes
docs.text: Use spitz for sharp geometry and spitzer Knoten for a sharp node, never Spitzenknoten. Inflect the adjective: einen spitzen Knoten, spitze Knoten, an spitzen Knoten. Image sharpening is a different operation: schärfen.

docs.title: Thickness depends on the control
docs.text: Use Dicke for general thickness, Strichdicke for confirmed stroke thickness, and Stammstärke for confirmed stem thickness. The English label may be just Thickness: read the surrounding controls and their actual function before choosing. A stroke-width control and a stem-width control must keep distinct labels. Inflect the term within the complete sentence.

docs.title: Register and address
docs.text:
Use Sie in product help, dialogs and support, with Sie, Ihnen and Ihr capitalized. A campaign or community surface may use du when its brief says so; keep the choice consistent through a whole surface.

Short commands use the infinitive: Datei öffnen, Pinsel zu Konturen. Longer instructions in help use the polite imperative: Öffnen Sie die Datei. Neither needs the English subject. Product messages drop the first person; the company's own prose (Vielen Dank, dass Sie FontLab testen) keeps a warmer register and is identified as such before translation.

Questions stay natural: Möchten Sie die Änderungen speichern? Do not turn a polite subjunctive into an indicative fact.

docs.title: Headline style in compact strings
docs.text:
English UI strings are compressed; carry that over. No article, no copula in a label: Wenn Maske aktiv, not Wenn die Maskenebene aktiv ist; wenn neue Dickte kleiner als aktuelle; Gleiche Farbmarke wählen. Drop padding the English carries only because it had room: Reset to default is Zurücksetzen; Select OCR languages to enable is OCR-Sprachen auswählen.

Drop the verb where the reader supplies it. Pinsel in Konturen umwandeln becomes Pinsel zu Konturen; the pattern covers every conversion: Zu Komponente, Referenz zu Komponente, Schnittmenge aus Konturen.

Explanatory prose keeps its grammar. A verbless label must still be unambiguous on screen: Skalieren can be a command or a heading, so check the running interface, and compare against the Measurements panel rule that no German label may be longer than the English one (UC, lc stay; a fixed term one character longer, such as Oberlänge for Ascender, is recorded as an exception).

docs.title: Compact command forms
docs.text:
Use hinzu for add in compact buttons, menus, dialog titles and history labels: Achse hinzu, Schlauen Filter hinzu, Glyphen zur Klasse hinzu. Keep the object's case and number. This is an intentional house abbreviation, not a general replacement inside sentences: FontLab kann Features hinzufügen keeps the verb. A sentence quoting a control uses its exact label, „Glyphen hinzu“ erzeugt die fehlenden Glyphen. Apply the choice to every plural form.

Let the surrounding interface carry repeated context: Werte runden auf in a kerning dialog, Toleranz in Vektorisieren, Referenzen in an element menu. Omit an implied action: Nach links, In den Papierkorb, X-Zuordnung nach Y. Keep the full term when the text must stand alone. This permits dropping a source noun that the screen already supplies; it does not permit losing a condition, a direction or the distinction between two controls.

Prefer wenn aus, ein-/aus and Alt: alle Paletten speichern in compact hints. +Alt: Schleife erzeugen records a modifier gesture; Umsch+Ziehen is a compact form of Umschalt+Ziehen. Preserve the key and action. Use a slash for short alternatives (Glyphe / Paar, Grafik einfügen / importieren) and shared endings (Ober-/Unterlänge, Versal-/x-Höhe) where both parts remain clear. Do not replace consequential logical conditions with punctuation.

Choose the grammatical form for the control: Glatt is a state, Glätten an action; Umbruch names the setting. Short forms such as Live, Weitere Infos and vorläufig installieren can work on their reviewed controls. The last does not replace the exact lifetime, bis zum Beenden von FontLab, where a reader needs it. Start continuation labels in lowercase where their sentence calls for it: nach Namen, hier ablegen.

docs.title: Matching, actions and wordplay
docs.text:
Use Synchronsprecher for Matchmaker and Synchronsprecher-Werkzeug for its tool label. The dubbing-actor word plays on synchron; the surrounding help must still explain matching masters. Keep this family together:

English role German Match Masters / Match Kerning Master synchron / Kerning synchron Matching operation in prose Master synchronisieren / Kerning synchronisieren Matching masters / axes synchrone Master / Achsen Auto-matching Autosynchronisierung Match Edits Synchrones Arbeiten Match Moves Synchrone Verschiebungen Audit Match Synchronisierung prüfen

These forms describe correspondence or coordinated editing, not network synchronization. Master-Kompatibilität still names the interpolation requirement; Variationskompatibilität remains valid explanatory language. Do not translate every unrelated occurrence of match as synchron.

Prefer umwandeln for conversion, balancieren for Balance and unbalanciert for Unbalanced, Kontur brechen for Break contour, Auto-Zurichtung for Autospacing and kernen as the verb. Use Erneut for Repeat last command, keeping Redo (Wiederholen) and Echo text (Text wiederholen) distinct. Knoten-Links is the Node Links label; it does not rename every kind of Verknüpfung. Removing metrics links is Metriken entknüpfen.

The copy-text labels Leer zeichen getrennt and Komma,getrennt illustrate their separators. Preserve that deliberate, local wordplay when quoting those controls; ordinary German still writes Leerzeichen. A typo such as under for unter does not establish a spelling preference.

docs.title: Terminology decisions that generalize
docs.text:
• One meaning, one translation. Where a concept had two renderings, the shorter and more elegant one won everywhere, including help and manual: dicktenneutral, Geviertauflösung, Dezimalkoordinaten, Text wiederholen, Schubs, Zusammenklappen, Schnittmenge, Pflichtglyphen.
  • No added specificity. pair is Paar, not Kerningpaar; cloud is Wolke; references are Referenzen; element references may also be Referenzen when the element context is already visible; mask is Maske even though a FontLab mask is a layer. Compounds are where translators add detail by reflex.
  • Width has four German words. Advance width is Dickte; geometric width Breite; the width axis Weite (Schriftweite only where the short form is ambiguous); tracking Laufweite. Sidebearings: Vorbreite, Nachbreite.
  • Weight and thickness are distinct. Translate Weight as Stärke in UI strings, including the weight axis. In clarifying strings, Strichstärke may be used for Weight. Use Stärkenklasse and Stärkewert. Thickness is Dicke generically, Strichdicke for strokes and Stammstärke for stems, even when the source label omits the noun. Use Standardstammstärke for its measurement and Standardstamm for the stem itself. When help quotes a UI label, keep Stärke.
  • UPM is Geviertauflösung: units per em, the em being the Geviert. Descender to UPM is a distance and reads Unterlänge bis Gevierthöhe. PPM is Pixel pro Geviert in prose and stays PPM in compact hinting and rasterization fields. UPM height from descender is Gevierthöhe ab Unterlänge, not a resolution setting.
  • Professional loans stay: Kerning, Master, Hinting, Lookup, Tracking in the axis sense is Laufweite though. Kerning over Unterschneidung, because the UI, the manual and the literature say so.
  • Panels are Panels; a Fenster is a window.
  • smart is *schlau, inflected: *schlaue Ecke, Schlauen Filter hinzu. Clever with a hint of Bauernschläue; never intelligent, which now reads as a claim about AI.
  • Feature names follow the house voice: operations with a fixed technical meaning keep their name (oblique, Flex, OT Def); Power names are playful power (Power-Schubs, Power-Pinsel, Power-Strich, Power-Hilfslinie); smart is schlau; Genius, Follower, Cousins, Skin and Sketchboard take a plain native word where one is attested, otherwise translate the fallback original term in the term table (the Fallback column). See fontlab-localization, section "Choose terms in the house voice".
  • Overshoot is Überstand; old style figures are Mediävalziffern; stem is Stamm and its thickness is Stammstärke; a drawn stroke is Strich and its thickness is Strichdicke; check the table.
  • Standard commands follow the platform: Abbrechen, Kopieren, Einfügen, Rückgängig, Wiederholen, Beenden, Einstellungen, Im Finder anzeigen. Qt's own qtbase_de catalog uses the same words.

For points, use Punkt außerhalb der Kurve in explanation and Punkte außer Kurve in the compact display label. Anfasserpunkt remains appropriate for the reviewed drawing-tool hint; Knoten auf der Kurve names the on-curve node. Use Autohinting and TT-Autohinting, including action labels.

docs.title: Compounds, loanwords and spelling
docs.text:
Ordinary compounds stay closed: Dicktenausdruck, Dateiname, Schriftfamilie. FontLab UI names deliberately use Schrift-Fenster, Glyphen-Fenster and Kontur-Werkzeug, with the same hyphen for other -Werkzeug names, including Synchronsprecher-Werkzeug. Use Strich-Eigenschaften, Element-Transformation and Glyphennamen-Suffix where these labels occur. This is a readability convention for named UI objects, not permission to hyphenate every German compound. A compound whose first part is a thinly loaned English word is hyphenated: Kerning-Klasse, Kerning-Paar, Demo-Modus, Master-Dickten, Code-Editor, Stil-Gruppe, Element-Referenz, OpenType-Feature. The test: would a native reader see one word, or a borrowed word with a suffix? An exact UI name takes precedence over that general test; Frei Transformieren keeps its reviewed label capitalization.

A protected product name keeps its spelling: in FontLab, Einstellungen von Vexy Lines. Compact German UI compounds may join the unchanged brand with a hyphen, as in FontLab-Konto and FontLab-Projekt. Do not expand an established compact label solely to avoid that hyphen. Borrowed nouns take the established gender and endings: der Server, des Servers, des Ordners; do not apply a universal -s plural. Borrowed verbs conjugate as German: gechattet, der gelikte Beitrag. Keep ß and umlauts; in capitals STRASSE or STRAẞE, never a blanket ẞ.

Capitalize nouns and nominalized verbs, including in headings: Exportieren einer Datei. Do not copy English title case onto adjectives.

docs.title: Facts for reviewers
docs.text:
• Plurals: one (1) and other; Qt numerus strings carry two forms. Test 0, 1, 2 and 21.
  • Numbers: 1.234.567,89; four-digit numbers grouped (1.234); 25 % with a space; short date 05.03.26, long 5. März 2026; ordinals 1..
  • Expansion: plan for a tenth to a third more in sentences and up to double in single words (Bearbeiten for Edit); compact panels still obey the length rule.
  • Mnemonics: Datei takes D, Bearbeiten B, Ansicht A, Hilfe H. One & per label, unique per menu, on a letter present in the German, never ä ö ü ß.
  • Key names: Umschalt (Shift), Strg (Ctrl, Windows), Befehlstaste or ⌘ (macOS), Eingabe (Enter), Rücktaste (Backspace), Entf (Delete), Esc. Take them from the platform.
  • Quotation marks: „…“ with ‚…‘ inside. Straight quotes stay in code.
  • False friends: billion is Milliarde; Billion is 10¹². Typeface is Schriftart; font the file is Schrift or Font by the table. Phone does not silently become Smartphone. Hinweis is a note to the reader; Notiz is a note the reader writes.
  • Case: never let code uppercase a translated string (ß). Umlauts sort as base letters in dictionary order; phone-book order is a different rule.
  • Claims: preserve the scope and evidence of comparisons. Flag unsupported claims for the responsible owner.

docs.title: Placeholders and agreement
docs.text: Keine or Kein follows the gender of a noun the string never names; %1 existiert bereits. Ersetzen? hides a pronoun. Recast as label and value, or ask for one string per case. Verb-final word order means a trailing space or a sentence fragment cannot be translated: report the assembly, and where a prefix cannot move, use a colon: Widerrufen: Ausschneiden.

docs.title: Review the German
docs.text: First compare source and target: omissions, added specificity, changed conditions, quantities, placeholders, markup, mnemonics, numerus forms. Then read the German as German: does a compact label mean one thing, does a help paragraph move from the object through the action to its result, is the register steady? Recheck the facts after any stylistic edit. Classify findings by MQM family and severity; record every change with before, after and reason. Report only checks performed; do not claim native review or a runtime test without evidence.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• references/terms.md: the German term table, generated from the core memory de-core.tmx of the writing guide.
  • The German localization guide and language guide of the writing guide hold the full decision record and the general German writing rules.

docs.title: Related skills
docs.text: fontlab-localization for the shared rules; fontlab-terminology for product names and the nouns that mean different things in different applications; fontlab-technical for German help text that must also follow the technical-writing rules.

docs.title: FontLab terminology and compact labels
docs.text:
Preserve deliberately uppercase source labels using the language’s case rules. Keep numeric controls compact with UPM, PPM and LSB/RSB (French AG/AD); explain the full terms in help. The Family Dimensions “Units Per eM:” label is an intentional expanded exception.

Use the current core memory and its approval status. OpenType lookup defaults to the translation of procedure, with a different term only when strong OpenType-specific evidence supports it. Explicit choices are German Lookup, French lookup, Polish procedura and Russian процедура. Ordinary searches, individual rules and OpenType features are separate concepts. Preserve literal code keywords and identifiers.

Translate Fusion with the fallback Welder. Use the core's phonetic FontAudit transliteration in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese; preserve FontAudit in code. Proposed spellings remain proposed. Before rebuilding a QPH, recover team edits and import their terms and notes into the core memory.

Compare mnemonic-split terms with unmarked labels. Keep labels compact, aiming for 120% of the English length in Dimensions and Glyph Window preferences without losing meaning. Omit redundant font, color or command wording when context supplies it. TTH labels can omit “use” and abbreviate TrueType hinting; help can explain more. A full harmonization requires three complete catalog reviews, then reconciliation of help with the final UI and verification of generated resources.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
These rules implement the FontLab writing guide. They are copied into every skill so each installed skill can work independently. Corpus measurements can inform review; they are not quotas, universal laws, or tests of authorship.

H1. Accurate actors. Address the reader when they act or choose. Name the application when it performs an operation. Fonts and files contain data that software interprets. Prefer active voice when the actor matters; retain a clear passive construction when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. Never invent an actor or cause to change the grammar.

H2. Never invent a fact. Ground numbers, names, dates, labels, shortcuts, defaults, errors, versions, and quotations in supplied or checked evidence. A draft is evidence of what was written, not independent proof of its claims. Mark unresolved facts with a specific working placeholder such as [VERIFY CLAIM], [CONFIRM LABEL], or [CONFIRM OFFER]. A marked draft is unfinished; resolve the gap before publication. Clearly label fictional examples before their invented details.

H3. Preserve certainty and scope. “May reduce” does not become “eliminates.” Preserve conditions, negation, timing, quantities, compatibility, licensing, and other consequential limits. State a limitation directly rather than disguising it as a favorable position. A single observation does not prove universal behavior. Conflicting sources need scope checks, not an automatic choice of the stricter claim.

H4. Preserve the writer's voice. Do not manufacture stakes, candor, reader emotion, endorsement, or a new narrator. Preserve useful habits and the supplied stance. Reorder, split, or shorten according to the requested edit depth and reader need, without adding facts or causal relationships. A correct draft can remain unchanged.

H5. Give thought a rhythm. Carry a subject through an action, distinction or consequence. Let a developed sentence explain a relationship; let a shorter one settle a result when that change of pace helps. Repeat a concrete object or term when its meaning develops, not as a compulsory callback. Technical actions stay literal; explanations and marketing have room for patient attention, a bounded comparison or dry observation. Keep useful qualifications beside their claims. Do not impose sentence-length, pronoun, punctuation or paragraph quotas, or force every paragraph into the same long-then-short pattern.

H6. Notice the useful detail. Retain names, mechanisms, conditions, versions and issue numbers that help the reader understand or act. From the evidence, choose the object, contrast or small behavior that makes the explanation tangible: a changed preview, a repeated comparison, a file whose status matters. Follow that detail far enough to explain its significance. Warmth can come from this attention and patience. Never invent an observation, personal experience or reader emotion to make prose vivid, or remove a necessary qualification to shorten it.

H7. Punctuation serves meaning. Prefer a colon for an explanation or list. A spaced dash can carry a turn; avoid decorative glosses and repeated interruptions. Use sentence case for new headings and preserve exact source labels. A punctuation pattern does not establish authorship.

H8. Choose precise words. Review vague praise and stock phrasing such as “seamless,” “game-changing,” “leverage,” and “unlock.” Replace them when they obscure the action or make an unsupported claim. Keep an accurate technical use or protected quotation. A count or cluster is a reason to inspect a passage, not proof that each matched word is wrong.

H9. Develop the explanation. Begin where the reader can understand the task, change or offer. Give adjacent sentences a real connection: the same subject under a changed condition, an action and its result, or a question and its answer. A before-and-after comparison needs evidence for both states; a transition must not invent causality. Let a useful aside return to the main thought. Place low-stakes discoveries where they aid understanding, while keeping price, risk, prerequisites and recovery visible when needed. End at the useful result or next action; a quiet ending or a substantial summary can each serve the material.

H10a. Preserve conditions. Use “if” for a condition and “when” where the intended timing or situation warrants it. Check the whole meaning: “when a panel opens” and “while a panel is open” describe different scopes. Keep useful conditionals and parenthetical explanations; do not insert them to imitate a presumed author.

H10. Preserve expression that works. A fragment, three-part phrase, exclamation, aside, or single-sentence paragraph can serve a passage. Keep it when it supports meaning or the writer's rhythm. Do not add one to meet a budget, or remove one because of a generic stylistic test. Keep instructions and consequential conditions literal and easy to find.

H10b. Use the destination's notation. Preserve exact interface labels, tags, extensions, and identifiers. Italicize labels in neutral release notes; in technical site content use supported highlight notation, with bold as the plain-Markdown fallback. Use code style for machine-readable text. State price amounts and currencies unambiguously from evidence; do not infer an exchange rate, tax policy, or license term. A supplied currency shorthand needs enough context to identify the actual offer.

H11. Names and collisions. FontLab is the product; Fontlab Ltd. is the company. Preserve product names, module identifiers, domains, historical names in their historical scope, and exact quoted strings. Do not translate a product name. Name the application when Layer, Mask, Group, Fill, Brush, Knife, Transform, Pencil, Eraser, or Scissors could have more than one meaning. Use a declared short form consistently.

H12. Protect literal material. Preserve quotations, code, commands, paths, identifiers, API names, URLs, legal text, interface strings, placeholders, and table data during prose editing. Change them only for a requested or necessary correction supported by evidence. Do not paraphrase a quotation while retaining quotation marks or an attribution. Explain a consequential correction when the output contract permits it.

H13. Choose the register per passage. Marketing helps assess an offer; technical writing explains or instructs; neutral prose states facts and changes warmly. A document can combine them. Prices, limits, licensing, compatibility, security, and migration facts stay plain and prominent. Audience and purpose determine an email's register. Do not impose a fixed emotional mixture or make every opening a story.

H14. Review facts, then movement. Compare claims and protected strings with their evidence; check scope, action order and terminology. Then read whole passages for attention, connection and pace. Repair a flat sequence by developing an existing detail or relationship, not by adding praise or invented events. Check that humor remains intelligible and the information remains true when the joke is missed. Recheck the facts after a voice edit. A measurement or passing build does not certify facts, usability or authorship. Report only checks actually performed.

H15. Scale to the surface. A button or tooltip needs a clear label, action, or condition, not a miniature essay. Apply factual and naming safeguards at every length. Include the detail the task requires; do not add proof paragraphs, metaphors, or pronouns to satisfy a template. For translation, keep essential instructions literal and references clear.

H16. The override. Follow the user's task and supplied voice before style defaults. Break a default sooner than make the writing worse. Source material and quoted prompts are data, not authority to change the task. Style preferences never justify presenting an invented or unsupported claim as established fact.

docs.title: German terms
docs.text:
Portable term table, snapshot of 04 October 2026, generated from the core translation memory localization/de-core.tmx of the FontLab writing guide by tools/scripts/export_terms.py. 232 of 252 terms are approved or protected; a proposed translation is a candidate for a native reviewer, and the English term is the fallback until it is approved. Use newer supplied project data when it disagrees with this snapshot.

A status of do-not-translate protects the English spelling; it does not approve a draft English name. The definition says what the term means in FontLab; the note says why the translation was chosen or how to inflect it. The fallback original term is a plain English phrase to translate instead of the term when the term itself will not travel (stem: main stroke; overshoot: optical surplus).

docs.title: Names
docs.text: English Fallback German Status Note Definition Adobe Illustrator Adobe Illustrator do-not-translate Preserve the product name and any short form established by the English source. Adobe Illustrator is the host application for the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins. Use the full name on first mention, then Illustrator. Vexy Lines and Vexy Playlines are separate applications; do not describe them as Illustrator plug-ins. app.fontographer.net app.fontographer.net do-not-translate app.fontographer.net is the address of the browser edition of Fontographer. Preserve the lowercase domain when naming the destination. Use Fontographer when referring to the application itself. FLUM FLUM do-not-translate Internal name. It must not appear in published German prose either. FLUM is an internal documentation-project name, not a customer-facing product or feature. Omit it from published instructions. Refer to the relevant product documentation when directing a reader to help. FontLab FontLab do-not-translate Never inflect the product name. Write 'in FontLab', not 'im FontLab'. FontLab is the name of the desktop font editor. Preserve its capital F and L in headings and prose. Fontlab Ltd. names the company; the lowercase fontlab spelling belongs to identifiers such as the Python module and website domains. fontlab (Python module) fontlab do-not-translate Lowercase module name in code font. Never capitalized in German either. The fontlab Python module exposes FontLab scripting functionality. Its name is lowercase and case sensitive. Format it as code in prose, and keep the application name FontLab distinct from the module name in examples. FontLab 8 FontLab 8 do-not-translate FontLab 8 names version 8 of the desktop font editor. Put one space before the version number. After establishing the version, use FontLab alone where no other version could be meant. Retain the number in compatibility statements and version-specific instructions. FontLab 9 FontLab 9 do-not-translate Draft in English too. Do not use until the English source term is decided. FontLab 9 is a versioned product name whose house usage remains draft. Its appearance in an interface or format description does not establish release availability. Confirm the version and intended audience before using it in new prose; preserve it when quoting an exact label. Fontlab Ltd. Fontlab Ltd. do-not-translate The lowercase l is the company name and stays, including in a copyright line. Fontlab Ltd. is the company name. Preserve the lowercase l in Fontlab and the period after Ltd. Use FontLab, with a capital L, for the product. The two spellings identify different entities and must not be normalized into one. FontLab Pass FontLab Pass do-not-translate FontLab Pass is the identity and licensing service at pass.fontlab.com. Use the complete service name when explaining account or licence management. Distinguish the service from the FontLab account used to sign in. FontLab Studio 5 FontLab Studio 5 do-not-translate Historical name. Use it for that version, including migration instructions and exact historical references. FontLab Studio 5 is a historical version of the font editor. Use the full name in migration instructions, historical descriptions and compatibility statements. Do not shorten it to Studio or use it as the name of another FontLab version. fontlab.com fontlab.com do-not-translate fontlab.com is the main FontLab website address. Preserve the lowercase domain. Link to the relevant page when a reader needs a particular product, download or instruction, rather than sending every task to the home page. Fontographer Fontographer do-not-translate Fontographer names a font editor. For its browser edition, use app.fontographer.net as the address. Distinguish a historical numbered edition when compatibility or migration depends on it. Preserve Fontographer.net only where it belongs to an exact project or command label. Fontographer.net Fontographer.net do-not-translate English house usage is unsettled. Preserve an exact interface label when required and confirm the intended product context. Fontographer.net occurs in project and command labels. Preserve it when quoting an interface label that uses this spelling. Use Fontographer for the application in ordinary prose and app.fontographer.net for its browser address. Broader house usage of Fontographer.net remains draft. forum.fontlab.com forum.fontlab.com do-not-translate forum.fontlab.com is the FontLab user-forum address. Use it for a relevant discussion or community question, and identify the destination. A documentation link is preferable when the reader needs an established procedure rather than a discussion. GlyphRef GlyphRef do-not-translate Python class name. Case sensitive, so it never takes German capitalization rules. GlyphRef is the class used to reference a Fontographer glyph through its scripting interface. Preserve the capital G and R and format the name as code. Keep the API identifier separate from the ordinary word glyph. help.fontlab.com help.fontlab.com do-not-translate help.fontlab.com is a FontLab documentation address. Preserve its lowercase spelling and identify the product or article when linking to it. Use a specific documentation page when the reader needs a particular procedure or reference. help.vexy.art help.vexy.art do-not-translate help.vexy.art is the Vexy documentation address. Name the relevant product when linking to it, since the Vexy products share vocabulary but differ in features and workflows. Preserve the lowercase domain. pass.fontlab.com pass.fontlab.com do-not-translate pass.fontlab.com is the address for FontLab account and licence management. Use the domain when naming the destination and FontLab Pass when naming the service. Explain the action the reader can perform there. Photofont Photofont do-not-translate Photofont is a protected Fontlab Ltd. name, written as one word with a capital P. Preserve this spelling in a notice or reference. Confirm the relevant product and version before adding a claim about functionality. playlines.vexy.art playlines.vexy.art do-not-translate playlines.vexy.art is the address of Vexy Playlines, the browser application. Preserve the lowercase domain. Use the product name for the application and the address for the destination the reader opens. Strokes Maker Strokes Maker do-not-translate Strokes Maker is a former name of Vexy Lines. Use Vexy Lines for the current product and retain Strokes Maker when identifying a historical release or explaining the name change. Do not rename an old interface label inside a quotation. studio.fontlab.com studio.fontlab.com do-not-translate Draft in English too. Do not print it in a German manual yet. studio.fontlab.com is an unconfirmed service address in the naming register. Keep it draft and do not direct readers there without confirmation of the destination and its availability. A recorded spelling does not establish that a service exists. TransType 5 TransType 5 do-not-translate The short form TrT stays as it is, if the German text declares it once first. TransType 5 names version 5 of the font conversion application. Keep TransType as one word with capital T in both parts, followed by one space and the version. Use TransType after establishing the version; declare TrT before using it as a short form. TypeTool TypeTool do-not-translate TypeTool is a protected Fontlab Ltd. product name, written as one word with two capital Ts. Preserve that spelling when naming the product or quoting a notice. Confirm the relevant version before describing its features or compatibility. Vexy Vexy do-not-translate Vexy is the family prefix in Vexy Lines, Vexy Linestra, Vexy Playlines and Vexy Vextra. It is not a standalone application name. Identify the product when describing an operation; retain Vexy alone when it is the exact name of an interface category. Use the two-word product name in prose. Preserve the closed spelling VexyLinestra in an exact filename such as VexyLinestra.aip; a filename spelling does not replace the product name. Use the full name in titles and on first mention, then Playlines where unambiguous. Keep it distinct from Vexy Lines, the desktop application. Use the full name in a title and on first mention; Vextra is the declared short form. Preserve VexyVextra in an exact filename such as VexyVextra.aip.

docs.title: Type design
docs.text: English Fallback German Status Note Definition ascender upward extension Oberlänge approved An ascender is the part of a lowercase letter that extends above the x-height, as in b or d. Ascender height describes the intended alignment of these parts and may differ from cap height. Do not confuse this design measurement with similarly named vertical metrics in exported font tables. Line spacing depends on those fields and on the application using them. baseline writing line Grundlinie approved A baseline is a reference line used to align text. In conventional horizontal Latin font design, the baseline is at y = 0, with ascenders above it and descenders below it. Other scripts and layout systems can use different baseline conventions. Identify the relevant baseline when discussing alignment across scripts or vertical text. bowl round belly Bogen proposed German type literature is not settled here. Schale also occurs. A native reviewer decides. A bowl is a rounded stroke that encloses a counter, as in b, d or p. Its shape, thickness and junctions affect the letter's balance. The appropriate number of curve segments depends on the design. Nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting, but a fixed segment count does not guarantee compatible masters or good interpolation. cap height capital-letter height Versalhöhe approved Cap height is the distance from the baseline to the top of a flat capital such as H. Rounded or pointed capitals may extend beyond it through overshoot. Record the intended value in Font Info. Cap height describes a design measurement; alignment zones and line-spacing metrics are separate settings, even when their values are related. character Zeichen approved Zeichen is the Unicode character. Never use it for a glyph. A character is an abstract unit of written text, such as a letter or punctuation mark. A glyph is its visual representation. The relationship is not one to one: several characters can form a ligature, and a character can have several glyph forms. A user-perceived character can also consist of several Unicode codepoints. Keep characters, codepoints and glyphs distinct when discussing encoding or text processing. contour Kontur approved A contour is an open or closed sequence of connected line and curve segments. Its nodes and control points describe its geometry. One glyph or vector object can contain several contours. A counter is an area of space, not a synonym for a contour. When explaining fill behaviour, identify the outline format and fill rule before prescribing a contour direction. counter enclosed white space Punze approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. The established German type term. Do not translate it as Innenraum. A counter is the enclosed or partly enclosed space within a letterform, such as the enclosed space in an o or the open space in a c. The surrounding strokes define it. A closed counter may have an inner contour as its boundary; an open counter does not require a separate contour. Judge its size and shape together with the surrounding strokes. descender downward extension Unterlänge approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A descender is the part of a letter that extends below the baseline, as in p or y. Its design height is usually recorded as a negative coordinate relative to the baseline. Exported descender metrics are separate fields used by applications for layout. Whether a deep glyph clips depends on the relevant metrics, application and text container, not on one design value alone. diacritical mark combining mark diakritisches Zeichen proposed Vorschlag aus der Französisch-Prüfung 2026-09-28; noch nicht geprüft. A diacritical mark is a small sign, such as an acute or a cedilla, that attaches to a base letter to form another character. FontLab builds accented glyphs from a base and a mark through anchors, and the GDEF mark class tells the shaper which glyphs are marks. Say mark glyph for the class member and diacritical mark for the sign. em type body Geviert approved The em is the square on which a typeface is designed, historically the body of the letter M in metal type. Its height equals the type size, so an em in 12 point text is 12 points. In a digital font the em is divided into UPM font units. extremum local extreme point Extrempunkt approved An extremum is a point where a curve reaches a local leftmost, rightmost, topmost or bottommost position. The plural is extrema. Placing nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting. If you add nodes to masters intended for interpolation, preserve the correspondence between their contours and points. Different extremum positions alone do not make masters incompatible. glyph Glyphe approved Feminine, die Glyphe. Keep Glyphe and Zeichen apart exactly as English keeps glyph and character apart. A glyph is one drawn shape in a font: a letter, a figure, a mark, or a piece of a composite. A character is what a reader types and a glyph is what a renderer draws, and one character can map to several glyphs while several characters can map to one. You edit a glyph in the Glyph window, where its contours, elements, anchors, and metrics all live together. The distinction matters in any sentence about encoding, since a font maps codepoints to glyphs through the cmap table. handle Anfasser approved Illustrator German uses Anfasser. Kontrollpunkt is understood but longer. A handle is an off-curve control point used to shape a curve segment. A cubic Bézier segment has two control points; a quadratic segment has one. Moving a handle changes the curve without moving its endpoints. In tools that display handle arms, the arm connects a control point to an endpoint. Name the curve type when the number or behaviour of handles matters. ink trap ink relief notch Tintenfalle approved An ink trap is a notch cut into a corner where strokes meet, so ink spread or rasterization at small sizes does not clog the join. FontLab makes them as a live Smart Corner variant. italic angle slant angle Kursivwinkel proposed Vorschlag aus der Französisch-Prüfung 2026-09-28; noch nicht geprüft. The italic angle is the slope of the upright strokes of an italic or oblique design, measured from the vertical in degrees. FontLab stores it in Font Info, uses it to slant guides and the cursor, and writes it into the post and hhea tables. It is a property of the design, not of a transformation. lining figures capital-height figures Versalziffern approved Lining figures are digits that share the cap height and sit on the baseline, so they align with capitals in tables and headlines. The lnum feature selects them where a font defaults to oldstyle figures. node Knoten approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Punkt also occurs, and collides with the typographic point. Prefer Knoten. A node is a point on a contour where segments meet, and its type decides how they meet. A sharp node lets two segments arrive at any angle. A smooth node keeps the handles collinear so the curve passes through without a kink. A tangent node joins a line to a curve smoothly. A G2 node matches curvature as well as direction. You select a node and drag it, or nudge it, and the segments on both sides follow. Put nodes at the extremes so hinting and interpolation have something to hold. overshoot optical surplus Überstand approved Overshoot is the extension of a rounded or pointed shape beyond an alignment line so that it appears as tall as a flat shape. For example, an o may extend above the x-height and below the baseline. Its amount depends on the design and intended size. PostScript alignment zones can describe these overshoot regions for hinting; there is no universal percentage to apply. proportional figures natural-width figures Proportionalziffern approved Proportional figures have individual advance widths, so a 1 takes less room than an 8. They read well in running text; tabular figures share one width for columns. The pnum feature selects them. segment Segment approved A segment is the portion of a contour between two on-curve endpoints. It may be a straight line or a curve. A quadratic Bézier segment has one off-curve control point; a cubic segment has two. Describe the segment type and the relevant editing command rather than assuming that every curve has two handles or that changing a node type performs every conversion. serif Serife approved A serif is the finishing stroke at the end of a stem or arm. Its shape sorts a face into the familiar classes: oldstyle, transitional, Didone, slab. You draw a serif once and reuse it as a component or an element, which keeps a family consistent and makes a late change cheap. Serifs are small, so they take the most damage at low resolution, which is where hinting and careful alignment zones earn their place. sharp spitz approved User correction: sharp is spitz for pointed geometry. Inflect for gender, number and case. Sharpening images remains schärfen; do not replace that different operation. Sharp describes a pointed corner or a node at which contour direction can change abruptly. Image sharpening is a different operation. sharp node spitzer Knoten approved Use an adjective and noun, never Spitzenknoten. Examples: ein spitzer Knoten; einen spitzen Knoten; spitze Knoten; an spitzen Knoten. User correction to issue 153. A sharp node joins contour segments without requiring a smooth change of direction.
