They are separate from Unicode assignments and glyph indices, and need not survive in every exported format. After renaming a glyph, check references in feature code, classes and scripts, including references the editor cannot update automatically. GPOS GPOS do-not-translate GPOS is the OpenType table that holds positioning: kerning, mark attachment, cursive attachment, and any rule that moves a glyph without replacing it. FontLab writes your kerning here, as pairs and as class based positioning, and builds the mark lookups from your anchors. You reach it through feature code rather than by editing the table. A font may also carry a legacy kern table; modern text engines read GPOS and many ignore the other. GSUB GSUB do-not-translate GSUB is the OpenType table containing glyph-substitution lookups. It supports operations such as replacing a glyph with an alternate, forming a ligature or selecting a form from its context. FontLab compiles feature code into these structures. To diagnose a missing substitution, check the glyphs, compiled rules, feature selection, language and shaping order in the target application. ligature joined letters ligadura approved A ligature is a glyph used to represent a sequence of characters, such as fi. OpenType substitution can replace several glyphs with one ligature glyph. The liga and dlig features distinguish standard and discretionary ligatures. Shaping does not change the underlying text; whether a later document export preserves searchable text also depends on that export and its text mappings. localized forms language-specific variants formas localizadas approved Localized forms are glyph variants selected for a text run's language. The OpenType locl feature can provide these substitutions, for example Bulgarian forms of Cyrillic letters. The shaping engine needs the relevant language information, which the application may obtain from a setting or other context. The substitution changes glyph selection, not the underlying characters or their codepoints. lookup procedure procedimiento approved User/team procedure fallback. No sufficiently strong established OpenType-specific alternative verified in the reviewed primary sources. Keep the approved contextual Rules panel title. Preserve literal FEA lookup/lookupflag keywords, identifiers and OpenType structure names. Ordinary search senses are separate. A lookup groups substitution or positioning rules of one type in GSUB or GPOS. Features reference lookups, and several features can share one. The shaping engine selects features and may process them in script-specific stages; within a stage, LookupList order matters. Source-code order alone does not describe the complete shaping sequence. Inspect the compiled tables and the target engine when diagnosing ordering problems. mark glyph combining mark glyph marca approved A mark glyph is an accent or other combining mark that attaches to a base glyph through anchors. The GDEF table classes it as a mark so shaping engines position it rather than advancing past it. nonspacing mark zero-width combining mark marca sin avance approved A nonspacing mark is the Unicode general category Mn: a combining mark with zero advance, such as a combining acute. It differs from FontLab's nonspacing element, which is a property of an element inside a glyph. oldstyle figures lowercase-style figures cifras elzevirianas approved Oldstyle figures are numerals with varying heights, often including forms with ascenders and descenders. The OpenType onum feature selects them when provided by the font. Figure height and figure width are separate choices: oldstyle figures can be proportional or tabular. Use tabular widths when numerals must align in columns, whether their forms are oldstyle or lining. OpenType class layout glyph group clase OpenType approved The OT Def field is Def. OT. An OpenType class is a named group of glyphs that feature code can address at once, written with an at sign before the name. One rule over two classes replaces a page of single rules, and one edit to a class reaches every rule that cites it. You define classes in the Classes panel or in feature code, and you keep their order stable, because a substitution between two classes pairs them by position. Kerning classes are a separate mechanism with the same idea. OpenType feature layout feature función OpenType approved Align this compound with the approved issue 153 feature terminology and the current Features panel. Keep feature tags and literal FEA code unchanged. An OpenType feature identifies typographic behaviour through a four-character tag, such as liga, smcp or ss01. Feature records reference substitution or positioning lookups. In FontLab, you can write feature code and compile it into the font. Whether and when a feature is applied depends on the shaping engine, script, language and application settings; not every feature is a user-controlled switch. OS/2 table tabla OS/2 proposed Preserve the literal OpenType tag OS/2; translate the common noun table. This follows the English glossary translatable status and existing localized technical prose. Proposed editorial correction, not a new team approval. The OS/2 table carries the font's metadata for applications: vertical metrics, weight and width classes, embedding permissions, the panose values, and the codepage and Unicode range bits that say what the font covers. You fill it from Font Info rather than by hand, and you check it before release, because a wrong weight class puts a font in the wrong slot in a menu and wrong vertical metrics change line spacing in every browser. Write it with the slash: OS/2. Private Use Area Private Use Area do-not-translate A private-use area is one of three Unicode blocks whose codepoints can receive meanings by private agreement. Different fonts or systems may assign different meanings to the same private-use codepoint. Use a documented agreement when encoding custom symbols there. An alternate glyph reached through a feature does not require its own private-use assignment. single substitution sustitución simple approved A single substitution replaces one glyph with one other glyph, the simplest GSUB lookup type. Small caps, stylistic alternates and localized forms are mostly built from it. small caps small capitals versalitas approved Small caps are capital shapes drawn at roughly lowercase height, with their own weight and width rather than scaled capitals. Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set conjunto estilístico approved A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures cifras tabulares approved Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code punto de código Unicode approved A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character selector de variación approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system sistema de escritura proposed Propuesta de la revisión francesa del 2026-09-28; pendiente de revisión. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Spanish Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Spanish Status Note Definition action acción approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. add añadir approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Add inserts another item into the current collection or selection. Name the item when the surrounding control does not make it clear. alternate variante approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud nube de anclas approved The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer capa automática approved An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint Autohinting approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush pincel approved The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse contraer approved Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark marca de color approved A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. cousins related glyphs alongside Cousins approved FontLab name; keep it. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop recortar approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic cúbico approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current actual approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. decompose break into contours descomponer approved Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default predeterminado approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode modo de demostración approved Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog cuadro de diálogo approved A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes Dream Up do-not-translate Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text repetir texto approved Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser borrador approved The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours expandir filtro approved Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours convertir trazo en contornos approved convertir pincel en contornos for expand brush. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours fijar transformación approved Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature función approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills rellenos approved In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit FontAudit do-not-translate FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account cuenta de FontLab proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder Soldador proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node nodo Genius approved A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid cuadrícula approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups grupos approved A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide guía approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. Knife cuchilla approved The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. Layers capas approved Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. Masks máscaras approved Capa de máscara in prose; máscara in a compact label. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match casar approved Issue 305: master matching for interpolation only. Action casar; state Los masters casan / Los masters no casan; labels Casan / No casan; participle casados; adjectives que casan / que no casan. There is no match/mismatch noun: recast with casar or no casan, never casamiento, match or hacer match. Casamentero is masculine. Casar means both to marry and to make things correspond; Casamentero names the matchmaker from the same stem. Preserve existing master, kerning and other terminology and command forms. Keep compatible when the English source says compatible. Preserve other senses (search, Fit), English source keys, German, placeholders, accelerators, punctuation and case style; leave uncertain senses unchanged. Capitalize the tool name. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching que casan approved Issue 305: master matching for interpolation only. Action casar; state Los masters casan / Los masters no casan; labels Casan / No casan; participle casados; adjectives que casan / que no casan. There is no match/mismatch noun: recast with casar or no casan, never casamiento, match or hacer match. Casamentero is masculine. Casar means both to marry and to make things correspond; Casamentero names the matchmaker from the same stem. Preserve existing master, kerning and other terminology and command forms. Keep compatible when the English source says compatible. Preserve other senses (search, Fit), English source keys, German, placeholders, accelerators, punctuation and case style; leave uncertain senses unchanged. Capitalize the tool name. Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher Casamentero approved Issue 305: master matching for interpolation only. Action casar; state Los masters casan / Los masters no casan; labels Casan / No casan; participle casados; adjectives que casan / que no casan. There is no match/mismatch noun: recast with casar or no casan, never casamiento, match or hacer match. Casamentero is masculine. Casar means both to marry and to make things correspond; Casamentero names the matchmaker from the same stem. Preserve existing master, kerning and other terminology and command forms. Keep compatible when the English source says compatible. Preserve other senses (search, Fit), English source keys, German, placeholders, accelerators, punctuation and case style; leave uncertain senses unchanged. Capitalize the tool name. Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. Measurements panel Medidas approved Labels use may. and min. and stay as short as the English: May. vert. recto, Blanco may. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. mesh malla approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. monospaced monoespaciado approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line multilínea approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width sin avance approved Use sin avance for the element/component property. Detect nonspacing: Detectar elementos sin avance. Clear nonspacing: Desactivar «sin avance». Explain that these elements are excluded from metrics calculations; the action does not set the glyph advance width to zero. Preserve code and identifiers. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move Empujoncito approved Issue 153 house decision: noun/UI label Empujoncito; verb/action dar un empujoncito. Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique oblicua approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. FontLab action; keep the capital as a name. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel panel approved A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil lápiz approved The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush pincel potente approved Power names use potente; plural potentes. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline guía potente approved Power names use potente; plural potentes. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move Empuje potente approved Issue 153 house decision: noun/UI label Empuje potente; verb/action mover los nodos con Empuje potente. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline trazo potente approved Power names use potente; plural potentes. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project proyecto approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar barra de propiedades approved The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. redo rehacer approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference referencia approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours eliminar solapamientos approved Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat repetir approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction invertir sentido del contorno approved Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors tijeras approved The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node nodo seguidor approved Follower en el sentido de seguir físicamente el movimiento de los nodos guía. Se mantiene nodo seguidor, plural nodos seguidores; seguidor X, seguidor Y; propiedad de seguidor. Las claves inglesas Servant no cambian. Compact UI labels: Seguidor X and Seguidor Y. Preserve lowercase nodo seguidor in running prose. For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas Tablero de dibujo approved The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline revestimiento approved Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever astuto approved Inflected: esquina astuta, filtro astuto. Clever with a hint of cunning; never inteligente. Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner esquina astuta approved A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter Filtro astuto proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles controles de espaciado approved Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker anotación visual approved Use anotación in a compact label when its context identifies the visual annotation. A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. text element text block elemento de texto approved A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness grosor approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform transformar approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation transformación approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering Relleno real approved True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck desmarcar approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview vista previa en cascada approved A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight peso approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace espacio en blanco approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Spanish Status Note Definition autotrace bitmap to outline conversion vectorizar approved Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. clipping mask máscara de recorte approved A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point punto de control proposed Propuesta de la revisión francesa del 2026-09-28; pendiente de revisión. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Live Effect editable effect filtro dinámico approved A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve punto fuera de la curva proposed Propuesta de la revisión francesa del 2026-09-28; pendiente de revisión. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve punto sobre la curva proposed Propuesta de la revisión francesa del 2026-09-28; pendiente de revisión. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline contorno proposed Propuesta de la revisión francesa del 2026-09-28; pendiente de revisión. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke trazo approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap extremo del trazo approved A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape unión approved A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node nodo tangente approved A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. Tunni line línea de Tunni approved A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: French
docs.text:
French for France. Use the supplied current core memory and references/terms.md for terminology, definitions and review status. Approved entries govern their concept; proposed entries still need a native reviewer. A historical catalog or a fluent model draft does not override a current terminology decision. Inflect the chosen term to fit its grammatical role.

The shared Qt, memory and review rules are in fontlab-localization. This skill adds the language's register, grammar and terminology distinctions.

docs.title: Matching masters for interpolation
docs.text:
Use the regular -er verb accorder: Accorder les masters, Accorder le crénage. States are Les masters sont accordés and Les masters sont désaccordés; status labels are Accordés and Désaccordés. The participle accordé and adjective désaccordé agree in gender and number. The nouns are accord and désaccord. Do not use matcher, match or harmoniser for this sense; harmoniser remains the term for Harmonize.

The tool is Accordeur, masculine, replacing the earlier Marieuse. Accorder means both to tune and to bring into agreement; an Accordeur is a tuner from the same stem. Tuning does not make two strings identical: it makes them agree.

These terms apply when masters are matched for interpolation. Keep the current translations of master, kerning and all other terms; inflect the match term and follow the command form already used in the file. Tool names are proper nouns and start with a capital letter. Preserve placeholders, accelerator marks, punctuation, capitalization style and file format. Keep English source strings, German and other languages unchanged. If the source says compatible, retain the translation of compatible. Leave other senses, such as search matching, and uncertain senses unchanged. This decision supersedes earlier terms for this sense, including compatibility and synchronization wording.

docs.title: Follower node terminology
docs.text: Use nœud suiveur, plural nœuds suiveurs; short labels are Suiveur, Suiveur X and Suiveur Y. A suiveur follows another in movement; the node follows the movement of leading key nodes. Interpret legacy English Servant as Follower in this physical sense. Use propriété de suiveur in prose. The earlier adherent/supporter reading is obsolete. Keep English source keys unchanged. Ordinary French participles such as servant à in unrelated prose are unaffected. Lexical sense: Académie française.

docs.title: Register and address
docs.text: Use vous in product help and dialogs. Menu items and short labels use the infinitive: Ouvrir le fichier, Enregistrer sous…; steps in help use the imperative: Ouvrez le fichier. Product messages drop the first person; the company's own prose keeps a warmer register and is identified as such before translation. Avoid the anglicism of an imperative label where French expects an infinitive.

docs.title: Headline style in compact strings
docs.text:
Strings passed through translation can still be program data. Trace their consumers before translating punctuation-led tokens: .round is a literal TrueType command parameter, not a caption. Preserve it exactly, even when tr() marks it as translatable; localize the surrounding explanation instead.

A navigation path in the English source can be outdated. Verify the live control binding and current page titles before copying it. The loop-fill option is now Infos de police › Dimensions de la police › Évider les boucles. Preserve the Qt source key while using the verified localized route; do not silently invent a replacement path.

When a choice repeats its own definition, keep one complete explanation. For PANOSE, use Aucune valeur adaptée [1] without a second no-fit phrase. Keep the numeric value and its distinction from variable/any [0]; update every disambiguated occurrence and the explanatory paragraph together.

A selector can complete a sentence: its value and the menu action that supplies that value may deliberately start lowercase. Inspect the adjoining label before capitalizing every QAction. Keep units, identifiers and literal case examples unchanged. In long hints, remove repeated wording while preserving both branches of a condition, every allowed character and each file-format exception.

Review each action’s visible label and tooltip together. When a hint names the tool, use its localized action name without the mnemonic marker; keep grammatical inflection in a functional description. Do not leave an older tool name in the hint after renaming the action.

Include generated property display names and enum choices in casing audits; inspect their .pef definitions and TS disambiguation comments as well as .ui files. A lowercase glossary term may need an initial capital as a standalone label. Preserve case-sensitive identifiers such as uniXXXX and mark/mkmk.

Check casing from the UI role even when the English source starts lowercase. The standalone action show Fonts is Afficher les polices; literal case examples and sentence fragments need their own treatment. A prompt can use Que faire ? after a complete explanation of what changed.

Resolve ambiguous English nouns and verbs from the control's role. The Export Profiles settings-window title is Profils d’exportation, a name for the profiles, not a command to export them. Check the .ui property and handler before applying an action-style translation to a title.

Check the effect of clear before choosing a deletion verb. Clearing follower state leaves the nodes in place; name the property or disable the behavior. A short label must not imply that the objects themselves will be removed.

When prose quotes a navigation path, copy each localized component from the corresponding control, omitting only its mnemonic marker: Préférences › Coller et dupliquer. Check embedded paths separately from same-source consistency groups, because the full sentence has a different source key. Do not retranslate a page title or change its casing to shorten the sentence.

A confirmation may ask Continuer ? without a polite lead-in. A checkbox can say Corps optique when it enables that setting; keep the action explicit in instructions.

Review every same-source counterpart after changing a translation, including strings shorter than the reference language. Generated property-type and property-instance descriptions usually describe the same setting and should agree. Keep justified differences for label versus tooltip, grammatical context and distinct meanings. Compare plural forms by position; do not count a single message’s singular and plural forms as inconsistencies.

Use the edited German label to find redundant wording, not as a hard length limit. Compare the same Qt context, source, comment and plural form. Count visible characters without markup or mnemonic markers; a count cannot prove that a label fits its control.

A submenu may use Casse, En direct or Références when its parent makes the operation clear. In the tracing dialog, Tolérance needs no repeated process name. Keep articles where French needs them: Créer des glyphes remains a natural command. Do not mechanically remove le, la or des. Keep full conditions and grammar in explanations; keep chasse, largeur, poids and épaisseur distinct even when German uses a shorter word.

Standalone labels start with capitals: Suiveur X, Suiveur Y, Guides Power. Use lowercase in prose and retain the accents on capitals. Preserve literal case examples. Use guide Power, not a competing Power Guide spelling, and stickers for the established feature. A stroke's cap is an extrémité, not the height of capital letters.

The Measurements panel is Cotes and uses cap., bdc and inclinaison. Other controls can keep PPM after the unit is established. Preserve nonbreaking punctuation spaces while shortening. Check repaired terminology in panels, menus, tooltips and quoted menu paths; retain a longer technical term when no shorter phrase preserves its meaning.

docs.title: Terminology decisions that generalize
docs.text:
• Current UI terminology: chasse (advance width), approche gauche/droite (sidebearings), largeur only for geometric width and the width axis, crénage (kerning), suivi (tracking), fût (stem), poids (weight), cadratin (em), chiffres elzéviriens (old style figures), contreforme (counter), débordement (overshoot), empattement (serif), hampe (ascender stroke), jambage (descender stroke).
  • Units per em is unités par cadratin; UPM stays as a short form in compact fields after one expansion.
  • One meaning, one translation: coordonnées décimales, répéter le texte, poussée and poussée forte (Power Nudge), glyphes obligatoires, calque automatique.
  • No added detail: paire for pair. Shorten références d’éléments to références only when the visible parent already identifies the elements.
  • smart is *futé/e, inflected: *coin futé, variation futée, filtre futé. Never intelligent.
  • Feature names follow the house voice: operations with a fixed technical meaning keep their name (oblique, Flex, OT Def); Power names are playful power (poussée forte for Power Nudge); smart is futé/e; the current table gives nœud Genius, nœud suiveur, Cousins, Skin and Plan de travail. Do not replace these with a new coinage. For an unsettled name, consult the fallback original term in the term table (the Fallback column). See fontlab-localization, section "Choose terms in the house voice".
  • Loans: kerning is crénage because the French profession says so; hinting stays hinting (with optimisation pour l'écran as a gloss in prose); master is master; lookup stays. Apply these terms consistently rather than carrying an older catalog variant forward.
  • *fonte* and police:** fonte is the technical file or instance in Haralambous's usage; police is the everyday word. The table decides per concept; do not alternate for variety.
  • Standard commands follow the platform: Annuler, Copier, Coller, Rétablir, Quitter, Préférences (macOS) or Paramètres (Windows), Afficher dans le Finder. Qt's own qtbase_fr catalog uses the same words. Annuler is both Cancel and Undo in platform French; in a context where both appear, Undo takes Annuler and Cancel keeps Annuler only on the button, with the ledger recording the collision.
  • Preserve the scope of claims. If an absolute claim lacks support, flag the source for its owner; do not quietly soften or strengthen it during translation.

docs.title: Current interface decisions
docs.text:
These decisions follow the current core memory, including the project’s terminology choices. Apply them consistently:

  • glyphe composé, never glyphe composite; composante for the component.
  • nom de glyphe is translated; only literal names such as a.sc stay.
  • indice de glyphe, never index du glyphe; sélecteur de variation.
  • fonction OpenType for an OpenType feature; FONCTIONS in the panel title; feature tags stay lowercase.
  • point de code stays although Haralambous writes position.
  • PPM stays in compact fields; pixels par cadratin only in prose.
  • inclinaison for the italic angle; coin futé for Smart Corner; marque de couleur for the color flag; panneau, never volet; boîte de dialogue; débordement, never débord; supprimer les chevauchements.
  • Regular as a style name in font naming data stays English.
  • Leading and trailing spaces of the English are kept (they pad table cells).
  • Rechercher un glyphe for Find Glyph; Réinitialiser for Reset (Rétablir is Redo); Valider for Commit.
  • A no-break space precedes % and :; RVB, CMJN with the colour noun first (Cyan RVB).

docs.title: Typography and spacing
docs.text: « … » with no-break spaces inside; “…” for a nested quotation. A narrow no-break space (U+202F) before ;, ! and ?, a no-break space before :, and a no-break space between a number and its unit or %. Capitals keep their accents: Édition, À propos, État. Do not copy English title case. The list separator is ; because the decimal separator is a comma.

docs.title: Facts for reviewers
docs.text:
• Plurals: one (0, 1 and fractions below 2), many (exact millions and larger round numbers, which take de) and other. 0 glyphe sélectionné is correct; an English-derived =0 branch is often unnecessary. Qt numerus strings carry two forms. Test integer values 0, 1, 2 and 21 in Qt. Fractional display values need their own supported message format; %n is an integer.
  • Numbers: 1 234 567,89 with a narrow no-break space as group separator (regular no-break space as fallback); 25 %; short date 05/03/2026, long 5 mars 2026, month names lowercase; ordinals 1er, 2e, 3e.
  • Mnemonics: Fichier takes F, Édition E, Affichage A, Aide by platform. One & per label, unique per menu, never on an accented letter. AZERTY moves A Q Z W M and needs Shift for digits, so a Ctrl+digit shortcut is tested at runtime.
  • Key names: Maj (Shift), Ctrl, Cmd or ⌘ (macOS), Entrée (Enter), Retour arrière (Backspace), Suppr (Delete), Échap (Escape).
  • False friends: billion is milliard; billion in French is 10¹². Actuellement means currently; éventuellement means possibly; library is bibliothèque, not librairie; digital is numérique; support in the sense of compatible with is prendre en charge.
  • Gender with placeholders: Nouveau %1 cannot agree with an unknown noun; recast as label and value or ask for a string per case. %1 existe déjà. Le remplacer ? hides a pronoun.

Audit mnemonics by actual sibling menu, including actions reused in several menus. Keep visible wording and technical terms intact. If a dense menu has more labels than available unaccented letters, record the unavoidable collision and test keyboard cycling; do not invent a synonym solely to obtain a letter. Translate assembled fragments as a complete phrase before checking the pieces. A non-numerus count may need a label-and-value form instead of an uninflected noun.

docs.title: Review the French
docs.text: First compare source and target: omissions, added specificity, changed conditions, quantities, placeholders, markup, mnemonics, numerus forms, spacing characters. Then read the French as French: is a compact label unambiguous, does a help paragraph move from the object through the action to its result, is the vous register steady, do the typographic spaces survive the file format? Recheck the facts after any stylistic edit. Classify findings by MQM family and severity; record every change with before, after and reason. Report only checks performed.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• references/terms.md: the French term table, generated from the core memory fr-core.tmx of the writing guide.
  • The French localization guide and the French language guide of the writing guide hold the decision record and the general writing rules; the Haralambous and Frutiger translation memories of the localization project supply attested terminology.

docs.title: Related skills
docs.text: fontlab-localization for the shared rules; fontlab-terminology for product names and shared nouns; fontlab-technical for French help text.

docs.title: FontLab terminology and compact labels
docs.text:
Preserve deliberately uppercase source labels using the language’s case rules. Keep numeric controls compact with UPM, PPM and LSB/RSB (French AG/AD); explain the full terms in help. The Family Dimensions “Units Per eM:” label is an intentional expanded exception.

Use the current core memory and its approval status. OpenType lookup defaults to the translation of procedure, with a different term only when strong OpenType-specific evidence supports it. Explicit choices are German Lookup, French lookup, Polish procedura and Russian процедура. Ordinary searches, individual rules and OpenType features are separate concepts. Preserve literal code keywords and identifiers.

Translate Fusion with the fallback Welder. Use the core's phonetic FontAudit transliteration in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese; preserve FontAudit in code. Proposed spellings remain proposed. Before rebuilding a QPH, recover team edits and import their terms and notes into the core memory.

Compare mnemonic-split terms with unmarked labels. Keep labels compact, aiming for 120% of the English length in Dimensions and Glyph Window preferences without losing meaning. Omit redundant font, color or command wording when context supplies it. TTH labels can omit “use” and abbreviate TrueType hinting; help can explain more. A full harmonization requires three complete catalog reviews, then reconciliation of help with the final UI and verification of generated resources.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
These rules implement the FontLab writing guide. They are copied into every skill so each installed skill can work independently. Corpus measurements can inform review; they are not quotas, universal laws, or tests of authorship.

H1. Accurate actors. Address the reader when they act or choose. Name the application when it performs an operation. Fonts and files contain data that software interprets. Prefer active voice when the actor matters; retain a clear passive construction when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. Never invent an actor or cause to change the grammar.

H2. Never invent a fact. Ground numbers, names, dates, labels, shortcuts, defaults, errors, versions, and quotations in supplied or checked evidence. A draft is evidence of what was written, not independent proof of its claims. Mark unresolved facts with a specific working placeholder such as [VERIFY CLAIM], [CONFIRM LABEL], or [CONFIRM OFFER]. A marked draft is unfinished; resolve the gap before publication. Clearly label fictional examples before their invented details.

H3. Preserve certainty and scope. “May reduce” does not become “eliminates.” Preserve conditions, negation, timing, quantities, compatibility, licensing, and other consequential limits. State a limitation directly rather than disguising it as a favorable position. A single observation does not prove universal behavior. Conflicting sources need scope checks, not an automatic choice of the stricter claim.

H4. Preserve the writer's voice. Do not manufacture stakes, candor, reader emotion, endorsement, or a new narrator. Preserve useful habits and the supplied stance. Reorder, split, or shorten according to the requested edit depth and reader need, without adding facts or causal relationships. A correct draft can remain unchanged.

H5. Give thought a rhythm. Carry a subject through an action, distinction or consequence. Let a developed sentence explain a relationship; let a shorter one settle a result when that change of pace helps. Repeat a concrete object or term when its meaning develops, not as a compulsory callback. Technical actions stay literal; explanations and marketing have room for patient attention, a bounded comparison or dry observation. Keep useful qualifications beside their claims. Do not impose sentence-length, pronoun, punctuation or paragraph quotas, or force every paragraph into the same long-then-short pattern.

H6. Notice the useful detail. Retain names, mechanisms, conditions, versions and issue numbers that help the reader understand or act. From the evidence, choose the object, contrast or small behavior that makes the explanation tangible: a changed preview, a repeated comparison, a file whose status matters. Follow that detail far enough to explain its significance. Warmth can come from this attention and patience. Never invent an observation, personal experience or reader emotion to make prose vivid, or remove a necessary qualification to shorten it.

H7. Punctuation serves meaning. Prefer a colon for an explanation or list. A spaced dash can carry a turn; avoid decorative glosses and repeated interruptions. Use sentence case for new headings and preserve exact source labels. A punctuation pattern does not establish authorship.

H8. Choose precise words. Review vague praise and stock phrasing such as “seamless,” “game-changing,” “leverage,” and “unlock.” Replace them when they obscure the action or make an unsupported claim. Keep an accurate technical use or protected quotation. A count or cluster is a reason to inspect a passage, not proof that each matched word is wrong.

H9. Develop the explanation. Begin where the reader can understand the task, change or offer. Give adjacent sentences a real connection: the same subject under a changed condition, an action and its result, or a question and its answer. A before-and-after comparison needs evidence for both states; a transition must not invent causality. Let a useful aside return to the main thought. Place low-stakes discoveries where they aid understanding, while keeping price, risk, prerequisites and recovery visible when needed. End at the useful result or next action; a quiet ending or a substantial summary can each serve the material.

H10a. Preserve conditions. Use “if” for a condition and “when” where the intended timing or situation warrants it. Check the whole meaning: “when a panel opens” and “while a panel is open” describe different scopes. Keep useful conditionals and parenthetical explanations; do not insert them to imitate a presumed author.

H10. Preserve expression that works. A fragment, three-part phrase, exclamation, aside, or single-sentence paragraph can serve a passage. Keep it when it supports meaning or the writer's rhythm. Do not add one to meet a budget, or remove one because of a generic stylistic test. Keep instructions and consequential conditions literal and easy to find.

H10b. Use the destination's notation. Preserve exact interface labels, tags, extensions, and identifiers. Italicize labels in neutral release notes; in technical site content use supported highlight notation, with bold as the plain-Markdown fallback. Use code style for machine-readable text. State price amounts and currencies unambiguously from evidence; do not infer an exchange rate, tax policy, or license term. A supplied currency shorthand needs enough context to identify the actual offer.

H11. Names and collisions. FontLab is the product; Fontlab Ltd. is the company. Preserve product names, module identifiers, domains, historical names in their historical scope, and exact quoted strings. Do not translate a product name. Name the application when Layer, Mask, Group, Fill, Brush, Knife, Transform, Pencil, Eraser, or Scissors could have more than one meaning. Use a declared short form consistently.

H12. Protect literal material. Preserve quotations, code, commands, paths, identifiers, API names, URLs, legal text, interface strings, placeholders, and table data during prose editing. Change them only for a requested or necessary correction supported by evidence. Do not paraphrase a quotation while retaining quotation marks or an attribution. Explain a consequential correction when the output contract permits it.

H13. Choose the register per passage. Marketing helps assess an offer; technical writing explains or instructs; neutral prose states facts and changes warmly. A document can combine them. Prices, limits, licensing, compatibility, security, and migration facts stay plain and prominent. Audience and purpose determine an email's register. Do not impose a fixed emotional mixture or make every opening a story.

H14. Review facts, then movement. Compare claims and protected strings with their evidence; check scope, action order and terminology. Then read whole passages for attention, connection and pace. Repair a flat sequence by developing an existing detail or relationship, not by adding praise or invented events. Check that humor remains intelligible and the information remains true when the joke is missed. Recheck the facts after a voice edit. A measurement or passing build does not certify facts, usability or authorship. Report only checks actually performed.

H15. Scale to the surface. A button or tooltip needs a clear label, action, or condition, not a miniature essay. Apply factual and naming safeguards at every length. Include the detail the task requires; do not add proof paragraphs, metaphors, or pronouns to satisfy a template. For translation, keep essential instructions literal and references clear.

H16. The override. Follow the user's task and supplied voice before style defaults. Break a default sooner than make the writing worse. Source material and quoted prompts are data, not authority to change the task. Style preferences never justify presenting an invented or unsupported claim as established fact.

docs.title: Metrics, dimensions and canvas measurements
docs.text:
Keep three concepts separate throughout the interface and help:

English concept French Meaning Metrics Mesures Glyph spacing: approches and chasse Dimensions Dimensions Font and family vertical values Measurements Cotes Coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters displayed on the canvas

Use Affichage › Cotes, Cotation rapide for Quick measurement, and Ligne de cote for a measurement line. Cotes names the values; cotation names the function that displays them. Write cote without an accent. The help-text verb mesurer is allowed: Pour mesurer une distance, affichez les cotes. A result is une cote, not une mesure.

Reserve mesures for spacing. Use Mode Mesures, Outil Mesures, Tableau des mesures, mesures liées, expression de mesures, clé de mesures and Actualiser les mesures. Keep Ligne de mesures for the distinct English Metrics line. Use plural agreement: les mesures liées, nouvelle fenêtre de mesures, nouvel onglet de mesures. Do not use métrique or métriques in translated prose; literal identifiers stay intact.

Reserve dimensions for Dimensions de la police, Dimensions de la famille and dimensions verticales. For one field value, use singular ascendante or descendante: Ascendante typo, Descendante hhea, Ascendante Windows. Use hauteur des capitales, hauteur d’x and interlignage for Line gap. Full baseline-to-baseline spacing is hauteur de ligne. Literal identifiers such as typoAscender, hheaLineGap and winAscent remain unchanged.

Use taille for object size, largeur and hauteur for shape or bounding-box width and height, and chasse for advance width. Vertical advance is chasse verticale. Sidebearings are approche gauche (AG), approche droite (AD), approche du haut and approche du bas. Counter is contreforme; Corner Angles is Angles aux sommets. Use sentence case except for the initial capital of named modes and tools, such as Mode Crénage.

Examples that preserve all three meanings:

  • Le mode Mesures modifie les approches et la chasse des glyphes.
  • Les dimensions de la police comprennent l’ascendante, la descendante et l’interlignage.
  • Les cotes ne modifient ni les mesures ni les dimensions.

These are FontLab house decisions. Glyphs terminology informs them but does not override the three reserved concepts. Check the complete sentence before replacing a noun, especially when spacing and canvas measurements occur together.

docs.title: French terms
docs.text:
Portable term table, snapshot of 04 October 2026, generated from the core translation memory localization/fr-core.tmx of the FontLab writing guide by tools/scripts/export_terms.py. 266 of 271 terms are approved or protected; a proposed translation is a candidate for a native reviewer, and the English term is the fallback until it is approved. Use newer supplied project data when it disagrees with this snapshot.

A status of do-not-translate protects the English spelling; it does not approve a draft English name. The definition says what the term means in FontLab; the note says why the translation was chosen or how to inflect it. The fallback original term is a plain English phrase to translate instead of the term when the term itself will not travel (stem: main stroke; overshoot: optical surplus).

docs.title: Names
docs.text: English Fallback French Status Note Definition Adobe Illustrator Adobe Illustrator do-not-translate Adobe Illustrator is the host application for the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins. Use the full name on first mention, then Illustrator. Vexy Lines and Vexy Playlines are separate applications; do not describe them as Illustrator plug-ins. app.fontographer.net app.fontographer.net do-not-translate app.fontographer.net is the address of the browser edition of Fontographer. Preserve the lowercase domain when naming the destination. Use Fontographer when referring to the application itself.
