An instruction cites a CVT entry rather than a raw number, so one change to the table reaches every glyph that cites it. You work with it through the TrueType Hinting panel. It ships in the font, alongside the instructions themselves and the prep and fpgm programs that set the machine up. design space variation range डिज़ाइन स्पेस proposed No Hindi attestation; transliterated professional loan, since Indian type designers learn the term in English. A design space describes the positions defined by a font project's variation axes. Masters provide source data at specified locations; instances represent results at selected locations. User coordinates and internal design coordinates may be connected by a mapping, or may have the same values. State which coordinate system a number belongs to when the distinction affects a procedure. device correction per-size pixel correction डिवाइस सुधार proposed No attestation; डिवाइस is the Apple/Microsoft loan; सुधार is the natural word for a correction. A device correction adjusts a kerning or positioning value by whole pixels at one pixel size, to fix rounding at that size only. Stored in GPOS device tables; rarely needed on modern rasterizers. dimensions आयाम proposed Microsoft Hindi word for dimensions; kept distinct from मेट्रिक्स and माप. The font or family vertical values, such as ascender, descender, capital height, x-height and line gap. Distinguish these values from glyph spacing and canvas measurements. element एलिमेंट proposed Loan as on the Adobe Hindi site (एलिमेंट्स) and in Apple (टेक्स्ट एलिमेंट). Rejected अवयव/तत्व (Krita): bookish, and they blur element with component. An element is FontLab's container for a piece of drawing inside a glyph: one or more contours, an image, or a reference to another element. A glyph holds elements, and an element holds contours, which is the layer of structure that makes a serif or a stem reusable across a family. You work with elements in the Elements panel and with the Element tool. The word is FontLab's own; other editors call the nearest thing a path group or a component. element reference shared drawing link एलिमेंट रेफ़रेंस proposed Derived from एलिमेंट and रेफ़रेंस. An element reference is a placed copy of an element that still points at the original. Edit the original and every reference updates. You use references to share a serif, a stem, or a whole letter across a family, and you decompose a reference only when a glyph genuinely needs to diverge. A component is the familiar case of an element reference: one glyph placed inside another. Keep references intact through the design phase, since decomposing early throws away the link that makes a late change cheap. family dimensions परिवार आयाम proposed Derived; परिवार is Apple Font Book's word for a font family. The vertical values used to establish line layout for a font family. Platform-specific ascender, descender and line-gap fields belong to this group. Flex फ़्लेक्स proposed Fixed name of a PostScript hint, transliterated like ओब्लीक; never translated. Flex is a PostScript hint that flattens a shallow curve, such as a cup serif, to a straight line at small sizes. FontLab marks glyphs that carry it. Keep the name. font dimensions फ़ॉन्ट आयाम proposed Derived from आयाम. The design dimensions of a font master, including ascender, descender, capital height and x-height. These values describe the vertical proportions of the design. font target export target लक्ष्य फ़ॉन्ट proposed No attestation; fallback 'export target' rendered as 'target font', like Polish; लक्ष्य is the Microsoft word. A font target is what TransType produces from a source: the output font, with its format, its names, and the filters applied on the way. Sources go in on one side and targets come out on the other, and one source can produce several targets. You set the target options before you convert, and you name the target in a procedure step so a reader knows which side of the conversion a setting belongs to. font unit फ़ॉन्ट यूनिट proposed No attestation; everyday loan यूनिट, matching the expansion यूनिट प्रति एम. Rejected इकाई (formal). A font unit is the coordinate step of a font's design grid. UPM says how many of them make one em, so a 700 unit stem in a 1000 UPM font is 70 percent of the em. Metrics, kerning values and node coordinates are all stated in font units. fractional coordinates non-integer coordinates दशमलव निर्देशांक proposed No attestation; 'decimal coordinates', as German and French did; दशमलव is everyday, निर्देशांक the Microsoft and school word. Fractional coordinates are node positions with decimal places, kept for curve fidelity while you draw. Font formats store integers, so FontLab rounds on export or when you turn on Round coordinates for the font. friendly glyph name readable glyph name पठनीय ग्लिफ़ नाम proposed No attestation; fallback 'readable glyph name' translated. A friendly glyph name is the readable name FontLab shows for editing, such as Aacute, as opposed to the production name written into the exported font, such as uni00C1. FontLab can keep both and convert on export. ghost hint edge-only fitting instruction घोस्ट हिंट proposed No attestation; loan compound. A translated भूत हिंट was rejected as comic without being clearer. A ghost hint is a PostScript hint with a special width that marks one edge, such as the top of a round letter, when there is no stem to hint. It aligns that edge to an alignment zone. hint screen fitting instruction हिंट proposed No Hindi attestation; transliterated professional loan, since Indian type designers learn the term in English. Rejected संकेत (Apple/Microsoft): the office sense of a tip or cue. A hint is a stored instruction that tells a rasterizer how to align a stem or a zone to the pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hints describe stems and zones; TrueType hints are instructions. FontLab draws hints in the Glyph window and generates them with autohinting. The word stays English in every language. hint zone hinting height band हिंट ज़ोन proposed Derived from हिंट; ज़ोन is the everyday loan. A hint zone is a horizontal band, such as the baseline or the x-height, inside which a rasterizer snaps overshoots to the same pixel row. FontLab stores zones in Font Info and shows them in the Glyph window. An alignment zone is the PostScript name for the same thing; hint zone is the general term. hinting screen fitting हिंटिंग proposed Derived from हिंट; no Hindi attestation; transliterated professional loan, since Indian type designers learn the term in English. Hinting is the extra information a font carries so that its outlines land predictably on a pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hinting declares stems and alignment zones and leaves the rasterizer to interpret them. TrueType hinting gives instructions that move points explicitly, with the control values in the CVT table. You work on PostScript hints in the glyph and in Font Info, and on TrueType hints with the TrueType Hinting tool and panel. Autohinting produces a starting point you then correct. instance generated design इंस्टेंस proposed No typographic attestation; common software loan (Microsoft Hindi documentation). Rejected उदाहरण, which means an example, not a generated font. An instance is a particular result at a location in a font's variation space. A named instance, such as Semibold, gives a selected location a name that applications can present. Other locations need not have names. In FontLab, configured instances can be exported as static fonts or included as named instances in a variable font. interpolation इंटरपोलेशन proposed Loan. Rejected अंतर्वेशन (Krita): a mathematics-textbook Sanskritism designers do not use. Interpolation calculates values between source values. In font design, it can calculate outlines, metrics and other data from masters at specified design-space locations. Outline interpolation requires corresponding contour and point structures. Structural compatibility makes the calculation possible, but does not guarantee a good drawing: inspect intermediate results as well as the masters. Extrapolation calculates beyond the source range. kern exception pair spacing exception कर्निंग अपवाद proposed No attestation; अपवाद is the common word for an exception. A kern exception is a pair value that overrides what the classes would otherwise apply. One member of a class rarely behaves like the rest, and the exception says so without breaking the class apart. You create one in the Kerning panel by kerning the single pair while its classes stay in place. Keep exceptions few: a class with many exceptions is the wrong class, and the cheaper fix is to split it rather than to list every disagreement. kerning pair spacing correction कर्निंग proposed Adobe Hindi site, Apple CoreText (कर्निंग नहीं) and Microsoft Word all use the loan. Verb: कर्न करें (Adobe: 'टाइप को मैन्युअल रूप से कर्न करना'). Kerning adjusts the spacing of particular glyph combinations beyond their normal advances. A pair such as AV may need a different gap from the one produced by its unadjusted metrics. OpenType fonts commonly store horizontal kerning in GPOS lookups associated with the kern feature; some formats and workflows use a separate kern table. Name the mechanism when it matters to export or compatibility. kerning class pair spacing group कर्निंग क्लास proposed Derived; क्लास as in Apple Font Book (Class = क्लास). A kerning class groups glyphs that need the same kerning. You put every glyph that behaves alike on one side into one class, then kern the class once instead of kerning each pair inside it. FontLab applies the class value to every member pair and keeps single pairs as exceptions where a member needs its own value. Classes matter because a text face carries thousands of readable pairs, and a hand kerned list of that size is unmaintainable. FontLab writes the result into GPOS as class based positioning. kerning pair spacing-corrected pair कर्निंग जोड़ा proposed Adobe Hindi site (कर्निंग जोड़े, कर्निंग जोड़ों). Rejected LibreOffice's युग्म (Sanskritized). A kerning pair associates two glyphs, or two kerning classes, with a spacing adjustment. In horizontal kerning, a negative value normally reduces the gap and a positive value increases it. An individual glyph pair may provide an exception to class kerning, but it can also exist without a class rule. Check pairs in representative text as well as in isolation. left sidebearing बाईं साइडबेयरिंग proposed Derived from साइडबेयरिंग (feminine); Apple uses बाईं/दाईं for left/right. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the glyph origin and the left edge of its outline. It contributes to the glyph advance width and its spacing. Lib Lib proposed Mirrors the UFO lib key; kept in Latin like German, French and Polish. Lib is the custom metadata dictionary of a font or a master, mirroring the UFO lib and stored in VFJ. Scripts and tools keep their own keys there. line gap पंक्ति अंतराल proposed No attestation; natural words; पंक्ति for a text line as in Microsoft Hindi. The line gap is extra vertical space between lines that a font recommends beyond ascender and descender. hhea and OS/2 each store one. line height पंक्ति ऊँचाई proposed No attestation; natural words, parallel to पंक्ति अंतराल. The distance between successive text baselines. It includes the relevant ascender, descender and line-gap contributions; line gap alone is only the additional space. link metrics tie spacing to another glyph मेट्रिक्स लिंक करें proposed No attestation; command form with the everyday loan लिंक. Link metrics ties a glyph's sidebearing or advance width to another glyph or to an expression, so the value follows its source. FontLab shows linked metrics with the expression and updates them when the source changes. linked metrics लिंक किए गए मेट्रिक्स proposed Derived from मेट्रिक्स लिंक करें; participle pattern as in Apple's इंस्टॉल किया गया. Glyph spacing values linked to another glyph or to an expression. Updating the source or expression changes the dependent advance width or sidebearings. mark attachment combining mark positioning मार्क अटैचमेंट proposed No attestation; loan of the OpenType term on मार्क. Mark attachment positions a combining mark relative to a base glyph, a ligature component or another mark. OpenType GPOS lookups describe the anchor relationships, and the shaping engine applies the positioning during layout. FontLab can generate attachment code from suitable anchors. Check the relevant generation settings and test combinations, including stacked marks, rather than assuming that every anchor automatically becomes a lookup. master source design मास्टर proposed Loan, as in Microsoft PowerPoint/Visio Hindi; no Hindi word names an interpolation source. Rejected स्वामी/प्रधान (wrong sense). A master provides source outlines and other font data at a specified location in a design space. Masters can describe weight, width or other variations, including intermediate locations. FontLab uses corresponding data from masters to calculate instances. For outline interpolation, check contour and point compatibility in each affected glyph; the word master alone does not guarantee that every glyph is present or compatible. master compatibility matching master structure मास्टर संगतता proposed Derived from मास्टर; संगतता is the Microsoft word for compatibility. Master compatibility is the condition every glyph must meet before it can interpolate: the same number of contours in the same order, with the same number of nodes and the same start point in each. FontLab reports incompatible glyphs and gives you Matchmaker to repair them by matching contours and start points between masters. Fix compatibility before you tune shapes, because a repair that reorders nodes moves every curve that depends on them. metrics मेट्रिक्स proposed Apple Font Book (Metrics = मेट्रिक्स). Treated as masculine plural. Metrics are the measurements that place a glyph in a line: its advance width and its two sidebearings. Vertical metrics are a separate set, the font wide values for ascender, descender, and line gap. You work on horizontal metrics in the Metrics panel and with the Metrics tool, and on vertical metrics in Font Info. Say which set you mean whenever a page discusses both, because a reader who applies a horizontal instruction to the vertical fields breaks line spacing everywhere the font is used. metrics expression मेट्रिक्स एक्सप्रेशन proposed No attestation; loan एक्सप्रेशन. Rejected Microsoft's व्यंजक, which also means a consonant, awkward in a font editor. An expression that calculates a glyph advance width or sidebearing from other values. It describes a spacing relationship rather than a canvas measurement. metrics key मेट्रिक्स कुंजी proposed Derived; कुंजी (Microsoft) because the loan की would read as the Hindi genitive particle. A glyph reference or expression used to derive a spacing value. The referenced value determines an advance width or sidebearing. pin पिन proposed Issue 160 catalog family review: named point inside an element, distinct from a glyph-layer anchor. Proteus Resources/helptips.json def.anchorpin defines the behavior. Preserve this term across panel, tool, action and help labels; proposed terminology, not native-team approval. A pin is a named point inside an element. Use pins to position elements with expressions and to attach elements to each other. An anchor is a named point in a glyph layer, used for component placement and mark attachment. Create either with the Guides tool and edit it in the Anchors and Pins panel. PPM pixels per type body PPM proposed Abbreviation kept in Latin for compact hinting fields; in prose expand as पिक्सेल प्रति एम. Corpus hits for ppm are parts per million. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. PPM, pixels per em, is the size at which a rasterizer renders a font: how many pixels one em occupies. TrueType hints, device corrections and bitmap strikes are specified per PPM. In explanatory prose expand it; in hinting fields the short form is usual. production glyph name shipping glyph name प्रोडक्शन ग्लिफ़ नाम proposed No attestation; loan प्रोडक्शन; rejected उत्पादन (manufacturing). A production glyph name is the name written into the exported font, chosen for compatibility with tools and the Adobe Glyph List, such as uni00C1 rather than Aacute. rendering drawing on screen रेंडरिंग proposed Inkscape Hindi; common loan. Rendering is the conversion of an outline into pixels on a screen or a printer. The rasterizer of the operating system or of FontLab's preview reads the outline, applies the hints and paints the result. FontLab previews rendering at chosen pixel sizes so you can judge hints. Rasterization names the same step from the pixel side. required glyphs mandatory glyphs आवश्यक ग्लिफ़ proposed आवश्यक as in Apple CoreText (Required Ligatures). Required glyphs are the ones the OpenType specification and common tools expect at the start of a font: .notdef, NULL or uni0000, CR or uni000D and space. FontLab can add them on export. right sidebearing दाईं साइडबेयरिंग proposed Derived from साइडबेयरिंग (feminine). Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the right edge of a glyph outline and the end of its advance width. It contributes to spacing. sidebearing side space साइडबेयरिंग proposed No Hindi attestation; transliterated professional loan, since Indian type designers learn the term in English. Feminine. Rejected a calque of the fallback (बग़ल की रिक्ति): too close to spacing. A sidebearing is the space between a glyph's outline and the edge of its advance width: the left sidebearing before the shape, the right sidebearing after it. Together with the advance width it sets how the glyph spaces against every other glyph, which is the work that carries a text face further than kerning does. You edit sidebearings in the Metrics panel or with the Metrics tool, one glyph at a time or across a selection, and you check them in a word rather than in isolation. size आकार proposed Apple Font Book (फ़ॉन्ट आकार, ग्लिफ़ आकार). Adobe's site also uses साइज़, rejected because आकार is natural and established. The size of an object or the chosen size of displayed text. Name a specific width or height when only one direction is intended. spacing स्पेसिंग proposed Apple CoreText/Font Book (कैपिटल स्पेसिंग, संख्या स्पेसिंग) and Adobe Hindi site. Microsoft's रिक्ति is the rejected alternative. The adjustment of glyph advance widths and sidebearings to establish the space between letters. Kerning makes additional adjustments to particular pairs. standard stem reference stem width मानक स्टेम proposed Derived; मानक as in Apple's मानक फ़ॉन्ट. Standard stems are the representative horizontal and vertical stem widths declared in a font for hinting. The rasterizer snaps stems near those widths to the same pixel count, so like stems stay alike at small sizes. stem link stem tie स्टेम लिंक proposed Derived from स्टेम and लिंक. A stem link ties two edges of a stroke together as a stem, so hinting can hold their distance as the size changes. A vertical link governs a horizontal measurement and a horizontal link governs a vertical one. You add links in the glyph, either by hand or from an autohinting pass, and you keep them consistent with the standard stem widths declared in Font Info. Vextra reuses the term for the paired edges it detects in artwork that is not type. styling group name शैली समूह नाम proposed Built from Apple's शैली (style), समूह and नाम. The styling group name, SGN, ties together the styles an application reaches through its bold and italic buttons, and the styling link value and styling link name say which slot each style takes in that group. The mechanism is older than typographic family names and narrower: four slots, no more. You set these fields in TransType when a family has to behave correctly in applications that still drive style selection from those buttons. subsetting cutting down a font सबसेटिंग proposed No attestation; loan; the Adobe Hindi site uses सबसेट. Subsetting exports only part of a font, such as the glyphs a page uses or one codepage, to make a smaller file. The OS/2 embedding bits can forbid it. top sidebearing ऊपरी साइडबेयरिंग proposed Derived from साइडबेयरिंग. The space above the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. tracking uniform letter spacing ट्रैकिंग proposed Adobe Hindi site (कर्निंग, ट्रैकिंग और लीडिंग). Krita's ट्रेकिंग is a misspelling. Tracking changes the spacing across a run of text, rather than correcting particular pairs as kerning does. Layout applications apply it to text. TransType's Tracking filter changes spacing in the font data itself. That changes the font's starting metrics; a layout application can still apply additional tracking to text set in the resulting font. TrueType instruction pixel fitting instruction TrueType निर्देश proposed No attestation; TrueType stays Latin (Apple); निर्देश is the Microsoft word for an instruction. A TrueType instruction is one step of the program a TrueType font runs to fit an outline to the pixel grid. Instructions are the TrueType form of hints. FontLab writes them from visual TrueType hints and can keep the ones a font already has. Say instruction for the code and hint for what the reader draws. typographic family name टाइपोग्राफ़िक परिवार नाम proposed Built from Apple Font Book's परिवार and नाम; टाइपोग्राफ़िक as on the Adobe Hindi site. The typographic family name, TFN, is the name that groups every style of a family under one entry, and the typographic style name, TSN, is what distinguishes a style inside it. They sit beside the older four style family and style names that legacy applications read. You set them in TransType and in Font Info, and you keep them consistent across a family, because an app that reads these fields builds its font menu from them. update metrics मेट्रिक्स अपडेट करें proposed No attestation; command form; अपडेट is the common loan. Recalculate glyph spacing values from their links or expressions. This command updates the advance widths and sidebearings that depend on those relationships. variable font वेरिएबल फ़ॉन्ट proposed No attestation; loan in general Hindi web usage. Rejected परिवर्तनीय फ़ॉन्ट (reads as 'convertible'). A variable font contains data for design variation along one or more axes. Applications select axis values and calculate the corresponding outlines and other variable data. Named instances identify selected locations, but users are not limited to those locations when the application exposes axis controls. A variable font's supported range depends on its data; it need not contain every style in the family. variation location position in the variation range वेरिएशन स्थान proposed No attestation; स्थान is Apple's word for a location; वेरिएशन matches वेरिएबल फ़ॉन्ट. A variation location is a point in the design space, given as one value per axis. Masters and instances each have one, and the Variations panel slider shows the current one. vertical advance glyph box height लंबवत एडवांस proposed Derived; लंबवत is Apple CoreText's word for vertical. The vertical advance is the distance a glyph advances in vertical text, the counterpart of advance width for East Asian layout. Stored in vmtx. vertical metrics लंबवत मेट्रिक्स proposed Apple's लंबवत and मेट्रिक्स. The font-wide vertical values used for line layout, including ascender, descender and line gap. FontLab groups these as dimensions, distinct from glyph spacing metrics. visual kerning shape-measured spacing correction विज़ुअल कर्निंग proposed No attestation; loan विज़ुअल as on the Adobe Hindi site; rejected दृश्य कर्निंग (reads as 'visible kerning'). Visual kerning is kerning that FontLab proposes by measuring the shapes, so that a font gets a usable first pass without a person typing thousands of values. You run it over a selection, then review what it produced, because a measurement of two outlines does not know about the words a reader will meet. Treat the result as a draft: keep the pairs it got right, correct the ones it did not, and kern the difficult pairs by eye in real words. weight axis thickness axis वज़न अक्ष proposed Derived from वज़न and अक्ष. The weight axis, tag wght, varies stroke thickness from light to bold. In a variable font it is the most common axis; its master locations use the usWeightClass scale, such as 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. weight class वज़न क्लास proposed Derived; क्लास as in Apple Font Book. The weight class is the OS/2 value from 100 to 900 that tells applications how heavy a style is, with 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. Style linking and menus rely on it. width axis narrow-to-wide axis चौड़ाई अक्ष proposed Derived; चौड़ाई is Apple CoreText's word for width. The width axis, tag wdth, varies letter proportions from condensed to extended. It is distinct from advance width, which is the spacing of one glyph, and from the geometric width of a shape. Its scale is a percentage of normal width. width class चौड़ाई क्लास proposed Derived; a classification, not the axis value. The width class is the OS/2 value from 1, ultra condensed, to 9, ultra expanded, that tells applications how wide a style is. It is a classification, not the width axis value and not the advance width.

docs.title: OpenType
docs.text: English Fallback Hindi Status Note Definition Adobe Glyph List Adobe Glyph List do-not-translate The Adobe Glyph List maps standard glyph names to Unicode codepoints, so that a glyph named aacute is understood as U plus 00E1 by any tool that follows it. You name glyphs by it wherever it covers the character, because tools and text engines can then infer the mapping without being told twice. Where it does not cover a glyph, you fall back to a consistent scheme of your own and assign codepoints explicitly. Write the name in full on first mention, then AGL. alternate glyph glyph variant वैकल्पिक ग्लिफ़ proposed Derived from Apple's वैकल्पिक (वैकल्पिक अक्षर). An alternate glyph is another form of the same character, selected through an OpenType feature such as salt or a stylistic set. Its name usually carries a suffix, as in a.alt or g.ss01. cmap cmap do-not-translate The cmap table maps character codes to glyph indices. Its Unicode subtables provide the initial mapping used in text rendering; other subtables support particular encodings or variation sequences. FontLab generates these mappings from the project's encoding data. A glyph without its own Unicode assignment can still appear in typed text through substitution, such as a ligature or alternate selected by the shaping engine. code page legacy character table कोड पेज proposed Loan; Microsoft Windows Hindi keeps Code page in English. A code page is a numbered legacy encoding, such as Windows 1250 for Central European languages, that maps one byte to one character. The OS/2 table lists the code pages a font supports, and FontLab derives that list from the glyphs present. Write two words. color font table कलर फ़ॉन्ट टेबल proposed Apple CoreText writes कलर ग्लिफ़्स; टेबल for a table inside a font. Colour-font tables store data for colour glyph rendering. Formats include COLR with CPAL, SVG, sbix, and CBDT with CBLC. They differ in how they describe vector or bitmap content and in application support. Including several formats can extend coverage, but does not guarantee rendering in every application. Identify the exported formats and test the intended targets. contextual alternates context-dependent variants प्रासंगिक विकल्प proposed Exact feature name in Apple CoreText, Microsoft Word and on the Adobe Hindi site. Contextual alternates, the calt feature, cover substitutions an app makes because of what sits around a glyph rather than because a reader asked. In a script face the text engine replaces an entry stroke after a letter that already ends in one, and in a face with repeating shapes it replaces the second of a pair. You write the rules with context in feature code, and apps usually leave calt on by default, which makes it the feature most likely to surprise you when a rule is too broad. cursive attachment joined-script connection कर्सिव अटैचमेंट proposed Apple CoreText writes कर्सिव; अटैचमेंट parallels मार्क अटैचमेंट. Rejected Apple's प्रवाहमय कनेक्शन (a different feature label). Cursive attachment joins glyphs by matching an exit anchor of one glyph to the entry anchor of the next, so connected scripts such as Arabic and Nastaliq flow. It is the curs feature, built from anchors. design languages डिज़ाइन भाषाएँ proposed No attestation; Apple's भाषाएँ with डिज़ाइन (Apple: 'इनके लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया'). Design languages, the meta table dlng record, list the languages the typeface was designed for. Supported languages, slng, list every language it can set. Both are language tags, not feature tags. encoding एनकोडिंग proposed Apple Character Viewer. An encoding maps character codes to glyphs. Unicode is the encoding modern fonts use; legacy encodings such as Mac Roman or a code page map one byte to one glyph. FontLab shows the font in a chosen encoding in the Font window and writes the cmap from it. Say encoding for the mapping and code page for a numbered legacy table. feature code layout rule code फ़ीचर कोड proposed Derived from फ़ीचर; कोड is the everyday loan. Feature code is the text syntax that describes OpenType features: classes, lookups, substitution and positioning rules, grouped into features by tag. It is usually called FEA, after the file extension. You edit it in the Features panel, compile it to check for errors, and keep it under the same review as the drawings, since a rule that fires on the wrong glyph is as visible as a wrong outline. FontLab compiles it into GSUB and GPOS at export. fractions भिन्न proposed Apple CoreText, Keynote, Pages; the school word. Fractions are numerical forms such as ½. In OpenType, the frac feature supports diagonal fraction composition through glyph substitution. A font may provide precomposed fraction glyphs, numerator and denominator forms, or both. The separate numr and dnom features provide numerator and denominator forms. Do not substitute the sups and subs feature names for these mechanisms or promise support for every input sequence without testing it. glyph index glyph number ग्लिफ़ इंडेक्स proposed Apple Font Book (ग्लिफ़ इंडेक्स और नाम). A glyph index is the number a glyph occupies in the font's own order, counting from zero. Text engines work in indices after the cmap has done its job, and binary tables reference glyphs by index rather than by name. You rarely set one by hand, but you meet it when you inspect a compiled font or debug a lookup that fires on the wrong glyph. The index depends on glyph order, so it changes when the order does. glyph name ग्लिफ़ नाम proposed Apple Font Book pattern (शैली नाम, फ़ाइल नाम). A glyph name identifies a glyph in an editing project, feature code or a tool's data. Names such as a, a.sc and a.alt can distinguish related drawings. They are separate from Unicode assignments and glyph indices, and need not survive in every exported format. After renaming a glyph, check references in feature code, classes and scripts, including references the editor cannot update automatically. GPOS GPOS do-not-translate GPOS is the OpenType table that holds positioning: kerning, mark attachment, cursive attachment, and any rule that moves a glyph without replacing it. FontLab writes your kerning here, as pairs and as class based positioning, and builds the mark lookups from your anchors. You reach it through feature code rather than by editing the table. A font may also carry a legacy kern table; modern text engines read GPOS and many ignore the other. GSUB GSUB do-not-translate GSUB is the OpenType table containing glyph-substitution lookups. It supports operations such as replacing a glyph with an alternate, forming a ligature or selecting a form from its context. FontLab compiles feature code into these structures. To diagnose a missing substitution, check the glyphs, compiled rules, feature selection, language and shaping order in the target application. ligature joined letters लिगेचर proposed Loan (Adobe Hindi site: लिगचर; Hindi design teaching: लिगेचर). Apple and Microsoft use संयुक्ताक्षर, rejected because in Indian type literature that is the Devanagari conjunct, which a font editor must keep apart from a typographic ligature. A ligature is a glyph used to represent a sequence of characters, such as fi. OpenType substitution can replace several glyphs with one ligature glyph. The liga and dlig features distinguish standard and discretionary ligatures. Shaping does not change the underlying text; whether a later document export preserves searchable text also depends on that export and its text mappings. localized forms language-specific variants स्थानीयकृत रूप proposed No attestation; Microsoft's स्थानीयकृत with Apple's रूप for forms. Localized forms are glyph variants selected for a text run's language. The OpenType locl feature can provide these substitutions, for example Bulgarian forms of Cyrillic letters. The shaping engine needs the relevant language information, which the application may obtain from a setting or other context. The substitution changes glyph selection, not the underlying characters or their codepoints. lookup procedure प्रक्रिया approved User/team procedure fallback. No sufficiently strong established OpenType-specific alternative verified in the reviewed primary sources. Keep the approved contextual Rules panel title. Preserve literal FEA lookup/lookupflag keywords, identifiers and OpenType structure names. Ordinary search senses are separate. A lookup groups substitution or positioning rules of one type in GSUB or GPOS. Features reference lookups, and several features can share one. The shaping engine selects features and may process them in script-specific stages; within a stage, LookupList order matters. Source-code order alone does not describe the complete shaping sequence. Inspect the compiled tables and the target engine when diagnosing ordering problems. mark glyph combining mark glyph मार्क ग्लिफ़ proposed Derived from मार्क and ग्लिफ़. A mark glyph is an accent or other combining mark that attaches to a base glyph through anchors. The GDEF table classes it as a mark so shaping engines position it rather than advancing past it. nonspacing mark zero-width combining mark नॉन-स्पेसिंग मार्क proposed Derived from नॉन-स्पेसिंग and मार्क; names the Unicode category Mn. A nonspacing mark is the Unicode general category Mn: a combining mark with zero advance, such as a combining acute. It differs from FontLab's nonspacing element, which is a property of an element inside a glyph. oldstyle figures lowercase-style figures पुरानी शैली के अंक proposed Apple CoreText (Old-Style Figures = पुरानी-शैली के अंक). Rejected Apple's other string पुरानी शैली की आकृतियाँ: आकृति is a shape, not a numeral. Oldstyle figures are numerals with varying heights, often including forms with ascenders and descenders. The OpenType onum feature selects them when provided by the font. Figure height and figure width are separate choices: oldstyle figures can be proportional or tabular. Use tabular widths when numerals must align in columns, whether their forms are oldstyle or lining. OpenType class layout glyph group OpenType क्लास proposed Derived; क्लास as in Apple Font Book. An OpenType class is a named group of glyphs that feature code can address at once, written with an at sign before the name. One rule over two classes replaces a page of single rules, and one edit to a class reaches every rule that cites it. You define classes in the Classes panel or in feature code, and you keep their order stable, because a substitution between two classes pairs them by position. Kerning classes are a separate mechanism with the same idea. OpenType feature layout feature OpenType फ़ीचर proposed Apple keeps OpenType in Latin and uses फ़ीचर. An OpenType feature identifies typographic behaviour through a four-character tag, such as liga, smcp or ss01. Feature records reference substitution or positioning lookups. In FontLab, you can write feature code and compile it into the font. Whether and when a feature is applied depends on the shaping engine, script, language and application settings; not every feature is a user-controlled switch. OS/2 table OS/2 टेबल proposed Tag in Latin; टेबल for a table inside a font. The OS/2 table carries the font's metadata for applications: vertical metrics, weight and width classes, embedding permissions, the panose values, and the codepage and Unicode range bits that say what the font covers. You fill it from Font Info rather than by hand, and you check it before release, because a wrong weight class puts a font in the wrong slot in a menu and wrong vertical metrics change line spacing in every browser. Write it with the slash: OS/2. Private Use Area Private Use Area do-not-translate A private-use area is one of three Unicode blocks whose codepoints can receive meanings by private agreement. Different fonts or systems may assign different meanings to the same private-use codepoint. Use a documented agreement when encoding custom symbols there. An alternate glyph reached through a feature does not require its own private-use assignment. single substitution सिंगल सब्स्टिट्यूशन proposed Apple CoreText uses सब्स्टिट्यूशन (लंबवत सब्स्टिट्यूशन); name of a GSUB lookup type. A single substitution replaces one glyph with one other glyph, the simplest GSUB lookup type. Small caps, stylistic alternates and localized forms are mostly built from it. small caps small capitals स्मॉल कैपिटल proposed Apple CoreText OpenType.strings (Small Capitals = स्मॉल कैपिटल). Rejected Apple's other rendering स्मॉल लेटर, which means lowercase, and Word's छोटे कैप्स. Small caps are capital shapes drawn at roughly lowercase height, with their own weight and width rather than scaled capitals. Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set स्टायलिस्टिक सेट proposed Apple CoreText (Stylistic Set %d = स्टायलिस्टिक सेट %d). Rejected Microsoft's शैलीयुक्त सेट. A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures सारणीबद्ध अंक proposed From Apple CoreText सारणीबद्ध (Tabular numbers = सारणीबद्ध संख्याएँ) with अंक. Alternative टैब्यूलर अंक (Apple also writes टैब्यूलर). Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code Unicode कोडपॉइंट proposed No attestation; Unicode in Latin as a standard's name, with the loan कोडपॉइंट. The corpus fallback pick वर्ण कोड ('character code') is the rejected alternative. A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character वेरिएशन सिलेक्टर proposed No attestation; loan of the Unicode term. A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system लेखन प्रणाली proposed Natural Hindi. Rejected Microsoft's लेखन सिस्टम. The OpenType script in this sense is लिपि (Apple Font Book), never स्क्रिप्ट. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Hindi Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Hindi Status Note Definition action क्रिया proposed Apple AppKit and Microsoft Office Hindi glossaries. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. add जोड़ें proposed Apple (फ़ॉन्ट जोड़ें), Adobe, Microsoft. Short imperative as the guide requires; compact labels may use the same form. Add inserts another item into the current collection or selection. Name the item when the surrounding control does not make it clear. alternate वैकल्पिक रूप proposed Apple CoreText (Alternate Forms = वैकल्पिक रूप). Bare विकल्प was rejected as the standalone noun because it is also the standard word for an option. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud एंकर बादल proposed Derived from एंकर; बादल is the plain word, and avoids क्लाउड, which in Hindi IT means cloud storage. The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer ऑटो लेयर proposed Derived from लेयर; ऑटो as in Apple CoreText (विशेषक ऑटो स्तर). An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint ऑटोहिंट करें proposed Command form derived from हिंट. Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush ब्रश proposed Adobe, Apple, Inkscape, Krita. Rejected तूलिका (literary). The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse समेटें proposed Apple Font Book and VoiceOver. समेटना is 'to gather together', which also fits nodes collapsing to one point. Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark रंग फ़्लैग proposed No attestation; natural रंग with the Microsoft loan फ़्लैग. Rejected रंग चिह्न, since चिह्न is overloaded. A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. corner angles कोनों के कोण proposed No attestation; natural words कोना (corner) and कोण (angle). The angles at contour vertices. These geometric measurements describe how adjacent segments meet at a corner and can be displayed on the canvas. cousins related glyphs alongside रिश्तेदार proposed House voice: 'relatives', a collective everyday word, since Hindi has no single word for cousins. Rejected the transliteration कज़िन्स. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop क्रॉप करें proposed Apple Photos and GIMP use the loan क्रॉप; imperative with करें. Rejected काँट-छाँट (clumsy in labels). Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic क्यूबिक proposed No Hindi attestation; transliterated professional loan, since Indian type designers learn the term in English. Rejected घन (Blender): a cube or the third power, not a curve degree. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current वर्तमान proposed Apple (वर्तमान यूज़र), Microsoft. Inflect as an invariable adjective. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. cusp नोक proposed No attestation; natural word for a sharp point; pairs with नुकीला (sharp). A cusp is a sharp point where a curve changes direction abruptly. Keep it distinct from a smooth join. decompose break into contours कंपोनेंट तोड़ें proposed No attestation; fallback 'break into contours' in the craftsman's verb तोड़ना, naming the object as German and Polish do. Rejected विघटित करें. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default डिफ़ॉल्ट proposed Apple Font Book and CoreText. Rejected तयशुदा/पूर्वन्यस्त (open-source coinages). A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode डेमो मोड proposed No attestation; both loans are everyday Hindi (Apple: सैंपल मोड). Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog डायलॉग proposed Apple (डायलॉग चेतावनियाँ) and Krita. Rejected संवाद (a conversation). A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes सपने बुनें proposed House voice: the idiom सपने बुनना, to weave dreams. Rejected the corpus fallback pick आकृतियाँ जनरेट करें (a description, not a name). Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text टेक्स्ट दोहराएँ proposed No attestation; fallback 'repeated text' translated as a command, like German Text wiederholen. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser रबर proposed Krita and Tux Paint; the everyday Indian word for a pencil eraser, in the house's handyman voice. Rejected इरेज़र (general software), understood but less homely. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours फ़िल्टर पक्का करें proposed No attestation; fallback 'bake filter into contours': पक्का means both baked and permanent. Rejected Apple's विस्तारित करें (to unfold a list). Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours स्ट्रोक पक्का करें proposed Same verb as फ़िल्टर पक्का करें. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours ट्रांसफ़ॉर्मेशन पक्का करें proposed Same verb as फ़िल्टर पक्का करें. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature फ़ीचर proposed Apple CoreText/Font Book (सभी टाइपोग्राफ़ी फ़ीचर, फ़ीचर सक्षम). Feature tags stay in Latin. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills भरण proposed Apple Keynote/Pages and Microsoft Publisher. Rejected the loan फ़िल. Singular and plural are the same. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit फ़ॉन्टऑडिट proposed User requires phonetic transliteration, explicitly including Chinese. Russian and Ukrainian spellings were recovered from team QPH; other spellings are proposals. Retain the FontAudit identity; do not translate as a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account FontLab खाता proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder वेल्डर proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node जीनियस नोड proposed Name transliterated, as German, French and Polish keep Genius; जीनियस is everyday Hindi. A Hindi rendering (प्रतिभाशाली) would be long and solemn. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid ग्रिड proposed Apple Font Book, Adobe, Microsoft, Inkscape. Distinct from जाल (mesh). A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups समूह proposed Apple, Microsoft, Inkscape. Plural label is also समूह. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide गाइड proposed Apple Keynote/Pages, Inkscape and the Adobe Hindi site (ग्रिड्स और गाइड्स). A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. kerning mode कर्निंग मोड proposed Derived from कर्निंग. The editing mode for adjusting spacing between pairs of glyphs. It changes pair adjustments rather than the individual glyph sidebearings. Knife चाकू proposed Apple (Freeform, Keynote, Pages); the real tool's name. The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. layer लेयर proposed Loan used across Hindi graphics teaching and on the Adobe Hindi site (लेयर्स). Rejected परत/स्तर (Blender, Krita, LibreOffice): स्तर also means 'level'. A layer holds one drawing or part of a document. In FontLab, the context identifies the glyph layer; name the application when another product uses a different layer model. Layers लेयर proposed Plural of लेयर; Hindi loans keep the singular form in labels (Apple: फ़ॉन्ट for Fonts). The panel is लेयर और मास्टर. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark मार्क proposed Loan of the OpenType term. Rejected चिह्न (Microsoft, Inkscape): it is Apple's word for any symbol, and मात्रा would cover only vowel signs. A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks मास्क proposed Loan, as on the Adobe Hindi site. Rejected आवरण (Blender): a cover, and a FontLab mask hides nothing. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match मिलान करें proposed मिलान in Microsoft and Apple Keynote Hindi; verb form with करें. Corporate माचिस (matchstick) is the wrong sense. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching मेल खाने वाले proposed From Apple's मेल खाना (फ़िल्टर मानदंड से मेल खाने वाला); participle form, inflect for gender and number. Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher जोड़ीसाज़ proposed House voice coinage: जोड़ी (a matched pair) with the craftsman suffix -साज़ (घड़ीसाज़). Hindi has no single neutral word for a matchmaker; बिचौलिया means a tout. Rejected the transliteration मैचमेकर. Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. measurement line माप रेखा proposed Derived from माप and रेखा. A line that shows a measured distance in the drawing. Distinguish this geometric measurement from a metrics line used to calculate sidebearings. measurements माप proposed No attestation; natural Hindi for a measurement; kept distinct from मेट्रिक्स (spacing) and आयाम (font dimensions). Values displayed on the canvas to describe geometry, such as coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters. Showing measurements does not modify glyph spacing or font dimensions. Measurements panel माप पैनल proposed Derived from माप; short enough for the compact panel. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge मर्ज करें proposed Adobe InDesign and Microsoft Office Hindi. Rejected मिलाएँ, kept free for matching (मिलान). Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh जाल proposed Blender and Krita Hindi; natural word for a net. Kept distinct from ग्रिड. A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. metrics mode मेट्रिक्स मोड proposed Derived from मेट्रिक्स. The editing mode for adjusting glyph advance widths and sidebearings. It changes the spacing of glyphs rather than the vertical dimensions of the font or the visibility of measurements. metrics table मेट्रिक्स तालिका proposed Derived; तालिका is the interface table (Microsoft), kept apart from टेबल, used for tables inside a font. The table of glyph spacing values, including advance widths and sidebearings. It lets the user inspect or edit spacing values together. metrics tool मेट्रिक्स टूल proposed Derived; टूल is the Adobe and Apple Hindi word for a tool. The tool that edits glyph advance widths and sidebearings. Use it to adjust glyph spacing; canvas measurement overlays display values without changing those spacing values. monospaced मोनोस्पेस proposed Apple Font Book (मोनोस्पेस, मोनोस्पेस्ड). The shorter form is used as an invariable adjective. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line बहु-पंक्ति proposed No attestation; पंक्ति is the Microsoft/Apple word for a line or row; बहु- is the productive prefix for multi-. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width नॉन-स्पेसिंग proposed No attestation; loan built on स्पेसिंग; fallback 'zero-width' was rejected because the element keeps its width and is only ignored in metrics. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move धक्का proposed House voice: the everyday word for a shove, like German Schubs; command form धक्का दें. Rejected Microsoft's नज करें (an opaque loan). Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique ओब्लीक proposed Apple CoreText style name; fixed name of the FontLab operation. Rejected तिर्यक/तिरछा: any slant. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel पैनल proposed Apple, Microsoft, Adobe Hindi site. Panel names precede it: कर्निंग पैनल. A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil पेंसिल proposed Apple and Microsoft. The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush दमदार ब्रश proposed House voice: दमदार is the advertising word for 'packs a punch' (the Adobe Hindi site writes दमदार टूल्स). Rejected the transliteration पावर and शक्ति (an industrial rating). A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline दमदार गाइड proposed Derived from दमदार and गाइड. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move दमदार धक्का proposed Derived from दमदार and धक्का. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline दमदार स्ट्रोक proposed Derived from दमदार and स्ट्रोक. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project प्रोजेक्ट approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar प्रॉपर्टी बार proposed No attestation; loan compound on the model of Apple's फ़िल्टर बार and साइडबार. The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. quick measurement त्वरित माप proposed Derived; त्वरित is Microsoft's standard word for Quick. The function that displays measurements near the pointer while editing outlines. It reports geometry on the canvas without changing the glyph spacing values. redo फिर करें proposed Apple AppKit Undo.strings; platform word for a standard OS command. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference रेफ़रेंस proposed Loan. Apple/Microsoft use संदर्भ, rejected here because संदर्भ is also the everyday word for 'context' (contextual = प्रासंगिक/संदर्भ मेनू) and would blur element references with contexts. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours ओवरलैप हटाएँ proposed Apple CoreText uses ओवरलैप (ओवरलैप रोक) and हटाएँ for Remove. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat दोहराएँ proposed Apple and Microsoft. Distinct from फिर करें (redo). Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction कॉन्टूर उलटें proposed No attestation; उलटना is the everyday verb for turning something the other way. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors कैंची proposed Apple and Microsoft Word; the real tool's name. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node पिछलग्गू नोड proposed Read as Follower node. पिछलग्गू is the colloquial word for one who tags along behind, in the house voice. Rejected अनुगामी (formal) and फ़ॉलोअर (the social-media sense the principles rule out). For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas स्केचबोर्ड proposed Transliterated: स्केच and बोर्ड are both everyday Hindi, so the name is understood as it stands. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline छिलका proposed House voice, parallel to Polish skórka: the peel of a fruit. Rejected त्वचा (Blender: human skin) and the transliteration स्किन. Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever चतुर proposed House voice: the plain folk-tale word for clever with a hint of cunning, and invariable. Rejected the transliteration स्मार्ट (Apple, Adobe) because a Hindi rendering is understood, and बुद्धिमान (intelligent). Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner चतुर कोना proposed Derived from चतुर and natural कोना. A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter चतुर फ़िल्टर proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles स्पेसिंग नियंत्रण proposed No attestation; स्पेसिंग plus नियंत्रण (Apple: विशेषक नियंत्रण). Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker स्टिकर proposed Apple and Microsoft Hindi. A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. tab टैब proposed Apple and Microsoft. The tab character stays literal in code. A tab selects one page or document within a set. A tab character in text is a different meaning and must retain its literal representation in code. text element text block टेक्स्ट एलिमेंट proposed Apple VoiceOver has the same compound; consistent with एलिमेंट. A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness मोटाई proposed Microsoft Publisher and Krita; natural Hindi. Kept distinct from वज़न (typeface weight). Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform ट्रांसफ़ॉर्म proposed Loan (general-software evidence ट्रांस्फ़ॉर्म); command form ट्रांसफ़ॉर्म करें. Rejected रूपांतरण (Krita), kept for file conversion. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas.
