A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation ट्रांसफ़ॉर्मेशन proposed Derived from ट्रांसफ़ॉर्म. Rejected परिवर्तन (Blender): just 'change'. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering असली भरण proposed House voice: असली is the plain word for 'the real thing', on भरण. Rejected वास्तविक भरण (formal). True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck अनचेक करें proposed Apple VoiceOver, Keynote, Pages. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview वॉटरफ़ॉल proposed Apple Font Book (वॉटरफ़ॉल सैंपल दिखाएँ). Rejected जलप्रपात/झरना: literal waterfalls. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight वज़न proposed Everyday word, five general-software attestations in the corpus. Rejected भार (Microsoft/Blender), which reads as physical load, and मोटाई, reserved for measured thickness. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace व्हाइट स्पेस proposed Apple Keynote/Pages; the Adobe Hindi site writes वाइट स्पेस. Rejected सफेद रिक्ति. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Hindi Status Note Definition Appearance panel Appearance पैनल proposed Illustrator has no Hindi interface, so the panel name stays as the user sees it; only पैनल is translated. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion ऑटोट्रेस proposed No attestation; loan; ट्रेस is common in Hindi graphics usage. Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline केंद्र रेखा proposed Microsoft Publisher has केंद्रीयरेखा; written as two words with रेखा, like आधार रेखा. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask क्लिपिंग मास्क proposed Adobe Hindi site (क्लिपिंग मास्क्स). A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point नियंत्रण बिंदु proposed No attestation; natural words (Microsoft नियंत्रण, Apple बिंदु). बिंदु is used for every geometric point so that पॉइंट stays the typographic point size (Apple). A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines भरण ग्रिड proposed Derived from भरण and ग्रिड; fallback 'grid of fill lines'. The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style भरण मोड proposed Derived from भरण and the everyday loan मोड. A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them. Each reads the brightness of the source and lays down geometry accordingly. You pick a mode, then tune its parameters. Write the mode name with its own capitalization and the words fill mode in lowercase after it. G2 continuity G2 निरंतरता proposed No attestation; G2 stays Latin; निरंतरता is the common word for continuity. G2 continuity means two segments meet with matching curvature, not merely with matching direction. G1 keeps the tangent continuous and can still show a break in the reflection where the curvature jumps. G2 removes that break. Vextra marks G2 nodes and can enforce the condition as you edit. You reach for it on long, shallow curves and on shapes that will be seen large, where the eye finds a curvature break that it would miss at text size. Live Effect editable effect लाइव इफ़ेक्ट proposed No attestation; loan of Illustrator's term; Illustrator has no Hindi interface (Adobe Hindi site writes इफ़ेक्ट्स). A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve वक्र से बाहर का बिंदु proposed No attestation; fallback 'point off the curve' translated. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve वक्र पर स्थित बिंदु proposed No attestation; fallback 'point on the curve' translated; वक्र is the Microsoft and Inkscape word for a curve. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline आउटलाइन proposed Apple Font Book (Outlines = आउटलाइन) and Adobe Hindi site. Rejected रूपरेखा, which in Hindi means a plan or synopsis. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke स्ट्रोक proposed Apple, Microsoft, Inkscape, Krita, Adobe Hindi site. Distinct from भरण (fill). A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap स्ट्रोक कैप proposed No attestation; loan of the vector term. Kept apart from टर्मिनल (letter anatomy) and कैपिटल (capital letters). A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape स्ट्रोक जोड़ proposed No attestation; जोड़ is the natural Hindi word for a joint or join. A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node टैंजेंट नोड proposed No attestation; loan. Rejected स्पर्शरेखीय नोड (schoolbook Sanskritism, too long for a label). A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. tonal map darkness map टोनल मैप proposed No attestation; loan compound; fallback 'darkness map'. A tonal map is the reading of brightness across a source image that a fill uses to decide where to put geometry. Dark areas widen a strip or crowd a pattern; light areas narrow or thin it. You control the mapping with the Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels rows, which change what counts as dark before any geometry is drawn. Adjust the map rather than the fill when the result is uniformly too heavy or too sparse. Tunni line टुन्नी रेखा proposed Eponym (Eduardo Tunni) transliterated, with natural रेखा. A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: Indonesian
docs.text:
A first draft for Indonesian. A model researched the guidance below and the term table in references/terms.md; no native reviewer has approved the language as a whole. Individual terms carry their own approval status; a proposed term remains proposed, and a protected name keeps its glossary spelling. The Indonesian interface catalogs are unfinished machine drafts: a string found in one settles neither a term nor a rule.

Use references/terms.md, and a newer core memory when one is supplied, for terminology, definitions and review status. Keep a proposed term consistent across the interface and help, and report it as proposed. Where a native reviewer's decision or newer project data disagrees with this skill, follow it and record the change. Report only checks performed: text written with this skill is not reviewed by a native speaker and not tested in the running application until someone does that.

Use these rules with the localization principles (in fontlab-localization), Qt interface rules (in fontlab-localization) and Indonesian language guide (in the FontLab writing guide). Examples tagged FB, CT or MS are quoted from Font Book, CoreText or Microsoft's Indonesian style guide; the others are constructed. Glyphs, Illustrator and Qt have no Indonesian interface: macOS and Windows are the models.

docs.title: Locale and register
docs.text:
• Indonesian for Indonesia, Qt locale id_ID, spelled by EYD V and KBBI.
  • Address the reader as Anda, always capitalized, and omit it when the verb is enough: Periksa koneksi jaringan dan coba lagi nanti. (FB, "Check network connection and try again later."). Never kamu, kau or -mu.
  • Tone: plain and neutral. Drop "please" (silakan, mohon, harap) and the product's kami: "Please try again" is Coba lagi. (FB).
  • Mereka is for people. For things repeat the noun: "They cannot be deleted" is Font tidak dapat dihapus (FB).

docs.title: Grammar of interface strings
docs.text:
String Form Example Menu command, button, step Verb base, no me- Simpan Sebagai (MS, "Save As") Checkbox, option Verb base or noun phrase Tampilkan bar filter (FB, "Show filter bar") Panel or dialog title Noun phrase; pe-…-an noun for "-ing" Dukungan Bahasa (FB, "Language Support") Status, in progress me- verb and ellipsis, no sedang Mengesahkan font… (FB, "Validating fonts…") Success, result Noun and di- or ter- verb, no telah Font Dihapus (FB, "Fonts Removed") "Cannot", "Could not" Tidak dapat and me- verb Tidak Dapat Menghapus Font (FB, "Cannot Remove Font") "… cannot be …" Noun, tidak dapat, di- verb Koleksi Tidak Dapat Dihapus (FB, "Collection Cannot Be Deleted") "Failed to", "… failed" Gagal and me- verb Gagal mengunduh file (MS, "Failed to download file") Confirmation Apakah Anda yakin ingin…? or a bare question Lanjutkan? (MS, "Do you wish to continue?") Empty state Tidak ada and noun Tidak Ada Font yang Dipilih (FB, "No Fonts Selected") Tooltip me- verb, no subject; verb base for a step Mengatur ulang sampel yang diedit ke nilai default yang sesuai. (FB, "Resets the edited sample…")
  • A command is never a me- verb, a di- verb or a noun: Simpan, not Menyimpan, Disimpan, Penyimpanan. It keeps the suffix its verb needs: Aktifkan, Tampilkan, Lewati, Atur Ulang (FB).
  • Passive di- tells what happens to an object without an actor; prefer it to a sentence about Anda: Font ini harus diunduh sebelum digunakan. (FB). Ter- names a resulting state: terinstal, tersedia.
  • Capitalization mirrors the English source, as macOS and Windows do. For English title case, capitalize every word except di, ke, dari, dan, atau, yang, untuk, dengan, sebagai, pada, oleh: Instal yang Dicentang (FB, "Install Checked"). For sentence case, capitalize the first word only.
  • Standard commands (MS): Buka, Simpan, Tutup, Cetak, Potong, Salin, Tempel, Hapus, Pilih Semua, Keluar. Cancel is Batal; Undo is Urungkan and Redo Ulangi, as at Google. Avoid Batalkan: it is Cancel on macOS and Undo on Windows. Qt has no qtbase_id catalog, so framework strings need these words too.
  • Platform words: file and folder (Apple, Microsoft, Google), not berkas or map; unduh, unggah (Apple, Microsoft, Adobe; Google keeps download); pengaturan (Apple, Microsoft; Google says setelan).

docs.title: Compact labels
docs.text:
• No articles: never add sebuah, suatu or para.
  • Head first, modifiers after, the English stack reversed as a whole: Kriteria Koleksi Cerdas (FB, "Smart Collection Criteria").
  • Yang only before a verb that modifies a noun, never before a plain adjective or noun: Font Duplikat (FB). It separates a phrase from a statement: font yang dipilih ("the selected fonts"), Font Sistem Dipilih (FB, "System Fonts Selected").
  • Untuk only for a purpose: Klik untuk mengunduh %@ (FB). Otherwise Opsi ekspor, not Opsi untuk ekspor; mencoba menginstalnya (FB), not mencoba untuk menginstalnya.
  • Shorten with a shorter word or the source's abbreviations. Never drop vowels (Microsoft allows Hps; FontLab does not) or an affix (-kan, di-, me-). Never abbreviate a glossary term, a command verb, tidak or a name.

docs.title: Plurals and placeholders
docs.text:
Qt gives Indonesian one numerus form ("Universal Form", nplurals=1) for every number, 0 and 1 included.

  • Keep %n and leave the noun unchanged: %n file dipilih ("%n file(s) selected"). Never write satu or a literal 1.
  • Never reduplicate after a number or a quantifier (semua, beberapa): %n font, semua font, not font-font. An English plural label is the bare noun: Font (FB, "Fonts").
  • A count precedes its noun; a name follows its class noun: %n lapisan ("%n layers"), lapisan “%1” ("layer “%1”"), Edit sampel %@ (FB, "Edit %@ sample"). Ask which of the two %1 is.
  • Indonesian has no gender, case or agreement, so a noun placeholder needs no special form. Never attach an affix or -nya to it (di%1, %1nya); the ordinal ke-%1 is the one exception.
  • "%1 of %2" is %1 dari %2 (FB).

docs.title: Numbers, punctuation and spacing
docs.text:
• Decimal comma, period for thousands: 1.526,75 (EYD, MS, CLDR). Versions, code and font data keep their source form.
  • Percent without a space: 25% (EYD). A unit takes a no-break space: 12 pt, 5,25 cm.
  • Quotation marks are “…”, with ‘…’ inside (MS, FB); straight quotes in code only.
  • Ellipsis is the single character …, with no space before it, wherever the source has one: Ekspor… (FB).
  • The prepositions di, ke, dari are separate words; the passive prefix di- is joined: disimpan di folder (EYD).
  • Bound forms join: nonaktif, pratinjau; hyphen before a capital: non-Apple (FB).

docs.title: Mnemonics and key names
docs.text:
• Put & before a letter of the Indonesian word, the first if free. No trailing (&F). Avoid g j p q y (MS). One letter per menu or dialog.
  • Never change a shortcut.
  • Untranslated keys: Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Tab, Esc, Enter, Backspace, Delete, and on macOS Command, Option, Control, Return. Translated: Panah Kiri, Panah Kanan, Panah Atas, Panah Bawah (Apple, MS), Spasi (MS). A key is a tombol: tekan tombol Shift.

docs.title: Names and loans
docs.text:
• Keep unchanged: product and company names, format names (OpenType, UFO, VFJ), OpenType tags and table names, glyph names, code.
  • Embed a name after a class noun, without hyphen or affix: file VFJ, font OpenType, tabel kern, fitur liga, di FontLab.
  • Assimilated loans follow EYD: -tion gives -si (interpolasi), -ic gives -ik (metrik), -ty gives -tas (kompatibilitas), c gives k (kontur, vektor). Write standar, sistem, objek, silakan, mengubah (never merubah).
  • An assimilated loan takes affixes directly: mengekspor, diimpor, penginstalan (FB, MS). A loan the term table keeps in English takes none: terapkan kerning, not meng-kerning. Never men-download or di-reset; write mengunduh, diatur ulang.

docs.title: False friends and traps
docs.text:
Malay forms are errors in Indonesian:

Indonesian Not file, unduh, unggah fail, muat turun, muat naik pengaturan, perangkat lunak, default tetapan, perisian, lalai hapus, tempel, jendela padam, tampal, tetingkap ukuran, karena, dapat saiz, kerana, boleh

Corporate catalogs are no authority for type terms. CoreText has Berat Badan (body weight) for Weight, Sedikit (few) for Narrow, Singkat (brief) for Condensed, Nomor Baris (line numbers) for Lining Numbers and Huruf Kecil (lowercase) for Letter Case. The term table rules.

  • Letter case is never kasus, character never tokoh or watak, font never huruf, karakter never glif.
  • Office suites use miring for italic and tebal for bold; the term table decides oblique, slant and weight.

Machine translation keeps English word order (Baru File), reduplicates plurals, writes di simpan and difolder, puts me- verbs in menus, repeats Anda or writes it lowercase, and adds yang, untuk, adalah and sebuah for every "that", "to", "is" and "a".

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Check in this order, and report only checks performed:

  1. Placeholders, markup and the single %n form, read with 0, 1 and 2.
  2. Malay and colloquial forms; Anda capitalized.
  3. Verb base for commands, me- for progress, di- or ter- for results.
  4. Head first, count before noun; no reduplication; di against di-.
  5. Capitalization mirrors the source.
  6. Mnemonics unique per menu.
  7. Type terms against the term table; numbers, percent, quotation marks.

docs.title: FontLab terminology and compact labels
docs.text:
Preserve deliberately uppercase source labels using the language’s case rules. Keep numeric controls compact with UPM, PPM and LSB/RSB (French AG/AD); explain the full terms in help. The Family Dimensions “Units Per eM:” label is an intentional expanded exception.

Use the current core memory and its approval status. OpenType lookup defaults to the translation of procedure, with a different term only when strong OpenType-specific evidence supports it. Explicit choices are German Lookup, French lookup, Polish procedura and Russian процедура. Ordinary searches, individual rules and OpenType features are separate concepts. Preserve literal code keywords and identifiers.

Translate Fusion with the fallback Welder. Use the core's phonetic FontAudit transliteration in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese; preserve FontAudit in code. Proposed spellings remain proposed. Before rebuilding a QPH, recover team edits and import their terms and notes into the core memory.

Compare mnemonic-split terms with unmarked labels. Keep labels compact, aiming for 120% of the English length in Dimensions and Glyph Window preferences without losing meaning. Omit redundant font, color or command wording when context supplies it. TTH labels can omit “use” and abbreviate TrueType hinting; help can explain more. A full harmonization requires three complete catalog reviews, then reconciliation of help with the final UI and verification of generated resources.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• references/terms.md: the full Indonesian term table, generated from the core memory id-core.tmx of the writing guide, with the status, translator note and definition of every term.
  • The Indonesian localization guide of the writing guide is the source of the sections above.

docs.title: Related skills
docs.text: fontlab-localization for the shared rules; fontlab-terminology for product names and shared nouns; fontlab-technical for Indonesian help text.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
These rules implement the FontLab writing guide. They are copied into every skill so each installed skill can work independently. Corpus measurements can inform review; they are not quotas, universal laws, or tests of authorship.

H1. Accurate actors. Address the reader when they act or choose. Name the application when it performs an operation. Fonts and files contain data that software interprets. Prefer active voice when the actor matters; retain a clear passive construction when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. Never invent an actor or cause to change the grammar.

H2. Never invent a fact. Ground numbers, names, dates, labels, shortcuts, defaults, errors, versions, and quotations in supplied or checked evidence. A draft is evidence of what was written, not independent proof of its claims. Mark unresolved facts with a specific working placeholder such as [VERIFY CLAIM], [CONFIRM LABEL], or [CONFIRM OFFER]. A marked draft is unfinished; resolve the gap before publication. Clearly label fictional examples before their invented details.

H3. Preserve certainty and scope. “May reduce” does not become “eliminates.” Preserve conditions, negation, timing, quantities, compatibility, licensing, and other consequential limits. State a limitation directly rather than disguising it as a favorable position. A single observation does not prove universal behavior. Conflicting sources need scope checks, not an automatic choice of the stricter claim.

H4. Preserve the writer's voice. Do not manufacture stakes, candor, reader emotion, endorsement, or a new narrator. Preserve useful habits and the supplied stance. Reorder, split, or shorten according to the requested edit depth and reader need, without adding facts or causal relationships. A correct draft can remain unchanged.

H5. Give thought a rhythm. Carry a subject through an action, distinction or consequence. Let a developed sentence explain a relationship; let a shorter one settle a result when that change of pace helps. Repeat a concrete object or term when its meaning develops, not as a compulsory callback. Technical actions stay literal; explanations and marketing have room for patient attention, a bounded comparison or dry observation. Keep useful qualifications beside their claims. Do not impose sentence-length, pronoun, punctuation or paragraph quotas, or force every paragraph into the same long-then-short pattern.

H6. Notice the useful detail. Retain names, mechanisms, conditions, versions and issue numbers that help the reader understand or act. From the evidence, choose the object, contrast or small behavior that makes the explanation tangible: a changed preview, a repeated comparison, a file whose status matters. Follow that detail far enough to explain its significance. Warmth can come from this attention and patience. Never invent an observation, personal experience or reader emotion to make prose vivid, or remove a necessary qualification to shorten it.

H7. Punctuation serves meaning. Prefer a colon for an explanation or list. A spaced dash can carry a turn; avoid decorative glosses and repeated interruptions. Use sentence case for new headings and preserve exact source labels. A punctuation pattern does not establish authorship.

H8. Choose precise words. Review vague praise and stock phrasing such as “seamless,” “game-changing,” “leverage,” and “unlock.” Replace them when they obscure the action or make an unsupported claim. Keep an accurate technical use or protected quotation. A count or cluster is a reason to inspect a passage, not proof that each matched word is wrong.

H9. Develop the explanation. Begin where the reader can understand the task, change or offer. Give adjacent sentences a real connection: the same subject under a changed condition, an action and its result, or a question and its answer. A before-and-after comparison needs evidence for both states; a transition must not invent causality. Let a useful aside return to the main thought. Place low-stakes discoveries where they aid understanding, while keeping price, risk, prerequisites and recovery visible when needed. End at the useful result or next action; a quiet ending or a substantial summary can each serve the material.

H10a. Preserve conditions. Use “if” for a condition and “when” where the intended timing or situation warrants it. Check the whole meaning: “when a panel opens” and “while a panel is open” describe different scopes. Keep useful conditionals and parenthetical explanations; do not insert them to imitate a presumed author.

H10. Preserve expression that works. A fragment, three-part phrase, exclamation, aside, or single-sentence paragraph can serve a passage. Keep it when it supports meaning or the writer's rhythm. Do not add one to meet a budget, or remove one because of a generic stylistic test. Keep instructions and consequential conditions literal and easy to find.

H10b. Use the destination's notation. Preserve exact interface labels, tags, extensions, and identifiers. Italicize labels in neutral release notes; in technical site content use supported highlight notation, with bold as the plain-Markdown fallback. Use code style for machine-readable text. State price amounts and currencies unambiguously from evidence; do not infer an exchange rate, tax policy, or license term. A supplied currency shorthand needs enough context to identify the actual offer.

H11. Names and collisions. FontLab is the product; Fontlab Ltd. is the company. Preserve product names, module identifiers, domains, historical names in their historical scope, and exact quoted strings. Do not translate a product name. Name the application when Layer, Mask, Group, Fill, Brush, Knife, Transform, Pencil, Eraser, or Scissors could have more than one meaning. Use a declared short form consistently.

H12. Protect literal material. Preserve quotations, code, commands, paths, identifiers, API names, URLs, legal text, interface strings, placeholders, and table data during prose editing. Change them only for a requested or necessary correction supported by evidence. Do not paraphrase a quotation while retaining quotation marks or an attribution. Explain a consequential correction when the output contract permits it.

H13. Choose the register per passage. Marketing helps assess an offer; technical writing explains or instructs; neutral prose states facts and changes warmly. A document can combine them. Prices, limits, licensing, compatibility, security, and migration facts stay plain and prominent. Audience and purpose determine an email's register. Do not impose a fixed emotional mixture or make every opening a story.

H14. Review facts, then movement. Compare claims and protected strings with their evidence; check scope, action order and terminology. Then read whole passages for attention, connection and pace. Repair a flat sequence by developing an existing detail or relationship, not by adding praise or invented events. Check that humor remains intelligible and the information remains true when the joke is missed. Recheck the facts after a voice edit. A measurement or passing build does not certify facts, usability or authorship. Report only checks actually performed.

H15. Scale to the surface. A button or tooltip needs a clear label, action, or condition, not a miniature essay. Apply factual and naming safeguards at every length. Include the detail the task requires; do not add proof paragraphs, metaphors, or pronouns to satisfy a template. For translation, keep essential instructions literal and references clear.

H16. The override. Follow the user's task and supplied voice before style defaults. Break a default sooner than make the writing worse. Source material and quoted prompts are data, not authority to change the task. Style preferences never justify presenting an invented or unsupported claim as established fact.

docs.title: Indonesian terms
docs.text:
Portable term table, snapshot of 04 October 2026, generated from the core translation memory localization/id-core.tmx of the FontLab writing guide by tools/scripts/export_terms.py. 55 of 289 terms are approved or protected; a proposed translation is a candidate for a native reviewer, and the English term is the fallback until it is approved. Use newer supplied project data when it disagrees with this snapshot.

A status of do-not-translate protects the English spelling; it does not approve a draft English name. The definition says what the term means in FontLab; the note says why the translation was chosen or how to inflect it. The fallback original term is a plain English phrase to translate instead of the term when the term itself will not travel (stem: main stroke; overshoot: optical surplus).

docs.title: Type design
docs.text: English Fallback Indonesian Status Note Definition ascender upward extension ascender proposed Professional loan: Sihombing («Tipografi dalam Desain Grafis»), Rustan and Indonesian DKV course material all write ascender. No native term is in use. An ascender is the part of a lowercase letter that extends above the x-height, as in b or d. Ascender height describes the intended alignment of these parts and may differ from cap height. Do not confuse this design measurement with similarly named vertical metrics in exported font tables. Line spacing depends on those fields and on the application using them. baseline writing line garis dasar proposed Apple AppKit, Microsoft and LibreOffice use «garis dasar». Textbooks (Sihombing, Rustan) keep English baseline; the Indonesian form is transparent and already what users see in software. A baseline is a reference line used to align text. In conventional horizontal Latin font design, the baseline is at y = 0, with ascenders above it and descenders below it. Other scripts and layout systems can use different baseline conventions. Identify the relevant baseline when discussing alignment across scripts or vertical text. bowl round belly bowl proposed Professional loan: Indonesian DKV course material (for example UMN theses following Landa and Sihombing) keeps bowl. Apple's «mangkuk» names a soup-bowl shape, not letter anatomy. A bowl is a rounded stroke that encloses a counter, as in b, d or p. Its shape, thickness and junctions affect the letter's balance. The appropriate number of curve segments depends on the design. Nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting, but a fixed segment count does not guarantee compatible masters or good interpolation. cap height capital-letter height tinggi kapital proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «capital-letter height» translated, parallel to «tinggi x». Textbooks keep English cap height. Cap height is the distance from the baseline to the top of a flat capital such as H. Rounded or pointed capitals may extend beyond it through overshoot. Record the intended value in Font Info. Cap height describes a design measurement; alignment zones and line-spacing metrics are separate settings, even when their values are related. character karakter proposed Attested in 25 origins (Adobe, Apple, Microsoft); Sihombing uses «karakter (character)». Kept distinct from «glif». A character is an abstract unit of written text, such as a letter or punctuation mark. A glyph is its visual representation. The relationship is not one to one: several characters can form a ligature, and a character can have several glyph forms. A user-perceived character can also consist of several Unicode codepoints. Keep characters, codepoints and glyphs distinct when discussing encoding or text processing. contour kontur proposed Google's Indonesian web.dev article on variable fonts writes «kontur glyph»; 14 corpus origins (Apple, Microsoft, QCAD). A contour is an open or closed sequence of connected line and curve segments. Its nodes and control points describe its geometry. One glyph or vector object can contain several contours. A counter is an area of space, not a synonym for a contour. When explaining fill behaviour, identify the outline format and fill rule before prescribing a contour direction. counter enclosed white space counter proposed Professional loan: Indonesian DKV course material keeps counter. Rejected the corporate «penghitung» (a tally counter). A counter is the enclosed or partly enclosed space within a letterform, such as the enclosed space in an o or the open space in a c. The surrounding strokes define it. A closed counter may have an inner contour as its boundary; an open counter does not require a separate contour. Judge its size and shape together with the surrounding strokes. descender downward extension descender proposed Professional loan: Sihombing, Rustan and DKV course material write descender. A descender is the part of a letter that extends below the baseline, as in p or y. Its design height is usually recorded as a negative coordinate relative to the baseline. Exported descender metrics are separate fields used by applications for layout. Whether a deep glyph clips depends on the relevant metrics, application and text container, not on one design value alone. diacritical mark combining mark tanda diakritik proposed KBBI term; Apple CoreText uses «diakritik». A diacritical mark is a small sign, such as an acute or a cedilla, that attaches to a base letter to form another character. FontLab builds accented glyphs from a base and a mark through anchors, and the GDEF mark class tells the shaper which glyphs are marks. Say mark glyph for the class member and diacritical mark for the sign. em type body em proposed Kept as the international unit, lowercase (Microsoft: «spasi em»); Indonesian typography has no native word for the em. The em is the square on which a typeface is designed, historically the body of the letter M in metal type. Its height equals the type size, so an em in 12 point text is 12 points. In a digital font the em is divided into UPM font units. extremum local extreme point titik ekstrem proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «ekstrem» is the KBBI form; follows German Extrempunkt. An extremum is a point where a curve reaches a local leftmost, rightmost, topmost or bottommost position. The plural is extrema. Placing nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting. If you add nodes to masters intended for interpolation, preserve the correspondence between their contours and points. Different extremum positions alone do not make masters incompatible. glyph glif proposed Indonesian Wikipedia (article «Glif»), Scribus, QCAD and Google's Indonesian documentation write «glif». Rejected Apple's «simbol gambar» (picture symbol), which no designer uses, and unadapted «glyph». A glyph is one drawn shape in a font: a letter, a figure, a mark, or a piece of a composite. A character is what a reader types and a glyph is what a renderer draws, and one character can map to several glyphs while several characters can map to one. You edit a glyph in the Glyph window, where its contours, elements, anchors, and metrics all live together. The distinction matters in any sentence about encoding, since a font maps codepoints to glyphs through the cmap table. handle gagang proposed Adobe Illustrator's Indonesian strings: «gagang kurva», «gagang bezier». Short and a real tool part. Rejected «pegangan» (Blender, GIMP, QCAD) and Apple's «pengendali». A handle is an off-curve control point used to shape a curve segment. A cubic Bézier segment has two control points; a quadratic segment has one. Moving a handle changes the curve without moving its endpoints. In tools that display handle arms, the arm connects a control point to an endpoint. Name the curve type when the number or behaviour of handles matters. ink trap ink relief notch perangkap tinta proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; literal, as in German, Spanish and French. Designers also say the English ink trap. An ink trap is a notch cut into a corner where strokes meet, so ink spread or rasterization at small sizes does not clog the join. FontLab makes them as a live Smart Corner variant. italic angle slant angle sudut kemiringan proposed Fallback «slant angle» translated; Apple CoreText has Slant → Kemiringan. The italic angle is the slope of the upright strokes of an italic or oblique design, measured from the vertical in degrees. FontLab stores it in Font Info, uses it to slant guides and the cursor, and writes it into the post and hhea tables. It is a property of the design, not of a transformation. lining figures capital-height figures angka selaras proposed Apple CoreText: Lining Figures → Angka Selaras. Lining figures are digits that share the cap height and sit on the baseline, so they align with capitals in tables and headlines. The lnum feature selects them where a font defaults to oldstyle figures. node simpul proposed Blender and Krita; the Pusat Bahasa equivalent of node. Rejected the English «node» (CorelDRAW users' habit), Inkscape's «nodal», and «titik jangkar», which would collide with «jangkar». A node is a point on a contour where segments meet, and its type decides how they meet. A sharp node lets two segments arrive at any angle. A smooth node keeps the handles collinear so the curve passes through without a kink. A tangent node joins a line to a curve smoothly. A G2 node matches curvature as well as direction. You select a node and drag it, or nudge it, and the segments on both sides follow. Put nodes at the extremes so hinting and interpolation have something to hold. overshoot optical surplus overshoot proposed Professional loan: Indonesian typography writing that cites Rustan and Sihombing uses overshoot. The fallback would give «kelebihan optis», which nobody writes. Overshoot is the extension of a rounded or pointed shape beyond an alignment line so that it appears as tall as a flat shape. For example, an o may extend above the x-height and below the baseline. Its amount depends on the design and intended size. PostScript alignment zones can describe these overshoot regions for hinting; there is no universal percentage to apply. proportional figures natural-width figures angka proporsional proposed Apple CoreText: Proportional Numbers → Angka Proporsional. Proportional figures have individual advance widths, so a 1 takes less room than an 8. They read well in running text; tabular figures share one width for columns. The pnum feature selects them. segment segmen proposed Apple, Blender; KBBI. A segment is the portion of a contour between two on-curve endpoints. It may be a straight line or a curve. A quadratic Bézier segment has one off-curve control point; a cubic segment has two. Describe the segment type and the relevant editing command rather than assuming that every curve has two handles or that changing a node type performs every conversion. serif serif proposed Apple Font Book, Microsoft and every Indonesian textbook keep «serif». «Kait», «kaki» and «sirip» occur only as explanations. A serif is the finishing stroke at the end of a stem or arm. Its shape sorts a face into the familiar classes: oldstyle, transitional, Didone, slab. You draw a serif once and reuse it as a component or an element, which keeps a family consistent and makes a late change cheap. Serifs are small, so they take the most damage at low resolution, which is where hinting and careful alignment zones earn their place. sharp tajam proposed Adobe, Apple (7 origins). Sharp describes a pointed corner or a node at which contour direction can change abruptly. Image sharpening is a different operation. sharp node simpul tajam proposed From «simpul» and «tajam». A sharp node joins contour segments without requiring a smooth change of direction. The handles of adjacent segments need not be collinear; a smooth node constrains their direction. stem main stroke batang proposed Sihombing writes «batang (stem)»; Google's Indonesian web.dev uses «batang vertikal». Some DKV material keeps English stem. A stem is a main stroke of a letter, usually the vertical one: the two uprights of an H, the single upright of an l. Stem width sets the weight of a face, and stems that disagree across a family break its rhythm. You measure a stem with the Measurement tool and record the standard widths in Font Info, where hinting and the stem links read them. Vextra reuses the word for the paired edges it detects in general artwork, not only in letters. swash flourish swash proposed Professional loan: Indonesian DKV material and Indonesian script-font foundries keep swash. Apple wavers between «hiasan» and «ekor». A swash is a decorative flourish that extends a letter, often on a capital or a terminal. Swash alternates live in the swsh feature and in glyphs with a swash suffix. terminal stroke ending terminal proposed Sihombing: «… garis akhir sebagai penutup yang disebut terminal». A terminal is the end of a stroke without a serif, such as the ending of a c or f. Its shape may be rounded, angled or cut off, depending on the design. Compare related terminals across a typeface at the intended reading size. The anatomical term does not prescribe how to construct or store the shape in an editor. UPM units per type body UPM proposed The abbreviation also fits the Indonesian expansion «unit per em»; write that out in prose. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. UPM, units per em, specifies how many font units make up one em. It sets the scale for outline coordinates and metrics when a renderer converts them to a text size. Values such as 1000 and 2048 are common; TrueType outlines do not require a power of two. When changing UPM, distinguish changing the scale value from rescaling the outlines and metrics. winding direction drawing direction arah kontur proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «drawing direction» rendered as contour direction, as German and Polish did. Winding direction is the order in which a contour runs, clockwise or counter-clockwise, and it decides which areas the renderer fills. FontLab follows the PostScript convention: outer contours wind counter-clockwise and counters wind clockwise. The letter O is two contours, one each way. You check direction before you export, and reverse a contour when a counter fills solid or an outer shape turns hollow. A renderer applies the rule at draw time, so the error shows in the proof rather than in the editor. x-height small-letter height tinggi x proposed Inkscape: «tinggi-x». Textbooks (Sihombing, Rustan) keep English x-height. Written without the hyphen, as an ordinary Indonesian noun phrase, parallel to «tinggi kapital». The x-height is the height of a lowercase x above the baseline, and it stands for the height of the lowercase in general. It does more for apparent size than the point size does: two faces at the same size look different when their x-heights differ. You record it in Font Info so hinting and alignment zones can use it, and you draw round letters slightly above it to allow for overshoot. Write it lowercase with a hyphen, even at the start of a sentence recast to avoid one.

docs.title: Font engineering
docs.text: English Fallback Indonesian Status Note Definition advance height tinggi glif proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; counterpart of «lebar glif» (advance width); same concept as vertical advance. It is the box height, not the outline height. The distance the text position advances vertically after a glyph. It is the vertical counterpart of advance width, not the height of the visible outline. advance width glyph box width lebar glif proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «glyph box width» translated, shortened as Glyphs does with Width. Rejected the calque «lebar maju» and Apple's bare «lebar», which is kept for geometric width and the width axis. Advance width is the horizontal distance allocated to a glyph before layout adjustments, measured in font units. In an OpenType font, the base values are stored in the hmtx table. Kerning and other positioning operations can adjust advances during layout without rewriting those base values. Advance width differs from the visible outline width; a space can have an advance without an outline. alignment zone height band for snapping zona perataan proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; built from «perataan» (alignment; Apple, LibreOffice) and «zona»; parallel to «zona hint». An alignment zone is a region around a common vertical alignment, such as the baseline or cap height, used in PostScript hinting. It can include the overshoot of rounded letters. A rasterizer uses zone information when fitting outlines to a pixel grid. Keep this mechanism distinct from design measurements and from the control-value and instruction mechanisms used in TrueType hinting. anchor attachment point jangkar proposed Apple, Microsoft, GIMP, Krita and LibreOffice all use «jangkar». Illustrator's «titik jangkar» is its anchor point, which FontLab calls a node, so the node is «simpul» to keep the two apart. An anchor is a named attachment point in a glyph that says where a mark belongs. A base letter carries a top anchor, and the accent carries a matching one, so the accent lands in the same relation on every letter that uses it. You place anchors in the Anchors and Pins panel, and FontLab uses them both to build composites and to generate mark attachment lookups in GPOS, which is what positions marks in text the font never composed itself. anti-aliasing edge smoothing anti-aliasing proposed Krita, QCAD and Inkscape keep the English; hyphenated form as the definition asks. GIMP's «antialias» is the rejected variant. Anti-aliasing paints partly covered pixels in intermediate shades so a rendered outline looks smooth. FontLab's preview can show anti-aliased, monochrome or subpixel rendering so you can check how hints behave under each. Write the hyphenated form. autohinting automatic screen fitting hinting otomatis proposed «Hinting» is the attested loan (GIMP); «otomatis» follows the noun in Indonesian, so no «auto-» prefix. Autohinting generates hints for a font from its outlines and its declared stems and zones, in one pass over the glyphs. It is a starting point rather than a finish: it hints the regular cases well and leaves the awkward glyphs for you. You run it after the alignment zones and standard stem widths are correct in Font Info, because it reads them. Then you check the glyphs that matter at text sizes and correct by hand what the pass got wrong. axis sumbu proposed Google's Indonesian variable-font documentation (web.dev) and Microsoft Learn use «sumbu»; 11 corpus origins. An axis is one dimension of font variation, such as weight, width or optical size. In an OpenType variable font, each axis has a four-character tag and a minimum, default and maximum value. Registered tags, such as wght, have defined meanings. Preserve tag spelling and case, and check the axis registry when assigning a custom tag. axis map axis value mapping peta sumbu proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «axis value mapping» translated from the chosen «sumbu». An axis map converts user coordinates on an axis, such as weight 400, to the design coordinates of the masters. It is stored in the avar table and lets a slider feel even when masters are not. bottom sidebearing sidebearing bawah proposed From the loan «sidebearing» plus the Indonesian direction word. The space below the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. component komponen proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft (9 origins). A component is a reference to another glyph placed inside this one, so that aacute holds the a and the acute rather than copies of their outlines. Change the source glyph and every glyph that references it follows. You build composites from components, position them with anchors, and keep them as references through to export, where a TrueType flavoured font stores them in the glyf table. In FontLab a component is one kind of element reference. composite glyph assembled glyph glif komposit proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «komposit» is the KBBI adjective for assembled; from «glif». A composite glyph is built from references to other glyphs rather than from its own outlines: an accented letter, a currency symbol with a bar, a stacked fraction. You assemble it from components and anchor them to the base, so a change to the base or to the mark reaches every composite that uses it. Composites keep a large accented character set consistent and small. A composite that has been decomposed is no longer one, and no longer follows its sources. conversion profile export settings set profil konversi proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; plain compound of two established loans. A conversion profile is the saved set of choices TransType applies to a conversion: the output format, the naming scheme, the filters, and the options that go with them. You build a profile once for a job you repeat, then run it over a new set of sources without repeating the decisions. It matters because a family converted with two different sets of options ships as two families that do not quite match, which shows up in a font menu rather than in a test. CVT table tabel CVT proposed Tag protected, noun translated; «tabel» as in Apple ATS «tabel ‘kern’». The CVT table holds the control values that TrueType hinting instructions refer to: the stem widths, heights, and other measurements a font wants held constant across glyphs. An instruction cites a CVT entry rather than a raw number, so one change to the table reaches every glyph that cites it. You work with it through the TrueType Hinting panel. It ships in the font, alongside the instructions themselves and the prep and fpgm programs that set the machine up. design space variation range ruang desain proposed Google's Indonesian web.dev article on variable fonts: «ruang desain font variabel». A design space describes the positions defined by a font project's variation axes. Masters provide source data at specified locations; instances represent results at selected locations. User coordinates and internal design coordinates may be connected by a mapping, or may have the same values. State which coordinate system a number belongs to when the distinction affects a procedure. device correction per-size pixel correction koreksi ukuran proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «per-size pixel correction» translated, as German, Spanish, French and Polish did. A device correction adjusts a kerning or positioning value by whole pixels at one pixel size, to fix rounding at that size only. Stored in GPOS device tables; rarely needed on modern rasterizers. dimensions dimensi proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; KBBI loan; names the font's vertical values, kept apart from «metrik» and «pengukuran». The font or family vertical values, such as ascender, descender, capital height, x-height and line gap. Distinguish these values from glyph spacing and canvas measurements. element elemen proposed Apple, Microsoft, Krita (7 origins). An element is FontLab's container for a piece of drawing inside a glyph: one or more contours, an image, or a reference to another element. A glyph holds elements, and an element holds contours, which is the layer of structure that makes a serif or a stem reusable across a family. You work with elements in the Elements panel and with the Element tool. The word is FontLab's own; other editors call the nearest thing a path group or a component. element reference shared drawing link referensi elemen proposed From «referensi» and «elemen». An element reference is a placed copy of an element that still points at the original. Edit the original and every reference updates. You use references to share a serif, a stem, or a whole letter across a family, and you decompose a reference only when a glyph genuinely needs to diverge. A component is the familiar case of an element reference: one glyph placed inside another. Keep references intact through the design phase, since decomposing early throws away the link that makes a late change cheap. family dimensions dimensi keluarga proposed From «dimensi». «Keluarga» is the designers' word for a font family (LibreOffice, BINUS); Apple's «kumpulan» is not used in the profession. The vertical values used to establish line layout for a font family. Platform-specific ascender, descender and line-gap fields belong to this group. Flex Flex proposed A fixed PostScript operation name; kept. Flex is a PostScript hint that flattens a shallow curve, such as a cup serif, to a straight line at small sizes. FontLab marks glyphs that carry it. Keep the name. font dimensions dimensi font proposed From «dimensi»; «font» is the universal Indonesian word (Apple, Microsoft, Adobe, Google), not KBBI's «fon» or LibreOffice's «fonta». The design dimensions of a font master, including ascender, descender, capital height and x-height. These values describe the vertical proportions of the design. font target export target font tujuan proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «tujuan» is destination (Apple: «folder tujuan»). A font target is what TransType produces from a source: the output font, with its format, its names, and the filters applied on the way. Sources go in on one side and targets come out on the other, and one source can produce several targets. You set the target options before you convert, and you name the target in a procedure step so a reader knows which side of the conversion a setting belongs to. font unit unit font proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; plain compound; «unit» also keeps the UPM abbreviation valid in Indonesian. A font unit is the coordinate step of a font's design grid. UPM says how many of them make one em, so a 700 unit stem in a 1000 UPM font is 70 percent of the em. Metrics, kerning values and node coordinates are all stated in font units. fractional coordinates non-integer coordinates koordinat pecahan proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «pecahan» is a fraction; «koordinat desimal» is the rejected alternative. Fractional coordinates are node positions with decimal places, kept for curve fidelity while you draw. Font formats store integers, so FontLab rounds on export or when you turn on Round coordinates for the font. friendly glyph name readable glyph name nama glif terbaca proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «readable glyph name» translated. Rejected the literal «nama ramah». A friendly glyph name is the readable name FontLab shows for editing, such as Aacute, as opposed to the production name written into the exported font, such as uni00C1. FontLab can keep both and convert on export. ghost hint edge-only fitting instruction hint hantu proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; literal and a little playful, like French hint fantôme and Polish hint widmo. A ghost hint is a PostScript hint with a special width that marks one edge, such as the top of a round letter, when there is no stem to hint. It aligns that edge to an alignment zone. hint screen fitting instruction hint proposed The definition keeps the word English in every language. Rejected Apple and Microsoft «petunjuk», an ordinary tip. A hint is a stored instruction that tells a rasterizer how to align a stem or a zone to the pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hints describe stems and zones; TrueType hints are instructions. FontLab draws hints in the Glyph window and generates them with autohinting. The word stays English in every language. hint zone hinting height band zona hint proposed From the loan «hint». A hint zone is a horizontal band, such as the baseline or the x-height, inside which a rasterizer snaps overshoots to the same pixel row. FontLab stores zones in Font Info and shows them in the Glyph window. An alignment zone is the PostScript name for the same thing; hint zone is the general term. hinting screen fitting hinting proposed GIMP keeps «Hinting»; Indonesian font makers use the loan. Hinting is the extra information a font carries so that its outlines land predictably on a pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hinting declares stems and alignment zones and leaves the rasterizer to interpret them. TrueType hinting gives instructions that move points explicitly, with the control values in the CVT table. You work on PostScript hints in the glyph and in Font Info, and on TrueType hints with the TrueType Hinting tool and panel. Autohinting produces a starting point you then correct. instance generated design instans proposed Adapted loan, attested in Microsoft Word. Google's documentation keeps English «instance»; «contoh» (Adobe, Apple, Blender) means example and was rejected. An instance is a particular result at a location in a font's variation space. A named instance, such as Semibold, gives a selected location a name that applications can present. Other locations need not have names. In FontLab, configured instances can be exported as static fonts or included as named instances in a variable font. interpolation interpolasi proposed GIMP, Krita, Microsoft; Google's web.dev article. Interpolation calculates values between source values. In font design, it can calculate outlines, metrics and other data from masters at specified design-space locations. Outline interpolation requires corresponding contour and point structures. Structural compatibility makes the calculation possible, but does not guarantee a good drawing: inspect intermediate results as well as the masters. Extrapolation calculates beyond the source range. kern exception pair spacing exception pengecualian kerning proposed From «kerning». A kern exception is a pair value that overrides what the classes would otherwise apply. One member of a class rarely behaves like the rest, and the exception says so without breaking the class apart. You create one in the Kerning panel by kerning the single pair while its classes stay in place. Keep exceptions few: a class with many exceptions is the wrong class, and the cheaper fix is to split it rather than to list every disagreement. kerning pair spacing correction kerning proposed Professional loan: Adobe, Apple AppKit, Inkscape, Scribus and Indonesian typography courses. Rejected Microsoft's «rapatkan dua karakter» and the paraphrase «jarak antarhuruf». Kerning adjusts the spacing of particular glyph combinations beyond their normal advances. A pair such as AV may need a different gap from the one produced by its unadjusted metrics. OpenType fonts commonly store horizontal kerning in GPOS lookups associated with the kern feature; some formats and workflows use a separate kern table. Name the mechanism when it matters to export or compatibility. kerning class pair spacing group kelas kerning proposed From «kerning». A kerning class groups glyphs that need the same kerning. You put every glyph that behaves alike on one side into one class, then kern the class once instead of kerning each pair inside it. FontLab applies the class value to every member pair and keeps single pairs as exceptions where a member needs its own value. Classes matter because a text face carries thousands of readable pairs, and a hand kerned list of that size is unmaintainable. FontLab writes the result into GPOS as class based positioning. kerning pair spacing-corrected pair pasangan kerning proposed From «kerning»; «pasangan» is a pair. A kerning pair associates two glyphs, or two kerning classes, with a spacing adjustment. In horizontal kerning, a negative value normally reduces the gap and a positive value increases it. An individual glyph pair may provide an exception to class kerning, but it can also exist without a class rule. Check pairs in representative text as well as in isolation. left sidebearing sidebearing kiri proposed From the loan «sidebearing». Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the glyph origin and the left edge of its outline. It contributes to the glyph advance width and its spacing. Lib Lib proposed Identifier mirroring the UFO lib; kept. Lib is the custom metadata dictionary of a font or a master, mirroring the UFO lib and stored in VFJ. Scripts and tools keep their own keys there. line gap celah baris proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «celah» is a gap, «baris» a line of text. Kept apart from «tinggi baris». The line gap is extra vertical space between lines that a font recommends beyond ascender and descender. hhea and OS/2 each store one. line height tinggi baris proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; literal, with «baris» for a line of text; the usual rendering of CSS line height. The distance between successive text baselines. It includes the relevant ascender, descender and line-gap contributions; line gap alone is only the additional space. link metrics tie spacing to another glyph tautkan metrik proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «tautkan» is the standard verb for link (Apple, Microsoft). Link metrics ties a glyph's sidebearing or advance width to another glyph or to an expression, so the value follows its source. FontLab shows linked metrics with the expression and updates them when the source changes. linked metrics metrik tertaut proposed From «tautkan metrik». Glyph spacing values linked to another glyph or to an expression. Updating the source or expression changes the dependent advance width or sidebearings. mark attachment combining mark positioning penempelan tanda proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «combining mark positioning» translated; «menempel» is to stick onto. Rejected «lampiran», a file attachment. Mark attachment positions a combining mark relative to a base glyph, a ligature component or another mark. OpenType GPOS lookups describe the anchor relationships, and the shaping engine applies the positioning during layout. FontLab can generate attachment code from suitable anchors. Check the relevant generation settings and test combinations, including stacked marks, rather than assuming that every anchor automatically becomes a lookup. master source design master proposed Professional loan: BINUS's Indonesian article on variable fonts and Microsoft keep «master». LibreOffice's «induk» (parent) is the rejected native word. A master provides source outlines and other font data at a specified location in a design space. Masters can describe weight, width or other variations, including intermediate locations. FontLab uses corresponding data from masters to calculate instances. For outline interpolation, check contour and point compatibility in each affected glyph; the word master alone does not guarantee that every glyph is present or compatible. master compatibility matching master structure kompatibilitas master proposed From «master»; Google's web.dev: «kontur yang kompatibel dengan interpolasi». Master compatibility is the condition every glyph must meet before it can interpolate: the same number of contours in the same order, with the same number of nodes and the same start point in each. FontLab reports incompatible glyphs and gives you Matchmaker to repair them by matching contours and start points between masters. Fix compatibility before you tune shapes, because a repair that reorders nodes moves every curve that depends on them. metrics metrik proposed Apple Font Book: «Metrik». Metrics are the measurements that place a glyph in a line: its advance width and its two sidebearings. Vertical metrics are a separate set, the font wide values for ascender, descender, and line gap. You work on horizontal metrics in the Metrics panel and with the Metrics tool, and on vertical metrics in Font Info. Say which set you mean whenever a page discusses both, because a reader who applies a horizontal instruction to the vertical fields breaks line spacing everywhere the font is used. metrics expression ekspresi metrik proposed From «metrik». An expression that calculates a glyph advance width or sidebearing from other values. It describes a spacing relationship rather than a canvas measurement. metrics key kunci metrik proposed From «metrik». A glyph reference or expression used to derive a spacing value. The referenced value determines an advance width or sidebearing. pin pin proposed Proposed form retained from the current FontLab UI. A pin is a named positioning point, distinct from an anchor used for glyph attachment. A pin is a named point inside an element. Use pins to position elements with expressions and to attach elements to each other. An anchor is a named point in a glyph layer, used for component placement and mark attachment. Create either with the Guides tool and edit it in the Anchors and Pins panel. PPM pixels per type body PPM proposed The abbreviation also fits the Indonesian expansion «piksel per em»; write that out in prose. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. PPM, pixels per em, is the size at which a rasterizer renders a font: how many pixels one em occupies. TrueType hints, device corrections and bitmap strikes are specified per PPM. In explanatory prose expand it; in hinting fields the short form is usual. production glyph name shipping glyph name nama glif produksi proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; literal, from «nama glif». A production glyph name is the name written into the exported font, chosen for compatibility with tools and the Adobe Glyph List, such as uni00C1 rather than Aacute. rendering drawing on screen rendering proposed Google's Indonesian documentation writes «rendering» and «merender»; Blender and Scribus keep «render». Rejected Apple's «penyajian» and Adobe's «mengolah». Rendering is the conversion of an outline into pixels on a screen or a printer. The rasterizer of the operating system or of FontLab's preview reads the outline, applies the hints and paints the result. FontLab previews rendering at chosen pixel sizes so you can judge hints. Rasterization names the same step from the pixel side. required glyphs mandatory glyphs glif wajib proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «mandatory glyphs» translated. Required glyphs are the ones the OpenType specification and common tools expect at the start of a font: .notdef, NULL or uni0000, CR or uni000D and space. FontLab can add them on export. right sidebearing sidebearing kanan proposed From the loan «sidebearing». Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the right edge of a glyph outline and the end of its advance width. It contributes to spacing. sidebearing side space sidebearing proposed No Indonesian term is attested; Indonesian font makers work in English-language editors and say sidebearing, so the loan is kept. The fallback «side space» would give «jarak sisi», the alternative for a reviewer to weigh. A sidebearing is the space between a glyph's outline and the edge of its advance width: the left sidebearing before the shape, the right sidebearing after it. Together with the advance width it sets how the glyph spaces against every other glyph, which is the work that carries a text face further than kerning does. You edit sidebearings in the Metrics panel or with the Metrics tool, one glyph at a time or across a selection, and you check them in a word rather than in isolation. size ukuran proposed Apple: «Ukuran Font». The size of an object or the chosen size of displayed text. Name a specific width or height when only one direction is intended. spacing spasi proposed Apple CoreText: Spacing → Spasi. «Spasi» also names a space character, so prose may need «pengaturan spasi». The adjustment of glyph advance widths and sidebearings to establish the space between letters. Kerning makes additional adjustments to particular pairs. standard stem reference stem width batang standar proposed From «batang». Standard stems are the representative horizontal and vertical stem widths declared in a font for hinting. The rasterizer snaps stems near those widths to the same pixel count, so like stems stay alike at small sizes. stem link stem tie tautan batang proposed From «batang» and «tautan» (link). A stem link ties two edges of a stroke together as a stem, so hinting can hold their distance as the size changes. A vertical link governs a horizontal measurement and a horizontal link governs a vertical one. You add links in the glyph, either by hand or from an autohinting pass, and you keep them consistent with the standard stem widths declared in Font Info. Vextra reuses the term for the paired edges it detects in artwork that is not type. styling group name nama grup gaya proposed «Gaya» is style in Apple Font Book («Nama gaya»); «grup» as chosen for group. The styling group name, SGN, ties together the styles an application reaches through its bold and italic buttons, and the styling link value and styling link name say which slot each style takes in that group. The mechanism is older than typographic family names and narrower: four slots, no more. You set these fields in TransType when a family has to behave correctly in applications that still drive style selection from those buttons. subsetting cutting down a font pembuatan subset proposed Scribus and Microsoft keep «subset»; «pembuatan» names the process. Subsetting exports only part of a font, such as the glyphs a page uses or one codepage, to make a smaller file. The OS/2 embedding bits can forbid it. top sidebearing sidebearing atas proposed From the loan «sidebearing». The space above the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. tracking uniform letter spacing tracking proposed Professional loan: Telkom University's typography primer and DKV course material write tracking. Rejected Apple and Microsoft «pelacakan», which is surveillance tracking. Tracking changes the spacing across a run of text, rather than correcting particular pairs as kerning does. Layout applications apply it to text. TransType's Tracking filter changes spacing in the font data itself. That changes the font's starting metrics; a layout application can still apply additional tracking to text set in the resulting font. TrueType instruction pixel fitting instruction instruksi TrueType proposed Brand protected; KBBI «instruksi». A TrueType instruction is one step of the program a TrueType font runs to fit an outline to the pixel grid. Instructions are the TrueType form of hints. FontLab writes them from visual TrueType hints and can keep the ones a font already has. Say instruction for the code and hint for what the reader draws. typographic family name nama keluarga tipografis proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «keluarga» as designers say it (LibreOffice, BINUS), not Apple's «kumpulan»; «tipografis» is the KBBI adjective. The typographic family name, TFN, is the name that groups every style of a family under one entry, and the typographic style name, TSN, is what distinguishes a style inside it. They sit beside the older four style family and style names that legacy applications read. You set them in TransType and in Font Info, and you keep them consistent across a family, because an app that reads these fields builds its font menu from them. update metrics perbarui metrik proposed «Perbarui» is the standard Update verb (Apple, Microsoft). Recalculate glyph spacing values from their links or expressions. This command updates the advance widths and sidebearings that depend on those relationships. variable font font variabel proposed Google's Indonesian web.dev article: «font variabel». A variable font contains data for design variation along one or more axes. Applications select axis values and calculate the corresponding outlines and other variable data. Named instances identify selected locations, but users are not limited to those locations when the application exposes axis controls. A variable font's supported range depends on its data; it need not contain every style in the family. variation location position in the variation range lokasi variasi proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; Google's web.dev speaks of «lokasi sumbu». A variation location is a point in the design space, given as one value per axis. Masters and instances each have one, and the Variations panel slider shows the current one. vertical advance glyph box height tinggi glif proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «glyph box height» translated; same concept as advance height. The vertical advance is the distance a glyph advances in vertical text, the counterpart of advance width for East Asian layout. Stored in vmtx. vertical metrics metrik vertikal proposed From «metrik». The font-wide vertical values used for line layout, including ascender, descender and line gap. FontLab groups these as dimensions, distinct from glyph spacing metrics. visual kerning shape-measured spacing correction kerning visual proposed From «kerning». Visual kerning is kerning that FontLab proposes by measuring the shapes, so that a font gets a usable first pass without a person typing thousands of values. You run it over a selection, then review what it produced, because a measurement of two outlines does not know about the words a reader will meet. Treat the result as a draft: keep the pairs it got right, correct the ones it did not, and kern the difficult pairs by eye in real words. weight axis thickness axis sumbu bobot proposed From «sumbu» and «bobot». The weight axis, tag wght, varies stroke thickness from light to bold. In a variable font it is the most common axis; its master locations use the usWeightClass scale, such as 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. weight class kelas bobot proposed From «bobot». The weight class is the OS/2 value from 100 to 900 that tells applications how heavy a style is, with 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. Style linking and menus rely on it. width axis narrow-to-wide axis sumbu lebar proposed Google's web.dev: «sumbu Lebar». The width axis, tag wdth, varies letter proportions from condensed to extended. It is distinct from advance width, which is the spacing of one glyph, and from the geometric width of a shape. Its scale is a percentage of normal width. width class kelas lebar proposed From «lebar» (Apple CoreText: Width → Lebar). The width class is the OS/2 value from 1, ultra condensed, to 9, ultra expanded, that tells applications how wide a style is. It is a classification, not the width axis value and not the advance width.

docs.title: OpenType
docs.text: English Fallback Indonesian Status Note Definition Adobe Glyph List Adobe Glyph List do-not-translate The Adobe Glyph List maps standard glyph names to Unicode codepoints, so that a glyph named aacute is understood as U plus 00E1 by any tool that follows it. You name glyphs by it wherever it covers the character, because tools and text engines can then infer the mapping without being told twice. Where it does not cover a glyph, you fall back to a consistent scheme of your own and assign codepoints explicitly. Write the name in full on first mention, then AGL. alternate glyph glyph variant glif alternatif proposed Apple CoreText and the Typography panel use «alternatif» for alternates; noun from the chosen «glif». An alternate glyph is another form of the same character, selected through an OpenType feature such as salt or a stylistic set. Its name usually carries a suffix, as in a.alt or g.ss01. cmap cmap do-not-translate The cmap table maps character codes to glyph indices. Its Unicode subtables provide the initial mapping used in text rendering; other subtables support particular encodings or variation sequences. FontLab generates these mappings from the project's encoding data. A glyph without its own Unicode assignment can still appear in typed text through substitution, such as a ligature or alternate selected by the shaping engine. code page legacy character table halaman kode proposed Standard Microsoft Windows Indonesian rendering of code page; two words as the definition asks. A code page is a numbered legacy encoding, such as Windows 1250 for Central European languages, that maps one byte to one character. The OS/2 table lists the code pages a font supports, and FontLab derives that list from the glyphs present.
