Write two words. color font table tabel font berwarna proposed «Tabel» for a font table (Apple ATS: «tabel ‘kern’»); «font berwarna» is the natural adjective form. Colour-font tables store data for colour glyph rendering. Formats include COLR with CPAL, SVG, sbix, and CBDT with CBLC. They differ in how they describe vector or bitmap content and in application support. Including several formats can extend coverage, but does not guarantee rendering in every application. Identify the exported formats and test the intended targets. contextual alternates context-dependent variants alternatif kontekstual proposed Apple CoreText: Contextual Alternates → Alternatif Kontekstual. Contextual alternates, the calt feature, cover substitutions an app makes because of what sits around a glyph rather than because a reader asked. In a script face the text engine replaces an entry stroke after a letter that already ends in one, and in a face with repeating shapes it replaces the second of a pair. You write the rules with context in feature code, and apps usually leave calt on by default, which makes it the feature most likely to surprise you when a rule is too broad. cursive attachment joined-script connection sambungan kursif proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «joined-script connection» translated; «sambungan» is a join or connection. Cursive attachment joins glyphs by matching an exit anchor of one glyph to the entry anchor of the next, so connected scripts such as Arabic and Nastaliq flow. It is the curs feature, built from anchors. design languages bahasa sasaran proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; follows the reviewed languages (target languages); the literal «bahasa desain» means a visual design language. Design languages, the meta table dlng record, list the languages the typeface was designed for. Supported languages, slng, list every language it can set. Both are language tags, not feature tags. encoding pengodean proposed KBBI form; Apple and Microsoft Excel. Rejected the nonstandard «pengkodean» and the bare English. An encoding maps character codes to glyphs. Unicode is the encoding modern fonts use; legacy encodings such as Mac Roman or a code page map one byte to one glyph. FontLab shows the font in a chosen encoding in the Font window and writes the cmap from it. Say encoding for the mapping and code page for a numbered legacy table. feature code layout rule code kode fitur proposed From «fitur». Feature code is the text syntax that describes OpenType features: classes, lookups, substitution and positioning rules, grouped into features by tag. It is usually called FEA, after the file extension. You edit it in the Features panel, compile it to check for errors, and keep it under the same review as the drawings, since a rule that fires on the wrong glyph is as visible as a wrong outline. FontLab compiles it into GSUB and GPOS at export. fractions pecahan proposed Apple CoreText: Fractions → Pecahan. Fractions are numerical forms such as ½. In OpenType, the frac feature supports diagonal fraction composition through glyph substitution. A font may provide precomposed fraction glyphs, numerator and denominator forms, or both. The separate numr and dnom features provide numerator and denominator forms. Do not substitute the sups and subs feature names for these mechanisms or promise support for every input sequence without testing it. glyph index glyph number indeks glif proposed Apple Font Book has «Indeks … Simbol Gambar»; rebuilt on «glif». A glyph index is the number a glyph occupies in the font's own order, counting from zero. Text engines work in indices after the cmap has done its job, and binary tables reference glyphs by index rather than by name. You rarely set one by hand, but you meet it when you inspect a compiled font or debug a lookup that fires on the wrong glyph. The index depends on glyph order, so it changes when the order does. glyph name nama glif proposed From «glif». A glyph name identifies a glyph in an editing project, feature code or a tool's data. Names such as a, a.sc and a.alt can distinguish related drawings. They are separate from Unicode assignments and glyph indices, and need not survive in every exported format. After renaming a glyph, check references in feature code, classes and scripts, including references the editor cannot update automatically. GPOS GPOS do-not-translate GPOS is the OpenType table that holds positioning: kerning, mark attachment, cursive attachment, and any rule that moves a glyph without replacing it. FontLab writes your kerning here, as pairs and as class based positioning, and builds the mark lookups from your anchors. You reach it through feature code rather than by editing the table. A font may also carry a legacy kern table; modern text engines read GPOS and many ignore the other. GSUB GSUB do-not-translate GSUB is the OpenType table containing glyph-substitution lookups. It supports operations such as replacing a glyph with an alternate, forming a ligature or selecting a form from its context. FontLab compiles feature code into these structures. To diagnose a missing substitution, check the glyphs, compiled rules, feature selection, language and shaping order in the target application. ligature joined letters ligatur proposed Apple AppKit and CoreText; KBBI form. A ligature is a glyph used to represent a sequence of characters, such as fi. OpenType substitution can replace several glyphs with one ligature glyph. The liga and dlig features distinguish standard and discretionary ligatures. Shaping does not change the underlying text; whether a later document export preserves searchable text also depends on that export and its text mappings. localized forms language-specific variants bentuk lokal proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; Apple CoreText uses «bentuk» for Forms; follows Polish formy lokalne. Localized forms are glyph variants selected for a text run's language. The OpenType locl feature can provide these substitutions, for example Bulgarian forms of Cyrillic letters. The shaping engine needs the relevant language information, which the application may obtain from a setting or other context. The substitution changes glyph selection, not the underlying characters or their codepoints. lookup procedure prosedur approved User/team procedure fallback. No sufficiently strong established OpenType-specific alternative verified in the reviewed primary sources. Keep the approved contextual Rules panel title. Preserve literal FEA lookup/lookupflag keywords, identifiers and OpenType structure names. Ordinary search senses are separate. A lookup groups substitution or positioning rules of one type in GSUB or GPOS. Features reference lookups, and several features can share one. The shaping engine selects features and may process them in script-specific stages; within a stage, LookupList order matters. Source-code order alone does not describe the complete shaping sequence. Inspect the compiled tables and the target engine when diagnosing ordering problems. mark glyph combining mark glyph glif tanda proposed From «glif» and «tanda». A mark glyph is an accent or other combining mark that attaches to a base glyph through anchors. The GDEF table classes it as a mark so shaping engines position it rather than advancing past it. nonspacing mark zero-width combining mark tanda tanpa lebar proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «zero-width combining mark» translated. A nonspacing mark is the Unicode general category Mn: a combining mark with zero advance, such as a combining acute. It differs from FontLab's nonspacing element, which is a property of an element inside a glyph. oldstyle figures lowercase-style figures angka gaya lama proposed Apple CoreText: Oldstyle Figures → Angka gaya lama. Oldstyle figures are numerals with varying heights, often including forms with ascenders and descenders. The OpenType onum feature selects them when provided by the font. Figure height and figure width are separate choices: oldstyle figures can be proportional or tabular. Use tabular widths when numerals must align in columns, whether their forms are oldstyle or lining. OpenType class layout glyph group kelas OpenType proposed Brand protected, noun translated. An OpenType class is a named group of glyphs that feature code can address at once, written with an at sign before the name. One rule over two classes replaces a page of single rules, and one edit to a class reaches every rule that cites it. You define classes in the Classes panel or in feature code, and you keep their order stable, because a substitution between two classes pairs them by position. Kerning classes are a separate mechanism with the same idea. OpenType feature layout feature fitur OpenType proposed From «fitur»; Google's Indonesian documentation writes «fitur font». An OpenType feature identifies typographic behaviour through a four-character tag, such as liga, smcp or ss01. Feature records reference substitution or positioning lookups. In FontLab, you can write feature code and compile it into the font. Whether and when a feature is applied depends on the shaping engine, script, language and application settings; not every feature is a user-controlled switch. OS/2 table tabel OS/2 proposed Tag protected, noun translated. The OS/2 table carries the font's metadata for applications: vertical metrics, weight and width classes, embedding permissions, the panose values, and the codepage and Unicode range bits that say what the font covers. You fill it from Font Info rather than by hand, and you check it before release, because a wrong weight class puts a font in the wrong slot in a menu and wrong vertical metrics change line spacing in every browser. Write it with the slash: OS/2. Private Use Area Private Use Area do-not-translate A private-use area is one of three Unicode blocks whose codepoints can receive meanings by private agreement. Different fonts or systems may assign different meanings to the same private-use codepoint. Use a documented agreement when encoding custom symbols there. An alternate glyph reached through a feature does not require its own private-use assignment. single substitution substitusi tunggal proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; KBBI «substitusi». A single substitution replaces one glyph with one other glyph, the simplest GSUB lookup type. Small caps, stylistic alternates and localized forms are mostly built from it. small caps small capitals kapital kecil proposed Apple CoreText: Small Caps → Kapital Kecil. Rejected Microsoft's «huruf kecil», which means lowercase. Small caps are capital shapes drawn at roughly lowercase height, with their own weight and width rather than scaled capitals. Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set set gaya proposed Microsoft Publisher: «Set Gaya». Rejected Apple's «kumpulan gaya», because «kumpulan» is Apple's word for a font family, and Word's «set bergaya». A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures angka tabular proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; parallel to «angka proporsional»; «tabular» is a KBBI adjective. Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code titik kode Unicode proposed Literal rendering of code point, the usual one in Indonesian technical writing, with Unicode protected; not confirmed in an authoritative source. The fallback evidence «kode karakter» is the rejected looser term. A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character pemilih variasi proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «pemilih» is a selector or picker (Apple, Microsoft). A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system aksara proposed The Indonesian word for a script (aksara Latin, aksara Arab, aksara Jawa); Indonesian Wikipedia defines «aksara atau sistem penulisan». It cannot be confused with a Python «skrip». Microsoft's «sistem penulisan» is the rejected longer form. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Indonesian Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Indonesian Status Note Definition action tindakan proposed Platform word (Apple and Microsoft Indonesian UI, 16 general-software origins). Rejected «aksi», used by Blender, GIMP, Inkscape and Krita, which reads as stunt or protest. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. add tambah proposed Attested in 25 origins (Adobe, Apple, Microsoft). The bare root is the compact label; «tambahkan» is the form with an object in running text. Add inserts another item into the current collection or selection. Name the item when the surrounding control does not make it clear. alternate alternatif proposed Apple CoreText (Alternates → Alternatif) and Microsoft. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud awan jangkar proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; literal compound of «jangkar» (anchor), like German Ankerwolke and Polish chmura kotwic. The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer lapisan otomatis proposed From «lapisan» (layer); Indonesian puts «otomatis» after the noun (Apple, LibreOffice «… Otomatis»). FontLab's machine-translated Indonesian site has the same phrase. An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint hint otomatis proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; command label built from the loan «hint» plus «otomatis», the pattern of «Kern Otomatis». The process is «hinting otomatis». Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush Kuas proposed Adobe Illustrator, Apple and Krita (18 origins). The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse ciutkan proposed Apple and Microsoft (14 origins) for Collapse. Here it pulls nodes to one point without merging, so «satukan» and «gabungkan» were rejected. Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark bendera warna proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «bendera» is the flag of Apple Mail and Finder. Rejected «tanda warna» because «tanda» is the positioning mark. A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. corner angles sudut pojok proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «sudut» means both angle and corner, so the corner is «pojok» here to avoid «sudut sudut». The angles at contour vertices. These geometric measurements describe how adjacent segments meet at a corner and can be displayed on the canvas. cousins related glyphs alongside sepupu proposed House voice: the plain family word for cousins; Indonesian needs no plural form. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop pangkas proposed Adobe Illustrator and Microsoft Office. Rejected «potong» (Apple Photos), which is Cut in every Edit menu. Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic kubik proposed Blender; KBBI adjective. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current saat ini proposed Apple and Microsoft (13 origins): «pengguna saat ini». It follows the noun: «lapisan saat ini». Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. cusp titik runcing proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «runcing» is pointed. Inkscape's «simpul puncak» and «penyudutan» are inconsistent; «tajam» is kept for sharp. A cusp is a sharp point where a curve changes direction abruptly. Keep it distinct from a smooth join. decompose break into contours uraikan proposed «Menguraikan» is to break down into parts (KBBI); QCAD uses «uraikan» for exploding text into outlines. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default default proposed Platform word: Apple, Microsoft, Adobe and Google Indonesian all write «default» (28 origins). Rejected LibreOffice's «baku» and the native «bawaan», which is good Indonesian but not what the OS shows. A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode mode demo proposed Both words are established loans; Indonesian order. Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog dialog proposed Apple, Microsoft (17 origins). A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes Sulap proposed House voice: «sulap» is a conjuring trick and «disulap jadi …» is the everyday idiom for magical transformation, matching Polish wyczaruj. The plain fallback is «buat bentuk». Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text gema teks proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «gema» is an echo; rejected «ulangi teks», which collides with Repeat. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser Penghapus proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft (14 origins). The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours filter ke kontur proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback translated in the «X ke Y» label pattern of Inkscape's «Sapuan ke Tapak». Adobe's «perluas» for Expand would read as enlarge. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours goresan ke kontur proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; same pattern as «filter ke kontur». In running text: «ubah goresan menjadi kontur». Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours terapkan transformasi proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «bake transformation into contours» rendered as apply, as French did. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature fitur proposed Google, Microsoft and Inkscape use «fitur»; tags stay literal. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills Isian proposed Microsoft uses «isian» for the noun. Rejected «isi» (Apple, Inkscape), which also means content. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit FontAudit do-not-translate FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account akun FontLab proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder Pengelas proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node simpul Genius proposed From «simpul»; Genius kept as the feature's name, as in German, Spanish, French and Polish. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid kisi proposed Adobe Illustrator and Microsoft (28 origins). The loan «grid» is common in speech. A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups Grup proposed Microsoft and Adobe (11 origins). Inkscape's «kelompok» is the rejected alternative. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide garis bantu proposed Inkscape («Garis Bantu») and everyday designers' usage; unambiguous like German Hilfslinie. Rejected the more frequent «panduan» (Adobe, Apple, Microsoft), which also means a manual or guidebook. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. kerning mode mode kerning proposed From «kerning». The editing mode for adjusting spacing between pairs of glyphs. It changes pair adjustments rather than the individual glyph sidebearings. Knife Pisau proposed The real tool's name; Apple, Krita. The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. layer lapisan proposed GIMP, Krita, QCAD, Microsoft (20 origins). Inkscape's «lapis» and the English «layer» are the rejected variants. A layer holds one drawing or part of a document. In FontLab, the context identifies the glyph layer; name the application when another product uses a different layer model. Layers Lapisan proposed As «lapisan»; Indonesian has no plural form. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark tanda proposed Adobe and Microsoft; Apple CoreText: «tanda vokal». The verb form «tandai» is to flag something, a different meaning. A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks Masker proposed GIMP and Blender. Krita and Adobe's web strings keep «mask». A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match cocokkan proposed Apple: «Cocokkan» (5). Apple's shape name «korek api» is a matchstick. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching cocok proposed Apple Web Inspector; root of «cocokkan». Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher Mak Comblang proposed House voice: the Indonesian go-between who pairs people up, the equivalent of Polish swat. The plain fallback is «pencocok master». Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. measurement line garis ukur proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; a line that shows a measured distance; kept apart from «metrik». A line that shows a measured distance in the drawing. Distinguish this geometric measurement from a metrics line used to calculate sidebearings. measurements pengukuran proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; geometry shown on the canvas; kept apart from «metrik» (spacing) and «dimensi» (font heights). Values displayed on the canvas to describe geometry, such as coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters. Showing measurements does not modify glyph spacing or font dimensions. Measurements panel panel Pengukuran proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «pengukuran» is 10 letters against 12 for Measurements, within the panel's length rule. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge gabungkan proposed Apple, Microsoft (13 origins); «gabung» is the compact label. Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh jaring proposed Blender glosses mesh as «jaring». Rejected Microsoft's «jala» (a fishing net) and Krita's wrong «bertautan»; kept apart from «kisi» (grid). A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. metrics mode mode metrik proposed From «metrik». The editing mode for adjusting glyph advance widths and sidebearings. It changes the spacing of glyphs rather than the vertical dimensions of the font or the visibility of measurements. metrics table tabel metrik proposed From «metrik». The table of glyph spacing values, including advance widths and sidebearings. It lets the user inspect or edit spacing values together. metrics tool alat metrik proposed From «metrik»; «alat» is the tool word in Adobe's Indonesian strings. The tool that edits glyph advance widths and sidebearings. Use it to adjust glyph spacing; canvas measurement overlays display values without changing those spacing values. monospaced lebar tetap proposed Apple Font Utility and Microsoft render Fixed Width as «lebar tetap». Apple Font Book leaves Monospaced in English; CoreText's «berspasi tunggal» was rejected. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line multibaris proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «baris» is a line of text; Scribus's «banyak-garis» uses the wrong word for line. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width tanpa lebar proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «zero-width» translated: the element adds nothing to «lebar glif». Rejected «tanpa spasi», which means without spaces. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move Senggol proposed Blender uses «senggol» for a nudging brush; a small push with the elbow, everyday and a little cheeky. Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique Oblique proposed Fixed FontLab operation; kept. Apple writes «Miring Oblique» for the style name. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel panel proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft (12 origins). A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil Pensil proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft (19 origins). The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush Kuas sakti proposed House voice: «sakti» is the comic-book and folk-tale word for magically powerful (jurus sakti, kartu sakti), the wink the Power names want. Rejected «super», «turbo» and the untranslated Power. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline Garis bantu sakti proposed As «Kuas sakti», on the chosen «garis bantu». A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move Senggol sakti proposed As «Kuas sakti», on «Senggol». Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline Goresan sakti proposed As «Kuas sakti», on «goresan». A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project proyek approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar bilah properti proposed Microsoft renders a bar as «bilah» («bilah alat»); «properti» is the standard loan. The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. quick measurement pengukuran cepat proposed From «pengukuran». The function that displays measurements near the pointer while editing outlines. It reports geometry on the canvas without changing the glyph spacing values. redo lakukan ulang proposed Microsoft Word. Chosen over «ulangi» (Adobe, Excel) and Apple's «ulang» because Repeat is «ulangi» and the two commands must stay apart. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference referensi proposed Apple, Microsoft (18 origins). «Rujukan» is the rejected native alternative. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours hapus tumpang tindih proposed «Tumpang tindih» is overlap in Apple and Microsoft. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat ulangi proposed Apple, Microsoft, Krita (18 origins). Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction balik arah kontur proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; from «arah kontur»; «balik» is to flip. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors Gunting proposed The real tool's name; Apple, Microsoft. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node simpul pengikut proposed Follower node: «pengikut» is one who follows, from «ikut». For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas papan sketsa proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; plain compound: a board for sketches. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline kulit proposed The everyday word; also the peel of a fruit, as in Polish skórka. Adobe and Apple attest «kulit». Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever cerdik proposed The word for the trickster mouse-deer of folk tales (si Kancil yang cerdik): clever with a hint of cunning. Rejected Apple's «cerdas», the word in «kecerdasan buatan» (AI), and Microsoft's «pintar». Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner sudut cerdik proposed From «cerdik»; «sudut» is a shape corner (Microsoft, Krita). A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter Filter Cerdik proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles kontrol spasi proposed From «spasi». Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker stiker proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft. A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. tab tab proposed Apple, Microsoft (22 origins). A tab selects one page or document within a set. A tab character in text is a different meaning and must retain its literal representation in code. text element text block elemen teks proposed Apple; from «elemen». A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness ketebalan proposed Microsoft, Blender (8 origins). Kept for geometry; weight is «bobot». Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform Transformasi proposed Adobe, Blender, Microsoft (10 origins). Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation transformasi proposed Blender, GIMP, Inkscape, Microsoft. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering Isian sejati proposed House voice: «sejati» is true or genuine with some swagger (pendekar sejati), shorter than «isian sebenarnya». True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck hapus centang proposed Apple, Microsoft (9 origins). Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview air terjun proposed The plain word (8 general-software origins); Apple Font Book leaves Waterfall in English. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight bobot proposed Microsoft, LibreOffice; Google's Indonesian documentation («rentang bobot»). Rejected Apple's «berat» (CoreText even has «berat badan», body weight) and «ketebalan», kept for measured thickness. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace spasi kosong proposed Apple and Microsoft Office. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Indonesian Status Note Definition Appearance panel panel Appearance proposed Illustrator has no Indonesian interface, so the reader sees the English label; only the noun «panel» is Indonesian. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion jiplak otomatis proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «menjiplak» is what one does with tracing paper («kertas jiplak»), the craftsman's verb. Rejected Adobe's web strings «lacak»/«jejak» (track, footprint) and the abstract «vektorisasi». Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline garis tengah proposed Microsoft Publisher. Note that «garis tengah» also means diameter in school geometry; context (stroke, tracing) disambiguates. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask masker pemotong proposed Adobe Illustrator web strings have «mask pemotongan»; rebuilt on the chosen «masker» with the agent noun. Designers also say the English clipping mask. A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point titik kontrol proposed Blender and QCAD. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines Kisi isian proposed From «kisi» (grid) and «isian» (fill). The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style mode isian proposed From «isian»; Blender has «mode isi». A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them. Each reads the brightness of the source and lays down geometry accordingly. You pick a mode, then tune its parameters. Write the mode name with its own capitalization and the words fill mode in lowercase after it. G2 continuity kontinuitas G2 proposed KBBI «kontinuitas»; G2 kept. G2 continuity means two segments meet with matching curvature, not merely with matching direction. G1 keeps the tangent continuous and can still show a break in the reflection where the curvature jumps. G2 removes that break. Vextra marks G2 nodes and can enforce the condition as you edit. You reach for it on long, shallow curves and on shapes that will be seen large, where the eye finds a curvature break that it would miss at text size. Live Effect editable effect efek live proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; «live» is a current loan (siaran live); «efek langsung» would read as a direct effect. Illustrator itself is not localized into Indonesian. A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve titik di luar kurva proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback translated. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve titik pada kurva proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback translated. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline garis luar proposed Microsoft uses «garis luar» for a shape outline. Rejected Apple's «kerangka» (skeleton, document outline). Kept apart from «kontur», one path; designers also say the English outline. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke goresan proposed Adobe Illustrator and Apple; Google's web.dev writes «goresan yang lebih tipis» of letters. Rejected Inkscape's «sapuan» and «coretan», a scribble. A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap ujung goresan proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «stroke end cap» translated. «Terminal» is kept for letter anatomy. A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape sambungan goresan proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; fallback «stroke corner shape» rendered with «sambungan», a join. A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node simpul singgung proposed «Garis singgung» is the Indonesian mathematical term for a tangent (QCAD). «Tangen» is the trigonometric function. A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. tonal map darkness map peta tonal proposed No Indonesian attestation in the corpus or the web sources checked; literal; follows Polish mapa tonalna. A tonal map is the reading of brightness across a source image that a fill uses to decide where to put geometry. Dark areas widen a strip or crowd a pattern; light areas narrow or thin it. You control the mapping with the Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels rows, which change what counts as dark before any geometry is drawn. Adjust the map rather than the fill when the result is uniformly too heavy or too sparse. Tunni line garis Tunni proposed Eponym; Indonesian puts the name after the noun without inflection. A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: Italian
docs.text:
A first draft for Italian. A model researched the guidance below and the term table in references/terms.md; no native reviewer has approved the language as a whole. Individual terms carry their own approval status; a proposed term remains proposed, and a protected name keeps its glossary spelling. The Italian interface catalogs are unfinished machine drafts: a string found in one settles neither a term nor a rule.

Use references/terms.md, and a newer core memory when one is supplied, for terminology, definitions and review status. Keep a proposed term consistent across the interface and help, and report it as proposed. Where a native reviewer's decision or newer project data disagrees with this skill, follow it and record the change. Report only checks performed: text written with this skill is not reviewed by a native speaker and not tested in the running application until someone does that.

Use these rules with the localization principles (in fontlab-localization), Qt interface rules (in fontlab-localization) and Italian language guide (in the FontLab writing guide). Examples tagged FB, G3, FF, Qt, AI or MS are quoted from Font Book, Glyphs 3, FontForge, Qt's qtbase_it catalog, Adobe Illustrator's help or Microsoft's Italian style guide. Untagged examples are constructed.

docs.title: Locale and register
docs.text:
• Italian for Italy, Qt locale it_IT.
  • Address the reader as tu, omitting the pronoun and the possessive: Controlla la selezione e riprova (FB, "Check your selection and try again"). Never Lei, voi, Si prega di or an impersonal infinitive (Selezionare un master).
  • Drop per favore, exclamation marks and the product's first person: "Please try again" is Riprova. (FB).
  • Do not assign the reader a gender: Confermi di voler…? (FB), not Sei sicuro…?; Ti diamo il benvenuto (MS), not Benvenuto.

docs.title: Grammar of interface strings
docs.text:
String Form Example Command, button, step Imperative, tu form Salva con nome… (FF, MS, "Save As…") Checkbox, option Imperative or noun phrase Centra sempre il glifo attivo (G3, "Always center active glyph") Panel or dialog title Noun phrase, no article Zone di allineamento (G3, "Alignment Zones") Status, in progress Action noun and in corso… Convalida in corso… (FB, "Validation in progress…") Success Noun and agreeing participle Esportazione completata (G3, "Export Finished") Failed attempt Impossibile and infinitive, or noun and non riuscito/a Impossibile rimuovere il font (FB, "Cannot Remove Font") Present limitation Non è possibile and infinitive Non è possibile eliminarli né disattivarli. (FB, "These fonts cannot be deleted or deactivated.") Confirmation Vuoi…?, Confermi di voler…? Vuoi disattivare i font? (FB, "Do You Want to Deactivate Fonts?") Tooltip Third-person present Aggiunge un nuovo elemento. (G3, "Adds a new item.")
  • A command is the second-person singular imperative, as on macOS, Windows, Adobe and Qt: Apri, Chiudi, Scegli, Aggiungi. Never the infinitive (Aggiungere Asse, G3) or voi.
  • A negative command is Non and the infinitive: Non salvare (Qt).
  • Sentence case in every label, as Apple, Microsoft, Adobe and Qt do: Incolla sopra (AI), not Alternative Contestuali (G3).
  • Standard commands take the words of Qt's catalog: Annulla (both Undo and Cancel), Ripristina (Redo), Taglia, Copia, Incolla, Elimina (Delete), Seleziona tutto, Esci, Ripristina (Reset), Preferenze. Save As is Salva con nome…, as on Windows and at Adobe. The canonical core follows macOS and Adobe with Ripristina for Redo. Reset also uses Ripristina, with its object or valori predefiniti when needed to distinguish the action. Do not reintroduce Rifai from older Qt text. Remove is Rimuovi, Clear Cancella.

docs.title: Compact labels
docs.text:
• Drop the article before the object of a short command: Aggiungi ancora (G3), Esporta font (FB). Keep it after tutti and in full sentences: Seleziona tutti i livelli (G3), Impossibile aprire il file.
  • Keep prepositions and fuse them with the article: Allinea a sinistra, Mostra nel Finder (G3), Opzioni di esportazione. Only nome, tipo, formato and numero may take a bare noun, as on macOS: Nome famiglia, Numero glifi (FB).
  • An abbreviation ends in a consonant and a period: Impostaz. (MS). Unit symbols take no period: pt, mm.
  • Never abbreviate a glossary term, a command verb or a name, and never drop an accent or a preposition to save space.

docs.title: Plurals and placeholders
docs.text:
Qt gives Italian two numerus forms: singular for 1 only, plural for 0 and for 2 and more (the English rule in numerus.cpp).

  • Keep %n in both forms: %n file selezionato, %n file selezionati (so 0 file selezionati).
  • Agree noun, adjective, participle and verb in each form: È stato rilevato %n problema minore, Sono stati rilevati %n problemi minori (after FB). A loan noun stays unchanged while its participle agrees: %n font rimosso, %n font rimossi.
  • A count in %1 gets no plural choice. Use label and value: Glifi: %1.

A placeholder for a noun hides its gender, number and first sound, so articles, elisions, participles and pronouns can fail.

  • When the class is known, name it and agree with it: Il file “%1” è bloccato (after G3).
  • Otherwise use a form that does not agree: Impossibile eliminare %1, Installazione di %1 non riuscita (after MS), Eliminazione completata: %1.
  • Put a simple preposition before a placeholder, never an article or a fused form: Aggiungi font a %1… (after FB), not al %1, dell’%1. Never write il/la or eliminato/a.
  • A one-word value agrees with a noun the string does not show: Nuovo font, Nuova lingua (FF); Nessuno or Nessuna. Find the noun from the control.

docs.title: Numbers, punctuation and spacing
docs.text:
• Decimal comma; period for thousands from five digits (CLDR): 1234,5, 12.345,6. Qt formats %L1. Versions, code and font data keep their source form.
  • Percent without a space: 25%. A unit takes a no-break space: 12 pt.
  • Quotation marks are “…” around names and values, as on macOS: Contiene “%1” (after FB). «…» belongs to editorial prose; straight quotes to code.
  • The apostrophe is ’: l’ancora, un po’. It never replaces an accent.
  • Accents: grave in è, cioè, à, ì, ò, ù; acute in perché, né, sé. Capitals keep them: È disponibile, never E’.
  • Ellipsis is the single character …, with no space before it, wherever the source has one.
  • No space before : ; ? !. Lowercase after a colon. Final punctuation follows the source.

docs.title: Mnemonics and key names
docs.text:
• Put & before a letter of the Italian word, as Qt does: &Salva, &Apri, &Chiudi, Ann&ulla, &Taglia. No trailing (&H) as in FontForge.
  • Never mark à è é ì ò ù. Prefer the first letter, then another consonant; avoid g j p q y. One letter per menu or dialog.
  • Key names in text are Adobe's Italian names on both platforms: Maiusc, Ctrl, Alt, Invio (Enter and Return), Canc, Backspace, Esc, Tab, barra spaziatrice, freccia su, freccia giù, freccia sinistra, freccia destra; on macOS Comando, Opzione, Control. Join keys with +: Maiusc+Ctrl+Z. Not Shift, Enter, Delete, Option or MAIUSC. Never change a shortcut.

docs.title: Names and loans
docs.text:
• Keep unchanged: product, company and format names (OpenType, UFO, VFJ), OpenType tags and table names, glyph names, code.
  • Embed a name after a class noun, without hyphen or ending: file VFJ, font OpenType, la tabella kern. The article agrees with the class noun. An application takes no article: in FontLab, Esci da FontLab.
  • A loan keeps its English spelling, takes an Italian gender and never a plural s: il font, i font, i file, i master, la password. Glyphs 3 slips into Tags, Presets, hints.
  • The article follows the next sound: l’ancora, un’istanza (not un istanza, G3), dell’asse; lo, gli, uno before s and consonant or z: lo spessore, gli stili, uno script, lo zoom; silent h: l’hint, gli hint.
  • The term table decides which loans exist. Adobe, Glyphs 3 and FontForge keep font and file but say livello for layer.
  • Do not coin verbs from English: modificare, not editare; fare clic, not cliccare (both G3); impostare, not settare.

docs.title: False friends and traps
docs.text:
Reject the office-suite sense of a type term; the term table rules.

Word Use carattere A character only. macOS carattere tipografico (typeface) and Qt Carattere (font) are office senses: a font is font, a glyph glifo. tipo Kind: Tipo di asse (FF). Never typeface or type. grassetto, corsivo The Bold and Italic styles. Weight is peso, thickness spessore; cursive joining is not corsivo. maiuscole/minuscole Letter case, never caso. A stroke cap is not maiuscole (G3). suggerimento A tip, never a hint (FF Auto Suggerimento Font, "Auto Hinting Font").

Machine translation copies English title case and word order (Left-to-right varianti, G3), puts infinitives in commands, repeats tuo, writes E’ and perchè, renders "actually" as attualmente (currently) and "is saving" as sta salvando for Salvataggio in corso….

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Check in this order, and report only checks performed:

  1. Placeholders, markup and both %n forms, read with 0, 1 and 2.
  2. Tu imperative in commands; no infinitive, voi or Lei.
  3. Status, success, failure against limitation.
  4. Gender, number and elision, above all around placeholders.
  5. Sentence case; accents (È, perché); apostrophe ’.
  6. Mnemonics: unique per menu, on unaccented letters.
  7. Type terms against the term table; carattere, font, glifo.
  8. Numbers, percent, quotation marks, key names.

docs.title: FontLab terminology and compact labels
docs.text:
Preserve deliberately uppercase source labels using the language’s case rules. Keep numeric controls compact with UPM, PPM and LSB/RSB (French AG/AD); explain the full terms in help. The Family Dimensions “Units Per eM:” label is an intentional expanded exception.

Use the current core memory and its approval status. OpenType lookup defaults to the translation of procedure, with a different term only when strong OpenType-specific evidence supports it. Explicit choices are German Lookup, French lookup, Polish procedura and Russian процедура. Ordinary searches, individual rules and OpenType features are separate concepts. Preserve literal code keywords and identifiers.

Translate Fusion with the fallback Welder. Use the core's phonetic FontAudit transliteration in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese; preserve FontAudit in code. Proposed spellings remain proposed. Before rebuilding a QPH, recover team edits and import their terms and notes into the core memory.

Compare mnemonic-split terms with unmarked labels. Keep labels compact, aiming for 120% of the English length in Dimensions and Glyph Window preferences without losing meaning. Omit redundant font, color or command wording when context supplies it. TTH labels can omit “use” and abbreviate TrueType hinting; help can explain more. A full harmonization requires three complete catalog reviews, then reconciliation of help with the final UI and verification of generated resources.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• references/terms.md: the full Italian term table, generated from the core memory it-core.tmx of the writing guide, with the status, translator note and definition of every term.
  • The Italian localization guide of the writing guide is the source of the sections above.

docs.title: Related skills
docs.text: fontlab-localization for the shared rules; fontlab-terminology for product names and shared nouns; fontlab-technical for Italian help text.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
These rules implement the FontLab writing guide. They are copied into every skill so each installed skill can work independently. Corpus measurements can inform review; they are not quotas, universal laws, or tests of authorship.

H1. Accurate actors. Address the reader when they act or choose. Name the application when it performs an operation. Fonts and files contain data that software interprets. Prefer active voice when the actor matters; retain a clear passive construction when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. Never invent an actor or cause to change the grammar.

H2. Never invent a fact. Ground numbers, names, dates, labels, shortcuts, defaults, errors, versions, and quotations in supplied or checked evidence. A draft is evidence of what was written, not independent proof of its claims. Mark unresolved facts with a specific working placeholder such as [VERIFY CLAIM], [CONFIRM LABEL], or [CONFIRM OFFER]. A marked draft is unfinished; resolve the gap before publication. Clearly label fictional examples before their invented details.

H3. Preserve certainty and scope. “May reduce” does not become “eliminates.” Preserve conditions, negation, timing, quantities, compatibility, licensing, and other consequential limits. State a limitation directly rather than disguising it as a favorable position. A single observation does not prove universal behavior. Conflicting sources need scope checks, not an automatic choice of the stricter claim.

H4. Preserve the writer's voice. Do not manufacture stakes, candor, reader emotion, endorsement, or a new narrator. Preserve useful habits and the supplied stance. Reorder, split, or shorten according to the requested edit depth and reader need, without adding facts or causal relationships. A correct draft can remain unchanged.

H5. Give thought a rhythm. Carry a subject through an action, distinction or consequence. Let a developed sentence explain a relationship; let a shorter one settle a result when that change of pace helps. Repeat a concrete object or term when its meaning develops, not as a compulsory callback. Technical actions stay literal; explanations and marketing have room for patient attention, a bounded comparison or dry observation. Keep useful qualifications beside their claims. Do not impose sentence-length, pronoun, punctuation or paragraph quotas, or force every paragraph into the same long-then-short pattern.

H6. Notice the useful detail. Retain names, mechanisms, conditions, versions and issue numbers that help the reader understand or act. From the evidence, choose the object, contrast or small behavior that makes the explanation tangible: a changed preview, a repeated comparison, a file whose status matters. Follow that detail far enough to explain its significance. Warmth can come from this attention and patience. Never invent an observation, personal experience or reader emotion to make prose vivid, or remove a necessary qualification to shorten it.

H7. Punctuation serves meaning. Prefer a colon for an explanation or list. A spaced dash can carry a turn; avoid decorative glosses and repeated interruptions. Use sentence case for new headings and preserve exact source labels. A punctuation pattern does not establish authorship.

H8. Choose precise words. Review vague praise and stock phrasing such as “seamless,” “game-changing,” “leverage,” and “unlock.” Replace them when they obscure the action or make an unsupported claim. Keep an accurate technical use or protected quotation. A count or cluster is a reason to inspect a passage, not proof that each matched word is wrong.

H9. Develop the explanation. Begin where the reader can understand the task, change or offer. Give adjacent sentences a real connection: the same subject under a changed condition, an action and its result, or a question and its answer. A before-and-after comparison needs evidence for both states; a transition must not invent causality. Let a useful aside return to the main thought. Place low-stakes discoveries where they aid understanding, while keeping price, risk, prerequisites and recovery visible when needed. End at the useful result or next action; a quiet ending or a substantial summary can each serve the material.

H10a. Preserve conditions. Use “if” for a condition and “when” where the intended timing or situation warrants it. Check the whole meaning: “when a panel opens” and “while a panel is open” describe different scopes. Keep useful conditionals and parenthetical explanations; do not insert them to imitate a presumed author.
