In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse contrai proposed Apple and Font Book use Contrai for Collapse, and contrarre in un punto reads naturally for nodes drawn to one point. Rejected comprimi (Microsoft, suggests compression) and collassa (Blender jargon). Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark etichetta colore proposed Glyphs 3 it calls the colour mark of a glyph cell Etichetta colore. Rejected bandiera (Glyphs 3 it Flags, a literal slip) and contrassegno. A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. corner angles angoli ai vertici proposed No attestation; translated from the definition, as French did. The angles at contour vertices. These geometric measurements describe how adjacent segments meet at a corner and can be displayed on the canvas. cousins related glyphs alongside cugini proposed House voice: the plain family word. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop ritaglia proposed Glyphs 3 it (Ritaglia immagine), Adobe and Apple. Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic cubico proposed Standard mathematical adjective (curva di Bézier cubica); agree with the noun. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current attuale proposed Glyphs 3 it (master attuale), FontForge it and Apple Font Book use attuale; corrente is the Microsoft habit. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. cusp cuspide proposed The Italian geometric term for a point where a curve reverses direction abruptly; no font-editor attestation. A cusp is a sharp point where a curve changes direction abruptly. Keep it distinct from a smooth join. decompose break into contours scomponi proposed Glyphs 3 it: Scomponi, Scomponi componenti. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default predefinito proposed Adobe InDesign and Microsoft Italian; Apple's di default is a loan with no adjective form. A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode modalità demo proposed No attestation needed: regular Italian UI compound. Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog finestra di dialogo proposed Apple, Adobe and Microsoft Italian. A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes inventa proposed House voice: the everyday verb for dreaming something up. No attestation. Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text ripeti testo proposed No attestation; fallback repeated text translated, as German, Spanish and French did. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser gomma proposed Adobe Illustrator (strumento Gomma) and Apple. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours espandi filtro proposed Formed with Adobe's Espandi (Espandi aspetto), the same verb as expand stroke. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours espandi tratto proposed FontForge it (Espandi il tratto); Adobe uses Espandi for turning live appearance into plain paths. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours espandi trasformazione proposed Kept in the espandi family with expand stroke and expand filter; no attestation. Rejected applica trasformazione (Blender), which hides that the live transformation is baked. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature funzione proposed Adobe InDesign Italian (funzione OpenType) and FontForge it (Funzioni); it also matches Spanish función and French fonction. Rejected funzionalità (Glyphs 3 it, Apple), which is longer and which Glyphs 3 it itself mixes with caratteristiche. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills riempimenti proposed Adobe (Riempimento) and Apple. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit FontAudit do-not-translate FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account account FontLab proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder Saldatore proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node nodo genio proposed House voice: genio is the plain Italian word. Compact label: Genio. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid griglia proposed Glyphs 3 it, FontForge it, Adobe and Apple. A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups gruppi proposed Glyphs 3 it (Gruppi di crenatura), Adobe and Apple. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide guida proposed Glyphs 3 it (Aggiungi guida, guida globale), FontForge it and Adobe InDesign. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. kerning mode modalità crenatura proposed Derived from crenatura; compact form like modalità demo. The editing mode for adjusting spacing between pairs of glyphs. It changes pair adjustments rather than the individual glyph sidebearings. Knife coltello proposed Glyphs 3 it (Coltello); the real tool's name. The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. layer livello proposed Glyphs 3 it, FontForge it, Adobe and Apple all use livello. Rejected the loan layer. A layer holds one drawing or part of a document. In FontLab, the context identifies the glyph layer; name the application when another product uses a different layer model. Layers livelli proposed Glyphs 3 it and Adobe; plural of livello. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark diacritico proposed Glyphs 3 it names the Mark category Diacritici. Rejected marca (FontForge it, a calque) and contrassegna (the verb, to flag). A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks maschere proposed Glyphs 3 it (Maschera), Apple and Inkscape. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match abbina proposed Abbinare is the plain Italian verb for making two things go together (abbinare i colori). No font-editor attestation. Rejected confronta and corrispondenza (Microsoft, the lookup-function sense). Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching abbinato proposed Participle of abbinare, the verb chosen for match; inflect for gender and number. Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher Cupido proposed House voice: fare da Cupido is the everyday Italian for playing matchmaker, and it pairs with abbina. Rejected sensale (the village go-between, now archaic), combinamatrimoni (too long) and paraninfo (literary). Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. measurement line linea di misura proposed Derived from misura. A line that shows a measured distance in the drawing. Distinguish this geometric measurement from a metrics line used to calculate sidebearings. measurements misure proposed Glyphs 3 it: Mostra le Misure. Values displayed on the canvas to describe geometry, such as coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters. Showing measurements does not modify glyph spacing or font dimensions. Measurements panel Misure proposed Name of the panel, from misure (Glyphs 3 it); shorter than the English. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge unisci proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft Italian all use Unisci. Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh trama proposed Adobe Illustrator Italian uses trama for a mesh (trama sfumata, strumento Trama). Rejected reticolo and the loan mesh (Blender); griglia is kept for grid. A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. metrics mode modalità metriche proposed Derived from metriche. The editing mode for adjusting glyph advance widths and sidebearings. It changes the spacing of glyphs rather than the vertical dimensions of the font or the visibility of measurements. metrics table tabella delle metriche proposed Derived from metriche. The table of glyph spacing values, including advance widths and sidebearings. It lets the user inspect or edit spacing values together. metrics tool strumento metriche proposed Derived from metriche. The tool that edits glyph advance widths and sidebearings. Use it to adjust glyph spacing; canvas measurement overlays display values without changing those spacing values. monospaced monospaziato proposed Italian edition of Bringhurst (caratteri monospaziati). Rejected a spaziatura uniforme (FontForge it) as too long for a label. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line multiriga proposed Microsoft Italian; riga is the Italian for a line of text. Rejected multilinea. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width senza avanzamento proposed No attestation for the FontLab property; it says the element adds nothing to the advance. A larghezza zero (Glyphs 3 it) is kept for the Unicode category. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move spintarella proposed House voice: a small friendly push, the everyday diminutive of spinta. Rejected Spingi (Microsoft). Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique obliquo proposed Obliquo is the established Italian typographic word for a slanted roman (Apple: Grassetto obliquo); use it only for this FontLab action, never for a plain slant (inclina). Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel pannello proposed Adobe, Apple and Glyphs 3 it (Pannello glifi). A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil matita proposed Glyphs 3 it (Strumento Matita), Adobe and Apple. The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush superpennello proposed House voice: super- as in supereroe keeps the wink of Power; pennello is the chosen noun. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline superguida proposed House voice: super- plus guida. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move superspinta proposed House voice: super- carries the superhero wink of the Power names; spinta is the noun behind spintarella. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline supertratto proposed House voice: super- plus tratto. Rejected Contorno evoluto (Inkscape), an industrial tone. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project progetto approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar barra delle proprietà proposed No attestation for the FontLab element; regular Italian UI compound (barra degli strumenti, barra laterale). The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. quick measurement misura rapida proposed Derived from misura. The function that displays measurements near the pointer while editing outlines. It reports geometry on the canvas without changing the glyph spacing values. redo ripristina proposed macOS and Adobe Italian pair Annulla with Ripristina. Rejected ripeti (Microsoft, Qt), because it is needed for Repeat. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference riferimento proposed FontForge it (Copia il riferimento) and Adobe InDesign. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours rimuovi sovrapposizione proposed Glyphs 3 it: Rimuovi sovrapposizione. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat ripeti proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft Italian; kept apart from redo (ripristina). Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction inverti contorno proposed Glyphs 3 it: Inverti contorno. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors forbici proposed Adobe Illustrator (strumento Forbici) and Apple. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node nodo inseguitore proposed Read as Follower node: inseguitore is the Italian technical word for something that follows a leader's movement (inseguitore solare). Rejected seguace, the social follower. Compact label: inseguitore. For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas blocco schizzi proposed House voice: the pad a designer sketches on. Rejected tavola da disegno, which is Illustrator's artboard. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline buccia proposed House voice: the skin of a fruit, which wraps the shape, as Polish skórka does. Rejected pelle (human skin). Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever furbo proposed House voice: furbo is the everyday Italian for sly and clever (una soluzione furba). Rejected intelligente (banned; Glyphs it has it) and astuto, which is bookish. Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner angolo furbo proposed Angolo is the Glyphs 3 it word for a corner; furbo per the house voice. A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter Filtro furbo proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles controlli di spaziatura proposed Derived from spaziatura; no attestation. Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker adesivo proposed The everyday Italian word for a sticker. Rejected autoadesivo (Microsoft, a self-adhesive label). A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. tab scheda proposed Glyphs 3 it (Nuova scheda) and Microsoft use scheda for a tab in a window. Rejected tabulazione, which is the tab character. A tab selects one page or document within a set. A tab character in text is a different meaning and must retain its literal representation in code. text element text block elemento di testo proposed Derived from elemento. A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness spessore proposed Italian edition of Hochuli (spessore del tratto), Gill (spessore) and Apple. Kept apart from peso, the typographic weight. Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform trasforma proposed Glyphs 3 it, Adobe and Apple: Trasforma. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation trasformazione proposed Glyphs 3 it (Trasformazioni) and Adobe. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering Nero su bianco proposed House voice: an everyday idiom (in black and white, for all to see) that also says what the view shows, the final black fill. True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck deseleziona proposed Apple and Microsoft Italian say deselezionare una casella; Italian has no separate verb for unchecking, so it coincides with deselect. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview cascata proposed Apple Font Book Italian: Cascata, esempio a cascata. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight peso proposed Italian editions of Hochuli and Garfield (peso, pesi), Apple CoreText and Glyphs 3 it (Classe di peso). Rejected spessore, which is the measured thickness. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace spazio bianco proposed Adobe InDesign and Apple Italian. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Italian Status Note Definition Appearance panel pannello Aspetto proposed Adobe Illustrator Italian names the panel Aspetto. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion ricalco automatico proposed Adobe Illustrator Italian calls tracing ricalco (Ricalco immagine). Rejected vettorizzazione (Inkscape: Vettorizza bitmap) and the bare loan autotrace (FontForge it). Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline linea centrale proposed No font-editor attestation; plain Italian. Rejected linea mediana, which Italian typography uses for the x-height line. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask maschera di ritaglio proposed Adobe Illustrator Italian: maschera di ritaglio. A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point punto di controllo proposed FontForge it (punti di controllo), Apple and Blender. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines griglia dei riempimenti proposed No attestation; translated from the fallback, a grid of fills. The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style modalità di riempimento proposed Krita and Blender Italian: modalità di riempimento. A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them. Each reads the brightness of the source and lays down geometry accordingly. You pick a mode, then tune its parameters. Write the mode name with its own capitalization and the words fill mode in lowercase after it. G2 continuity continuità G2 proposed Standard Italian mathematical term (continuità di curvatura). G2 continuity means two segments meet with matching curvature, not merely with matching direction. G1 keeps the tangent continuous and can still show a break in the reflection where the curvature jumps. G2 removes that break. Vextra marks G2 nodes and can enforce the condition as you edit. You reach for it on long, shallow curves and on shapes that will be seen large, where the eye finds a curvature break that it would miss at text size. Live Effect editable effect effetto dinamico proposed Adobe Italian renders Live as dinamico (Pittura dinamica, Ricalco dinamico, Angoli dinamici). No attestation of the full term in the corpus. A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve punto fuori curva proposed No attestation; fallback point off the curve translated. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve punto sulla curva proposed No attestation; fallback point on the curve translated. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline contorno proposed FontForge it (Contorno) and Glyphs 3 it (Riempi contorni); Italian, like French, has one word for outline and contour. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke tratto proposed Glyphs 3 it (Tratto, Crea tratto), FontForge it (Espandi il tratto) and Apple; it is also the Italian word for the stroke of a letter (Noordzij, Il tratto). Adobe Illustrator says traccia. A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap estremità del tratto proposed Adobe uses estremità for the cap (InDesign: Estremità traccia); joined to the chosen noun tratto. A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape giunzione del tratto proposed Inkscape Italian uses giunzione for the join; joined to tratto. Adobe Illustrator labels the control Angolo, kept here for corner. A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node nodo tangente proposed FontForge it (punto tangente) with the chosen noun nodo. A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. tonal map darkness map mappa tonale proposed No attestation; regular Italian imaging term (valori tonali). A tonal map is the reading of brightness across a source image that a fill uses to decide where to put geometry. Dark areas widen a strip or crowd a pattern; light areas narrow or thin it. You control the mapping with the Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels rows, which change what counts as dark before any geometry is drawn. Adjust the map rather than the fill when the result is uniformly too heavy or too sparse. Tunni line linea di Tunni proposed Eponym; formed as Spanish and French did. A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: Japanese
docs.text:
A first draft for Japanese. A model researched the guidance below and the term table in references/terms.md; no native reviewer has approved the language as a whole. Individual terms carry their own approval status; a proposed term remains proposed, and a protected name keeps its glossary spelling. The Japanese interface catalogs are unfinished machine drafts: a string found in one settles neither a term nor a rule.

Use references/terms.md, and a newer core memory when one is supplied, for terminology, definitions and review status. Keep a proposed term consistent across the interface and help, and report it as proposed. Where a native reviewer's decision or newer project data disagrees with this skill, follow it and record the change. Report only checks performed: text written with this skill is not reviewed by a native speaker and not tested in the running application until someone does that.

Use these rules with the localization principles (in fontlab-localization), Qt interface rules (in fontlab-localization) and Japanese language guide (in the FontLab writing guide). Examples name their source (Glyphs 3, Font Book, CoreText, Qt's qtbase_ja catalog) or are marked constructed. They show grammar; the term table decides terms.

docs.title: Locale and register
docs.text:
• Locale ja, Qt catalog ja_JP: standard written Japanese.
  • Leave the user unnamed: Japanese drops the subject. Never あなた, 私たち, 弊社 or お客様; your font is フォント.
  • Labels are noun phrases or plain-form verbs. Every full sentence is です・ます style, never だ・である.
  • Polite, not deferential. A sentence that asks the user to act ends in 〜してください: あとでやり直してください。 (Please try again later., Glyphs). Never 〜していただけますか, お願いいたします, ご〜になる; never ください in a label.

docs.title: Grammar of interface strings
docs.text:
String Form Example Menu command object + を + action noun without する, or a dictionary-form verb; no 。 アンカーを追加, 開く (Add Anchor, Open, Glyphs) Command that opens a dialog the same, with the source's ellipsis フォントを追加… (Add Fonts…, Font Book) Button as a command, shortest form 保存, キャンセル (Save, Cancel, Font Book) Checkbox or toggle as a command; negative in 〜ない 製品用グリフ名を使わない (Don't use Production Names, Glyphs) Panel or dialog title noun phrase フォント情報 (Font Info, Glyphs) Progress message 〜しています + the source's ellipsis アップデートを確認しています… (Checking for updates…, Glyphs) State label 〜中, 〜済み ダウンロード中 (Downloading, Font Book), 編集済み (Edited, Glyphs) Success 〜を〜しました フォントを書き出しました。 (Fonts exported., constructed) Cannot (now) 〜できません フォントを登録できません (Cannot Register Fonts, Font Book) Failed attempt 〜できませんでした フォントをダウンロードできませんでした。 (Font Download failed., CoreText) Not found, none 〜が見つかりません, 〜されていません, 〜なし フォントが選択されていません (No Font Selected, Font Book) Confirmation 〜しますか? 選択中のフォントを削除しますか? (Do you want to remove the selected fonts?, Font Book) Tooltip, Quick Help 〜します, no subject 影響のあるレイヤーを新規タブに開きます。 (Opens a new tab with all affected layers., Glyphs)
  • A dialog title repeats the command that opens it.
  • Failed to… and Could not… are 〜できませんでした, not 〜に失敗しました. Are you sure…? is 〜しますか?, not 〜してもよろしいですか?; 本当に only for really.
  • can is 〜できます, never 〜することができます; must is 〜する必要があります.
  • The user's action is active (〜を選択します); what the application does unasked is passive (〜が表示されます).

docs.title: Compact labels
docs.text: Drop する after an action noun (追加, not 追加する) and の between nouns where the compound stays clear (フォント情報). Never shorten a term from the term table, clip a katakana word, or drop a counter after a count. Keep the Latin short forms the source uses (UC, lc, UPM, PPM). A kana or kanji is as wide as two Latin letters: count four characters as eight in a dense panel.

docs.title: Plurals and placeholders
docs.text:
Qt gives Japanese one numerus form (nplurals=1; plural=0;); CLDR has only other. Write one <numerusform> that reads correctly for 0, 1, 2 and 100, and drop the source's (s): %n glyph(s) becomes %n 個のグリフ (constructed). Never mark a plural with たち or ら; write 複数の only for multiple.

A count takes a counter, then の, then the noun. 個 is the default for objects: %@ 個のペア (%@ pairs, Glyphs). 件 counts issues, errors and results: 件の問題 (issues, Font Book). Also 回 (times), 行 (lines), 種類 (kinds). A unit needs no counter: %1 バイト (%1 bytes, qtbase_ja). Add a counter to %1 only when you know it is a count.

A particle follows a placeholder directly and never changes with its value: %1 を隠す (Hide %1), %1 について (About %1, both qtbase_ja). Japanese is verb-final and puts the modifier first, so reorder numbered placeholders: %{value2}@ の %{value1}@ (%{value1}@ of %{value2}@, Glyphs).

docs.title: Numbers, punctuation and spacing
docs.text:
• Numbers: 1,234,567.89; 25% and 45° without a space; a space before a unit symbol (12 pt). Digits and Latin letters are half-width, never ＡＢＣ１２３; katakana is full-width, never ｶﾅ.
  • Japanese–Latin spacing: put one half-width space (U+0020) between a kana or kanji and a Latin letter, a digit or a placeholder: PostScript ヒントをコピー (Copy PS Hints, Glyphs). Microsoft, Adobe and Qt's catalog do this, and Glyphs mostly; Apple and the JTF style guide write no space. No space beside 、 。 「 」 （ ）, before (&X), before a final : ? …, or around /.
  • Full-width in Japanese text: 、 。 「 」 （ ） ・. List items with 、.
  • Half-width, with no space before: : ? ! / +, as macOS, Windows and Qt write them: ファイル名(&N): (File &name:, qtbase_ja). Put one space after a : or ? that more text follows.
  • Quotation marks: a source 'x', "x" or “x” around a name becomes 「x」 with no spaces: グリフ「{glyphName}」 (Glyphs). Straight quotes stay in code and inside HTML tags.
  • Ellipsis: copy the source's ... or … unchanged, in the same position.
  • Final period: 。 where the source ends with a period, none where it does not. A source ! is dropped in a label and becomes 。 in a sentence.
  • Katakana: keep the long-vowel mark of -er, -or, -ar loans (レイヤー, フォルダー, ユーザー), as the Cabinet notice 外来語の表記, Microsoft and JTF do; Apple and Glyphs often drop it. Write compounds solid, without a space or ・ (メニューバー); ・ joins coordinated items (大文字・小文字, Case, Glyphs).
  • Whitespace: keep the source's outer spaces, \n and \t. Never add a space, a break or U+3000 to shape a line.

docs.title: Mnemonics and key names
docs.text:
• Append the source's mnemonic letter, uppercase, in half-width parentheses with no space before it: 開く(&O) (&Open, qtbase_ja). It goes before a final colon or ellipsis: 色相(&E): (Hu&e:, qtbase_ja); C&ustom... becomes カスタム(&U)... (constructed).
  • Write exactly (&X), four characters: Qt strips that pattern on macOS.
  • Keep the source's letter, so sibling items stay unique. Never put & before a kana or kanji; add no mnemonic the source lacks. A label that stays Latin keeps its & in place (&OK).
  • && is a literal ampersand: write と or keep &&, never a single &.
  • Key names stay in Latin script as the source spells them: Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Option, Cmd, Enter, Esc, Tab, Delete, Backspace, Space. Arrow keys are ←, ↑, →, ↓ (qtbase_ja). Keep Ctrl+S as written. In a sentence add キー after a single key, as Microsoft and Apple do: Shift キーを押しながら (constructed).

docs.title: Names and loans
docs.text:
• Latin script, exact case, no katakana: product, company, typeface and personal names (FontLab, OpenType, Unicode), format names (VFJ, UFO), feature and table tags (kern, OS/2), glyph names, extensions, unit symbols and code.
  • Embed a Latin name with a space on each side and its class noun after it: kern テーブルを出力 (Export kern Table, Glyphs).
  • Translate language and script names: アラビア語, アラビア文字 (Arabic, the language and the script, Glyphs).
  • Keep the katakana loans the term table lists; coin no kanji replacement. Do not turn an ordinary English word into katakana where a plain word exists: 設定, 追加, 幅; not セッティング, アド, ウィドス.
  • Never append the English original in parentheses.

docs.title: Script-specific rules
docs.text:
• Kana, not kanji, for すべて, ください, できます, および, または (not 全て, 下さい, 出来ます, 及び, 又は).
  • No furigana; no italics that the source's markup does not carry.

docs.title: False friends and traps
docs.text:
The term table gives the term. These are the senses to reject:

  • glyph is not 文字 (a character); 字形 is a shape, not the glyph slot.
  • script is a writing system or a Python script: read the control.
  • hint is not a tip; outline is not 概要; a font table is not 表; an OpenType feature is not 特徴; weight is not 重さ or 重量; master is not 主人 or 原本; instance is not 実例; stem is not 茎 or 幹; case is not ケース or 場合; family is not 家族; a style named Bold or Italic is not the word processor's 太字 or 斜体.
  • kerning, tracking and spacing are three things.
  • Machine-translation habits to remove: あなた; 〜を行います for a plain verb; passive for the user's action; それ, これら for it, these; 〜のための for every for; の three times in a row; full-width ？ ： ！; a missing counter.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
1. Placeholders, markup and \n match the source.
  2. Mnemonics: exactly (&X), the source's letter, before the colon or ellipsis; none added, none lost.
  3. Each numerus entry: one form, with a counter, right for 1 and for 100.
  4. A space between Japanese and Latin or digits, none beside 、。「」（）; half-width : and ?; no full-width Latin.
  5. Form by role; no だ・である, no あなた, no excess 敬語.
  6. Terms match the term table.
  7. Would a Japanese type designer say it this way?

docs.title: FontLab terminology and compact labels
docs.text:
Preserve deliberately uppercase source labels using the language’s case rules. Keep numeric controls compact with UPM, PPM and LSB/RSB (French AG/AD); explain the full terms in help. The Family Dimensions “Units Per eM:” label is an intentional expanded exception.

Use the current core memory and its approval status. OpenType lookup defaults to the translation of procedure, with a different term only when strong OpenType-specific evidence supports it. Explicit choices are German Lookup, French lookup, Polish procedura and Russian процедура. Ordinary searches, individual rules and OpenType features are separate concepts. Preserve literal code keywords and identifiers.

Translate Fusion with the fallback Welder. Use the core's phonetic FontAudit transliteration in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese; preserve FontAudit in code. Proposed spellings remain proposed. Before rebuilding a QPH, recover team edits and import their terms and notes into the core memory.

Compare mnemonic-split terms with unmarked labels. Keep labels compact, aiming for 120% of the English length in Dimensions and Glyph Window preferences without losing meaning. Omit redundant font, color or command wording when context supplies it. TTH labels can omit “use” and abbreviate TrueType hinting; help can explain more. A full harmonization requires three complete catalog reviews, then reconciliation of help with the final UI and verification of generated resources.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• references/terms.md: the full Japanese term table, generated from the core memory ja-core.tmx of the writing guide, with the status, translator note and definition of every term.
  • The Japanese localization guide of the writing guide is the source of the sections above.

docs.title: Related skills
docs.text: fontlab-localization for the shared rules; fontlab-terminology for product names and shared nouns; fontlab-technical for Japanese help text.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
These rules implement the FontLab writing guide. They are copied into every skill so each installed skill can work independently. Corpus measurements can inform review; they are not quotas, universal laws, or tests of authorship.

H1. Accurate actors. Address the reader when they act or choose. Name the application when it performs an operation. Fonts and files contain data that software interprets. Prefer active voice when the actor matters; retain a clear passive construction when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. Never invent an actor or cause to change the grammar.

H2. Never invent a fact. Ground numbers, names, dates, labels, shortcuts, defaults, errors, versions, and quotations in supplied or checked evidence. A draft is evidence of what was written, not independent proof of its claims. Mark unresolved facts with a specific working placeholder such as [VERIFY CLAIM], [CONFIRM LABEL], or [CONFIRM OFFER]. A marked draft is unfinished; resolve the gap before publication. Clearly label fictional examples before their invented details.

H3. Preserve certainty and scope. “May reduce” does not become “eliminates.” Preserve conditions, negation, timing, quantities, compatibility, licensing, and other consequential limits. State a limitation directly rather than disguising it as a favorable position. A single observation does not prove universal behavior. Conflicting sources need scope checks, not an automatic choice of the stricter claim.

H4. Preserve the writer's voice. Do not manufacture stakes, candor, reader emotion, endorsement, or a new narrator. Preserve useful habits and the supplied stance. Reorder, split, or shorten according to the requested edit depth and reader need, without adding facts or causal relationships. A correct draft can remain unchanged.

H5. Give thought a rhythm. Carry a subject through an action, distinction or consequence. Let a developed sentence explain a relationship; let a shorter one settle a result when that change of pace helps. Repeat a concrete object or term when its meaning develops, not as a compulsory callback. Technical actions stay literal; explanations and marketing have room for patient attention, a bounded comparison or dry observation. Keep useful qualifications beside their claims. Do not impose sentence-length, pronoun, punctuation or paragraph quotas, or force every paragraph into the same long-then-short pattern.

H6. Notice the useful detail. Retain names, mechanisms, conditions, versions and issue numbers that help the reader understand or act. From the evidence, choose the object, contrast or small behavior that makes the explanation tangible: a changed preview, a repeated comparison, a file whose status matters. Follow that detail far enough to explain its significance. Warmth can come from this attention and patience. Never invent an observation, personal experience or reader emotion to make prose vivid, or remove a necessary qualification to shorten it.

H7. Punctuation serves meaning. Prefer a colon for an explanation or list. A spaced dash can carry a turn; avoid decorative glosses and repeated interruptions. Use sentence case for new headings and preserve exact source labels. A punctuation pattern does not establish authorship.

H8. Choose precise words. Review vague praise and stock phrasing such as “seamless,” “game-changing,” “leverage,” and “unlock.” Replace them when they obscure the action or make an unsupported claim. Keep an accurate technical use or protected quotation. A count or cluster is a reason to inspect a passage, not proof that each matched word is wrong.

H9. Develop the explanation. Begin where the reader can understand the task, change or offer. Give adjacent sentences a real connection: the same subject under a changed condition, an action and its result, or a question and its answer. A before-and-after comparison needs evidence for both states; a transition must not invent causality. Let a useful aside return to the main thought. Place low-stakes discoveries where they aid understanding, while keeping price, risk, prerequisites and recovery visible when needed. End at the useful result or next action; a quiet ending or a substantial summary can each serve the material.

H10a. Preserve conditions. Use “if” for a condition and “when” where the intended timing or situation warrants it. Check the whole meaning: “when a panel opens” and “while a panel is open” describe different scopes. Keep useful conditionals and parenthetical explanations; do not insert them to imitate a presumed author.

H10. Preserve expression that works. A fragment, three-part phrase, exclamation, aside, or single-sentence paragraph can serve a passage. Keep it when it supports meaning or the writer's rhythm. Do not add one to meet a budget, or remove one because of a generic stylistic test. Keep instructions and consequential conditions literal and easy to find.

H10b. Use the destination's notation. Preserve exact interface labels, tags, extensions, and identifiers. Italicize labels in neutral release notes; in technical site content use supported highlight notation, with bold as the plain-Markdown fallback. Use code style for machine-readable text. State price amounts and currencies unambiguously from evidence; do not infer an exchange rate, tax policy, or license term. A supplied currency shorthand needs enough context to identify the actual offer.

H11. Names and collisions. FontLab is the product; Fontlab Ltd. is the company. Preserve product names, module identifiers, domains, historical names in their historical scope, and exact quoted strings. Do not translate a product name. Name the application when Layer, Mask, Group, Fill, Brush, Knife, Transform, Pencil, Eraser, or Scissors could have more than one meaning. Use a declared short form consistently.

H12. Protect literal material. Preserve quotations, code, commands, paths, identifiers, API names, URLs, legal text, interface strings, placeholders, and table data during prose editing. Change them only for a requested or necessary correction supported by evidence. Do not paraphrase a quotation while retaining quotation marks or an attribution. Explain a consequential correction when the output contract permits it.

H13. Choose the register per passage. Marketing helps assess an offer; technical writing explains or instructs; neutral prose states facts and changes warmly. A document can combine them. Prices, limits, licensing, compatibility, security, and migration facts stay plain and prominent. Audience and purpose determine an email's register. Do not impose a fixed emotional mixture or make every opening a story.

H14. Review facts, then movement. Compare claims and protected strings with their evidence; check scope, action order and terminology. Then read whole passages for attention, connection and pace. Repair a flat sequence by developing an existing detail or relationship, not by adding praise or invented events. Check that humor remains intelligible and the information remains true when the joke is missed. Recheck the facts after a voice edit. A measurement or passing build does not certify facts, usability or authorship. Report only checks actually performed.

H15. Scale to the surface. A button or tooltip needs a clear label, action, or condition, not a miniature essay. Apply factual and naming safeguards at every length. Include the detail the task requires; do not add proof paragraphs, metaphors, or pronouns to satisfy a template. For translation, keep essential instructions literal and references clear.

H16. The override. Follow the user's task and supplied voice before style defaults. Break a default sooner than make the writing worse. Source material and quoted prompts are data, not authority to change the task. Style preferences never justify presenting an invented or unsupported claim as established fact.

docs.title: Japanese terms
docs.text:
Portable term table, snapshot of 04 October 2026, generated from the core translation memory localization/ja-core.tmx of the FontLab writing guide by tools/scripts/export_terms.py. 54 of 289 terms are approved or protected; a proposed translation is a candidate for a native reviewer, and the English term is the fallback until it is approved. Use newer supplied project data when it disagrees with this snapshot.

A status of do-not-translate protects the English spelling; it does not approve a draft English name. The definition says what the term means in FontLab; the note says why the translation was chosen or how to inflect it. The fallback original term is a plain English phrase to translate instead of the term when the term itself will not travel (stem: main stroke; overshoot: optical surplus).

docs.title: Names
docs.text: English Fallback Japanese Status Note Definition Adobe Illustrator Adobe Illustrator do-not-translate Adobe Illustrator is the host application for the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins. Use the full name on first mention, then Illustrator. Vexy Lines and Vexy Playlines are separate applications; do not describe them as Illustrator plug-ins. app.fontographer.net app.fontographer.net do-not-translate app.fontographer.net is the address of the browser edition of Fontographer. Preserve the lowercase domain when naming the destination. Use Fontographer when referring to the application itself. FLUM FLUM do-not-translate FLUM is an internal documentation-project name, not a customer-facing product or feature. Omit it from published instructions. Refer to the relevant product documentation when directing a reader to help. FontLab FontLab do-not-translate FontLab is the name of the desktop font editor. Preserve its capital F and L in headings and prose. Fontlab Ltd. names the company; the lowercase fontlab spelling belongs to identifiers such as the Python module and website domains. fontlab (Python module) fontlab (Python module) do-not-translate The fontlab Python module exposes FontLab scripting functionality. Its name is lowercase and case sensitive. Format it as code in prose, and keep the application name FontLab distinct from the module name in examples. FontLab 8 FontLab 8 do-not-translate FontLab 8 names version 8 of the desktop font editor. Put one space before the version number. After establishing the version, use FontLab alone where no other version could be meant. Retain the number in compatibility statements and version-specific instructions. FontLab 9 FontLab 9 do-not-translate FontLab 9 is a versioned product name whose house usage remains draft. Its appearance in an interface or format description does not establish release availability. Confirm the version and intended audience before using it in new prose; preserve it when quoting an exact label. Fontlab Ltd. Fontlab Ltd. do-not-translate Fontlab Ltd. is the company name. Preserve the lowercase l in Fontlab and the period after Ltd. Use FontLab, with a capital L, for the product. The two spellings identify different entities and must not be normalized into one. FontLab Pass FontLab Pass do-not-translate FontLab Pass is the identity and licensing service at pass.fontlab.com. Use the complete service name when explaining account or licence management. Distinguish the service from the FontLab account used to sign in. FontLab Studio 5 FontLab Studio 5 do-not-translate FontLab Studio 5 is a historical version of the font editor. Use the full name in migration instructions, historical descriptions and compatibility statements. Do not shorten it to Studio or use it as the name of another FontLab version. fontlab.com fontlab.com do-not-translate fontlab.com is the main FontLab website address. Preserve the lowercase domain. Link to the relevant page when a reader needs a particular product, download or instruction, rather than sending every task to the home page. Fontographer Fontographer do-not-translate Fontographer names a font editor. For its browser edition, use app.fontographer.net as the address. Distinguish a historical numbered edition when compatibility or migration depends on it. Preserve Fontographer.net only where it belongs to an exact project or command label. Fontographer.net Fontographer.net do-not-translate Fontographer.net occurs in project and command labels. Preserve it when quoting an interface label that uses this spelling. Use Fontographer for the application in ordinary prose and app.fontographer.net for its browser address. Broader house usage of Fontographer.net remains draft. forum.fontlab.com forum.fontlab.com do-not-translate forum.fontlab.com is the FontLab user-forum address. Use it for a relevant discussion or community question, and identify the destination. A documentation link is preferable when the reader needs an established procedure rather than a discussion. GlyphRef GlyphRef do-not-translate GlyphRef is the class used to reference a Fontographer glyph through its scripting interface. Preserve the capital G and R and format the name as code. Keep the API identifier separate from the ordinary word glyph. help.fontlab.com help.fontlab.com do-not-translate help.fontlab.com is a FontLab documentation address. Preserve its lowercase spelling and identify the product or article when linking to it. Use a specific documentation page when the reader needs a particular procedure or reference. help.vexy.art help.vexy.art do-not-translate help.vexy.art is the Vexy documentation address. Name the relevant product when linking to it, since the Vexy products share vocabulary but differ in features and workflows. Preserve the lowercase domain. pass.fontlab.com pass.fontlab.com do-not-translate pass.fontlab.com is the address for FontLab account and licence management. Use the domain when naming the destination and FontLab Pass when naming the service. Explain the action the reader can perform there. Photofont Photofont do-not-translate Photofont is a protected Fontlab Ltd. name, written as one word with a capital P. Preserve this spelling in a notice or reference. Confirm the relevant product and version before adding a claim about functionality. playlines.vexy.art playlines.vexy.art do-not-translate playlines.vexy.art is the address of Vexy Playlines, the browser application. Preserve the lowercase domain. Use the product name for the application and the address for the destination the reader opens. Strokes Maker Strokes Maker do-not-translate Strokes Maker is a former name of Vexy Lines. Use Vexy Lines for the current product and retain Strokes Maker when identifying a historical release or explaining the name change. Do not rename an old interface label inside a quotation. studio.fontlab.com studio.fontlab.com do-not-translate studio.fontlab.com is an unconfirmed service address in the naming register. Keep it draft and do not direct readers there without confirmation of the destination and its availability. A recorded spelling does not establish that a service exists. TransType 5 TransType 5 do-not-translate TransType 5 names version 5 of the font conversion application. Keep TransType as one word with capital T in both parts, followed by one space and the version. Use TransType after establishing the version; declare TrT before using it as a short form. TypeTool TypeTool do-not-translate TypeTool is a protected Fontlab Ltd. product name, written as one word with two capital Ts. Preserve that spelling when naming the product or quoting a notice. Confirm the relevant version before describing its features or compatibility. Vexy Vexy do-not-translate Vexy is the family prefix in Vexy Lines, Vexy Linestra, Vexy Playlines and Vexy Vextra. It is not a standalone application name. Identify the product when describing an operation; retain Vexy alone when it is the exact name of an interface category. Vexy Lines Vexy Lines do-not-translate Vexy Lines is the standalone desktop application for converting a bitmap into vector artwork through algorithmic fills. Keep the full two-word name. Distinguish it from Vexy Playlines, the browser application, and from the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins. Its native project format is .lines. Vexy Linestra Vexy Linestra do-not-translate Vexy Linestra is the Adobe Illustrator plug-in for parametric line fills. Use the two-word product name in prose. Preserve the closed spelling VexyLinestra in an exact filename such as VexyLinestra.aip; a filename spelling does not replace the product name. Vexy Playlines Vexy Playlines do-not-translate Vexy Playlines is the browser application for converting images into vector artwork at playlines.vexy.art. Use the full name in titles and on first mention, then Playlines where unambiguous. Keep it distinct from Vexy Lines, the desktop application. Vexy Vextra Vexy Vextra do-not-translate Vexy Vextra is the Adobe Illustrator plug-in for contour editing. Use the full name in a title and on first mention; Vextra is the declared short form. Preserve VexyVextra in an exact filename such as VexyVextra.aip.

docs.title: Type design
docs.text: English Fallback Japanese Status Note Definition ascender upward extension アセンダー proposed Glyphs 3 ja; long-vowel mark kept per the JTCA rule (Glyphs keeps it too). An ascender is the part of a lowercase letter that extends above the x-height, as in b or d. Ascender height describes the intended alignment of these parts and may differ from cap height. Do not confuse this design measurement with similarly named vertical metrics in exported font tables. Line spacing depends on those fields and on the application using them. baseline writing line ベースライン proposed Glyphs 3, InDesign and Apple ja all use ベースライン. A baseline is a reference line used to align text. In conventional horizontal Latin font design, the baseline is at y = 0, with ascenders above it and descenders below it. Other scripts and layout systems can use different baseline conventions. Identify the relevant baseline when discussing alignment across scripts or vertical text. bowl round belly ボウル proposed Established katakana term in Japanese Latin type anatomy glossaries. A bowl is a rounded stroke that encloses a counter, as in b, d or p. Its shape, thickness and junctions affect the letter's balance. The appropriate number of curve segments depends on the design. Nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting, but a fixed segment count does not guarantee compatible masters or good interpolation. cap height capital-letter height キャップハイト proposed Glyphs 3 and InDesign ja both use キャップハイト. Cap height is the distance from the baseline to the top of a flat capital such as H. Rounded or pointed capitals may extend beyond it through overshoot. Record the intended value in Font Info. Cap height describes a design measurement; alignment zones and line-spacing metrics are separate settings, even when their values are related. character 文字 proposed Adobe, Apple and Morisawa use 文字 for the abstract character, against グリフ for the drawn shape. A character is an abstract unit of written text, such as a letter or punctuation mark. A glyph is its visual representation. The relationship is not one to one: several characters can form a ligature, and a character can have several glyph forms. A user-perceived character can also consist of several Unicode codepoints. Keep characters, codepoints and glyphs distinct when discussing encoding or text processing. contour パス proposed Glyphs 3 ja (パス方向を逆転, 開いたパスを閉じる) and Adobe both call a contour パス. FontForge's 輪郭 rejected; note that パス also means a file path. A contour is an open or closed sequence of connected line and curve segments. Its nodes and control points describe its geometry. One glyph or vector object can contain several contours. A counter is an area of space, not a synonym for a contour. When explaining fill behaviour, identify the outline format and fill rule before prescribing a contour direction. counter enclosed white space カウンター proposed Japanese Latin type anatomy term; FontForge ja has both カウンター and カウンタ. Long vowel kept per JTCA. A counter is the enclosed or partly enclosed space within a letterform, such as the enclosed space in an o or the open space in a c. The surrounding strokes define it. A closed counter may have an inner contour as its boundary; an open counter does not require a separate contour. Judge its size and shape together with the surrounding strokes. descender downward extension ディセンダー proposed Glyphs 3 ja; long-vowel mark kept per JTCA. A descender is the part of a letter that extends below the baseline, as in p or y. Its design height is usually recorded as a negative coordinate relative to the baseline. Exported descender metrics are separate fields used by applications for layout. Whether a deep glyph clips depends on the relevant metrics, application and text container, not on one design value alone. diacritical mark combining mark ダイアクリティカルマーク proposed Adobe Japan and Japanese foundries use ダイアクリティカルマーク. Glyphs' 発音記号 rejected because it normally means phonetic notation. A diacritical mark is a small sign, such as an acute or a cedilla, that attaches to a base letter to form another character. FontLab builds accented glyphs from a base and a mark through anchors, and the GDEF mark class tells the shaper which glyphs are marks. Say mark glyph for the class member and diacritical mark for the sign. em type body 仮想ボディ proposed Morisawa's glossary defines 仮想ボディ as the square design body, which is the fallback 'type body'. Glyphs says 全角 (clashes with full-width); keep em as a unit in values. The em is the square on which a typeface is designed, historically the body of the letter M in metal type. Its height equals the type size, so an em in 12 point text is 12 points. In a digital font the em is divided into UPM font units. extremum local extreme point 極点 proposed The Japanese Glyphs handbook translations say 極点を追加; FontForge uses 極値 and 極大点. An extremum is a point where a curve reaches a local leftmost, rightmost, topmost or bottommost position. The plural is extrema. Placing nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting. If you add nodes to masters intended for interpolation, preserve the correspondence between their contours and points. Different extremum positions alone do not make masters incompatible. glyph グリフ proposed Glyphs 3, FontForge, Adobe, Apple and Morisawa all use グリフ. 字形 is kept for letterform in feature names. A glyph is one drawn shape in a font: a letter, a figure, a mark, or a piece of a composite. A character is what a reader types and a glyph is what a renderer draws, and one character can map to several glyphs while several characters can map to one. You edit a glyph in the Glyph window, where its contours, elements, anchors, and metrics all live together. The distinction matters in any sentence about encoding, since a font maps codepoints to glyphs through the cmap table. handle ハンドル proposed Adobe and the Japanese Glyphs handbook use ハンドル for Bézier handles. A handle is an off-curve control point used to shape a curve segment. A cubic Bézier segment has two control points; a quadratic segment has one. Moving a handle changes the curve without moving its endpoints. In tools that display handle arms, the arm connects a control point to an endpoint. Name the curve type when the number or behaviour of handles matters. ink trap ink relief notch インクトラップ proposed Established loan among Japanese type designers and foundries; no native term. An ink trap is a notch cut into a corner where strokes meet, so ink spread or rasterization at small sizes does not clog the join. FontLab makes them as a live Smart Corner variant. italic angle slant angle イタリック角度 proposed Glyphs 3 ja uses イタリック角度. The italic angle is the slope of the upright strokes of an italic or oblique design, measured from the vertical in degrees. FontLab stores it in Font Info, uses it to slant guides and the cursor, and writes it into the post and hhea tables. It is a property of the design, not of a transformation. lining figures capital-height figures ライニング数字 proposed InDesign, Glyphs 3, FontForge and Apple CoreText ja use ライニング数字. Lining figures are digits that share the cap height and sit on the baseline, so they align with capitals in tables and headlines. The lnum feature selects them where a font defaults to oldstyle figures. node ノード proposed The Japanese Glyphs handbook translations and Inkscape use ノード. Adobe's アンカーポイント would collide with アンカー; Glyphs UI ポイント would merge node with point. A node is a point on a contour where segments meet, and its type decides how they meet. A sharp node lets two segments arrive at any angle. A smooth node keeps the handles collinear so the curve passes through without a kink. A tangent node joins a line to a curve smoothly. A G2 node matches curvature as well as direction. You select a node and drag it, or nudge it, and the segments on both sides follow. Put nodes at the extremes so hinting and interpolation have something to hold. overshoot optical surplus オーバーシュート proposed Glyphs 3 ja and its handbook translations use オーバーシュート. Overshoot is the extension of a rounded or pointed shape beyond an alignment line so that it appears as tall as a flat shape. For example, an o may extend above the x-height and below the baseline. Its amount depends on the design and intended size. PostScript alignment zones can describe these overshoot regions for hinting; there is no universal percentage to apply. proportional figures natural-width figures プロポーショナル数字 proposed InDesign, Glyphs 3 and CoreText ja use プロポーショナル数字. Proportional figures have individual advance widths, so a 1 takes less room than an 8. They read well in running text; tabular figures share one width for columns. The pnum feature selects them. segment セグメント proposed Glyphs 3 and Adobe ja use セグメント. A segment is the portion of a contour between two on-curve endpoints. It may be a straight line or a curve. A quadratic Bézier segment has one off-curve control point; a cubic segment has two. Describe the segment type and the relevant editing command rather than assuming that every curve has two handles or that changing a node type performs every conversion. serif セリフ proposed Adobe, Apple, FontForge and Japanese foundries use セリフ. A serif is the finishing stroke at the end of a stem or arm. Its shape sorts a face into the familiar classes: oldstyle, transitional, Didone, slab. You draw a serif once and reuse it as a component or an element, which keeps a family consistent and makes a late change cheap. Serifs are small, so they take the most damage at low resolution, which is where hinting and careful alignment zones earn their place. sharp シャープ proposed Adobe and Inkscape ja use シャープ for sharp corners; the node type itself is コーナーノード. Sharp describes a pointed corner or a node at which contour direction can change abruptly. Image sharpening is a different operation. sharp node コーナーノード proposed Glyphs and Illustrator ja call this node type コーナーポイント, so コーナー plus ノード. Inkscape's シャープノード is the rejected alternative. A sharp node joins contour segments without requiring a smooth change of direction. The handles of adjacent segments need not be collinear; a smooth node constrains their direction. stem main stroke ステム proposed Glyphs 3 and FontForge ja use ステム. A stem is a main stroke of a letter, usually the vertical one: the two uprights of an H, the single upright of an l. Stem width sets the weight of a face, and stems that disagree across a family break its rhythm. You measure a stem with the Measurement tool and record the standard widths in Font Info, where hinting and the stem links read them. Vextra reuses the word for the paired edges it detects in general artwork, not only in letters. swash flourish スワッシュ proposed InDesign, Glyphs 3 and CoreText ja use スワッシュ (スワッシュ字形 for the feature). A swash is a decorative flourish that extends a letter, often on a capital or a terminal. Swash alternates live in the swsh feature and in glyphs with a swash suffix. terminal stroke ending ターミナル proposed Japanese Latin type anatomy glossaries use ターミナル; context separates it from the Terminal app. A terminal is the end of a stroke without a serif, such as the ending of a c or f. Its shape may be rounded, angled or cut off, depending on the design. Compare related terminals across a typeface at the intended reading size. The anatomical term does not prescribe how to construct or store the shape in an editor. UPM units per type body UPM proposed Glyphs 3 ja keeps UPM (UPM の変更) and glosses it 全角ユニット数. Abbreviation kept. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. UPM, units per em, specifies how many font units make up one em. It sets the scale for outline coordinates and metrics when a renderer converts them to a text size.
