FontLab can add them on export. right sidebearing 오른쪽 사이드베어링 proposed Glyphs 3 spells out RSB as 오른쪽 사이드 베어링; written with the closed 사이드베어링. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the right edge of a glyph outline and the end of its advance width. It contributes to spacing. sidebearing side space 사이드베어링 proposed KST dictionary headword; Glyphs 3 and Korean foundry writing (RixFont) use 사이드베어링. FontForge's 측면 베어링 is rejected. A sidebearing is the space between a glyph's outline and the edge of its advance width: the left sidebearing before the shape, the right sidebearing after it. Together with the advance width it sets how the glyph spaces against every other glyph, which is the work that carries a text face further than kerning does. You edit sidebearings in the Metrics panel or with the Metrics tool, one glyph at a time or across a selection, and you check them in a word rather than in isolation. size 크기 proposed Universal platform wording. The size of an object or the chosen size of displayed text. Name a specific width or height when only one direction is intended. spacing 글자사이 proposed KST dictionary headword for the space between letters (자간 redirects to it), and 글립스 타입 디자인 (Noh Eunyou, Ham Minjoo) titles its spacing chapters 글자 사이. Glyphs 3's UI loan 스페이싱 is the alternative. Only for letter spacing; other spacing is 간격. The adjustment of glyph advance widths and sidebearings to establish the space between letters. Kerning makes additional adjustments to particular pairs. standard stem reference stem width 표준 줄기 proposed Derived from 줄기; no attestation. Standard stems are the representative horizontal and vertical stem widths declared in a font for hinting. The rasterizer snaps stems near those widths to the same pixel count, so like stems stay alike at small sizes. stem link stem tie 줄기 링크 proposed Derived from 줄기; 링크 as the noun for a hinting link. No attestation. A stem link ties two edges of a stroke together as a stem, so hinting can hold their distance as the size changes. A vertical link governs a horizontal measurement and a horizontal link governs a vertical one. You add links in the glyph, either by hand or from an autohinting pass, and you keep them consistent with the standard stem widths declared in Font Info. Vextra reuses the term for the paired edges it detects in artwork that is not type. styling group name 스타일 그룹 이름 proposed No attestation; plain compound, following Glyphs 3's 스타일 for style names. The styling group name, SGN, ties together the styles an application reaches through its bold and italic buttons, and the styling link value and styling link name say which slot each style takes in that group. The mechanism is older than typographic family names and narrower: four slots, no more. You set these fields in TransType when a family has to behave correctly in applications that still drive style selection from those buttons. subsetting cutting down a font 서브세팅 proposed Loan used by Korean web-font engineering (폰트 서브세팅, 서브셋 폰트); no corpus attestation. Subsetting exports only part of a font, such as the glyphs a page uses or one codepage, to make a smaller file. The OS/2 embedding bits can forbid it. top sidebearing 위쪽 사이드베어링 proposed Derived from 사이드베어링; no separate attestation. The space above the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. tracking uniform letter spacing 트래킹 proposed KST dictionary headword, defined as changing 글자사이 by one value across a run. Adobe's 자간 is rejected because the KST dictionary redirects 자간 to 글자사이 (spacing). Tracking changes the spacing across a run of text, rather than correcting particular pairs as kerning does. Layout applications apply it to text. TransType's Tracking filter changes spacing in the font data itself. That changes the font's starting metrics; a layout application can still apply additional tracking to text set in the resulting font. TrueType instruction pixel fitting instruction TrueType 명령 proposed FontForge has TrueType 명령 and the KST dictionary 힌팅 명령; TrueType stays in Latin. A TrueType instruction is one step of the program a TrueType font runs to fit an outline to the pixel grid. Instructions are the TrueType form of hints. FontLab writes them from visual TrueType hints and can keep the ones a font already has. Say instruction for the code and hint for what the reader draws. typographic family name 타이포그래픽 글자 가족 이름 proposed Glyphs 3 translates Family Name as 글자 가족 이름 and uses 타이포그라픽 for Typographic; spelled 타이포그래픽 per the orthography and Apple. The typographic family name, TFN, is the name that groups every style of a family under one entry, and the typographic style name, TSN, is what distinguishes a style inside it. They sit beside the older four style family and style names that legacy applications read. You set them in TransType and in Font Info, and you keep them consistent across a family, because an app that reads these fields builds its font menu from them. update metrics 메트릭스 업데이트 proposed Glyphs 3 uses 업데이트 for its Update commands (왼쪽 사이드 베어링 업데이트). Recalculate glyph spacing values from their links or expressions. This command updates the advance widths and sidebearings that depend on those relationships. variable font 베리어블 폰트 proposed KST dictionary headword 베리어블폰트 and Sandoll; Glyphs 3 spells it 배리어블 폰트. Adobe and Microsoft say 가변 글꼴, the rejected alternative. A variable font contains data for design variation along one or more axes. Applications select axis values and calculate the corresponding outlines and other variable data. Named instances identify selected locations, but users are not limited to those locations when the application exposes axis controls. A variable font's supported range depends on its data; it need not contain every style in the family. variation location position in the variation range 디자인 공간 위치 proposed No attestation; fallback translated. Where the English says only location, write 위치. A variation location is a point in the design space, given as one value per axis. Masters and instances each have one, and the Variations panel slider shows the current one. vertical advance glyph box height 세로쓰기 글자높이 proposed Same measure as advance height, named for vertical setting (FontForge: 세로쓰기 이동폭); derived, no attestation. The vertical advance is the distance a glyph advances in vertical text, the counterpart of advance width for East Asian layout. Stored in vmtx. vertical metrics 세로 메트릭스 proposed Glyphs 3 uses 세로 메트릭스. The font-wide vertical values used for line layout, including ascender, descender and line gap. FontLab groups these as dimensions, distinct from glyph spacing metrics. visual kerning shape-measured spacing correction 시각적 커닝 proposed Adobe names optical kerning 시각적; derived from 커닝. Visual kerning is kerning that FontLab proposes by measuring the shapes, so that a font gets a usable first pass without a person typing thousands of values. You run it over a selection, then review what it produced, because a measurement of two outlines does not know about the words a reader will meet. Treat the result as a draft: keep the pairs it got right, correct the ones it did not, and kern the difficult pairs by eye in real words. weight axis thickness axis 굵기 축 proposed Sandoll uses 굵기 축. The weight axis, tag wght, varies stroke thickness from light to bold. In a variable font it is the most common axis; its master locations use the usWeightClass scale, such as 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. weight class 굵기 클래스 proposed Derived from 굵기 and Glyphs 3's 클래스 (너비 클래스); the corpus pick 가중치 is the statistics sense of weight. The weight class is the OS/2 value from 100 to 900 that tells applications how heavy a style is, with 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. Style linking and menus rely on it. width axis narrow-to-wide axis 너비 축 proposed Derived from 너비, Glyphs 3's word for width (너비 클래스); kept apart from 글자폭 (advance width). The width axis, tag wdth, varies letter proportions from condensed to extended. It is distinct from advance width, which is the spacing of one glyph, and from the geometric width of a shape. Its scale is a percentage of normal width. width class 너비 클래스 proposed Glyphs 3 translates Width Class as 너비 클래스. The width class is the OS/2 value from 1, ultra condensed, to 9, ultra expanded, that tells applications how wide a style is. It is a classification, not the width axis value and not the advance width.

docs.title: OpenType
docs.text: English Fallback Korean Status Note Definition Adobe Glyph List Adobe Glyph List do-not-translate The Adobe Glyph List maps standard glyph names to Unicode codepoints, so that a glyph named aacute is understood as U plus 00E1 by any tool that follows it. You name glyphs by it wherever it covers the character, because tools and text engines can then infer the mapping without being told twice. Where it does not cover a glyph, you fall back to a consistent scheme of your own and assign codepoints explicitly. Write the name in full on first mention, then AGL. alternate glyph glyph variant 대체 글리프 proposed Adobe uses 대체 글리프 and Sandoll 대체 글립; follows 글리프. An alternate glyph is another form of the same character, selected through an OpenType feature such as salt or a stylistic set. Its name usually carries a suffix, as in a.alt or g.ss01. cmap cmap do-not-translate The cmap table maps character codes to glyph indices. Its Unicode subtables provide the initial mapping used in text rendering; other subtables support particular encodings or variation sequences. FontLab generates these mappings from the project's encoding data. A glyph without its own Unicode assignment can still appear in typed text through substitution, such as a ligature or alternate selected by the shaping engine. code page legacy character table 코드 페이지 proposed Microsoft and FontForge (MS 코드 페이지) use 코드 페이지. A code page is a numbered legacy encoding, such as Windows 1250 for Central European languages, that maps one byte to one character. The OS/2 table lists the code pages a font supports, and FontLab derives that list from the glyphs present. Write two words. color font table 컬러 폰트 테이블 proposed Derived: 컬러 폰트 is the Korean foundry term and a table inside a font is 테이블 (FontForge); the tags stay Latin. Colour-font tables store data for colour glyph rendering. Formats include COLR with CPAL, SVG, sbix, and CBDT with CBLC. They differ in how they describe vector or bitmap content and in application support. Including several formats can extend coverage, but does not guarantee rendering in every application. Identify the exported formats and test the intended targets. contextual alternates context-dependent variants 문맥 대체 proposed Adobe's Korean OpenType help says 문맥 대체; Glyphs 3 has the longer 문맥에 따른 대체 문자. Contextual alternates, the calt feature, cover substitutions an app makes because of what sits around a glyph rather than because a reader asked. In a script face the text engine replaces an entry stroke after a letter that already ends in one, and in a face with repeating shapes it replaces the second of a pair. You write the rules with context in feature code, and apps usually leave calt on by default, which makes it the feature most likely to surprise you when a rule is too broad. cursive attachment joined-script connection 필기체 연결 proposed FontForge and Apple CoreText (Cursive Connection) use 필기체 연결. Cursive attachment joins glyphs by matching an exit anchor of one glyph to the entry anchor of the next, so connected scripts such as Arabic and Nastaliq flow. It is the curs feature, built from anchors. design languages 대상 언어 proposed No attestation; translated as target languages, as the four reviewed languages did. 디자인 언어 would read as a design style. Design languages, the meta table dlng record, list the languages the typeface was designed for. Supported languages, slng, list every language it can set. Both are language tags, not feature tags. encoding 인코딩 proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft and the KST dictionary use 인코딩. An encoding maps character codes to glyphs. Unicode is the encoding modern fonts use; legacy encodings such as Mac Roman or a code page map one byte to one glyph. FontLab shows the font in a chosen encoding in the Font window and writes the cmap from it. Say encoding for the mapping and code page for a numbered legacy table. feature code layout rule code 피처 코드 proposed Glyphs 3 uses 피처 코드 and 피처 파일. Feature code is the text syntax that describes OpenType features: classes, lookups, substitution and positioning rules, grouped into features by tag. It is usually called FEA, after the file extension. You edit it in the Features panel, compile it to check for errors, and keep it under the same review as the drawings, since a rule that fires on the wrong glyph is as visible as a wrong outline. FontLab compiles it into GSUB and GPOS at export. fractions 분수 proposed Adobe, Apple, FontForge and Sandoll use 분수. Fractions are numerical forms such as ½. In OpenType, the frac feature supports diagonal fraction composition through glyph substitution. A font may provide precomposed fraction glyphs, numerator and denominator forms, or both. The separate numr and dnom features provide numerator and denominator forms. Do not substitute the sups and subs feature names for these mechanisms or promise support for every input sequence without testing it. glyph index glyph number 글리프 인덱스 proposed Apple Font Book uses 글리프 인덱스. A glyph index is the number a glyph occupies in the font's own order, counting from zero. Text engines work in indices after the cmap has done its job, and binary tables reference glyphs by index rather than by name. You rarely set one by hand, but you meet it when you inspect a compiled font or debug a lookup that fires on the wrong glyph. The index depends on glyph order, so it changes when the order does. glyph name 글리프 이름 proposed Glyphs 3 and FontForge use 글리프 이름. A glyph name identifies a glyph in an editing project, feature code or a tool's data. Names such as a, a.sc and a.alt can distinguish related drawings. They are separate from Unicode assignments and glyph indices, and need not survive in every exported format. After renaming a glyph, check references in feature code, classes and scripts, including references the editor cannot update automatically. GPOS GPOS do-not-translate GPOS is the OpenType table that holds positioning: kerning, mark attachment, cursive attachment, and any rule that moves a glyph without replacing it. FontLab writes your kerning here, as pairs and as class based positioning, and builds the mark lookups from your anchors. You reach it through feature code rather than by editing the table. A font may also carry a legacy kern table; modern text engines read GPOS and many ignore the other. GSUB GSUB do-not-translate GSUB is the OpenType table containing glyph-substitution lookups. It supports operations such as replacing a glyph with an alternate, forming a ligature or selecting a form from its context. FontLab compiles feature code into these structures. To diagnose a missing substitution, check the glyphs, compiled rules, feature selection, language and shaping order in the target application. ligature joined letters 합자 proposed Glyphs 3, Apple, Adobe, Sandoll and the KST dictionary use 합자; KST's Latin-only headword 리거처 and FontForge's 합음자 are rejected. A ligature is a glyph used to represent a sequence of characters, such as fi. OpenType substitution can replace several glyphs with one ligature glyph. The liga and dlig features distinguish standard and discretionary ligatures. Shaping does not change the underlying text; whether a later document export preserves searchable text also depends on that export and its text mappings. localized forms language-specific variants 지역화된 형태 proposed Glyphs 3 has 지역화된 양식 and FontForge 지역화된 형식; 형태 is used instead of 양식 because Glyphs 3 itself uses 형태 for letterforms and 양식 reads as a document form. Localized forms are glyph variants selected for a text run's language. The OpenType locl feature can provide these substitutions, for example Bulgarian forms of Cyrillic letters. The shaping engine needs the relevant language information, which the application may obtain from a setting or other context. The substitution changes glyph selection, not the underlying characters or their codepoints. lookup procedure 프로시저 approved User/team procedure fallback. No sufficiently strong established OpenType-specific alternative verified in the reviewed primary sources. Keep the approved contextual Rules panel title. Preserve literal FEA lookup/lookupflag keywords, identifiers and OpenType structure names. Ordinary search senses are separate. A lookup groups substitution or positioning rules of one type in GSUB or GPOS. Features reference lookups, and several features can share one. The shaping engine selects features and may process them in script-specific stages; within a stage, LookupList order matters. Source-code order alone does not describe the complete shaping sequence. Inspect the compiled tables and the target engine when diagnosing ordering problems. mark glyph combining mark glyph 마크 글리프 proposed Derived from 마크 and 글리프. A mark glyph is an accent or other combining mark that attaches to a base glyph through anchors. The GDEF table classes it as a mark so shaping engines position it rather than advancing past it. nonspacing mark zero-width combining mark 폭 없는 마크 proposed No attestation; fallback (zero-width combining mark) translated with 마크 and 폭 from 글자폭. A nonspacing mark is the Unicode general category Mn: a combining mark with zero advance, such as a combining acute. It differs from FontLab's nonspacing element, which is a property of an element inside a glyph. oldstyle figures lowercase-style figures 올드스타일 숫자 proposed KST dictionary headword 올드스타일숫자, also FontForge, Apple and Sandoll (올드 스타일). Oldstyle figures are numerals with varying heights, often including forms with ascenders and descenders. The OpenType onum feature selects them when provided by the font. Figure height and figure width are separate choices: oldstyle figures can be proportional or tabular. Use tabular widths when numerals must align in columns, whether their forms are oldstyle or lining. OpenType class layout glyph group OpenType 클래스 proposed Glyphs 3 and FontForge use 클래스; OpenType stays in Latin as Adobe writes it. An OpenType class is a named group of glyphs that feature code can address at once, written with an at sign before the name. One rule over two classes replaces a page of single rules, and one edit to a class reaches every rule that cites it. You define classes in the Classes panel or in feature code, and you keep their order stable, because a substitution between two classes pairs them by position. Kerning classes are a separate mechanism with the same idea. OpenType feature layout feature OpenType 피처 proposed KST dictionary 오픈타입피처, Morisawa Korea and Sandoll 오픈타입 피처; OpenType kept in Latin as in Adobe's OpenType 기능. An OpenType feature identifies typographic behaviour through a four-character tag, such as liga, smcp or ss01. Feature records reference substitution or positioning lookups. In FontLab, you can write feature code and compile it into the font. Whether and when a feature is applied depends on the shaping engine, script, language and application settings; not every feature is a user-controlled switch. OS/2 table OS/2 테이블 proposed Tag kept, noun translated; 테이블 for a table inside a font (FontForge). The OS/2 table carries the font's metadata for applications: vertical metrics, weight and width classes, embedding permissions, the panose values, and the codepage and Unicode range bits that say what the font covers. You fill it from Font Info rather than by hand, and you check it before release, because a wrong weight class puts a font in the wrong slot in a menu and wrong vertical metrics change line spacing in every browser. Write it with the slash: OS/2. Private Use Area Private Use Area do-not-translate A private-use area is one of three Unicode blocks whose codepoints can receive meanings by private agreement. Different fonts or systems may assign different meanings to the same private-use codepoint. Use a documented agreement when encoding custom symbols there. An alternate glyph reached through a feature does not require its own private-use assignment. single substitution 단일 치환 proposed No fixed term; 치환 is the technical word for substitution and keeps GSUB rules apart from 대체 (alternates). FontForge has 단일 글리프로 대체. A single substitution replaces one glyph with one other glyph, the simplest GSUB lookup type. Small caps, stylistic alternates and localized forms are mostly built from it. small caps small capitals 작은 대문자 proposed Adobe, Apple and FontForge use 작은 대문자 (17 corpus origins) and 작은대문자 is a KST dictionary headword; designers also say 스몰캡. Small caps are capital shapes drawn at roughly lowercase height, with their own weight and width rather than scaled capitals. Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set 스타일 세트 proposed Adobe's Korean OpenType help and menu say 스타일 세트; Glyphs 3 has 스타일리스틱 세트 and Apple 문체 세트. A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures 고정폭 숫자 proposed FontForge and Apple (고정폭 숫자) and Sandoll (고정 폭 라이닝). Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code 유니코드 코드 포인트 proposed Glyphs 3, Apple and the KST dictionary write 유니코드; FontForge has 코드 포인트. A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character 이형 선택자 proposed No firm attestation; 이형 (variant form) plus 선택자, the usual Korean for a selector. FontForge's 변동 선택기 is rejected. A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system 문자 체계 proposed Standard Korean linguistic term; the Microsoft glossary's 쓰기 시스템 is a calque. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Korean Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Korean Status Note Definition action 동작 proposed Apple and Adobe (InDesign, Illustrator) use 동작 for an invokable operation; 액션 is Photoshop's recorded macro and 작업 is a task. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. add 추가 proposed Glyphs 3 (글리프 추가, 앵커 추가) and every platform use 추가; the corpus pick 더하기 is arithmetic addition. Add inserts another item into the current collection or selection. Name the item when the surrounding control does not make it clear. alternate 대체 proposed Glyphs 3 and Apple CoreText use 대체 for alternates. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud 앵커 구름 proposed No attestation; 앵커 plus the plain word for cloud. Where the English says only cloud, write 구름. The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer 자동 레이어 proposed No attestation; fallback idea rendered with the everyday 자동 and the chosen noun 레이어. An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint 자동 힌트 proposed Glyphs 3 and FontForge have 자동힌트 for the command; written as two words like other 자동 compounds. 오토힌트 (also Glyphs 3) is the rejected loan. Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush 붓 proposed House rule: a tool borrowed from a real tool takes the real tool's name, and 붓 is the brush a calligrapher holds. Adobe and Glyphs 3 use the loan 브러시/브러쉬, rejected. The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse 모으기 proposed No attestation for this node operation; the definition (bring selected nodes to one point) is translated with the plain verb. The corpus pick 축소 means shrinking a panel, a different action. Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark 색 라벨 proposed Glyphs 3 calls the same glyph colour marking 색 라벨 (Color Label). A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. corner angles 모서리 각도 proposed No attestation; 모서리 is the everyday word for a corner (Microsoft), used for every corner term here. The angles at contour vertices. These geometric measurements describe how adjacent segments meet at a corner and can be displayed on the canvas. cousins related glyphs alongside 사촌 proposed No attestation; the plain family word, in the house voice, as Polish did with kuzynostwo. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop 자르기 proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft use 자르기 (25 corpus origins). Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic 3차 proposed Korean mathematics calls a cubic curve 3차 곡선; the corpus loan 큐빅 means a gemstone in everyday Korean. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current 현재 proposed Universal platform wording. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. cusp 첨점 proposed Korean geometry term for a cusp; no type-specific attestation. A cusp is a sharp point where a curve changes direction abruptly. Keep it distinct from a smooth join. decompose break into contours 분해 proposed Glyphs 3 (컴포넌트 분해) and FontForge use 분해. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default 기본값 proposed Universal platform wording (47 corpus origins). A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode 데모 모드 proposed Standard Korean software wording; no type-specific source needed. Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog 대화 상자 proposed Microsoft and general Korean software wording. A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes 뚝딱 만들기 proposed No attestation; house voice. 뚝딱 is the sound of the folk-tale magic club that produces things at a stroke, so the name conjures as Polish wyczaruj does, and 만들기 still says it generates. Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text 텍스트 따라가기 proposed No attestation; fallback idea translated: the preview follows the text of the current window. 반복 is avoided because it is Repeat. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser 지우개 proposed The real tool's name; Adobe, Apple and Microsoft all use 지우개. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours 필터 확장 proposed Illustrator's Korean interface uses 확장 for Expand, the same bake-into-paths operation; no font tool attests the phrase. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours 획 확장 proposed Illustrator's 확장 (Expand) with 획 (stroke); FontForge's 스트로크 확장 has the same structure. Glyphs 3 words its own command 아웃라인 만들기. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours 변형 확장 proposed Derived from 확장 (Illustrator's Expand) and 변형; no attestation of the phrase. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature 피처 proposed Glyphs 3 (피처), the KST dictionary (오픈타입피처) and Sandoll use the loan; Adobe's 기능 is rejected because it also means any function of the application. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills 채우기 proposed Glyphs 3 (Fill is 채우기), Apple and Microsoft use 채우기. Illustrator's noun 칠 (paired with 획) is the rejected alternative; it is also the numeral seven. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit 폰트오디트 proposed User requires phonetic transliteration, explicitly including Chinese. Russian and Ukrainian spellings were recovered from team QPH; other spellings are proposals. Retain the FontAudit identity; do not translate as a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account FontLab 계정 proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder 용접공 proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node 천재 노드 proposed No attestation; house voice. The plain word for a genius, rather than the transliteration 지니어스. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid 그리드 proposed Glyphs 3, Adobe and the KST dictionary use 그리드; 격자 is the older alternative. A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups 그룹 proposed Glyphs 3 (커닝 그룹) and every platform use 그룹. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide 안내선 proposed Illustrator and InDesign call a guide 안내선, the native everyday word. Glyphs 3 has 가이드라인 and FontForge 가이드. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. kerning mode 커닝 모드 proposed Derived from 커닝. The editing mode for adjusting spacing between pairs of glyphs. It changes pair adjustments rather than the individual glyph sidebearings. Knife 칼 proposed House rule: the real tool's name. The corpus has 칼 five times; Glyphs 3's loan 나이프 is rejected. The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. layer 레이어 proposed Glyphs 3, Adobe, Apple and Microsoft use 레이어. A layer holds one drawing or part of a document. In FontLab, the context identifies the glyph layer; name the application when another product uses a different layer model. Layers 레이어 proposed Same noun; Korean does not mark the plural. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark 마크 proposed Glyphs 3 (Mark is 마크) and FontForge (기저마크) use 마크 for a combining mark; the corpus pick 표시 is the interface sense of marking something. A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks 마스크 proposed Adobe and Apple use 마스크; Korean does not mark the plural. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match 맞추기 proposed No type-specific attestation; the plain verb for making things correspond. The corpus pick 일치 names the state, and 경기 or 성냥 are other senses of match. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching 일치하는 proposed Platform wording for things that correspond (corpus: 일치). Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher 중매쟁이 proposed No attestation; house voice. The plain, slightly cheeky word for a village matchmaker, as Polish swat. Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. measurement line 측정선 proposed No attestation; plain compound of 측정 (measurement) and 선. A line that shows a measured distance in the drawing. Distinguish this geometric measurement from a metrics line used to calculate sidebearings. measurements 측정값 proposed Plain Korean for measured values shown on the canvas; no font-tool attestation. Values displayed on the canvas to describe geometry, such as coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters. Showing measurements does not modify glyph spacing or font dimensions. Measurements panel 측정 패널 proposed Derived from 측정; the panel title itself is 측정, which is no longer than the English. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge 병합 proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft use 병합 (23 corpus origins). Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh 메시 proposed Corpus has 메시 nine times and it follows the loanword orthography; Adobe's 망 is its gradient mesh. A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. metrics mode 메트릭스 모드 proposed Derived from 메트릭스. The editing mode for adjusting glyph advance widths and sidebearings. It changes the spacing of glyphs rather than the vertical dimensions of the font or the visibility of measurements. metrics table 메트릭스 표 proposed Derived; a table in the interface is 표, a table inside a font is 테이블. The table of glyph spacing values, including advance widths and sidebearings. It lets the user inspect or edit spacing values together. metrics tool 메트릭스 도구 proposed Derived from 메트릭스 and 도구 (Glyphs 3: Tools is 도구). The tool that edits glyph advance widths and sidebearings. Use it to adjust glyph spacing; canvas measurement overlays display values without changing those spacing values. monospaced 고정폭 proposed Apple Font Book, CoreText and FontForge use 고정폭 and Sandoll 고정 폭; the KST dictionary's 고정너비 is the rejected alternative. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line 여러 줄 proposed Adobe and Microsoft use 여러 줄. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width 메트릭스 제외 proposed No attestation; describes what the property does (excluded from metrics), as German and Polish did. Glyphs 3's 공간이 없는 is a literal calque and is rejected. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move 넛지 proposed Glyphs 3 uses 넛지 (노드 넛지 처리), and the word is widely known in Korean. 살짝 밀기 is the plain alternative. Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique 오블리크 proposed KST dictionary headword; a fixed operation name. Apple's 기울임체 names a style and would read as any slant. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel 패널 proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft and Glyphs 3 use 패널. A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil 연필 proposed The real tool's name; 23 corpus origins. Glyphs 3's 연필툴 adds a suffix the English does not have. The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush 파워 붓 proposed No attestation; house voice. 파워 keeps the energy-drink and 파워레인저 wink in Korean; 붓 from Brush. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline 파워 안내선 proposed No attestation; 파워 plus 안내선. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move 파워 넛지 proposed No attestation; 파워 plus 넛지. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline 파워 획 proposed No attestation; 파워 plus 획. The corpus calque 파워 자획 is rejected. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project 프로젝트 approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar 속성 막대 proposed No font-tool attestation; 속성 (properties) and 막대, the Apple and Photoshop word for a bar (옵션 막대, 필터 막대). The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. quick measurement 빠른 측정 proposed Derived from 측정; no attestation. The function that displays measurements near the pointer while editing outlines. It reports geometry on the canvas without changing the glyph spacing values. redo 다시 실행 proposed Platform wording (33 corpus origins). Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference 참조 proposed Adobe, Apple, Microsoft and FontForge use 참조. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours 겹침 제거 proposed Glyphs 3 says 오버랩 제거 and FontForge 겹쳐진 도형을 제거; the short native noun 겹침 is used instead of the loan. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat 반복 proposed Platform wording (30 corpus origins); distinct from 다시 실행 (Redo). Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction 윤곽선 방향 반전 proposed Glyphs 3 translates Reverse Contour exactly so. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors 가위 proposed The real tool's name; Adobe, Apple and Microsoft use 가위. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node 따라가는 노드 proposed No attestation; translates the fallback Follower node with the plain verb for following a leader's movement. Compact label: 따라가기. For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas 스케치판 proposed No attestation; house voice. 스케치 plus the native 판 (board), a plain word instead of the transliteration 스케치보드. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline 껍질 proposed No attestation; house voice. The peel or skin that wraps a fruit, as Polish skórka. 스킨 is rejected because in Korean it means a UI theme or a cosmetic toner. Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever 스마트 proposed Glyphs 3 (스마트 필터, 스마트 컴포넌트) and Photoshop (스마트 필터) attest 스마트 for exactly this kind of feature. In Korean it reads as handy and automated (스마트폰), not as an AI claim, so it is kept; 똑똑한 is the plain alternative if the owner wants the native wink. Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner 스마트 모서리 proposed Derived from 스마트 and 모서리 (corner). Glyphs 3 names its unrelated feature 코너 컴포넌트. A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter 스마트 필터 proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles 글자사이 컨트롤 proposed Derived from 글자사이; 컨트롤 is the platform word for an on-screen control. No attestation. Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker 스티커 proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft use 스티커. A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. tab 탭 proposed Universal platform wording. A tab selects one page or document within a set. A tab character in text is a different meaning and must retain its literal representation in code. text element text block 텍스트 요소 proposed Derived from 요소; Apple attests 텍스트 요소. A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness 두께 proposed Apple, Microsoft and type designers use 두께 for a measured thickness, distinct from 굵기 (weight). Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform 변형 proposed Glyphs 3, Illustrator and InDesign call Transform 변형 (17 corpus origins). The corpus pick 스케일 is only scaling. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation 변형 proposed Same noun as Transform; Korean does not separate the operation from its result. 변환 is kept for conversion. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering 진짜 채우기 proposed No attestation; house voice. The everyday word for real, with 채우기. True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck 선택 해제 proposed Apple and general platform wording. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview 폭포 proposed Apple Font Book calls this size-ladder sample 폭포. A descriptive 크기별 미리보기 is the alternative if the image does not carry. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight 굵기 proposed The KST dictionary and Sandoll use 굵기 for typeface weight; 가중치 and 무게 are other senses, and 두께 is kept for measured thickness. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace 공백 proposed Adobe, Apple and Microsoft use 공백. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Korean Status Note Definition Appearance panel 모양 패널 proposed Illustrator's Korean interface calls the Appearance panel 모양 패널. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion 자동 추적 proposed Adobe's Image Trace is 이미지 추적 and the corpus has 자동 추적; FontForge keeps autotrace in English. Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline 중심선 proposed Standard Korean for a centre line; attested in the Microsoft glossary. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask 클리핑 마스크 proposed Adobe Illustrator and Microsoft use 클리핑 마스크. A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point 제어점 proposed FontForge and Korean mathematics use 제어점 for a Bézier control point; 컨트롤 포인트 is the rejected loan. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines 채우기 그리드 proposed Derived from 채우기 and 그리드; no attestation. The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style 채우기 모드 proposed Derived from 채우기; the corpus attests 채우기 모드. A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them. Each reads the brightness of the source and lays down geometry accordingly. You pick a mode, then tune its parameters. Write the mode name with its own capitalization and the words fill mode in lowercase after it. G2 continuity G2 연속성 proposed Standard CAD and mathematics wording. G2 continuity means two segments meet with matching curvature, not merely with matching direction. G1 keeps the tangent continuous and can still show a break in the reflection where the curvature jumps. G2 removes that break. Vextra marks G2 nodes and can enforce the condition as you edit. You reach for it on long, shallow curves and on shapes that will be seen large, where the eye finds a curvature break that it would miss at text size. Live Effect editable effect 라이브 효과 proposed No verified attestation of the phrase; 효과 is Illustrator's Korean menu name for effects and 라이브 the loan Illustrator users know from 라이브 페인트. A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve 곡선 밖 점 proposed No attestation; fallback (point off the curve) translated. FontForge transliterates as 오프 커브 포인트. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve 곡선 위 점 proposed No attestation; fallback (point on the curve) translated, parallel to 곡선 밖 점. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline 아웃라인 proposed Glyphs 3 (아웃라인 채우기, 손상된 아웃라인), FontForge and KST's 아웃라인폰트 use the loan for the whole drawing, which keeps it apart from 윤곽선 (one contour). Adobe's 윤곽선 for outline is the rejected alternative. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke 획 proposed Glyphs 3 (Stroke is 획) and Illustrator's Stroke panel (획 패널) agree. The loan 스트로크 (FontForge; KST for a letter stroke) is rejected. A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap 획 끝모양 proposed The Adobe evidence gives 획 끝모양 for the shape at the end of a stroke. A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape 획 모서리 proposed No fixed term; fallback (stroke corner shape) translated with 모서리. Adobe's Stroke panel labels it 모퉁이 or 연결. A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node 접선 노드 proposed Corpus attests 접선 노드; 접선 is the geometry term for a tangent. A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. tonal map darkness map 톤 맵 proposed No attestation; 톤 is the designers' word for tonal value and 맵 the usual loan for a map of values. A tonal map is the reading of brightness across a source image that a fill uses to decide where to put geometry. Dark areas widen a strip or crowd a pattern; light areas narrow or thin it. You control the mapping with the Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels rows, which change what counts as dark before any geometry is drawn. Adjust the map rather than the fill when the result is uniformly too heavy or too sparse. Tunni line Tunni 선 proposed Eponym kept in Latin, noun translated. A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: Polish
docs.text:
Polish for Poland. Use the supplied current core memory and references/terms.md for terminology, definitions and review status. Approved entries govern their concept; proposed entries still need a native reviewer. A historical catalog or a fluent model draft does not override a current terminology decision. Inflect the chosen term to fit its grammatical role.

The shared Qt, memory and review rules are in fontlab-localization. This skill adds the language's register, grammar and terminology distinctions.

docs.title: Matching masters for interpolation
docs.text:
Use dopasować for the action, pasować for the state: Dopasuj mastery, Dopasuj kerning, Mastery pasują, Mastery nie pasują. Status labels are Pasują and Nie pasują; the participle is dopasowane, adjectives are pasujące and niepasujące, nouns are dopasowanie and niedopasowanie. Never use pasuj as a command or pasowanie as the noun. Do not change Dopasuj where it translates another operation, such as Fit.

The tool is Swatka, feminine: Swatki, Swatkę, Swatką. The everyday phrase pasować do siebie describes a couple that is a good match; dopasować names the action from the same stem, and Swatka is a matchmaker.

These terms apply when masters are matched for interpolation. Keep the current translations of master, kerning and all other terms; inflect the match term and follow the command form already used in the file. Tool names are proper nouns and start with a capital letter. Preserve placeholders, accelerator marks, punctuation, capitalization style and file format. Keep English source strings, German and other languages unchanged. If the source says compatible, retain the translation of compatible. Leave other senses, such as search matching, and uncertain senses unchanged. This decision supersedes earlier terms for this sense, including compatibility and synchronization wording.

docs.title: Follower node terminology
docs.text: Use węzeł naśladowca, with short type label Naśladowca and variants Naśladowca X and Naśladowca Y. The node follows the movement of leading key nodes. Interpret legacy English Servant as Follower in this physical sense. The earlier fan/supporter reading is obsolete. In prose use węzeł typu Naśladowca, węzły typu Naśladowca, węzła typu Naśladowca and węzłami typu Naśladowca to keep the type label stable while declining the surrounding noun. Use tryb Naśladowca and właściwość typu Naśladowca for the behavior. Keep English source keys unchanged. This term follows the user's explicit naming decision.

docs.title: Stroke, thickness and grammatical context
docs.text:
In the application UI, stroke is obrys. Use tęgość only for stroke thickness, grubość trzonu for stem thickness, and grubość for general thickness. A short English Thickness label does not establish which meaning applies: inspect the actual control and the surrounding labels.

Treat glossary entries as lemmas. Use Przekształć for a command and Transformacja for a panel, settings group or history entry; use Kadruj for the crop command. A checkbox describing a font takes Nieproporcjonalny, not the plural nieproporcjonalne. Keep cases and agreement in complete help sentences, including tęgość obrysu, tęgości obrysu and grubość trzonu.

docs.title: References, guides and components in context
docs.text:
Use odwołanie do elementu for a linked element reference, with odwołania, odwołań and odwołaniem in complete phrases. A measurement reference is a different concept: retain punkt odniesienia, wartość odniesienia and materiał odniesienia for geometry, comparison values and visual source material.

A positioning guide is prowadnica: dodaj prowadnicę, nazwa prowadnicy, usuń prowadnice, do prowadnic. A component is komponent, with genitive komponentu and plural komponenty. Use z komponentami and z komponentów; a change of noun can require a different preposition form as well as an ending.

docs.title: Register and address
docs.text:
Use the direct second person singular in product help and dialogs, without a capital: Otwórz plik, Czy chcesz kontynuować? Standard commands and short labels use the imperative, which is also the platform convention: Otwórz, Zapisz jako…, Cofnij. A noun phrase names a state or a panel: Ustawienia, Wygląd. Product messages drop the first person; the company's own prose keeps a warmer register and is identified as such before translation.

Distinguish the message states: Zapisz plik (label), Zapisz plik. (instruction), Zapisywanie pliku (in progress), Zapisano plik. (done), Nie udało się zapisać pliku. (failed attempt), Nie można zapisać pliku. (present limitation).

docs.title: Headline style in compact strings
docs.text:
Strings passed through translation can still be program data. Trace their consumers before translating punctuation-led tokens: .round is a literal TrueType command parameter, not a caption. Preserve it exactly, even when tr() marks it as translatable; localize the surrounding explanation instead.

A navigation path in the English source can be outdated. Verify the live control binding and current page titles before copying it. The loop-fill option is now Informacje o foncie › Wymiary fontu › Bez wypełnienia pętli. Preserve the Qt source key while using the verified localized route; do not silently invent a replacement path.

When a choice repeats its own definition, keep one complete explanation. For PANOSE, use Żadna wartość nie pasuje [1] without a second no-fit phrase. Keep the numeric value and its distinction from variable/any [0]; update every disambiguated occurrence and the explanatory paragraph together.

A selector can complete a sentence: its value and the menu action that supplies that value may deliberately start lowercase. Inspect the adjoining label before capitalizing every QAction. Keep units, identifiers and literal case examples unchanged. In long hints, remove repeated wording while preserving both branches of a condition, every allowed character and each file-format exception.

Review each action’s visible label and tooltip together. When a hint names the tool, use its localized action name without the mnemonic marker; keep grammatical inflection in a functional description. Do not leave an older tool name in the hint after renaming the action.

Include generated property display names and enum choices in casing audits; inspect their .pef definitions and TS disambiguation comments as well as .ui files. A lowercase glossary term may need an initial capital as a standalone label. Preserve case-sensitive identifiers such as uniXXXX and mark/mkmk.

Check casing from the UI role even when the English source starts lowercase. The standalone action show Fonts is Pokaż fonty; literal case examples and sentence fragments need their own treatment. Distinguish glyph tags (tagi) from OpenType feature tags by inspecting the affected object.

Resolve ambiguous English nouns and verbs from the control's role. The Export Profiles settings-window title is Profile eksportu, a name for the profiles, not a command to export them. Check the .ui property and handler before applying an action-style translation to a title.

Check the effect of clear before choosing a deletion verb. Clearing follower state leaves the nodes in place; name the property or disable the behavior. A short label must not imply that the objects themselves will be removed.

When prose quotes a navigation path, copy each localized component from the corresponding control, omitting only its mnemonic marker: Preferencje › Otwieranie fontów. Check embedded paths separately from same-source consistency groups, because the full sentence has a different source key. Do not retranslate a page title or change its casing to shorten the sentence.

In a message dialog use Nie pokazuj ponownie; the visible message supplies the object. An optical-size checkbox can say Rozmiar optyczny. Do not shorten a standalone warning by removing its scope or consequences.

Review every same-source counterpart after changing a translation, including strings shorter than the reference language.
