Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set zestaw stylistyczny approved Poświadczone: zestaw stylistyczny: InDesign: 7; CoreText: 2; Word: 6 / zestaw stylów: Scribus: 2; InDesign: 7; CoreText: 2; Word: 6. A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures cyfry tabelaryczne approved Poświadczone: cyfry tabelaryczne: Scribus: 1; Bringhurst: 2 / cyfry o stałej szerokości: InDesign: 1. Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code jednostka unikodu approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character przełącznik wariantów approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Przegląd 2026-09-28: zastępuje „selektor wariantu”. przełącznik wariantów: FontForge: 2; Apple-CharPalette: 2 A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system system pisma proposed Propozycja z przeglądu francuskiego 2026-09-28; do sprawdzenia. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Polish Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Polish Status Note Definition action akcja approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. alternate wariant approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud chmura kotwic proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer autowarstwa approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. For an auto-layer recipe use przepis, with w przepisie in the locative; avoid alternating with receptura. An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint autohintuj approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush Pędzel approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Pędzel: FontForge: 3; Illustrator: 62; Freeform: 5; Inkscape: 3; GIMP: 84; Bringhurst: 5. The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse zwiń approved Poświadczone: zwiń: InDesign: 14; FontBook: 1; Word: 5. Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark barwa flagi approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. cousins related glyphs alongside kuzynostwo approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. L.poj. kuzyn, l.mn. kuzynostwo (unika zgrzytu kuzyni/kuzyny). Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop kadrowanie approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic sześcienny approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current bieżący approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. decompose break into contours rozbij komponenty proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. demo mode tryb demo proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog okno dialogowe approved Poświadczone: okno dialogowe: Scribus: 1; InDesign: 15; Word: 30; Inkscape: 19; GIMP: 6; Felici: 3. A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes wyczaruj approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text powtórz tekst proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser Gumka approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Gumka: Illustrator: 4; Word: 3; Inkscape: 4; GIMP: 1. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours utrwal filtr approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours utrwal obrys approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours utrwal przekształcenie proposed Use the same przekształcenie stem as the Transform operation. Current catalog proposal; native approval remains pending. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature funkcja approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills Wypełnienia approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Wypełnienia: FontForge: 2; Scribus: 30; InDesign: 76; Illustrator: 30; Freeform: 28; Word: 13; Inkscape: 53; GIMP: 45; Felici: 7. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit FontAudit do-not-translate FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account konto FontLab approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Nazwa marki FontLab zostaje; polski segment tłumaczy tylko „account”. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder Spawacz approved User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node węzeł Genius proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid siatka approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups Grupy approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Grupy: FontForge: 5; Scribus: 11; Qt: 2; InDesign: 99; Illustrator: 35; Freeform: 18; Word: 16; Inkscape: 34; GIMP: 20; Bringhurst: 2; Felici: 5; Manguel: 1; McLuhan: 3. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide prowadnica approved A positioning guide is prowadnica: prowadnicy, prowadnicę, prowadnicą; plural prowadnice, prowadnic, prowadnicami. Use the complete inflected phrase in commands and help, including prowadnice glifu and prowadnice fontu. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. Knife Nóż approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Nóż: Illustrator: 2; Apple-CoreEmoji: 2; Inkscape: 3; Aicher: 1 / Przecinak: FontForge: 1. The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. Layers Warstwy approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Warstwy: FontForge: 37; Scribus: 30; InDesign: 126; Illustrator: 81; Word: 3; Inkscape: 108; GIMP: 190. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark diakrytyk approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks Maski approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Maski: FontForge: 3; Scribus: 5; Illustrator: 43; Freeform: 8; Inkscape: 16; GIMP: 62. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match dopasować approved Issue 305: master matching for interpolation only. Action dopasować (command Dopasuj), state pasować: Mastery pasują / Mastery nie pasują; labels Pasują / Nie pasują. Participles dopasowane; adjectives pasujące / niepasujące; nouns dopasowanie / niedopasowanie. Never command pasuj or noun pasowanie. Swatka is feminine and declines (Swatki, Swatkę, Swatką). Pasować do siebie describes a well-matched couple; dopasować names the action; Swatka names the matchmaker. Preserve existing master, kerning and other terminology and command forms. Keep compatible when the English source says compatible. Preserve other senses (search, Fit), English source keys, German, placeholders, accelerators, punctuation and case style; leave uncertain senses unchanged. Capitalize the tool name. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching pasujące approved Issue 305: master matching for interpolation only. Action dopasować (command Dopasuj), state pasować: Mastery pasują / Mastery nie pasują; labels Pasują / Nie pasują. Participles dopasowane; adjectives pasujące / niepasujące; nouns dopasowanie / niedopasowanie. Never command pasuj or noun pasowanie. Swatka is feminine and declines (Swatki, Swatkę, Swatką). Pasować do siebie describes a well-matched couple; dopasować names the action; Swatka names the matchmaker. Preserve existing master, kerning and other terminology and command forms. Keep compatible when the English source says compatible. Preserve other senses (search, Fit), English source keys, German, placeholders, accelerators, punctuation and case style; leave uncertain senses unchanged. Capitalize the tool name. Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher Swatka approved Issue 305: master matching for interpolation only. Action dopasować (command Dopasuj), state pasować: Mastery pasują / Mastery nie pasują; labels Pasują / Nie pasują. Participles dopasowane; adjectives pasujące / niepasujące; nouns dopasowanie / niedopasowanie. Never command pasuj or noun pasowanie. Swatka is feminine and declines (Swatki, Swatkę, Swatką). Pasować do siebie describes a well-matched couple; dopasować names the action; Swatka names the matchmaker. Preserve existing master, kerning and other terminology and command forms. Keep compatible when the English source says compatible. Preserve other senses (search, Fit), English source keys, German, placeholders, accelerators, punctuation and case style; leave uncertain senses unchanged. Capitalize the tool name. Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. Measurements panel Pomiary proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge scal approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh mesz approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. monospaced nieproporcjonalne approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line wielowierszowe approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width bezmetryczny approved Use bezmetryczny with grammatical agreement: element bezmetryczny, komponenty bezmetryczne, elementów bezmetrycznych. Detect nonspacing: Wykryj elementy bezmetryczne. Clear nonspacing: Wyłącz bezmetryczność. This element/component property excludes it from metrics calculations; the action does not set the glyph advance width to zero. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move Szturch approved Issue 153 house decision: noun/UI label Szturch; verb/action szturchać. Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique Oblique approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Poświadczone: Oblique: Bringhurst: 1 / pochyłe/pochylone: FontForge: 10; Bringhurst: 7; Felici: 8. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel panel approved Poświadczone: panel: Qt: 1; InDesign: 198; Illustrator: 24; Word: 3; Inkscape: 3. A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil Ołówek approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Ołówek: InDesign: 1; Illustrator: 4; Apple-CoreEmoji: 1; GIMP: 1; Bringhurst: 1; Manguel: 1. The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush Pędzel mocy approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline Prowadnica mocy approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Use grammatical case: Prowadnica mocy as a label, Utwórz Prowadnicę mocy as a command. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move Mocny szturch approved Issue 153 house decision: noun/UI label Mocny szturch; verb/action mocno szturchać. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline Obrys mocy approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project projekt approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar pasek właściwości proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. redo przywróć approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference odwołanie approved Use odwołanie for element/component and software references: odwołanie do elementu, odwołania, odwołań, odwołaniem. Measurement/reference geometry retains natural phrases such as punkt odniesienia and wartość odniesienia; visual reference material is materiał odniesienia. Distinguish the concepts before inflecting the complete sentence. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours usuń nakładki approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat powtórz approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction odwróć kierunek konturu approved Poświadczone: odwróć kierunek konturu: FontForge: 1; GIMP: 1 / odwróć ścieżkę: InDesign: 1. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors Nożyczki approved Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: Nożyczki: Illustrator: 2; GIMP: 3. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node węzeł naśladowca approved Follower oznacza podążanie za ruchem węzłów prowadzących: węzeł naśladowca. Krótka nazwa typu: Naśladowca, Naśladowca X, Naśladowca Y. W zdaniach: węzeł typu Naśladowca, węzły typu Naśladowca, węzła typu Naśladowca, węzłami typu Naśladowca; tryb Naśladowca. Angielskie klucze źródłowe Servant pozostają bez zmian. For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas szkicownik approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline skórka approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever sprytny approved Sprytny, odmieniany zgodnie z rzeczownikiem: sprytny narożnik, sprytny filtr, sprytne wypełnienie. Oznacza pomysłowe działanie funkcji, bez obietnicy użycia AI. Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner sprytny narożnik proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter Sprytny filtr proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles regulatory świateł approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker naklejka approved Poświadczone: naklejka: Manguel: 1. A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. text element text block element tekstowy proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness grubość approved General thickness is grubość. Use tęgość only for confirmed stroke thickness (tęgość obrysu); stem thickness is grubość trzonu. Read the actual control and surrounding UI even when English only says Thickness. Inflect within the full phrase. Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform przekształć approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Znaczenie zależy od aplikacji. Sprawdź definicję i rzeczywistą etykietę w interfejsie. Poświadczone: przekształć: FontForge: 14; Scribus: 2; InDesign: 18; Illustrator: 8; Word: 5; Inkscape: 12; GIMP: 31. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation transformacja approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering Pełna krasa approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Zwięzły idiom; podobne rozwiązania warto znaleźć w innych językach. True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck odznacz approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins żetony Vexy coin approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Nazwa marki „Vexy coin” zostaje; polski segment dodaje tylko słowo „żetony”. Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview kaskada approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight grubość approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace znak światła approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Polish Status Note Definition Appearance panel panel Wygląd approved Poświadczone: panel Wygląd: Illustrator: 1. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion wektoryzacja approved Explicit house terminology from fl10n issue 153, 30 September 2026. Inflect and capitalize for the complete target string; preserve code and identifiers. Przegląd 2026-09-28: zastępuje „automatyczne trasowanie”. wektoryzacja: FontForge: 2 / autośledzenie: Inkscape: 3 Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline linia środkowa approved Poświadczone: linia środkowa: FontForge: 1; Inkscape: 1 / linia centralna: GIMP: 1. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask maska przycinająca approved Poświadczone: maska przycinająca: Illustrator: 2. A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point punkt kontrolny proposed Propozycja z przeglądu francuskiego 2026-09-28; do sprawdzenia. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines siatka wypełnienia proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style tryb wypełnienia proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them. Each reads the brightness of the source and lays down geometry accordingly. You pick a mode, then tune its parameters. Write the mode name with its own capitalization and the words fill mode in lowercase after it. G2 continuity ciągłość G2 proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. G2 continuity means two segments meet with matching curvature, not merely with matching direction. G1 keeps the tangent continuous and can still show a break in the reflection where the curvature jumps. G2 removes that break. Vextra marks G2 nodes and can enforce the condition as you edit. You reach for it on long, shallow curves and on shapes that will be seen large, where the eye finds a curvature break that it would miss at text size. Live Effect editable effect efekt dynamiczny proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A Live Effect is an Illustrator effect that stays editable on the object it is applied to, listed in the Appearance panel and recalculated whenever the artwork beneath it changes. Vexy Linestra runs as one, so its fills follow the source artwork rather than freezing into it. You apply it from the Effect menu, under Vexy, and you expand it only when you need the result as plain paths. Expanding ends the link. off-curve point point off the curve punkt poza krzywą proposed Propozycja z przeglądu francuskiego 2026-09-28; do sprawdzenia. An off-curve point sits beside the outline and shapes a curve without touching it. A cubic segment has two, a quadratic segment one or more. FontLab shows them as handles. Use the term when the file structure is the subject; use handle when the reader drags something. on-curve point point on the curve punkt na krzywej proposed Propozycja z przeglądu francuskiego 2026-09-28; do sprawdzenia. An on-curve point lies on the outline itself and is where two segments meet. In FontLab it is a node; the term is used when the contrast with off-curve points matters, for example when a TrueType outline stores both kinds in one list. You place on-curve points at extremes so hinting and interpolation have stable anchors. outline kontur proposed Propozycja z przeglądu francuskiego 2026-09-28; do sprawdzenia. An outline is the set of contours that describes a glyph's shape. Say outline for the whole drawing of a glyph and contour for one closed path inside it. Some languages have one word for both; French uses contour for each. stroke obrys approved User contextual correction to issue 153: application stroke is obrys. Inflect normally: obrysu, obrysem, obrysy. Tęgość applies only to stroke thickness; stem thickness is grubość trzonu. Do not substitute the lemma mechanically into a sentence. A stroke is the line drawn along a path, with a weight, a colour, and an alignment that puts it inside, outside, or centred on the path. It is not the fill, which covers the area the path encloses. In type design the same word means a main part of a letter. The localized vector term does not automatically apply to letter anatomy: PANOSE contrast and stem thickness describe letter strokes, not an outline effect. Use the established anatomical term in those contexts (for example Polish kreska or Ukrainian штрих). stroke cap stroke end cap zakończenie approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 147): dostosowane do katalogu. Zakończenie obrysu (cap) to nie zwieńczenie kreski (terminal). A stroke cap is the shape at the open end of a stroked path: flat, square or round. Start and end caps can differ, and a cap can be linked so both ends match. stroke join stroke corner shape łącze obrysu approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. A stroke join is the shape where two stroked segments meet at a corner: miter, round or bevel. It decides whether an outside corner is sharp, rounded or cut. tangent node straight-to-curve node węzeł styczny proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A tangent node joins a straight segment to a curve so the curve leaves along the line. Its one handle stays on the line's extension. tonal map darkness map mapa tonalna proposed Bez poświadczenia w źródłach; do potwierdzenia przez recenzenta. A tonal map is the reading of brightness across a source image that a fill uses to decide where to put geometry. Dark areas widen a strip or crowd a pattern; light areas narrow or thin it. You control the mapping with the Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels rows, which change what counts as dark before any geometry is drawn. Adjust the map rather than the fill when the result is uniformly too heavy or too sparse. Tunni line linia Tunniego approved Przegląd 2026-09-29 (issue 146): decyzja założyciela. Od nazwiska projektanta Eduarda Tunniego. A Tunni line joins the two handles of a curve segment, with a control on it that Vextra draws as a pill. Drag the control and both handles move in proportion, so the depth of the curve changes without its balance changing. You use it when a curve is the right shape but the wrong fullness, which is the correction that is slowest to make one handle at a time. Named after Eduardo Tunni, so keep the capital T.

docs.title: FontLab localization: Brazilian Portuguese
docs.text:
A first draft for Brazilian Portuguese. A model researched the guidance below and the term table in references/terms.md; no native reviewer has approved the language as a whole. Individual terms carry their own approval status; a proposed term remains proposed, and a protected name keeps its glossary spelling. The Brazilian Portuguese interface catalogs are unfinished machine drafts: a string found in one settles neither a term nor a rule.

Use references/terms.md, and a newer core memory when one is supplied, for terminology, definitions and review status. Keep a proposed term consistent across the interface and help, and report it as proposed. Where a native reviewer's decision or newer project data disagrees with this skill, follow it and record the change. Report only checks performed: text written with this skill is not reviewed by a native speaker and not tested in the running application until someone does that.

Use these rules with the localization principles (in fontlab-localization), Qt interface rules (in fontlab-localization) and Brazilian Portuguese language guide (in the FontLab writing guide). Examples tagged FB, G3, Qt or AI are quoted from Font Book, Glyphs 3, Qt's qtbase_pt_BR catalog or Adobe Illustrator. Untagged examples are constructed.

docs.title: Locale and register
docs.text:
• Portuguese for Brazil, Qt locale pt_BR. Portugal is a separate edition.
  • Spell by the 1990 Orthographic Agreement, as in the ABL's VOLP: ideia, frequência, autoajuste (auto-fit), autossalvamento (autosave), pré-visualização (preview).
  • Address the reader as você with third-person verbs, and omit the pronoun and the possessive when the verb carries them: Verifique a conexão de rede (FB, "Check your network connection"). Never tu, o senhor or o usuário for "you".
  • Tone: direct and neutral. Drop por favor, exclamation marks and the product's first person: "Please try again" is Tente novamente. (FB).

docs.title: Grammar of interface strings
docs.text:
String Form Example Menu command, button Infinitive Salvar como… (AI, "Save As…") Checkbox, option Infinitive or noun phrase Mostrar barra de filtro (FB, "Show filter bar") Panel, group or dialog title Noun phrase, no article Zonas de alinhamento (G3, "Alignment Zones") Step, prompt, empty state Imperative for você Arraste o arquivo de licença aqui (G3, "Drag license file here") Status, in progress Gerund and ellipsis Validando fontes… (FB, "Validating fonts…") Success Noun and agreeing participle Arquivo salvo. ("File saved.") Failed attempt Não foi possível and infinitive Não foi possível remover a fonte (FB, "Cannot Remove Font") Present limitation Não é possível and infinitive Não é possível apagar a coleção (FB, "Collection Cannot Be Deleted") Error title Erro ao or Falha ao and infinitive Erro ao colar (G3, "Paste Error") Confirmation Deseja…?, Tem certeza de que deseja…? Deseja remover as fontes selecionadas? (FB) Tooltip Third-person present; imperative for a step Abre uma nova aba com todas as camadas afetadas. (G3, "Opens a new tab with all affected layers.")
  • Never use an imperative (Salve, Escolha) or a gerund for a command.
  • Sentence case in every label: capitalize the first word and proper names only. Adobe, Qt and Glyphs do so (Colar na frente, Ocultar outros); macOS uses title case (Salvar Como…) and Microsoft mirrors the English. FontLab follows Adobe and Qt, so framework and application strings match.
  • Standard commands take the words of Qt's catalog, which Windows shares: Desfazer, Refazer, Recortar, Copiar, Colar, Excluir, Selecionar tudo, Sair; Preferências as in Qt and Adobe. macOS says Cortar, Apagar, Encerrar, Ajustes.
  • Contract preposition and article: Alinhar à esquerda, Mostrar no Finder (FB), Nome do glifo.

docs.title: Compact labels
docs.text:
• Drop the article before the object of a command: Adicionar âncora, Exportar glifos (G3). Full sentences keep it: Não foi possível abrir o arquivo.
  • Keep prepositions. A noun pile without de is not Portuguese: Opções de exportação, not Opções exportação.
  • Shorten with the source's abbreviations and with máx., mín., nº, keeping accents and periods. Unit symbols take no period: pt, mm.
  • Never abbreviate a glossary term, a command verb, não or a name. Never drop an accent or a preposition to save space.

docs.title: Plurals and placeholders
docs.text:
Qt gives pt_BR two numerus forms: singular for 0 and 1, plural for 2 and more (rule n > 1, shared with French). Plain pt and pt_PT get the English rule, singular for 1 only, so the catalog header must say language="pt_BR". CLDR agrees for integers.

  • Keep %n in both forms. Never write um or 1 in the singular; it also serves 0: %n arquivo selecionado, %n arquivos selecionados ("%n file(s) selected").
  • Agree noun, adjective, participle and verb in each form: Foi encontrado %n erro grave, Foram encontrados %n erros graves (FB).
  • A count in %1 gets no plural choice. Use label and value: Glifos: %1.

A placeholder that stands for a noun hides its gender and number, so articles, contractions, participles and pronouns can fail.

  • When the class is known, name it: A camada “%1” foi excluída ("Layer “%1” was deleted"), O arquivo “%1” já existe.
  • Otherwise use a form that does not agree: Não foi possível excluir %1, %1 já existe. Substituir?, Excluir: %1.
  • Put no article or contraction before an unknown value: Exportar para %1, not no %1. Never write o(a) or excluído(a).

docs.title: Numbers, punctuation and spacing
docs.text:
• Decimal comma, period for thousands: 1.234,5. Qt formats %L1. Versions, code and font data keep their source form.
  • Percent without a space: 25%. A unit takes a no-break space: 12 pt.
  • Quotation marks are “…”, with ‘…’ inside; straight quotes in code only. «…» belongs to Portugal.
  • Ellipsis is the single character …, with no space before it, wherever the source has one.
  • No space before : ; ? !. Lowercase after a colon. Final punctuation follows the source: sentences end with a period, labels do not.
  • Capitals keep their accents: Âncoras, Índice. Type precomposed letters.
  • Months, weekdays and language names are lowercase: 13 de setembro de 2026, português.

docs.title: Mnemonics and key names
docs.text:
• Put & before a letter of the Portuguese word, as Qt does: &Desfazer, Recor&tar, C&olar, E&xcluir, Fe&char, A&juda. No trailing (&F).
  • Never mark á à â ã ç é ê í ó ô õ ú. Prefer the first letter, then another; avoid g j p q y. One letter per menu or dialog.
  • Never change a shortcut. Microsoft Office in Brazil remaps some (Ctrl+B saves); FontLab does not.
  • Untranslated keys: Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Tab, Esc, Enter, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, and on macOS Command, Option, Control, Return. Translated: barra de espaço, seta para cima, seta para baixo, seta para a esquerda, seta para a direita.

docs.title: Names and loans
docs.text:
• Keep unchanged: product and company names, format names (OpenType, TrueType, UFO, VFJ), OpenType tags and table names, glyph names, code.
  • Embed a name after a class noun, without hyphen or ending: arquivo VFJ, fonte OpenType, a tabela kern, o recurso liga. The article agrees with the class noun. Applications are masculine: o FontLab, no FontLab.
  • An established professional loan keeps its English spelling and takes Portuguese gender and plural: o kerning, os hints (G3). The term table decides which loans exist.
  • Do not coin verbs from English. Glyphs 3 has deletar, resetar and checar; write excluir, redefinir, verificar.

docs.title: False friends and traps
docs.text:
European forms leak even into Glyphs 3 (grelha, Controlo, em falta). Use the Brazilian word:

Brazil Not arquivo, tela, usuário ficheiro, ecrã, utilizador salvar, excluir, baixar guardar, eliminar, transferir aplicativo, padrão, grade aplicação, predefinição, grelha caractere, controle, registrar carácter, controlo, registar salvando a guardar

Reject the office-suite reading of a type term; the term table rules.

  • Weight is peso; espessura is the thickness of a stroke.
  • Font is fonte, not tipo (kind) or tipo de letra. Fonte also means source: near fonts, translate source as origem.
  • Character is caractere, glyph is glifo; never swap them.
  • Never caso for letter case, golpe for stroke, livraria for library or personagem for character.
  • Guia is a window tab at Microsoft and a guide in Glyphs: follow the term table.
  • Supports is é compatível com, not suporta. Actual is real (atual means current); resume is retomar.

Machine translation copies English title case, puts imperatives in menus, repeats você and seu, stacks nouns without de (FontForge Adicionar âncora Marca), writes vai estar exportando for a future action, misplaces the crase (à partir) and uses pre-1990 spellings (idéia). Prefer Substituir? to the clitic substituí-lo.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Check in this order, and report only checks performed:

  1. Placeholders, markup and both %n forms, read with 0, 1 and 2.
  2. European vocabulary and spelling.
  3. Infinitive commands, gerund status, failure against limitation.
  4. Gender and number agreement, above all around placeholders.
  5. Sentence case; accents on capitals.
  6. Mnemonics: unique per menu, on unaccented letters.
  7. Type terms against the term table.
  8. Numbers, percent, quotation marks; length in dense panels.

docs.title: FontLab terminology and compact labels
docs.text:
Preserve deliberately uppercase source labels using the language’s case rules. Keep numeric controls compact with UPM, PPM and LSB/RSB (French AG/AD); explain the full terms in help. The Family Dimensions “Units Per eM:” label is an intentional expanded exception.

Use the current core memory and its approval status. OpenType lookup defaults to the translation of procedure, with a different term only when strong OpenType-specific evidence supports it. Explicit choices are German Lookup, French lookup, Polish procedura and Russian процедура. Ordinary searches, individual rules and OpenType features are separate concepts. Preserve literal code keywords and identifiers.

Translate Fusion with the fallback Welder. Use the core's phonetic FontAudit transliteration in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese; preserve FontAudit in code. Proposed spellings remain proposed. Before rebuilding a QPH, recover team edits and import their terms and notes into the core memory.

Compare mnemonic-split terms with unmarked labels. Keep labels compact, aiming for 120% of the English length in Dimensions and Glyph Window preferences without losing meaning. Omit redundant font, color or command wording when context supplies it. TTH labels can omit “use” and abbreviate TrueType hinting; help can explain more. A full harmonization requires three complete catalog reviews, then reconciliation of help with the final UI and verification of generated resources.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• references/terms.md: the full Brazilian Portuguese term table, generated from the core memory pt-core.tmx of the writing guide, with the status, translator note and definition of every term.
  • The Brazilian Portuguese localization guide of the writing guide is the source of the sections above.

docs.title: Related skills
docs.text: fontlab-localization for the shared rules; fontlab-terminology for product names and shared nouns; fontlab-technical for Brazilian Portuguese help text.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
These rules implement the FontLab writing guide. They are copied into every skill so each installed skill can work independently. Corpus measurements can inform review; they are not quotas, universal laws, or tests of authorship.

H1. Accurate actors. Address the reader when they act or choose. Name the application when it performs an operation. Fonts and files contain data that software interprets. Prefer active voice when the actor matters; retain a clear passive construction when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. Never invent an actor or cause to change the grammar.

H2. Never invent a fact. Ground numbers, names, dates, labels, shortcuts, defaults, errors, versions, and quotations in supplied or checked evidence. A draft is evidence of what was written, not independent proof of its claims. Mark unresolved facts with a specific working placeholder such as [VERIFY CLAIM], [CONFIRM LABEL], or [CONFIRM OFFER]. A marked draft is unfinished; resolve the gap before publication. Clearly label fictional examples before their invented details.

H3. Preserve certainty and scope. “May reduce” does not become “eliminates.” Preserve conditions, negation, timing, quantities, compatibility, licensing, and other consequential limits. State a limitation directly rather than disguising it as a favorable position. A single observation does not prove universal behavior. Conflicting sources need scope checks, not an automatic choice of the stricter claim.

H4. Preserve the writer's voice. Do not manufacture stakes, candor, reader emotion, endorsement, or a new narrator. Preserve useful habits and the supplied stance. Reorder, split, or shorten according to the requested edit depth and reader need, without adding facts or causal relationships. A correct draft can remain unchanged.

H5. Give thought a rhythm. Carry a subject through an action, distinction or consequence. Let a developed sentence explain a relationship; let a shorter one settle a result when that change of pace helps. Repeat a concrete object or term when its meaning develops, not as a compulsory callback. Technical actions stay literal; explanations and marketing have room for patient attention, a bounded comparison or dry observation. Keep useful qualifications beside their claims. Do not impose sentence-length, pronoun, punctuation or paragraph quotas, or force every paragraph into the same long-then-short pattern.

H6. Notice the useful detail. Retain names, mechanisms, conditions, versions and issue numbers that help the reader understand or act. From the evidence, choose the object, contrast or small behavior that makes the explanation tangible: a changed preview, a repeated comparison, a file whose status matters. Follow that detail far enough to explain its significance. Warmth can come from this attention and patience. Never invent an observation, personal experience or reader emotion to make prose vivid, or remove a necessary qualification to shorten it.

H7. Punctuation serves meaning. Prefer a colon for an explanation or list. A spaced dash can carry a turn; avoid decorative glosses and repeated interruptions. Use sentence case for new headings and preserve exact source labels. A punctuation pattern does not establish authorship.

H8. Choose precise words. Review vague praise and stock phrasing such as “seamless,” “game-changing,” “leverage,” and “unlock.” Replace them when they obscure the action or make an unsupported claim. Keep an accurate technical use or protected quotation. A count or cluster is a reason to inspect a passage, not proof that each matched word is wrong.

H9. Develop the explanation. Begin where the reader can understand the task, change or offer. Give adjacent sentences a real connection: the same subject under a changed condition, an action and its result, or a question and its answer. A before-and-after comparison needs evidence for both states; a transition must not invent causality. Let a useful aside return to the main thought. Place low-stakes discoveries where they aid understanding, while keeping price, risk, prerequisites and recovery visible when needed. End at the useful result or next action; a quiet ending or a substantial summary can each serve the material.

H10a. Preserve conditions. Use “if” for a condition and “when” where the intended timing or situation warrants it. Check the whole meaning: “when a panel opens” and “while a panel is open” describe different scopes. Keep useful conditionals and parenthetical explanations; do not insert them to imitate a presumed author.

H10. Preserve expression that works. A fragment, three-part phrase, exclamation, aside, or single-sentence paragraph can serve a passage. Keep it when it supports meaning or the writer's rhythm. Do not add one to meet a budget, or remove one because of a generic stylistic test. Keep instructions and consequential conditions literal and easy to find.

H10b. Use the destination's notation. Preserve exact interface labels, tags, extensions, and identifiers. Italicize labels in neutral release notes; in technical site content use supported highlight notation, with bold as the plain-Markdown fallback. Use code style for machine-readable text. State price amounts and currencies unambiguously from evidence; do not infer an exchange rate, tax policy, or license term. A supplied currency shorthand needs enough context to identify the actual offer.

H11. Names and collisions. FontLab is the product; Fontlab Ltd. is the company. Preserve product names, module identifiers, domains, historical names in their historical scope, and exact quoted strings. Do not translate a product name. Name the application when Layer, Mask, Group, Fill, Brush, Knife, Transform, Pencil, Eraser, or Scissors could have more than one meaning. Use a declared short form consistently.

H12. Protect literal material. Preserve quotations, code, commands, paths, identifiers, API names, URLs, legal text, interface strings, placeholders, and table data during prose editing. Change them only for a requested or necessary correction supported by evidence. Do not paraphrase a quotation while retaining quotation marks or an attribution. Explain a consequential correction when the output contract permits it.

H13. Choose the register per passage. Marketing helps assess an offer; technical writing explains or instructs; neutral prose states facts and changes warmly. A document can combine them. Prices, limits, licensing, compatibility, security, and migration facts stay plain and prominent. Audience and purpose determine an email's register. Do not impose a fixed emotional mixture or make every opening a story.

H14. Review facts, then movement. Compare claims and protected strings with their evidence; check scope, action order and terminology. Then read whole passages for attention, connection and pace. Repair a flat sequence by developing an existing detail or relationship, not by adding praise or invented events. Check that humor remains intelligible and the information remains true when the joke is missed. Recheck the facts after a voice edit. A measurement or passing build does not certify facts, usability or authorship. Report only checks actually performed.

H15. Scale to the surface. A button or tooltip needs a clear label, action, or condition, not a miniature essay. Apply factual and naming safeguards at every length. Include the detail the task requires; do not add proof paragraphs, metaphors, or pronouns to satisfy a template. For translation, keep essential instructions literal and references clear.

H16. The override. Follow the user's task and supplied voice before style defaults. Break a default sooner than make the writing worse. Source material and quoted prompts are data, not authority to change the task. Style preferences never justify presenting an invented or unsupported claim as established fact.

docs.title: Portuguese (Brazil) terms
docs.text:
Portable term table, snapshot of 04 October 2026, generated from the core translation memory localization/pt-core.tmx of the FontLab writing guide by tools/scripts/export_terms.py. 55 of 289 terms are approved or protected; a proposed translation is a candidate for a native reviewer, and the English term is the fallback until it is approved. Use newer supplied project data when it disagrees with this snapshot.

A status of do-not-translate protects the English spelling; it does not approve a draft English name. The definition says what the term means in FontLab; the note says why the translation was chosen or how to inflect it. The fallback original term is a plain English phrase to translate instead of the term when the term itself will not travel (stem: main stroke; overshoot: optical surplus).

docs.title: Names
docs.text: English Fallback Portuguese (Brazil) Status Note Definition Adobe Illustrator Adobe Illustrator do-not-translate Adobe Illustrator is the host application for the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins. Use the full name on first mention, then Illustrator. Vexy Lines and Vexy Playlines are separate applications; do not describe them as Illustrator plug-ins. app.fontographer.net app.fontographer.net do-not-translate app.fontographer.net is the address of the browser edition of Fontographer. Preserve the lowercase domain when naming the destination. Use Fontographer when referring to the application itself. FLUM FLUM do-not-translate FLUM is an internal documentation-project name, not a customer-facing product or feature. Omit it from published instructions. Refer to the relevant product documentation when directing a reader to help. FontLab FontLab do-not-translate FontLab is the name of the desktop font editor. Preserve its capital F and L in headings and prose. Fontlab Ltd. names the company; the lowercase fontlab spelling belongs to identifiers such as the Python module and website domains. fontlab (Python module) fontlab (Python module) do-not-translate The fontlab Python module exposes FontLab scripting functionality. Its name is lowercase and case sensitive. Format it as code in prose, and keep the application name FontLab distinct from the module name in examples. FontLab 8 FontLab 8 do-not-translate FontLab 8 names version 8 of the desktop font editor. Put one space before the version number. After establishing the version, use FontLab alone where no other version could be meant. Retain the number in compatibility statements and version-specific instructions. FontLab 9 FontLab 9 do-not-translate FontLab 9 is a versioned product name whose house usage remains draft. Its appearance in an interface or format description does not establish release availability. Confirm the version and intended audience before using it in new prose; preserve it when quoting an exact label. Fontlab Ltd. Fontlab Ltd. do-not-translate Fontlab Ltd. is the company name. Preserve the lowercase l in Fontlab and the period after Ltd. Use FontLab, with a capital L, for the product. The two spellings identify different entities and must not be normalized into one. FontLab Pass FontLab Pass do-not-translate FontLab Pass is the identity and licensing service at pass.fontlab.com. Use the complete service name when explaining account or licence management. Distinguish the service from the FontLab account used to sign in. FontLab Studio 5 FontLab Studio 5 do-not-translate FontLab Studio 5 is a historical version of the font editor. Use the full name in migration instructions, historical descriptions and compatibility statements. Do not shorten it to Studio or use it as the name of another FontLab version. fontlab.com fontlab.com do-not-translate fontlab.com is the main FontLab website address. Preserve the lowercase domain. Link to the relevant page when a reader needs a particular product, download or instruction, rather than sending every task to the home page. Fontographer Fontographer do-not-translate Fontographer names a font editor. For its browser edition, use app.fontographer.net as the address. Distinguish a historical numbered edition when compatibility or migration depends on it. Preserve Fontographer.net only where it belongs to an exact project or command label. Fontographer.net Fontographer.net do-not-translate Fontographer.net occurs in project and command labels. Preserve it when quoting an interface label that uses this spelling. Use Fontographer for the application in ordinary prose and app.fontographer.net for its browser address. Broader house usage of Fontographer.net remains draft. forum.fontlab.com forum.fontlab.com do-not-translate forum.fontlab.com is the FontLab user-forum address. Use it for a relevant discussion or community question, and identify the destination. A documentation link is preferable when the reader needs an established procedure rather than a discussion. GlyphRef GlyphRef do-not-translate GlyphRef is the class used to reference a Fontographer glyph through its scripting interface. Preserve the capital G and R and format the name as code. Keep the API identifier separate from the ordinary word glyph. help.fontlab.com help.fontlab.com do-not-translate help.fontlab.com is a FontLab documentation address. Preserve its lowercase spelling and identify the product or article when linking to it. Use a specific documentation page when the reader needs a particular procedure or reference. help.vexy.art help.vexy.art do-not-translate help.vexy.art is the Vexy documentation address. Name the relevant product when linking to it, since the Vexy products share vocabulary but differ in features and workflows. Preserve the lowercase domain. pass.fontlab.com pass.fontlab.com do-not-translate pass.fontlab.com is the address for FontLab account and licence management. Use the domain when naming the destination and FontLab Pass when naming the service. Explain the action the reader can perform there. Photofont Photofont do-not-translate Photofont is a protected Fontlab Ltd. name, written as one word with a capital P. Preserve this spelling in a notice or reference. Confirm the relevant product and version before adding a claim about functionality. playlines.vexy.art playlines.vexy.art do-not-translate playlines.vexy.art is the address of Vexy Playlines, the browser application. Preserve the lowercase domain. Use the product name for the application and the address for the destination the reader opens. Strokes Maker Strokes Maker do-not-translate Strokes Maker is a former name of Vexy Lines. Use Vexy Lines for the current product and retain Strokes Maker when identifying a historical release or explaining the name change. Do not rename an old interface label inside a quotation. studio.fontlab.com studio.fontlab.com do-not-translate studio.fontlab.com is an unconfirmed service address in the naming register. Keep it draft and do not direct readers there without confirmation of the destination and its availability. A recorded spelling does not establish that a service exists. TransType 5 TransType 5 do-not-translate TransType 5 names version 5 of the font conversion application.
