Fractional coordinates are node positions with decimal places, kept for curve fidelity while you draw. Font formats store integers, so FontLab rounds on export or when you turn on Round coordinates for the font. friendly glyph name readable glyph name tên glyph dễ đọc proposed Fallback "readable glyph name" translated; derived from glyph. A friendly glyph name is the readable name FontLab shows for editing, such as Aacute, as opposed to the production name written into the exported font, such as uni00C1. FontLab can keep both and convert on export. ghost hint edge-only fitting instruction hint ma proposed Derived from hint, as Spanish hint fantasma and Polish hint widmo. A ghost hint is a PostScript hint with a special width that marks one edge, such as the top of a round letter, when there is no stem to hint. It aligns that edge to an alignment zone. hint screen fitting instruction hint proposed Attested professional loan (nya.vn's FontLab tutorials, iDesign). FontForge's gợi ý and mẹo read as tips and obscure the technical meaning. A hint is a stored instruction that tells a rasterizer how to align a stem or a zone to the pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hints describe stems and zones; TrueType hints are instructions. FontLab draws hints in the Glyph window and generates them with autohinting. The word stays English in every language. hint zone hinting height band vùng hint proposed Derived from hint and vùng (zone). A hint zone is a horizontal band, such as the baseline or the x-height, inside which a rasterizer snaps overshoots to the same pixel row. FontLab stores zones in Font Info and shows them in the Glyph window. An alignment zone is the PostScript name for the same thing; hint zone is the general term. hinting screen fitting hinting proposed Attested professional loan (nya.vn, iDesign); gợi ý rejected as for hint. Hinting is the extra information a font carries so that its outlines land predictably on a pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hinting declares stems and alignment zones and leaves the rasterizer to interpret them. TrueType hinting gives instructions that move points explicitly, with the control values in the CVT table. You work on PostScript hints in the glyph and in Font Info, and on TrueType hints with the TrueType Hinting tool and panel. Autohinting produces a starting point you then correct. instance generated design instance proposed nya.vn keeps Instance in its FontLab tutorials, glossed once as trường hợp nội suy. Thể hiện (programming) and phiên bản (version) rejected as misleading. An instance is a particular result at a location in a font's variation space. A named instance, such as Semibold, gives a selected location a name that applications can present. Other locations need not have names. In FontLab, configured instances can be exported as static fonts or included as named instances in a variable font. interpolation nội suy proposed Mathematical term; nya.vn, Blender and GIMP. Interpolation calculates values between source values. In font design, it can calculate outlines, metrics and other data from masters at specified design-space locations. Outline interpolation requires corresponding contour and point structures. Structural compatibility makes the calculation possible, but does not guarantee a good drawing: inspect intermediate results as well as the masters. Extrapolation calculates beyond the source range. kern exception pair spacing exception ngoại lệ kerning proposed Derived from kerning. A kern exception is a pair value that overrides what the classes would otherwise apply. One member of a class rarely behaves like the rest, and the exception says so without breaking the class apart. You create one in the Kerning panel by kerning the single pair while its classes stay in place. Keep exceptions few: a class with many exceptions is the wrong class, and the cheaper fix is to split it rather than to list every disagreement. kerning pair spacing correction kerning proposed Attested professional loan in all Vietnamese typography writing (nya.vn, dafont.vn, Font Chuẩn, The Design Council). FontForge's định chỗ and Apple's co giãn are not used by designers. Kerning adjusts the spacing of particular glyph combinations beyond their normal advances. A pair such as AV may need a different gap from the one produced by its unadjusted metrics. OpenType fonts commonly store horizontal kerning in GPOS lookups associated with the kern feature; some formats and workflows use a separate kern table. Name the mechanism when it matters to export or compatibility. kerning class pair spacing group class kerning proposed nya.vn mostly keeps Class (Class Kerning, Kerning Class). Its other rendering lớp kerning collides with lớp (layer), nhóm with groups, and FontForge's hạng never caught on. A kerning class groups glyphs that need the same kerning. You put every glyph that behaves alike on one side into one class, then kern the class once instead of kerning each pair inside it. FontLab applies the class value to every member pair and keeps single pairs as exceptions where a member needs its own value. Classes matter because a text face carries thousands of readable pairs, and a hand kerned list of that size is unmaintainable. FontLab writes the result into GPOS as class based positioning. kerning pair spacing-corrected pair cặp kerning proposed nya.vn: cặp Kerning. A kerning pair associates two glyphs, or two kerning classes, with a spacing adjustment. In horizontal kerning, a negative value normally reduces the gap and a positive value increases it. An individual glyph pair may provide an exception to class kerning, but it can also exist without a class rule. Check pairs in representative text as well as in isolation. left sidebearing lề trái proposed nya.vn glosses Left Sidebearing as khoảng rộng lề trái; derived from lề. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the glyph origin and the left edge of its outline. It contributes to the glyph advance width and its spacing. Lib Lib proposed Identifier of the UFO lib, kept as in all reviewed languages. Lib is the custom metadata dictionary of a font or a master, mirroring the UFO lib and stored in VFJ. Scripts and tools keep their own keys there. line gap khoảng hở dòng proposed No fixed term; coined to stay distinct from khoảng cách dòng, which in Vietnamese typography means leading (baseline to baseline). The line gap is extra vertical space between lines that a font recommends beyond ascender and descender. hhea and OS/2 each store one. line height chiều cao dòng proposed Usual Vietnamese rendering of line height in web and typography writing. The distance between successive text baselines. It includes the relevant ascender, descender and line-gap contributions; line gap alone is only the additional space. link metrics tie spacing to another glyph liên kết metrics proposed Derived from metrics; nya.vn uses liên kết for linking. Link metrics ties a glyph's sidebearing or advance width to another glyph or to an expression, so the value follows its source. FontLab shows linked metrics with the expression and updates them when the source changes. linked metrics metrics liên kết proposed Derived from metrics; the noun phrase of liên kết metrics. Glyph spacing values linked to another glyph or to an expression. Updating the source or expression changes the dependent advance width or sidebearings. mark attachment combining mark positioning gắn dấu proposed Derived from dấu (mark) and gắn (FontForge's verb for attachment). Mark attachment positions a combining mark relative to a base glyph, a ligature component or another mark. OpenType GPOS lookups describe the anchor relationships, and the shaping engine applies the positioning during layout. FontLab can generate attachment code from suitable anchors. Check the relevant generation settings and test combinations, including stacked marks, rather than assuming that every anchor automatically becomes a lookup. master source design master proposed Attested professional loan: nya.vn's FontLab tutorials keep Master and Font Master. LibreOffice's bản cái is the slide master and bản gốc reads as the original file. A master provides source outlines and other font data at a specified location in a design space. Masters can describe weight, width or other variations, including intermediate locations. FontLab uses corresponding data from masters to calculate instances. For outline interpolation, check contour and point compatibility in each affected glyph; the word master alone does not guarantee that every glyph is present or compatible. master compatibility matching master structure tương thích master proposed Derived from master; nya.vn speaks of lỗi không tương thích between masters. Master compatibility is the condition every glyph must meet before it can interpolate: the same number of contours in the same order, with the same number of nodes and the same start point in each. FontLab reports incompatible glyphs and gives you Matchmaker to repair them by matching contours and start points between masters. Fix compatibility before you tune shapes, because a repair that reorders nodes moves every curve that depends on them. metrics metrics proposed nya.vn's FontLab tutorials keep Metrics throughout. FontForge's đơn vị đo means units of measure, and số đo is taken by measurements. Metrics are the measurements that place a glyph in a line: its advance width and its two sidebearings. Vertical metrics are a separate set, the font wide values for ascender, descender, and line gap. You work on horizontal metrics in the Metrics panel and with the Metrics tool, and on vertical metrics in Font Info. Say which set you mean whenever a page discusses both, because a reader who applies a horizontal instruction to the vertical fields breaks line spacing everywhere the font is used. metrics expression biểu thức metrics proposed Derived from metrics. An expression that calculates a glyph advance width or sidebearing from other values. It describes a spacing relationship rather than a canvas measurement. metrics key khóa metrics proposed Derived from metrics. A glyph reference or expression used to derive a spacing value. The referenced value determines an advance width or sidebearing. pin ghim proposed Issue 160 catalog family review: named point inside an element, distinct from a glyph-layer anchor. Proteus Resources/helptips.json def.anchorpin defines the behavior. Preserve this term across panel, tool, action and help labels; proposed terminology, not native-team approval. A pin is a named point inside an element. Use pins to position elements with expressions and to attach elements to each other. An anchor is a named point in a glyph layer, used for component placement and mark attachment. Create either with the Guides tool and edit it in the Anchors and Pins panel. PPM pixels per type body số điểm ảnh mỗi em proposed Expansion of pixels per em; điểm ảnh is the Apple, Microsoft and FontForge word for pixel. Compact hinting fields keep PPM. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. PPM, pixels per em, is the size at which a rasterizer renders a font: how many pixels one em occupies. TrueType hints, device corrections and bitmap strikes are specified per PPM. In explanatory prose expand it; in hinting fields the short form is usual. production glyph name shipping glyph name tên glyph xuất bản proposed No attestation; fallback "shipping glyph name" translated; derived from glyph. A production glyph name is the name written into the exported font, chosen for compatibility with tools and the Adobe Glyph List, such as uni00C1 rather than Aacute. rendering drawing on screen kết xuất proposed Blender and Inkscape; the usual Vietnamese word for rendering. Rendering is the conversion of an outline into pixels on a screen or a printer. The rasterizer of the operating system or of FontLab's preview reads the outline, applies the hints and paints the result. FontLab previews rendering at chosen pixel sizes so you can judge hints. Rasterization names the same step from the pixel side. required glyphs mandatory glyphs glyph bắt buộc proposed Derived from glyph; fallback "mandatory glyphs". Required glyphs are the ones the OpenType specification and common tools expect at the start of a font: .notdef, NULL or uni0000, CR or uni000D and space. FontLab can add them on export. right sidebearing lề phải proposed nya.vn glosses Right Sidebearing as khoảng rộng lề phải; derived from lề. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the right edge of a glyph outline and the end of its advance width. It contributes to spacing. sidebearing side space lề bên proposed Fallback "side space" translated; nya.vn glosses the sidebearings as lề trái and lề phải, as Spanish margen. FontForge's vị trí phương hướng bên is a mistranslation; the loan sidebearing is the alternative. A sidebearing is the space between a glyph's outline and the edge of its advance width: the left sidebearing before the shape, the right sidebearing after it. Together with the advance width it sets how the glyph spaces against every other glyph, which is the work that carries a text face further than kerning does. You edit sidebearings in the Metrics panel or with the Metrics tool, one glyph at a time or across a selection, and you check them in a word rather than in isolation. size kích cỡ proposed Apple Font Book: Font Size = Kích cỡ Phông chữ. The size of an object or the chosen size of displayed text. Name a specific width or height when only one direction is intended. spacing giãn cách proposed Apple CoreText: Spacing = Giãn cách. The adjustment of glyph advance widths and sidebearings to establish the space between letters. Kerning makes additional adjustments to particular pairs. standard stem reference stem width nét chính chuẩn proposed Derived from nét chính; nya.vn: chiều rộng thân tiêu chuẩn. Standard stems are the representative horizontal and vertical stem widths declared in a font for hinting. The rasterizer snaps stems near those widths to the same pixel count, so like stems stay alike at small sizes. stem link stem tie liên kết nét chính proposed Derived from nét chính; nya.vn calls TrueType links Hint liên kết. A stem link ties two edges of a stroke together as a stem, so hinting can hold their distance as the size changes. A vertical link governs a horizontal measurement and a horizontal link governs a vertical one. You add links in the glyph, either by hand or from an autohinting pass, and you keep them consistent with the standard stem widths declared in Font Info. Vextra reuses the term for the paired edges it detects in artwork that is not type. styling group name tên nhóm kiểu proposed Derived from nhóm and Apple's kiểu (style); no attestation. The styling group name, SGN, ties together the styles an application reaches through its bold and italic buttons, and the styling link value and styling link name say which slot each style takes in that group. The mechanism is older than typographic family names and narrower: four slots, no more. You set these fields in TransType when a family has to behave correctly in applications that still drive style selection from those buttons. subsetting cutting down a font tạo tập con proposed Tập con is the Vietnamese term for a subset; Apple's chia nhỏ phông chữ is a paraphrase. Subsetting exports only part of a font, such as the glyphs a page uses or one codepage, to make a smaller file. The OS/2 embedding bits can forbid it. top sidebearing lề trên proposed Derived from lề (sidebearing); no attestation for the vertical sidebearings. The space above the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. tracking uniform letter spacing tracking proposed Attested professional loan beside kerning (dafont.vn, Font Chuẩn, nya.vn). Blender's giám sát is motion tracking; Apple's giãn cách ký tự is the descriptive alternative. Tracking changes the spacing across a run of text, rather than correcting particular pairs as kerning does. Layout applications apply it to text. TransType's Tracking filter changes spacing in the font data itself. That changes the font's starting metrics; a layout application can still apply additional tracking to text set in the resulting font. TrueType instruction pixel fitting instruction lệnh TrueType proposed Lệnh is the Vietnamese word for a program instruction. A TrueType instruction is one step of the program a TrueType font runs to fit an outline to the pixel grid. Instructions are the TrueType form of hints. FontLab writes them from visual TrueType hints and can keep the ones a font already has. Say instruction for the code and hint for what the reader draws. typographic family name tên họ phông chữ typographic proposed Họ phông chữ is Microsoft's and nya.vn's font family; typographic is left as the label of the name record because Vietnamese has no settled adjective. The typographic family name, TFN, is the name that groups every style of a family under one entry, and the typographic style name, TSN, is what distinguishes a style inside it. They sit beside the older four style family and style names that legacy applications read. You set them in TransType and in Font Info, and you keep them consistent across a family, because an app that reads these fields builds its font menu from them. update metrics cập nhật metrics proposed Derived from metrics. Recalculate glyph spacing values from their links or expressions. This command updates the advance widths and sidebearings that depend on those relationships. variable font phông chữ biến đổi proposed nya.vn (Font chữ biến đổi), dafont.vn and hocdohoa.org; Vietnamese writing also leaves variable font in English. A variable font contains data for design variation along one or more axes. Applications select axis values and calculate the corresponding outlines and other variable data. Named instances identify selected locations, but users are not limited to those locations when the application exposes axis controls. A variable font's supported range depends on its data; it need not contain every style in the family. variation location position in the variation range vị trí biến thể proposed Derived: nya.vn calls the axes trục biến thể and gives masters a tọa độ; vị trí is the plain word for location. A variation location is a point in the design space, given as one value per axis. Masters and instances each have one, and the Variations panel slider shows the current one. vertical advance glyph box height bước tiến dọc proposed No attestation; the fallback "glyph box height" would give chiều cao glyph, which reads as the outline height. The vertical advance is the distance a glyph advances in vertical text, the counterpart of advance width for East Asian layout. Stored in vmtx. vertical metrics metrics dọc proposed Derived from metrics. The font-wide vertical values used for line layout, including ascender, descender and line gap. FontLab groups these as dimensions, distinct from glyph spacing metrics. visual kerning shape-measured spacing correction kerning thị giác proposed Derived from kerning; thị giác is the designers' word for optical judgement. Visual kerning is kerning that FontLab proposes by measuring the shapes, so that a font gets a usable first pass without a person typing thousands of values. You run it over a selection, then review what it produced, because a measurement of two outlines does not know about the words a reader will meet. Treat the result as a draft: keep the pairs it got right, correct the ones it did not, and kern the difficult pairs by eye in real words. weight axis thickness axis trục độ đậm proposed Derived from trục and độ đậm. The weight axis, tag wght, varies stroke thickness from light to bold. In a variable font it is the most common axis; its master locations use the usWeightClass scale, such as 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. weight class cấp độ đậm proposed Derived from độ đậm; cấp is the plain word for a grade on a scale. FontForge's hạng đậm is the alternative. The weight class is the OS/2 value from 100 to 900 that tells applications how heavy a style is, with 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. Style linking and menus rely on it. width axis narrow-to-wide axis trục độ rộng proposed Derived from trục and độ rộng. The width axis, tag wdth, varies letter proportions from condensed to extended. It is distinct from advance width, which is the spacing of one glyph, and from the geometric width of a shape. Its scale is a percentage of normal width. width class cấp độ rộng proposed Derived as weight class; FontForge's hạng bề rộng is the alternative. The width class is the OS/2 value from 1, ultra condensed, to 9, ultra expanded, that tells applications how wide a style is. It is a classification, not the width axis value and not the advance width.

docs.title: OpenType
docs.text: English Fallback Vietnamese Status Note Definition Adobe Glyph List Adobe Glyph List do-not-translate The Adobe Glyph List maps standard glyph names to Unicode codepoints, so that a glyph named aacute is understood as U plus 00E1 by any tool that follows it. You name glyphs by it wherever it covers the character, because tools and text engines can then infer the mapping without being told twice. Where it does not cover a glyph, you fall back to a consistent scheme of your own and assign codepoints explicitly. Write the name in full on first mention, then AGL. alternate glyph glyph variant glyph thay thế proposed Derived from glyph + Apple CoreText's thay thế (Character Alternates = Ký tự Thay thế). Biến thể glyph rejected: biến thể is taken by font variation. An alternate glyph is another form of the same character, selected through an OpenType feature such as salt or a stylistic set. Its name usually carries a suffix, as in a.alt or g.ss01. cmap cmap do-not-translate The cmap table maps character codes to glyph indices. Its Unicode subtables provide the initial mapping used in text rendering; other subtables support particular encodings or variation sequences. FontLab generates these mappings from the project's encoding data. A glyph without its own Unicode assignment can still appear in typed text through substitution, such as a ligature or alternate selected by the shaping engine. code page legacy character table trang mã proposed Established Vietnamese IT term; nya.vn: trang mã ký tự (Codepages). A code page is a numbered legacy encoding, such as Windows 1250 for Central European languages, that maps one byte to one character. The OS/2 table lists the code pages a font supports, and FontLab derives that list from the glyphs present. Write two words. color font table bảng phông chữ màu proposed Derived: bảng is FontForge's word for a font table, phông chữ màu for colour font. Colour-font tables store data for colour glyph rendering. Formats include COLR with CPAL, SVG, sbix, and CBDT with CBLC. They differ in how they describe vector or bitmap content and in application support. Including several formats can extend coverage, but does not guarantee rendering in every application. Identify the exported formats and test the intended targets. contextual alternates context-dependent variants thay thế theo ngữ cảnh proposed Apple CoreText and Microsoft both use Thay thế Theo ngữ cảnh; FontForge's đồ xen kẽ ngữ cảnh rejected. Contextual alternates, the calt feature, cover substitutions an app makes because of what sits around a glyph rather than because a reader asked. In a script face the text engine replaces an entry stroke after a letter that already ends in one, and in a face with repeating shapes it replaces the second of a pair. You write the rules with context in feature code, and apps usually leave calt on by default, which makes it the feature most likely to surprise you when a rule is too broad. cursive attachment joined-script connection gắn chữ thảo proposed FontForge vi: gắn với chữ thảo, shortened; gắn is reused for mark attachment. Cursive attachment joins glyphs by matching an exit anchor of one glyph to the entry anchor of the next, so connected scripts such as Arabic and Nastaliq flow. It is the curs feature, built from anchors. design languages ngôn ngữ đích proposed Follows the reviewed languages (target languages); ngôn ngữ thiết kế would be read as a visual design language. Design languages, the meta table dlng record, list the languages the typeface was designed for. Supported languages, slng, list every language it can set. Both are language tags, not feature tags. encoding bảng mã proposed The Vietnamese font world's own word for an encoding (bảng mã Unicode, TCVN3, VNI; nya.vn). Apple's mã hóa names the process and also means encryption. An encoding maps character codes to glyphs. Unicode is the encoding modern fonts use; legacy encodings such as Mac Roman or a code page map one byte to one glyph. FontLab shows the font in a chosen encoding in the Font window and writes the cmap from it. Say encoding for the mapping and code page for a numbered legacy table. feature code layout rule code mã tính năng proposed Derived from tính năng; nya.vn calls FEA ngôn ngữ lập trình AFDKO. Feature code is the text syntax that describes OpenType features: classes, lookups, substitution and positioning rules, grouped into features by tag. It is usually called FEA, after the file extension. You edit it in the Features panel, compile it to check for errors, and keep it under the same review as the drawings, since a rule that fires on the wrong glyph is as visible as a wrong outline. FontLab compiles it into GSUB and GPOS at export. fractions phân số proposed Apple CoreText: Fractions = Phân số. Fractions are numerical forms such as ½. In OpenType, the frac feature supports diagonal fraction composition through glyph substitution. A font may provide precomposed fraction glyphs, numerator and denominator forms, or both. The separate numr and dnom features provide numerator and denominator forms. Do not substitute the sups and subs feature names for these mechanisms or promise support for every input sequence without testing it. glyph index glyph number chỉ số glyph proposed Derived from glyph; nya.vn describes Glyph Index as thứ tự của Glyph. A glyph index is the number a glyph occupies in the font's own order, counting from zero. Text engines work in indices after the cmap has done its job, and binary tables reference glyphs by index rather than by name. You rarely set one by hand, but you meet it when you inspect a compiled font or debug a lookup that fires on the wrong glyph. The index depends on glyph order, so it changes when the order does. glyph name tên glyph proposed nya.vn: tên Glyph. A glyph name identifies a glyph in an editing project, feature code or a tool's data. Names such as a, a.sc and a.alt can distinguish related drawings. They are separate from Unicode assignments and glyph indices, and need not survive in every exported format. After renaming a glyph, check references in feature code, classes and scripts, including references the editor cannot update automatically. GPOS GPOS do-not-translate GPOS is the OpenType table that holds positioning: kerning, mark attachment, cursive attachment, and any rule that moves a glyph without replacing it. FontLab writes your kerning here, as pairs and as class based positioning, and builds the mark lookups from your anchors. You reach it through feature code rather than by editing the table. A font may also carry a legacy kern table; modern text engines read GPOS and many ignore the other. GSUB GSUB do-not-translate GSUB is the OpenType table containing glyph-substitution lookups. It supports operations such as replacing a glyph with an alternate, forming a ligature or selecting a form from its context. FontLab compiles feature code into these structures. To diagnose a missing substitution, check the glyphs, compiled rules, feature selection, language and shaping order in the target application. ligature joined letters chữ ghép proposed Apple CoreText and Vietnamese typography glossaries. A ligature is a glyph used to represent a sequence of characters, such as fi. OpenType substitution can replace several glyphs with one ligature glyph. The liga and dlig features distinguish standard and discretionary ligatures. Shaping does not change the underlying text; whether a later document export preserves searchable text also depends on that export and its text mappings. localized forms language-specific variants dạng bản địa hóa proposed FontForge vi: hình đã địa phương hoá, modernised with Apple's dạng (forms) and the current word bản địa hóa. Localized forms are glyph variants selected for a text run's language. The OpenType locl feature can provide these substitutions, for example Bulgarian forms of Cyrillic letters. The shaping engine needs the relevant language information, which the application may obtain from a setting or other context. The substitution changes glyph selection, not the underlying characters or their codepoints. lookup procedure thủ tục approved User/team procedure fallback. No sufficiently strong established OpenType-specific alternative verified in the reviewed primary sources. Keep the approved contextual Rules panel title. Preserve literal FEA lookup/lookupflag keywords, identifiers and OpenType structure names. Ordinary search senses are separate. A lookup groups substitution or positioning rules of one type in GSUB or GPOS. Features reference lookups, and several features can share one. The shaping engine selects features and may process them in script-specific stages; within a stage, LookupList order matters. Source-code order alone does not describe the complete shaping sequence. Inspect the compiled tables and the target engine when diagnosing ordering problems. mark glyph combining mark glyph glyph dấu proposed nya.vn: Glyph dấu phụ; derived from glyph and dấu. A mark glyph is an accent or other combining mark that attaches to a base glyph through anchors. The GDEF table classes it as a mark so shaping engines position it rather than advancing past it. nonspacing mark zero-width combining mark dấu không chiếm chỗ proposed Derived from dấu and the rendering of nonspacing; no attestation. A nonspacing mark is the Unicode general category Mn: a combining mark with zero advance, such as a combining acute. It differs from FontLab's nonspacing element, which is a property of an element inside a glyph. oldstyle figures lowercase-style figures chữ số kiểu cũ proposed Apple CoreText (Oldstyle Figures = Chữ số Kiểu cũ) and Microsoft. Oldstyle figures are numerals with varying heights, often including forms with ascenders and descenders. The OpenType onum feature selects them when provided by the font. Figure height and figure width are separate choices: oldstyle figures can be proportional or tabular. Use tabular widths when numerals must align in columns, whether their forms are oldstyle or lining. OpenType class layout glyph group class OpenType proposed Derived from the loan class chosen for kerning class. An OpenType class is a named group of glyphs that feature code can address at once, written with an at sign before the name. One rule over two classes replaces a page of single rules, and one edit to a class reaches every rule that cites it. You define classes in the Classes panel or in feature code, and you keep their order stable, because a substitution between two classes pairs them by position. Kerning classes are a separate mechanism with the same idea. OpenType feature layout feature tính năng OpenType proposed dafont.vn and nya.vn: tính năng OpenType. An OpenType feature identifies typographic behaviour through a four-character tag, such as liga, smcp or ss01. Feature records reference substitution or positioning lookups. In FontLab, you can write feature code and compile it into the font. Whether and when a feature is applied depends on the shaping engine, script, language and application settings; not every feature is a user-controlled switch. OS/2 table bảng OS/2 proposed Tag protected, noun translated; bảng is FontForge's word for a font table. The OS/2 table carries the font's metadata for applications: vertical metrics, weight and width classes, embedding permissions, the panose values, and the codepage and Unicode range bits that say what the font covers. You fill it from Font Info rather than by hand, and you check it before release, because a wrong weight class puts a font in the wrong slot in a menu and wrong vertical metrics change line spacing in every browser. Write it with the slash: OS/2. Private Use Area Private Use Area do-not-translate A private-use area is one of three Unicode blocks whose codepoints can receive meanings by private agreement. Different fonts or systems may assign different meanings to the same private-use codepoint. Use a documented agreement when encoding custom symbols there. An alternate glyph reached through a feature does not require its own private-use assignment. single substitution thay thế đơn proposed FontForge vi: thay thế đơn. A single substitution replaces one glyph with one other glyph, the simplest GSUB lookup type. Small caps, stylistic alternates and localized forms are mostly built from it. small caps small capitals chữ hoa nhỏ proposed Apple CoreText: Small Caps = Chữ hoa Nhỏ; Microsoft agrees. Small caps are capital shapes drawn at roughly lowercase height, with their own weight and width rather than scaled capitals. Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set bộ phong cách proposed Apple CoreText uses phong cách for stylistic (Nhóm Phong cách %d); bộ is the word for a set. Microsoft's tập văn phong is about prose style. A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures chữ số dạng bảng proposed Apple CoreText: Tabular numbers = Số trong bảng; chữ số as in the other figure terms. Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code điểm mã Unicode proposed nya.vn's glossary: điểm mã Unicode; the standard Vietnamese rendering of code point. A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character bộ chọn biến thể proposed No attestation found; literal rendering with biến thể and bộ chọn (selector). A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system hệ chữ viết proposed The linguistic term in Vietnamese; Microsoft's hệ thống viết is a calque. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Vietnamese Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Vietnamese Status Note Definition action hành động proposed Apple (11 origins) and nya.vn's FontLab tutorials ("hành động – Actions") use hành động; thao tác rejected because it is the generic word for any editing step. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. add thêm proposed Platform word in Apple Vietnamese. Add inserts another item into the current collection or selection. Name the item when the surrounding control does not make it clear. alternate dạng thay thế proposed Apple CoreText: Alternate Forms = Dạng Thay thế; Microsoft also uses thay thế. Biến thể kept for variation. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud đám mây neo proposed Derived from neo (anchor) + đám mây; no attestation of the compound. The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer lớp tự động proposed Derived from lớp (layer); no attestation of the compound. An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint hint tự động proposed Derived from the loan hint; nya.vn keeps Autohint. FontForge's gợi ý tự động rejected with gợi ý. Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush cọ proposed Real tool's name; cọ is the majority rendering in the corpus (9 origins) and nya.vn calls the FontLab tool cọ vẽ. The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse thu gọn proposed Platform word (Apple Font Book, Microsoft), following the reviewed languages. For the node operation in the definition (nodes aligned to one point) chụm would be the plain verb; needs a reviewer's call per string. Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark cờ màu proposed No attestation; fallback "color mark" avoided because dấu is the word for a diacritic mark. Cờ follows the established gắn cờ for flagging. A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. corner angles góc tại đỉnh proposed No attestation; translated from the definition (angles at contour vertices), as French angles aux sommets. The angles at contour vertices. These geometric measurements describe how adjacent segments meet at a corner and can be displayed on the canvas. cousins related glyphs alongside họ hàng proposed House voice: the plain collective word for relatives, like Polish kuzynostwo; anh em họ rejected because it needs a plural. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop cắt xén proposed Apple Photos and Notes. Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic bậc ba proposed Mathematical term for the degree of a curve (đường cong bậc ba); FontForge's lập phương means a cube. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current hiện tại proposed Apple and Microsoft; nya.vn's hiện hành is the older bureaucratic word. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. cusp đỉnh nhọn proposed No attestation in type sources; plain description of a sharp point, derived from nhọn (sharp). A cusp is a sharp point where a curve changes direction abruptly. Keep it distinct from a smooth join. decompose break into contours phân rã proposed GIMP and general Vietnamese software usage for breaking a compound into parts; short enough for a menu. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default mặc định proposed Platform word in Apple Vietnamese. A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode chế độ demo proposed Demo is an everyday loan in Vietnamese; dùng thử would promise a time-limited trial. Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog hộp thoại proposed Platform word in Apple, Krita and QCAD. A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes hô biến proposed House voice: the Vietnamese conjuring word, like Polish wyczaruj; the corpus pick tạo hình is only a description. Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text lặp văn bản proposed No attestation; fallback "repeated text" translated in the compact verb form the reviewed languages use. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser tẩy proposed Real tool's name; Apple, Illustrator and Photoshop sources use tẩy. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours chốt bộ lọc proposed No attestation; fallback "bake filter into contours" translated with chốt (to lock in), one verb for the three expand commands as Polish utrwal. Mở rộng rejected: it means to widen. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours chốt nét proposed Same verb as expand filter; FontForge's mở rộng nét rejected as a literal calque meaning to widen the stroke. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours chốt phép biến đổi proposed Same verb as expand filter; follows German festschreiben and Spanish fijar. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates. The element then has an identity transformation and its contours carry the geometry directly. feature tính năng proposed FontForge vi, nya.vn (thẻ tính năng) and dafont.vn (tính năng OpenType). A feature in OpenType editing identifies typographic behavior implemented by substitution or positioning lookups. Feature tags are literal identifiers and remain unchanged in translation. Fills phần tô proposed Corpus alternative phần tô (2 origins); nya.vn says tô for FontLab's Fill tool. Lấp đầy rejected as the verb to fill up. In FontLab, the Fill tool sets enclosed regions as filled or unfilled by changing contour direction or applying a live Fill filter. In Vexy Lines, Linestra and Playlines, a fill mode is a method for generating artwork from an image, such as Halftone or Stipple. Name the application and distinguish the tool, the filled region and the generative mode. FontAudit FontAudit do-not-translate FontAudit is the FontLab panel that inspects outlines and reports the problems a proof will show later: unclosed contours, wrong winding directions, missing extreme nodes, near vertical segments, and the like. You run it over a glyph or a selection, read the findings, and fix what matters for the design rather than clearing every warning. In English write the FontAudit panel on first mention. Localized UI may transliterate the name into its writing system; keep the name distinct from a generic audit command. Preserve FontAudit in code and identifiers. FontLab account tài khoản FontLab proposed Translate the common noun account and inflect it in complete sentences; preserve the FontLab brand. German, Spanish and French wording is already used in current FontLab UI. Other language forms are proposals. Do not duplicate account when the surrounding sentence already translates it. A FontLab account is the identity used to sign in to FontLab services and manage licences. Keep the capital L in FontLab and lowercase account in English. Translate the common noun account while preserving the FontLab name. Distinguish the account from a licence, subscription or payment when more than one appears in the same explanation. Fusion Welder Thợ hàn proposed User decision 2026-10-04: translate the fallback Welder, the named live boolean group filter. Polish Spawacz is explicit; other renderings are proposals. Preserve Fusion in code identifiers. Fusion is FontLab's live boolean filter on an element group: add, subtract, intersect or exclude the overlapping contours while the parts stay editable. Intersect keeps only the overlap; expand the filter to bake the result. Genius node self-balancing node nút thiên tài proposed House voice, derived from nút; nya.vn's điểm thông minh rejected because thông minh is the AI word. A Genius node keeps its curves smooth and balanced automatically when neighbours move; FontLab adjusts its handles for you. A Follower node follows key nodes under Power Nudge. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. grid lưới proposed Apple, Adobe and nya.vn (Lưới – Grid). A grid is a set of regularly spaced reference lines or points used to position drawing objects. Keep it distinct from a mesh used for deformation. Groups nhóm proposed Apple, Microsoft and nya.vn. A group collects several things and treats them as one, and the things differ by product. In FontLab the word most often means a kerning group, the set of glyphs that kern alike, which the documentation also calls a kerning class. In Vexy Vextra, following Illustrator, a group is selected artwork bound into one object. In Vexy Lines a group bundles layers and carries its own source image, working like a folder. TransType adds a styling group that ties a family's styles into a menu. Say which you mean. guide đường gióng proposed Vietnamese design teaching (Mỹ thuật MS, Orion Creative) calls guides đường gióng. Nya.vn's đường dẫn rejected because it also means a file path; hướng dẫn means instructions. A guide is a reference line used to position or align drawing objects. Its name describes its role rather than a visible stroke in the exported glyph. kerning mode chế độ kerning proposed Derived from kerning; nya.vn: chế độ chỉnh sửa Kerning. The editing mode for adjusting spacing between pairs of glyphs. It changes pair adjustments rather than the individual glyph sidebearings. Knife dao proposed Real tool's name; Apple and nya.vn (công cụ dao). The Knife tool works along a line you drag across a shape, and what it leaves behind differs by product and by sub-tool. In FontLab it adds nodes where the line crosses a contour, breaks a closed contour into open paths, or slices one contour into two closed shapes, depending on which of its three sub-tools is active. In Fontographer it cuts through contours along the drawn path. In Vexy Lines it inserts points and splits curves. Say which app, which mode, and what the cut leaves. layer lớp proposed FontForge, GIMP, Krita, Apple and Adobe-related sources; nya.vn glosses Layer as lớp bản vẽ. A layer holds one drawing or part of a document. In FontLab, the context identifies the glyph layer; name the application when another product uses a different layer model. Layers lớp proposed Same word as layer; Vietnamese marks no plural. Layers hold the separate drawings a glyph or a document carries at once. In FontLab a glyph layer holds one master, a mask, or a background, and you manage them in the Layers and Masters panel, where switching layers switches which drawing you edit. In Vexy Lines a layer is a transparent sheet holding one or more fills, and it is the basic unit of a document, since artwork needs at least one. The two meanings sit close enough to be mistaken, so a sentence about layers names the application. mark dấu proposed FontForge vi (neo dấu) and Vietnamese typography writing, where dấu is the everyday word for any accent or tone mark. A mark in glyph positioning is a diacritical glyph positioned in relation to another glyph. A color mark or selection mark is a different interface meaning. Masks mặt nạ proposed Blender vi; nya.vn keeps Layer Mask in English. A mask holds a second drawing, and what it does with that drawing differs by product. In FontLab a mask is a glyph layer carrying a previous version or a reference shape, so you can compare the live outline against it and copy between them; it hides nothing. In Vexy Lines a mask is a vector stencil that decides where a layer's fills can draw, letting the fill through its transparent areas and holding it back elsewhere. Name the application, and in FontLab prefer the full phrase mask layer. match khớp proposed Apple, Blender and FontForge. Match makes selected properties correspond. The object and context determine whether this means synchronizing edits, matching geometry or comparing values. matching khớp nhau proposed Derived from khớp; đối chiếu means to compare. Matching describes objects or properties that correspond. Name the matched property when the interface context does not identify it. Matchmaker master matcher mai mối proposed House voice: the plain Vietnamese word for matchmaking, like Polish swat. Bà mối rejected as gendered; nya.vn keeps Matchmaker. Matchmaker is a FontLab tool for examining and correcting correspondence between glyph masters. It helps align contour order and start points for interpolation. Matching structures does not guarantee that intermediate outlines look right. Inspect the resulting interpolation; changing contour order or a start point can change correspondence without changing the outline's geometry at the master location. measurement line đường đo proposed Derived from đo (to measure); nya.vn: thước đo Measurement Line. A line that shows a measured distance in the drawing. Distinguish this geometric measurement from a metrics line used to calculate sidebearings. measurements số đo proposed Plain word for measured values; kept apart from kích thước (dimensions) and metrics. Values displayed on the canvas to describe geometry, such as coordinates, lengths, angles, tensions and counters. Showing measurements does not modify glyph spacing or font dimensions. Measurements panel bảng Số đo proposed Derived from số đo and bảng (panel). The Measurements panel lists measured dimensions of the current font: stems, serifs, overshoots, contrast and heights, separately for capitals and lowercase. Its labels are compact; translations must not exceed the English length. merge hợp nhất proposed Apple Finder and Illustrator sources. Merge combines items into a result. Name the items and explain what is retained when that distinction matters to the operation. mesh khung lưới proposed Blender vi; keeps mesh distinct from lưới (grid). A mesh is a network of connected points or cells used to describe or deform geometry. It is distinct from a drawing grid used for alignment. metrics mode chế độ metrics proposed nya.vn: chế độ chỉnh sửa Metrics. The editing mode for adjusting glyph advance widths and sidebearings. It changes the spacing of glyphs rather than the vertical dimensions of the font or the visibility of measurements. metrics table bảng metrics proposed nya.vn keeps Metrics Table; derived from metrics. The table of glyph spacing values, including advance widths and sidebearings. It lets the user inspect or edit spacing values together. metrics tool công cụ metrics proposed nya.vn: công cụ Metrics. The tool that edits glyph advance widths and sidebearings. Use it to adjust glyph spacing; canvas measurement overlays display values without changing those spacing values. monospaced đơn cách proposed FontForge vi and nya.vn (Font chữ đơn cách); Apple's giãn cách đơn is the longer alternative. Monospaced describes text or a typeface whose ordinary spacing glyphs have equal advance widths. Marks and special glyphs can have different spacing behavior. multi-line nhiều dòng proposed Plain Vietnamese; no competing term. Multi-line describes text or a control that contains more than one line. It does not imply more than one paragraph. nonspacing zero-width không chiếm chỗ proposed No attestation; fallback "zero-width" put in plain words (takes up no room), since the element stays visible but is ignored in metrics. A nonspacing element or component is excluded from metrics: it stays visible and is exported, but FontLab ignores it when it computes the advance width and sidebearings. Detect nonspacing marks accents and other marks in composites automatically. Nudge push move nhích proposed House voice: the everyday verb for moving something a little; Blender vi also uses nhích. Nudge moves the selected nodes and adjusts the nearby handles so the curve keeps its shape. Power Nudge extends the move to more of the contour. Both are FontLab names. Oblique Oblique proposed Fixed FontLab operation, kept; Apple's xiên names any slanted style. Oblique is FontLab's action that slants a layer and applies a fixed set of optical corrections, so the result is closer to a designed oblique than a plain skew. Keep the name in every language; a plain slant is something else. panel bảng proposed Apple, Illustrator-related sources and Vietnamese Adobe tutorials (bảng Character); nya.vn's bảng điều khiển is too long for labels. The word is shared with font tables. A panel groups related controls or information within an application's interface. It may be docked or floating, depending on the application. Use its displayed name followed by panel in lowercase, as in the Kerning panel. Distinguish panels, windows, dialogs and panes by their role and established product terminology, not solely by whether they float, dock or contain tabs. Pencil bút chì proposed Real tool's name; Apple and nya.vn. The Pencil tool draws freehand, and what it draws on differs by product. In FontLab it converts a freehand gesture into curves and line segments without asking you to think about node types. In Fontographer it is one of three outline drawing tools, beside Pen and Rapid. In Vexy Lines it creates and edits Handmade fills as vector lines. In Vexy Vextra it is the Correcting Pencil, which redraws part of an existing path as readily as it starts a new one. Power Brush power calligraphic brush siêu cọ proposed House voice: siêu is the comic-book word for super (Power Rangers are siêu nhân), and tăng lực, the energy-drink word, is the longer alternative. Derived from cọ. A Power Brush is a brush whose width can vary along the contour through thickness points. It stays live until you expand it. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. Power Guide power guideline siêu đường gióng proposed Same siêu as the other Power names; derived from đường gióng. A Power Guide is a guide that nodes can link to, so moving the guide moves the linked nodes with it. FontLab uses it to keep a stem or a height consistent across a glyph. Each language renders the name with the same playful power. Power Nudge power push move siêu nhích proposed Same siêu as the other Power names; derived from nhích. Nya.vn's di chuyển điểm thông minh is a description. Power Nudge distributes a move through a larger part of a contour by adjusting other nodes as well as the selected ones. FontLab and Vextra provide this editing mode. It differs from Nudge, which adjusts nearby handles. Power Nudge changes the geometry; inspect the result rather than promising an exactly preserved outline or a finished curve. Power Stroke power stroke outline siêu nét proposed Same siêu as the other Power names; Inkscape's nét vẽ quyền lực sounds like political power. A Power Stroke is a stroke whose thickness varies along the path, controlled by thickness points you place with the Thickness tool. The related Power Brush does the same for a brush. Both are FontLab names, rendered in each language's house voice. project dự án approved Team agreement recovered from Proteus QPH on 2026-10-04. Project names the editable document; do not replace it with package. A FontLab project is the editable font document, including the active document in save/close prompts and the document saved to a VFJ/VFC file or project folder or connected to GitHub. Use the project term consistently in this UI. Do not call it a package. Python packages, UFO Packages, Glyphs Packages, and web-font distribution packages are different concepts and retain their format/software terminology. Internal package identifiers and file extensions are not translated. property bar thanh thuộc tính proposed Standard interface wording (thanh + thuộc tính); nya.vn keeps Property Bar. The property bar is FontLab's context-sensitive strip of controls for the current tool or selection. Name the required selection or tool before referring to a control that appears only in that context. Use property bar for this product element; do not invent a universal rule that all toolbars have fixed contents. quick measurement đo nhanh proposed Derived from đo (to measure). The function that displays measurements near the pointer while editing outlines. It reports geometry on the canvas without changing the glyph spacing values. redo làm lại proposed Platform word in Apple and Adobe-related sources. Redo reapplies an operation that was undone. Repeat invokes an operation again and is a separate command. reference tham chiếu proposed Apple, FontForge and nya.vn. A reference points to another object rather than being an independent copy of it. Name the referenced object when the context does not identify it. Remove Overlap merge overlapping contours bỏ chồng lấp proposed FontForge vi: bỏ chỗ chồng lấp, shortened. Remove Overlap combines overlapping filled contour regions and removes their internal boundaries. It changes contour structure, so keep an editable source when the construction matters. Variable fonts can contain overlaps; removing them independently from masters can break point correspondence and interpolation. Apply the command or export option for the intended format and workflow, rather than treating it as mandatory for every font. repeat lặp lại proposed Platform word in Apple; distinct from làm lại (redo). Repeat invokes an operation again. Keep it distinct from Redo, which restores an operation after Undo. reverse contour flip drawing direction đảo chiều đường viền proposed Derived from đường viền and chiều (direction); nya.vn describes Reverse Contour as đảo ngược. Reverse contour flips the winding direction of a contour. PostScript and TrueType outlines use opposite conventions, and a contour that runs the wrong way fills or unfills the wrong region. Scissors kéo proposed Real tool's name; Apple and nya.vn (công cụ kéo). The word is also the verb to drag, so running text should say công cụ Kéo. The Scissors tool works on the joins in a path, and what it does with them differs by product. In FontLab it disconnects nodes into overlapping contours, creates overlaps, adds simple ink traps, and builds looped corners, with a toolbox of sub-tools under the Q shortcut. In Fontographer it breaks contours at selected points or segments, the targeted counterpart to Knife. In Vexy Vextra it extends and rebuilds path parts, building loop corners and joining open ends. Servant node Follower node nút bám theo proposed House voice for Follower node: a node that tags along behind its leaders. Nya.vn's điểm phụ thuộc (dependent point) rejected as the obsolete servant sense. For localization, read the legacy English source label Servant node as Follower node: a follower physically following a leader. This node follows the movement of neighboring key nodes when you move them with Power Nudge, so a whole feature moves together. Translate the motion-following role; the servant and social fan/supporter metaphors are obsolete. The English term and servant-node identifier remain compatibility lookup keys. Sigma Sigma do-not-translate Sigma is the Fontographer tool for variable font interpolation paths, sitting in the toolbar beside Transform and Meter. You use it to work with how a design moves through its variation space rather than to edit a single outline. The name is a single capitalized word and it does not take the word tool inside its name: write the Sigma tool. It is a Fontographer term with no counterpart in the other products. Sketchboard scratch canvas giấy nháp proposed House voice: scratch paper, the everyday thing you doodle on before committing; matches the fallback "scratch canvas". Bảng phác thảo rejected because bảng is the word for a panel. The Sketchboard is FontLab's unlimited canvas, a working surface where you can place glyphs, drawings, and reference images side by side outside the fixed frame of a glyph window. You use it to compare shapes, to sketch before committing, and to lay out material that has no single glyph to live in. The name is one word, capital S, and it is a FontLab term: no other product in the family has the surface or the word. Skin wrapping outline vỏ proposed House voice: the peel or skin of a fruit, like Polish skórka; da is human skin. Skin is a FontLab live filter that wraps a contour with a stroke of variable thickness, or cuts it into dashes. Expand the filter to get plain contours. Each language renders the name in the house voice. smart clever khéo proposed House voice: khéo is the plain word for deft or clever with one's hands and suits a tool. Thông minh is the AI word; lanh and khôn describe people, tinh ranh sounds devious. Smart prefixes FontLab features that decide details for you: Smart Corner, Smart Filter, Smart Pencil, Smart Link, smart fill. Usually translate the word as clever with a hint of cunning. Follow separately approved feature names: the Russian and Ukrainian Smart Filter terms are explicit exceptions. Smart Corner clever corner góc khéo proposed Derived from khéo (smart); nya.vn's góc thông minh rejected because thông minh is the AI word. A Smart Corner is a live treatment applied at a node, so a corner can be rounded, cut, or turned into an ink trap without the outline being redrawn. The treatment stays editable: change the value and the corner updates, and the underlying contour keeps its nodes. You apply it at the node rather than to the whole contour. FontLab groups it with Ink Traps among its live filters, and Vextra carries the same name. Smart Filter Bộ lọc khéo proposed Named glyph-selection filter; not a graphical live effect. Match this term in the Font window, Aidus settings, dialogs and help. A Smart Filter selects glyphs in the Font window using a saved condition. It filters the glyph list rather than changing outlines or applying graphical effects. Follow the language core for its name: Russian and Ukrainian have explicit feature-specific translations that differ from other Smart names. spacing controls side space handles tay cầm giãn cách proposed Derived: fallback "side space handles" with tay cầm (handle) and giãn cách (spacing). Spacing controls are the on canvas handles in the Metrics tool that let you drag sidebearings and advance widths directly in the text. sticker nhãn dán proposed The everyday Vietnamese word for a sticker (messaging apps). A sticker is a visual note you place on a glyph in FontLab, such as a checkmark or a comment, to mark work in progress. Stickers are annotations, not font data, and are not exported. tab tab proposed Apple keeps tab; thẻ is the rarer alternative. A tab selects one page or document within a set. A tab character in text is a different meaning and must retain its literal representation in code. text element text block phần tử văn bản proposed Derived from phần tử. A text element is a live element that renders a string of text from another font inside a glyph. Expanding it converts the letters into contours; FontLab uses it for placeholders and quick layout tests. thickness độ dày proposed Microsoft and Blender; nya.vn: độ dày nét. Thickness is the geometric distance across a stroke or shape. It is distinct from a typeface weight classification or weight axis. Transform biến đổi proposed Illustrator- and Photoshop-related sources; nya.vn: biến đổi hình học. Transform moves, scales, rotates, slants, or flips a selection. In FontLab the Transform panel applies a numeric transformation to glyphs, elements, or a selection, and it can run across a whole font. In Fontographer the Transform tool sits in the toolbar beside Meter and Sigma. In Vexy Lines the Transform tool manipulates artwork on the canvas. A panel, a tool, and a tool again: name the app and name the surface. transformation phép biến đổi proposed Derived from biến đổi; the mathematical noun. A transformation changes geometry, for example by moving, scaling, rotating or skewing it. Transform names the operation; transformation names the change. True Fill final black rendering tô thật proposed House voice: short and plain, the fill as it really is. No attestation; tô đúng is the alternative. True Fill is a Glyph window view that renders the glyph as it will fill when exported, honoring contour direction and overlaps, instead of the editing preview. Each language renders the name in the house voice. uncheck bỏ chọn proposed Platform word in Apple. Uncheck clears a selected checkbox. The resulting behavior depends on the option controlled by that checkbox. Vexy coins Vexy coins do-not-translate Vexy coins are credits used to pay for applicable Fontographer operations. Keep Vexy capitalized and coins lowercase in English. The common noun may translate around the protected Vexy name. State a confirmed charge before the reader performs the operation, and distinguish the credit balance from money, a licence or an account. waterfall size ladder preview thác nước proposed Apple Font Book and Microsoft render the font waterfall as thác nước. A waterfall shows the same glyph or text at a series of sizes, one line per size, to judge spacing and rendering across sizes. The Preview panel and the TrueType hinting tool provide one. weight độ đậm proposed Apple CoreText (Weight = Độ đậm) and FontForge; trọng lượng is physical weight. Weight describes the relative heaviness of a typeface or a value on its weight axis. It is distinct from a measured stroke thickness. whitespace khoảng trắng proposed General software usage; Blender's khoảng trống trắng is redundant. Whitespace is text made up of spacing characters rather than visible letterforms. Preserve literal characters when they form part of code, keys or file content.

docs.title: Vector drawing
docs.text: English Fallback Vietnamese Status Note Definition Appearance panel bảng Appearance proposed Illustrator has no Vietnamese interface, so the reader sees the panel under its English name; only the noun panel is translated. The Appearance panel is Illustrator's list of what is applied to the selected object: its fills, its strokes, and its live effects, in the order they stack. You send a reader there to confirm that a Vexy effect is present, to reorder it against a stroke, or to remove it. It belongs to Illustrator rather than to our products, so its name keeps Illustrator's capitalization and never takes a short form of our making. autotrace bitmap to outline conversion vector hóa tự động proposed Vector hóa is the designers' word for tracing a bitmap (Adobe's vn_vi pages use véc-tơ hóa); Inkscape's tự động truy tìm rejected as a mistranslation of trace. Autotrace converts a bitmap into vector paths by finding the edges in the image and fitting curves to them. The result depends on what you feed it: a clean, high contrast source traces well, and a soft or noisy one produces nodes nobody wants to edit. You prepare the image first, trace, then simplify. Tracing to outlines gives closed shapes with two edges, and tracing to centerlines gives single paths with a stroke. centerline đường tâm proposed Standard technical-drawing term for a centre line; Microsoft's bẫy đường trục is unrelated. A centerline runs down the middle of a stroke rather than around its edge, so the result is a single path with a stroke weight instead of a closed outline. Tracing to centerlines suits line art, engravings, and anything that was drawn as strokes in the first place. You choose it over outline tracing when the artwork will be scaled or restroked later, since a centerline keeps one editable path where an outline gives you two edges to maintain. clipping mask mặt nạ cắt proposed Derived from mặt nạ; a common rendering of clipping mask in Vietnamese design tutorials, not checked against a foundry source. A clipping mask is a shape that limits what is visible of the elements below it. Name the application: in FontLab it is an element property; a FontLab Mask layer is something else. control point control handle point điểm điều khiển proposed Blender and QCAD use điểm điều khiển. A control point is an off-curve point that pulls a Bézier segment toward itself without lying on the outline. You drag it to change the curvature between two nodes. FontLab shows control points as handles attached to their nodes, so in interface text the handle is what you drag and the control point is what the file stores. Fill Grid grid of fill lines lưới tô proposed Derived from lưới + tô; fallback "grid of fill lines" has no Vietnamese attestation. The Fill Grid is the area of the Linestra panel where you choose a fill mode from a grid of previews. Below it sit the parameter rows, which hold Thickness, Spacing, Angle, Organic, Brightness, Contrast, and Source Levels. You pick in the grid first, because the parameter rows change with the mode you choose. Both words are capitalized: it is a named part of the interface rather than a description of a grid. fill mode line fill style chế độ tô proposed Derived from tô; Blender's chế độ tô phủ kín is longer than needed. A fill mode is one of the named techniques that turn a source image into line work: Linear, Wave, Circular, Spiral, Halftone, Stipple, Hex, Contour, Low-Poly, Dither, Wireframe, Fractal, String Art, and ASCII among them.
