Use Vexy Lines for the current product and retain Strokes Maker when identifying a historical release or explaining the name change. Do not rename an old interface label inside a quotation. studio.fontlab.com studio.fontlab.com do-not-translate studio.fontlab.com is an unconfirmed service address in the naming register. Keep it draft and do not direct readers there without confirmation of the destination and its availability. A recorded spelling does not establish that a service exists. TransType 5 TransType 5 do-not-translate TransType 5 names version 5 of the font conversion application. Keep TransType as one word with capital T in both parts, followed by one space and the version. Use TransType after establishing the version; declare TrT before using it as a short form. TypeTool TypeTool do-not-translate TypeTool is a protected Fontlab Ltd. product name, written as one word with two capital Ts. Preserve that spelling when naming the product or quoting a notice. Confirm the relevant version before describing its features or compatibility. Vexy Vexy do-not-translate Vexy is the family prefix in Vexy Lines, Vexy Linestra, Vexy Playlines and Vexy Vextra. It is not a standalone application name. Identify the product when describing an operation; retain Vexy alone when it is the exact name of an interface category. Vexy Lines Vexy Lines do-not-translate Vexy Lines is the standalone desktop application for converting a bitmap into vector artwork through algorithmic fills. Keep the full two-word name. Distinguish it from Vexy Playlines, the browser application, and from the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins. Its native project format is .lines. Vexy Linestra Vexy Linestra do-not-translate Vexy Linestra is the Adobe Illustrator plug-in for parametric line fills. Use the two-word product name in prose. Preserve the closed spelling VexyLinestra in an exact filename such as VexyLinestra.aip; a filename spelling does not replace the product name. Vexy Playlines Vexy Playlines do-not-translate Vexy Playlines is the browser application for converting images into vector artwork at playlines.vexy.art. Use the full name in titles and on first mention, then Playlines where unambiguous. Keep it distinct from Vexy Lines, the desktop application. Vexy Vextra Vexy Vextra do-not-translate Vexy Vextra is the Adobe Illustrator plug-in for contour editing. Use the full name in a title and on first mention; Vextra is the declared short form. Preserve VexyVextra in an exact filename such as VexyVextra.aip.

docs.title: Type design
docs.text: English Fallback Chinese (Traditional) Status Note Definition ascender upward extension 上伸部 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), justfont's blog, Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and InDesign zh-TW all use 上伸部; the mainland 上升部 is not used in Taiwan. An ascender is the part of a lowercase letter that extends above the x-height, as in b or d. Ascender height describes the intended alignment of these parts and may differ from cap height. Do not confuse this design measurement with similarly named vertical metrics in exported font tables. Line spacing depends on those fields and on the application using them. baseline writing line 基線 proposed Universal: jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), Glyphs 3 zh-Hant, Adobe and Apple zh-TW. A baseline is a reference line used to align text. In conventional horizontal Latin font design, the baseline is at y = 0, with ascenders above it and descenders below it. Other scripts and layout systems can use different baseline conventions. Identify the relevant baseline when discussing alignment across scripts or vertical text. bowl round belly 字碗 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) lists bowl as 字碗; Apple's shape name 碗 is the wrong sense. A bowl is a rounded stroke that encloses a counter, as in b, d or p. Its shape, thickness and junctions affect the letter's balance. The appropriate number of curve segments depends on the design. Nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting, but a fixed segment count does not guarantee compatible masters or good interpolation. cap height capital-letter height 大寫字高 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), justfont's blog and Glyphs 3 zh-Hant use 大寫字高. Cap height is the distance from the baseline to the top of a flat capital such as H. Rounded or pointed capitals may extend beyond it through overshoot. Record the intended value in Font Info. Cap height describes a design measurement; alignment zones and line-spacing metrics are separate settings, even when their values are related. character 字元 proposed Universal in Taiwan (Apple, Adobe, Microsoft, justfont); kept distinct from 字符, the glyph. The mainland uses 字符 for character, so the two catalogs must not be converted mechanically. A character is an abstract unit of written text, such as a letter or punctuation mark. A glyph is its visual representation. The relationship is not one to one: several characters can form a ligature, and a character can have several glyph forms. A user-perceived character can also consist of several Unicode codepoints. Keep characters, codepoints and glyphs distinct when discussing encoding or text processing. contour 輪廓 proposed FontForge zh_TW uses 輪廓 for one contour (命名輪廓, 關閉開放輪廓); Glyphs 3 zh-Hant says 路徑 and 外框. Unlike Simplified, Taiwan usage lets contour (輪廓) and outline (外框) keep separate words. A contour is an open or closed sequence of connected line and curve segments. Its nodes and control points describe its geometry. One glyph or vector object can contain several contours. A counter is an area of space, not a synonym for a contour. When explaining fill behaviour, identify the outline format and fill rule before prescribing a contour direction. counter enclosed white space 字腔 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) and justfont's blog use 字腔 for counter, closed or open; 字懷 is their word for the Hanzi concept and 計數器 is the office-suite sense. A counter is the enclosed or partly enclosed space within a letterform, such as the enclosed space in an o or the open space in a c. The surrounding strokes define it. A closed counter may have an inner contour as its boundary; an open counter does not require a separate contour. Judge its size and shape together with the surrounding strokes. descender downward extension 下伸部 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), justfont's blog, Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and InDesign zh-TW all use 下伸部. A descender is the part of a letter that extends below the baseline, as in p or y. Its design height is usually recorded as a negative coordinate relative to the baseline. Exported descender metrics are separate fields used by applications for layout. Whether a deep glyph clips depends on the relevant metrics, application and text container, not on one design value alone. diacritical mark combining mark 變音符號 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts and Apple zh-TW use 變音符號; 附加符號 is the alternative. A diacritical mark is a small sign, such as an acute or a cedilla, that attaches to a base letter to form another character. FontLab builds accented glyphs from a base and a mark through anchors, and the GDEF mark class tells the shaper which glyphs are marks. Say mark glyph for the class member and diacritical mark for the sign. em type body 字身框 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) calls the design square 字身框; same concept as the Simplified decision. justfont's blog and FontForge zh_TW leave em in Latin script for the unit, which is the alternative. The em is the square on which a typeface is designed, historically the body of the letter M in metal type. Its height equals the type size, so an em in 12 point text is 12 points. In a digital font the em is divided into UPM font units. extremum local extreme point 極值點 proposed Mathematical term, shared with the Simplified decision; FontForge zh_TW's 末端 is a mistranslation. No Taiwan type source found, so check with a reviewer whether 極點 is preferred. An extremum is a point where a curve reaches a local leftmost, rightmost, topmost or bottommost position. The plural is extrema. Placing nodes at extrema can help editing and hinting. If you add nodes to masters intended for interpolation, preserve the correspondence between their contours and points. Different extremum positions alone do not make masters incompatible. glyph 字符 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) (字符 Glyph), Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and InDesign zh-TW use 字符; Apple zh-TW's 字形 is justfont's word for letterform and FontForge zh_TW's 字圖 is isolated. Departs from the Simplified 字形 on regional evidence. A glyph is one drawn shape in a font: a letter, a figure, a mark, or a piece of a composite. A character is what a reader types and a glyph is what a renderer draws, and one character can map to several glyphs while several characters can map to one. You edit a glyph in the Glyph window, where its contours, elements, anchors, and metrics all live together. The distinction matters in any sentence about encoding, since a font maps codepoints to glyphs through the cmap table. handle 控制桿 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's Glyphs 101 tutorials and Blender zh_HANT use 控制桿; Adobe zh-TW's 控制把手 and 方向控制點 are the alternatives, and 控制代碼 is the programming sense. A handle is an off-curve control point used to shape a curve segment. A cubic Bézier segment has two control points; a quadratic segment has one. Moving a handle changes the curve without moving its endpoints. In tools that display handle arms, the arm connects a control point to an endpoint. Name the curve type when the number or behaviour of handles matters. ink trap ink relief notch 墨溝 proposed justfont's blog glosses ink trap as 墨溝; 油墨陷阱 is the literal mainland rendering. An ink trap is a notch cut into a corner where strokes meet, so ink spread or rasterization at small sizes does not clog the join. FontLab makes them as a live Smart Corner variant. italic angle slant angle 斜體角度 proposed FontForge zh_TW uses 斜體角度 and 斜體 is the Apple, Adobe and Microsoft zh-TW word for italic; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 義大利體斜角 is the alternative. The italic angle is the slope of the upright strokes of an italic or oblique design, measured from the vertical in degrees. FontLab stores it in Font Info, uses it to slant guides and the cursor, and writes it into the post and hhea tables. It is a property of the design, not of a transformation. lining figures capital-height figures 等高數字 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) uses 等高數字; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 齊高數字 and InDesign's 齊線 are the alternatives. Lining figures are digits that share the cap height and sit on the baseline, so they align with capitals in tables and headlines. The lnum feature selects them where a font defaults to oldstyle figures. node 節點 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's Glyphs 101 and Inkscape zh_TW use 節點; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 控制點 rejected because it must name the off-curve control point. A node is a point on a contour where segments meet, and its type decides how they meet. A sharp node lets two segments arrive at any angle. A smooth node keeps the handles collinear so the curve passes through without a kink. A tangent node joins a line to a curve smoothly. A G2 node matches curvature as well as direction. You select a node and drag it, or nudge it, and the segments on both sides follow. Put nodes at the extremes so hinting and interpolation have something to hold. overshoot optical surplus 出框微調整 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), justfont's blog (出框微調整, overshoot) and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 出框微調整; Blender's 過衝 is the engineering sense. Overshoot is the extension of a rounded or pointed shape beyond an alignment line so that it appears as tall as a flat shape. For example, an o may extend above the x-height and below the baseline. Its amount depends on the design and intended size. PostScript alignment zones can describe these overshoot regions for hinting; there is no universal percentage to apply. proportional figures natural-width figures 比例寬數字 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant uses 比例寬數字; InDesign's 等比 rejected. Proportional figures have individual advance widths, so a 1 takes less room than an 8. They read well in running text; tabular figures share one width for columns. The pnum feature selects them. segment 線段 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant, Yin Tzu-Yuan and Inkscape zh_TW use 線段. A segment is the portion of a contour between two on-curve endpoints. It may be a straight line or a curve. A quadratic Bézier segment has one off-curve control point; a cubic segment has two. Describe the segment type and the relevant editing command rather than assuming that every curve has two handles or that changing a node type performs every conversion. serif 襯線 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) and FontForge zh_TW use 襯線 for the serif itself; 襯線體 names the typeface class. A serif is the finishing stroke at the end of a stem or arm. Its shape sorts a face into the familiar classes: oldstyle, transitional, Didone, slab. You draw a serif once and reuse it as a component or an element, which keeps a family consistent and makes a late change cheap. Serifs are small, so they take the most damage at low resolution, which is where hinting and careful alignment zones earn their place. sharp 尖角 proposed Adobe zh-TW uses 尖角 for a pointed corner; 銳利 and 銳利化 are image-sharpening words. Sharp describes a pointed corner or a node at which contour direction can change abruptly. Image sharpening is a different operation. sharp node 尖角節點 proposed Built from 尖角 and 節點. A sharp node joins contour segments without requiring a smooth change of direction. The handles of adjacent segments need not be collinear; a smooth node constrains their direction. stem main stroke 字幹 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and FontForge zh_TW use 字幹. A stem is a main stroke of a letter, usually the vertical one: the two uprights of an H, the single upright of an l. Stem width sets the weight of a face, and stems that disagree across a family break its rhythm. You measure a stem with the Measurement tool and record the standard widths in Font Info, where hinting and the stem links read them. Vextra reuses the word for the paired edges it detects in general artwork, not only in letters. swash flourish 花飾字 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant, Apple CoreText and InDesign zh-TW use 花飾字. A swash is a decorative flourish that extends a letter, often on a capital or a terminal. Swash alternates live in the swsh feature and in glyphs with a swash suffix. terminal stroke ending 末端 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) describes serifs as sitting at the 筆畫末端; its anatomy table gives 端點 for terminal, which is rejected here only because 端點 is the stroke cap. 終端機 is the computer terminal. A terminal is the end of a stroke without a serif, such as the ending of a c or f. Its shape may be rounded, angled or cut off, depending on the design. Compare related terminals across a typeface at the intended reading size. The anatomical term does not prescribe how to construct or store the shape in an editor. UPM units per type body UPM proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant keeps the acronym (變更 UPM, 調整至UPM); spell out as 每字身框單位數 in prose. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. UPM, units per em, specifies how many font units make up one em. It sets the scale for outline coordinates and metrics when a renderer converts them to a text size. Values such as 1000 and 2048 are common; TrueType outlines do not require a power of two. When changing UPM, distinguish changing the scale value from rescaling the outlines and metrics. winding direction drawing direction 輪廓方向 proposed Fallback drawing direction translated with 輪廓; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant says 外框方向 and Adobe 路徑方向. Winding direction is the order in which a contour runs, clockwise or counter-clockwise, and it decides which areas the renderer fills. FontLab follows the PostScript convention: outer contours wind counter-clockwise and counters wind clockwise. The letter O is two contours, one each way. You check direction before you export, and reverse a contour when a counter fills solid or an outer shape turns hollow. A renderer applies the rule at draw time, so the error shows in the proof rather than in the editor. x-height small-letter height x 字高 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), justfont's blog and Glyphs 3 zh-Hant use x 字高; FontForge zh_TW's 小寫字母高度 rejected. The x-height is the height of a lowercase x above the baseline, and it stands for the height of the lowercase in general. It does more for apparent size than the point size does: two faces at the same size look different when their x-heights differ. You record it in Font Info so hinting and alignment zones can use it, and you draw round letters slightly above it to allow for overshoot. Write it lowercase with a hyphen, even at the start of a sentence recast to avoid one.

docs.title: Font engineering
docs.text: English Fallback Chinese (Traditional) Status Note Definition advance height 直排字高 proposed Vertical counterpart of 字寬; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 垂直字高 and 垂直高度 for Vertical Width and uses 直排 for vertical setting. FontForge zh_TW's 垂直前加 rejected. The distance the text position advances vertically after a glyph. It is the vertical counterpart of advance width, not the height of the visible outline. advance width glyph box width 字寬 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant uses 字寬 for the glyph's advance (設定字寬, 左邊界+字寬); justfont's blog spells it out as 步進寬度, the form for explanatory prose. FontForge zh_TW's 前加寬度 rejected. Advance width is the horizontal distance allocated to a glyph before layout adjustments, measured in font units. In an OpenType font, the base values are stored in the hmtx table. Kerning and other positioning operations can adjust advances during layout without rewriting those base values. Advance width differs from the visible outline width; a space can have an advance without an outline. alignment zone height band for snapping 對齊區域 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts use 對齊區域. An alignment zone is a region around a common vertical alignment, such as the baseline or cap height, used in PostScript hinting. It can include the overshoot of rounded letters. A rasterizer uses zone information when fitting outlines to a pixel grid. Keep this mechanism distinct from design measurements and from the control-value and instruction mechanisms used in TrueType hinting. anchor attachment point 錨點 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant, FontForge zh_TW and Yin Tzu-Yuan's tutorials all use 錨點. An anchor is a named attachment point in a glyph that says where a mark belongs. A base letter carries a top anchor, and the accent carries a matching one, so the accent lands in the same relation on every letter that uses it. You place anchors in the Anchors and Pins panel, and FontLab uses them both to build composites and to generate mark attachment lookups in GPOS, which is what positions marks in text the font never composed itself. anti-aliasing edge smoothing 消除鋸齒 proposed FontForge zh_TW uses 消除鋸齒, the usual Adobe zh-TW wording; Krita's 反鋸齒 and 抗鋸齒 are the alternatives. Anti-aliasing paints partly covered pixels in intermediate shades so a rendered outline looks smooth. FontLab's preview can show anti-aliased, monochrome or subpixel rendering so you can check how hints behave under each. Write the hyphenated form. autohinting automatic screen fitting 自動 Hinting proposed Built from 自動 and the retained loan Hinting; justfont's blog also leaves hinting in English. Autohinting generates hints for a font from its outlines and its declared stems and zones, in one pass over the glyphs. It is a starting point rather than a finish: it hints the regular cases well and leaves the awkward glyphs for you. You run it after the alignment zones and standard stem widths are correct in Font Info, because it reads them. Then you check the glyphs that matter at text sizes and correct by hand what the pass got wrong. axis 變化軸 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan all call a variation axis 變化軸; bare 軸 is kept for compounds (字重軸). FontForge zh_TW's 軸線 and Microsoft's 座標軸 rejected. An axis is one dimension of font variation, such as weight, width or optical size. In an OpenType variable font, each axis has a four-character tag and a minimum, default and maximum value. Registered tags, such as wght, have defined meanings. Preserve tag spelling and case, and check the axis registry when assigning a custom tag. axis map axis value mapping 變化軸對應 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant renders Axis Mappings as 變化軸對應. An axis map converts user coordinates on an axis, such as weight 400, to the design coordinates of the masters. It is stored in the avar table and lets a slider feel even when masters are not. bottom sidebearing 下留白 proposed Derived from 留白; FontForge zh_TW has 底留白 for BBearing. The space below the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. component 組件 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 組件; 元件, the general software word (Adobe, Microsoft), rejected to keep component apart from element. A component is a reference to another glyph placed inside this one, so that aacute holds the a and the acute rather than copies of their outlines. Change the source glyph and every glyph that references it follows. You build composites from components, position them with anchors, and keep them as references through to export, where a TrueType flavoured font stores them in the glyf table. In FontLab a component is one kind of element reference. composite glyph assembled glyph 組合字符 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts say 組合字符 and FontForge zh_TW 組合字圖; the Simplified 复合 has no Taiwan attestation. A composite glyph is built from references to other glyphs rather than from its own outlines: an accented letter, a currency symbol with a bar, a stacked fraction. You assemble it from components and anchor them to the base, so a change to the base or to the mark reaches every composite that uses it. Composites keep a large accented character set consistent and small. A composite that has been decomposed is no longer one, and no longer follows its sources. conversion profile export settings set 轉換設定檔 proposed No attestation; fallback translated. 設定檔 is the Microsoft zh-TW word for a profile; Apple's 描述檔 is the alternative. A conversion profile is the saved set of choices TransType applies to a conversion: the output format, the naming scheme, the filters, and the options that go with them. You build a profile once for a job you repeat, then run it over a new set of sources without repeating the decisions. It matters because a family converted with two different sets of options ships as two families that do not quite match, which shows up in a font menu rather than in a test. CVT table CVT 表 proposed Tag protected, noun translated; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant uses 表 for every font table (kern表, STAT表). The CVT table holds the control values that TrueType hinting instructions refer to: the stem widths, heights, and other measurements a font wants held constant across glyphs. An instruction cites a CVT entry rather than a raw number, so one change to the table reaches every glyph that cites it. You work with it through the TrueType Hinting panel. It ships in the font, alongside the instructions themselves and the prep and fpgm programs that set the machine up. design space variation range 設計空間 proposed Literal and transparent; follows the Simplified decision. No Taiwan-specific attestation found. A design space describes the positions defined by a font project's variation axes. Masters provide source data at specified locations; instances represent results at selected locations. User coordinates and internal design coordinates may be connected by a mapping, or may have the same values. State which coordinate system a number belongs to when the distinction affects a procedure. device correction per-size pixel correction 裝置修正 proposed No fixed term; FontForge zh_TW speaks of 裝置表格, combined with 修正. A device correction adjusts a kerning or positioning value by whole pixels at one pixel size, to fix rounding at that size only. Stored in GPOS device tables; rarely needed on modern rasterizers. dimensions 尺寸 proposed Plain word for the set of vertical values; kept apart from 度量 (metrics) and 測量 (measurements). The font or family vertical values, such as ascender, descender, capital height, x-height and line gap. Distinguish these values from glyph spacing and canvas measurements. element 元素 proposed Standard rendering (Microsoft zh-TW, Blender, Krita); 元件 rejected because Adobe and Microsoft use it for components. An element is FontLab's container for a piece of drawing inside a glyph: one or more contours, an image, or a reference to another element. A glyph holds elements, and an element holds contours, which is the layer of structure that makes a serif or a stem reusable across a family. You work with elements in the Elements panel and with the Element tool. The word is FontLab's own; other editors call the nearest thing a path group or a component. element reference shared drawing link 元素參照 proposed Built from 元素 and 參照 (FontForge zh_TW uses 參照 for glyph references). An element reference is a placed copy of an element that still points at the original. Edit the original and every reference updates. You use references to share a serif, a stem, or a whole letter across a family, and you decompose a reference only when a glyph genuinely needs to diverge. A component is the familiar case of an element reference: one glyph placed inside another. Keep references intact through the design phase, since decomposing early throws away the link that makes a late change cheap. family dimensions 家族尺寸 proposed 家族 is the family word in Glyphs 3 zh-Hant (家族名稱) and justfont (字型家族); 尺寸 from dimensions. The vertical values used to establish line layout for a font family. Platform-specific ascender, descender and line-gap fields belong to this group. Flex Flex proposed Fixed PostScript hint name, kept as the glossary asks; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 彎曲 rejected. Flex is a PostScript hint that flattens a shallow curve, such as a cup serif, to a straight line at small sizes. FontLab marks glyphs that carry it. Keep the name. font dimensions 字型尺寸 proposed Built from 字型 and 尺寸 (dimensions). The design dimensions of a font master, including ascender, descender, capital height and x-height. These values describe the vertical proportions of the design. font target export target 目標字型 proposed No attestation; fallback translated, as French police cible. A font target is what TransType produces from a source: the output font, with its format, its names, and the filters applied on the way. Sources go in on one side and targets come out on the other, and one source can produce several targets. You set the target options before you convert, and you name the target in a procedure step so a reader knows which side of the conversion a setting belongs to. font unit 字型單位 proposed Common engineering term; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 單位 for font units. A font unit is the coordinate step of a font's design grid. UPM says how many of them make one em, so a 700 unit stem in a 1000 UPM font is 70 percent of the em. Metrics, kerning values and node coordinates are all stated in font units. fractional coordinates non-integer coordinates 小數座標 proposed No attestation; plain mathematical wording for non-integer coordinates, with the Taiwan spelling 座標. Fractional coordinates are node positions with decimal places, kept for curve fidelity while you draw. Font formats store integers, so FontLab rounds on export or when you turn on Round coordinates for the font. friendly glyph name readable glyph name 易懂字符名稱 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant calls nice names 易懂名稱 (建立字符的易懂名稱); FontForge zh_TW's 易記名稱 is the alternative. A friendly glyph name is the readable name FontLab shows for editing, such as Aacute, as opposed to the production name written into the exported font, such as uni00C1. FontLab can keep both and convert on export. ghost hint edge-only fitting instruction Ghost Hint proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant keeps the term in Latin script (上端 Ghost Hint, 建立 Ghost Hint); an attested loan, unlike the unattested 幽靈 Hint. A ghost hint is a PostScript hint with a special width that marks one edge, such as the top of a round letter, when there is no stem to hint. It aligns that edge to an alignment zone. hint screen fitting instruction Hint proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant keeps Hint in Latin script throughout (新增 Hint, 字幹 Hint) and the glossary says the word stays English; capitalised as the zh-TW guide asks for retained English words. Departs from the Simplified 渲染提示, which has no Taiwan attestation; FontForge zh_TW's 渲調 and Microsoft's 提示 rejected. A hint is a stored instruction that tells a rasterizer how to align a stem or a zone to the pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hints describe stems and zones; TrueType hints are instructions. FontLab draws hints in the Glyph window and generates them with autohinting. The word stays English in every language. hint zone hinting height band Hint 區域 proposed Built from the retained loan Hint and 區域 (Glyphs 3 zh-Hant: 對齊區域, 無指定區域); kept distinct from the PostScript 對齊區域. A hint zone is a horizontal band, such as the baseline or the x-height, inside which a rasterizer snaps overshoots to the same pixel row. FontLab stores zones in Font Info and shows them in the Glyph window. An alignment zone is the PostScript name for the same thing; hint zone is the general term. hinting screen fitting Hinting proposed justfont's blog and Glyphs 3 zh-Hant leave the word in English; Wikipedia's 字體微調 and Microsoft's 字型微調 rejected because 微調 also names kerning and nudging. Hinting is the extra information a font carries so that its outlines land predictably on a pixel grid at small sizes. PostScript hinting declares stems and alignment zones and leaves the rasterizer to interpret them. TrueType hinting gives instructions that move points explicitly, with the control values in the CVT table. You work on PostScript hints in the glyph and in Font Info, and on TrueType hints with the TrueType Hinting tool and panel. Autohinting produces a starting point you then correct. instance generated design 實體 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 實體 (新增實體, 匯出實體); InDesign's 實例 and Microsoft's 執行個體 rejected. An instance is a particular result at a location in a font's variation space. A named instance, such as Semibold, gives a selected location a name that applications can present. Other locations need not have names. In FontLab, configured instances can be exported as static fonts or included as named instances in a variable font. interpolation 內插 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant (內插, 重新內插) and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 內插; Blender's 插補 and the mainland 插值 rejected. Interpolation calculates values between source values. In font design, it can calculate outlines, metrics and other data from masters at specified design-space locations. Outline interpolation requires corresponding contour and point structures. Structural compatibility makes the calculation possible, but does not guarantee a good drawing: inspect intermediate results as well as the masters. Extrapolation calculates beyond the source range. kern exception pair spacing exception 調距例外 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts use 調距例外. A kern exception is a pair value that overrides what the classes would otherwise apply. One member of a class rarely behaves like the rest, and the exception says so without breaking the class apart. You create one in the Kerning panel by kerning the single pair while its classes stay in place. Keep exceptions few: a class with many exceptions is the wrong class, and the cheaper fix is to split it rather than to list every disagreement. kerning pair spacing correction 調距 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan's Glyphs 101 (間距和調距) use 調距, the working word of Taiwan type designers and the shortest. 字距微調 (FontForge zh_TW, Adobe zh-TW), justfont's 字間微調整 and InDesign's 字元間距微調 are the alternatives. Kerning adjusts the spacing of particular glyph combinations beyond their normal advances. A pair such as AV may need a different gap from the one produced by its unadjusted metrics. OpenType fonts commonly store horizontal kerning in GPOS lookups associated with the kern feature; some formats and workflows use a separate kern table. Name the mechanism when it matters to export or compatibility. kerning class pair spacing group 調距類別 proposed Built from 調距 and 類別, the word for class in Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and FontForge zh_TW (字距微調類別); Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 調距群組 translates kerning group. A kerning class groups glyphs that need the same kerning. You put every glyph that behaves alike on one side into one class, then kern the class once instead of kerning each pair inside it. FontLab applies the class value to every member pair and keeps single pairs as exceptions where a member needs its own value. Classes matter because a text face carries thousands of readable pairs, and a hand kerned list of that size is unmaintainable. FontLab writes the result into GPOS as class based positioning. kerning pair spacing-corrected pair 調距配對 proposed Built from 調距 and 配對 (FontForge zh_TW: 字距微調配對). A kerning pair associates two glyphs, or two kerning classes, with a spacing adjustment. In horizontal kerning, a negative value normally reduces the gap and a positive value increases it. An individual glyph pair may provide an exception to class kerning, but it can also exist without a class rule. Check pairs in representative text as well as in isolation. left sidebearing 左留白 proposed justfont's blog (左留白, left side bearing) and FontForge zh_TW use 左留白; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 左邊界 rejected with 邊界. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the glyph origin and the left edge of its outline. It contributes to the glyph advance width and its spacing. Lib Lib proposed Name of the UFO lib dictionary, kept as an identifier as in the reviewed languages. Lib is the custom metadata dictionary of a font or a master, mirroring the UFO lib and stored in VFJ. Scripts and tools keep their own keys there. line gap 行距 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) defines 行距 (Line Gap) as the gap between one line's descender line and the next line's ascender line. The line gap is extra vertical space between lines that a font recommends beyond ascender and descender. hhea and OS/2 each store one. line height 行高 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) and Glyphs 3 zh-Hant use 行高. The distance between successive text baselines. It includes the relevant ascender, descender and line-gap contributions; line gap alone is only the additional space. link metrics tie spacing to another glyph 連結度量 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant renders Link Metrics With Master as 將度量連結到主板; shortened. Link metrics ties a glyph's sidebearing or advance width to another glyph or to an expression, so the value follows its source. FontLab shows linked metrics with the expression and updates them when the source changes. linked metrics 連動度量 proposed Built from 度量 on the model of the Simplified 联动量度; no Taiwan attestation for the compound. Glyph spacing values linked to another glyph or to an expression. Updating the source or expression changes the dependent advance width or sidebearings. mark attachment combining mark positioning 標號定位 proposed Built from 標號; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 標號位置 for Mark Positioning. FontForge zh_TW's 標記附件 is a mistranslation. Mark attachment positions a combining mark relative to a base glyph, a ligature component or another mark. OpenType GPOS lookups describe the anchor relationships, and the shaping engine applies the positioning during layout. FontLab can generate attachment code from suitable anchors. Check the relevant generation settings and test combinations, including stacked marks, rather than assuming that every anchor automatically becomes a lookup. master source design 主板 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant wavers between 主板 and 主版; Yin Tzu-Yuan's Glyphs 101 and zh-TW scripts use 主板 throughout (多主板). 母版 is the mainland term and Microsoft's 母片 is the slide-master sense. A master provides source outlines and other font data at a specified location in a design space. Masters can describe weight, width or other variations, including intermediate locations. FontLab uses corresponding data from masters to calculate instances. For outline interpolation, check contour and point compatibility in each affected glyph; the word master alone does not guarantee that every glyph is present or compatible. master compatibility matching master structure 主板相容性 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 主版相容性; respelled with the chosen 主板. Master compatibility is the condition every glyph must meet before it can interpolate: the same number of contours in the same order, with the same number of nodes and the same start point in each. FontLab reports incompatible glyphs and gives you Matchmaker to repair them by matching contours and start points between masters. Fix compatibility before you tune shapes, because a repair that reorders nodes moves every curve that depends on them. metrics 度量 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant (顯示度量, 匯入度量資訊) and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 度量; Glyphs' stray 規格框, FontForge zh_TW's 字框 and Apple's 測量指標 rejected. Metrics are the measurements that place a glyph in a line: its advance width and its two sidebearings. Vertical metrics are a separate set, the font wide values for ascender, descender, and line gap. You work on horizontal metrics in the Metrics panel and with the Metrics tool, and on vertical metrics in Font Info. Say which set you mean whenever a page discusses both, because a reader who applies a horizontal instruction to the vertical fields breaks line spacing everywhere the font is used. metrics expression 度量運算式 proposed Built from 度量 and 運算式, the Taiwan word for an expression. An expression that calculates a glyph advance width or sidebearing from other values. It describes a spacing relationship rather than a canvas measurement. metrics key 度量鍵 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Yin Tzu-Yuan use 度量鍵 for metrics keys. A glyph reference or expression used to derive a spacing value. The referenced value determines an advance width or sidebearing. pin 圖釘 proposed Issue 160 catalog family review: named point inside an element, distinct from a glyph-layer anchor. Proteus Resources/helptips.json def.anchorpin defines the behavior. Preserve this term across panel, tool, action and help labels; proposed terminology, not native-team approval. A pin is a named point inside an element. Use pins to position elements with expressions and to attach elements to each other. An anchor is a named point in a glyph layer, used for component placement and mark attachment. Create either with the Guides tool and edit it in the Anchors and Pins panel. PPM pixels per type body PPM proposed Acronym kept in hinting fields; spell out as 每字身框像素數 in prose. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. PPM, pixels per em, is the size at which a rasterizer renders a font: how many pixels one em occupies. TrueType hints, device corrections and bitmap strikes are specified per PPM. In explanatory prose expand it; in hinting fields the short form is usual. production glyph name shipping glyph name 發行用字符名稱 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 建立發行用的字符名稱; its other renderings (輸出用名稱, 產品化名稱, 產品名稱) are inconsistent. A production glyph name is the name written into the exported font, chosen for compatibility with tools and the Adobe Glyph List, such as uni00C1 rather than Aacute. rendering drawing on screen 渲染 proposed justfont's blog (字型的渲染引擎) uses 渲染; 算繪 and Microsoft's 轉譯 are the alternatives. Rendering is the conversion of an outline into pixels on a screen or a printer. The rasterizer of the operating system or of FontLab's preview reads the outline, applies the hints and paints the result. FontLab previews rendering at chosen pixel sizes so you can judge hints. Rasterization names the same step from the pixel side. required glyphs mandatory glyphs 必要字符 proposed No attestation; fallback mandatory glyphs translated. Required glyphs are the ones the OpenType specification and common tools expect at the start of a font: .notdef, NULL or uni0000, CR or uni000D and space. FontLab can add them on export. right sidebearing 右留白 proposed justfont's blog (右留白, right side bearing) uses 右留白; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 右邊界 rejected with 邊界. Keep numeric controls compact: LSB/RSB (French AG/AD), UPM and PPM. Expanded terms belong in explanatory help; the full Family Dimensions Units Per eM label is an intentional exception. Team UI convention in Proteus 1751b28b0. The horizontal space between the right edge of a glyph outline and the end of its advance width. It contributes to spacing. sidebearing side space 側邊留白 proposed FontForge zh_TW renders Side Bearings as 側邊留白 and justfont's blog calls the sidebearing 留白; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 邊界 rejected because it also means bounds (圖層邊界). A sidebearing is the space between a glyph's outline and the edge of its advance width: the left sidebearing before the shape, the right sidebearing after it. Together with the advance width it sets how the glyph spaces against every other glyph, which is the work that carries a text face further than kerning does. You edit sidebearings in the Metrics panel or with the Metrics tool, one glyph at a time or across a selection, and you check them in a word rather than in isolation. size 大小 proposed Plain interface word (Apple, Microsoft zh-TW). The size of an object or the chosen size of displayed text. Name a specific width or height when only one direction is intended. spacing 間距 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's Glyphs 101 titles the lesson 間距和調距 (Spacing & Kerning); Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 空間 is a mistranslation. The Simplified 字间距 would read as tracking next to 字距調整. The adjustment of glyph advance widths and sidebearings to establish the space between letters. Kerning makes additional adjustments to particular pairs. standard stem reference stem width 標準字幹 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts use 標準字幹. Standard stems are the representative horizontal and vertical stem widths declared in a font for hinting. The rasterizer snaps stems near those widths to the same pixel count, so like stems stay alike at small sizes. stem link stem tie 字幹連結 proposed Built from 字幹 and 連結; no attestation. Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 字幹 Hint for a stem hint. A stem link ties two edges of a stroke together as a stem, so hinting can hold their distance as the size changes. A vertical link governs a horizontal measurement and a horizontal link governs a vertical one. You add links in the glyph, either by hand or from an autohinting pass, and you keep them consistent with the standard stem widths declared in Font Info. Vextra reuses the term for the paired edges it detects in artwork that is not type. styling group name 樣式群組名稱 proposed Built from 樣式 (Glyphs 3 zh-Hant: 樣式連結, 樣式名稱) and 群組; no attestation for the compound. The styling group name, SGN, ties together the styles an application reaches through its bold and italic buttons, and the styling link value and styling link name say which slot each style takes in that group. The mechanism is older than typographic family names and narrower: four slots, no more. You set these fields in TransType when a family has to behave correctly in applications that still drive style selection from those buttons. subsetting cutting down a font 子集化 proposed Follows the Simplified term; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant describes it as 抽出子集. Subsetting exports only part of a font, such as the glyphs a page uses or one codepage, to make a smaller file. The OS/2 embedding bits can forbid it. top sidebearing 上留白 proposed Derived from 留白, pairing 下留白. The space above the glyph outline within its vertical advance. This value participates in vertical text spacing rather than horizontal spacing. tracking uniform letter spacing 字距調整 proposed InDesign zh-TW uses 字距調整 for tracking and jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) gives 字距 for Tracking; kerning is 調距. Tracking changes the spacing across a run of text, rather than correcting particular pairs as kerning does. Layout applications apply it to text. TransType's Tracking filter changes spacing in the font data itself. That changes the font's starting metrics; a layout application can still apply additional tracking to text set in the resulting font. TrueType instruction pixel fitting instruction TrueType 指令 proposed FontForge zh_TW uses TrueType 指令; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 調節指令. A TrueType instruction is one step of the program a TrueType font runs to fit an outline to the pixel grid. Instructions are the TrueType form of hints. FontLab writes them from visual TrueType hints and can keep the ones a font already has. Say instruction for the code and hint for what the reader draws. typographic family name 排印家族名稱 proposed Built from 排印 (Glyphs 3 zh-Hant renders Typo Metrics as 排印學度量) and 家族名稱; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 建議的家族名稱 translates the older label Preferred Family. The typographic family name, TFN, is the name that groups every style of a family under one entry, and the typographic style name, TSN, is what distinguishes a style inside it. They sit beside the older four style family and style names that legacy applications read. You set them in TransType and in Font Info, and you keep them consistent across a family, because an app that reads these fields builds its font menu from them. update metrics 更新度量 proposed Built from 度量; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 更新左邊界 and similar. Recalculate glyph spacing values from their links or expressions. This command updates the advance widths and sidebearings that depend on those relationships. variable font 可變字型 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and InDesign zh-TW use 可變字型; jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) writes 可變式字型. A variable font contains data for design variation along one or more axes. Applications select axis values and calculate the corresponding outlines and other variable data. Named instances identify selected locations, but users are not limited to those locations when the application exposes axis controls. A variable font's supported range depends on its data; it need not contain every style in the family. variation location position in the variation range 位置 proposed Follows the reviewed German, French and Polish and the Simplified decision, which use the plain word for position. A variation location is a point in the design space, given as one value per axis. Masters and instances each have one, and the Variations panel slider shows the current one. vertical advance glyph box height 直排字高 proposed Same concept as advance height; see advance height. The vertical advance is the distance a glyph advances in vertical text, the counterpart of advance width for East Asian layout. Stored in vmtx. vertical metrics 垂直度量 proposed Built from 度量; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 直排度量 names vertical-writing metrics, whereas this term means the ascender, descender and line gap values of horizontal text. The font-wide vertical values used for line layout, including ascender, descender and line gap. FontLab groups these as dimensions, distinct from glyph spacing metrics. visual kerning shape-measured spacing correction 視覺調距 proposed Built from 視覺 and 調距; no attestation for the compound. Visual kerning is kerning that FontLab proposes by measuring the shapes, so that a font gets a usable first pass without a person typing thousands of values. You run it over a selection, then review what it produced, because a measurement of two outlines does not know about the words a reader will meet. Treat the result as a draft: keep the pairs it got right, correct the ones it did not, and kern the difficult pairs by eye in real words. weight axis thickness axis 字重軸 proposed Built from 字重 and 軸; Yin Tzu-Yuan writes 字重軸線. The weight axis, tag wght, varies stroke thickness from light to bold. In a variable font it is the most common axis; its master locations use the usWeightClass scale, such as 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. weight class 字重類別 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and FontForge zh_TW use 字重類別. The weight class is the OS/2 value from 100 to 900 that tells applications how heavy a style is, with 400 for Regular and 700 for Bold. Style linking and menus rely on it. width axis narrow-to-wide axis 寬度軸 proposed Built from 寬度 and 軸; 字寬 is reserved for the advance width. The width axis, tag wdth, varies letter proportions from condensed to extended. It is distinct from advance width, which is the spacing of one glyph, and from the geometric width of a shape. Its scale is a percentage of normal width. width class 寬度類別 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant uses 寬度類別. The width class is the OS/2 value from 1, ultra condensed, to 9, ultra expanded, that tells applications how wide a style is. It is a classification, not the width axis value and not the advance width.

docs.title: OpenType
docs.text: English Fallback Chinese (Traditional) Status Note Definition Adobe Glyph List Adobe Glyph List do-not-translate The Adobe Glyph List maps standard glyph names to Unicode codepoints, so that a glyph named aacute is understood as U plus 00E1 by any tool that follows it. You name glyphs by it wherever it covers the character, because tools and text engines can then infer the mapping without being told twice. Where it does not cover a glyph, you fall back to a consistent scheme of your own and assign codepoints explicitly. Write the name in full on first mention, then AGL. alternate glyph glyph variant 替代字符 proposed InDesign zh-TW uses 替代字符; built from 替代 and 字符. An alternate glyph is another form of the same character, selected through an OpenType feature such as salt or a stylistic set. Its name usually carries a suffix, as in a.alt or g.ss01. cmap cmap do-not-translate The cmap table maps character codes to glyph indices. Its Unicode subtables provide the initial mapping used in text rendering; other subtables support particular encodings or variation sequences. FontLab generates these mappings from the project's encoding data. A glyph without its own Unicode assignment can still appear in typed text through substitution, such as a ligature or alternate selected by the shaping engine. code page legacy character table 字碼頁 proposed Established Microsoft zh-TW term for a numbered legacy encoding. A code page is a numbered legacy encoding, such as Windows 1250 for Central European languages, that maps one byte to one character. The OS/2 table lists the code pages a font supports, and FontLab derives that list from the glyphs present. Write two words. color font table 彩色字型表 proposed 彩色字型 is the usual term for colour fonts and 表 names a font table (Glyphs 3 zh-Hant: COLR表, kern表). Colour-font tables store data for colour glyph rendering. Formats include COLR with CPAL, SVG, sbix, and CBDT with CBLC. They differ in how they describe vector or bitmap content and in application support. Including several formats can extend coverage, but does not guarantee rendering in every application. Identify the exported formats and test the intended targets. contextual alternates context-dependent variants 上下文替代字 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant, InDesign zh-TW and Word zh-TW all name the calt feature 上下文替代字; Apple's 上下文替用項目 rejected. Contextual alternates, the calt feature, cover substitutions an app makes because of what sits around a glyph rather than because a reader asked. In a script face the text engine replaces an entry stroke after a letter that already ends in one, and in a face with repeating shapes it replaces the second of a pair. You write the rules with context in feature code, and apps usually leave calt on by default, which makes it the feature most likely to surprise you when a rule is too broad. cursive attachment joined-script connection 連寫定位 proposed Follows the Simplified concept; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant renders Cursive Positioning as 連寫連接位置調整, shortened. FontForge zh_TW's 草寫附件 is a mistranslation of attachment. Cursive attachment joins glyphs by matching an exit anchor of one glyph to the entry anchor of the next, so connected scripts such as Arabic and Nastaliq flow. It is the curs feature, built from anchors. design languages 目標語言 proposed No attestation; follows the reviewed German, French and Polish (target languages) and the Simplified decision, because the literal 設計語言 means a visual design language. Design languages, the meta table dlng record, list the languages the typeface was designed for. Supported languages, slng, list every language it can set. Both are language tags, not feature tags. encoding 編碼 proposed Universal (FontForge, Apple, Adobe, Microsoft zh-TW). An encoding maps character codes to glyphs. Unicode is the encoding modern fonts use; legacy encodings such as Mac Roman or a code page map one byte to one glyph. FontLab shows the font in a chosen encoding in the Font window and writes the cmap from it. Say encoding for the mapping and code page for a numbered legacy table. feature code layout rule code 特性程式碼 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts say 特性程式碼; 程式碼 is the Taiwan word for code. Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 特性原始碼. Feature code is the text syntax that describes OpenType features: classes, lookups, substitution and positioning rules, grouped into features by tag. It is usually called FEA, after the file extension. You edit it in the Features panel, compile it to check for errors, and keep it under the same review as the drawings, since a rule that fires on the wrong glyph is as visible as a wrong outline. FontLab compiles it into GSUB and GPOS at export. fractions 分數 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Apple CoreText zh-TW use 分數; InDesign's 分數字 is longer. Fractions are numerical forms such as ½. In OpenType, the frac feature supports diagonal fraction composition through glyph substitution. A font may provide precomposed fraction glyphs, numerator and denominator forms, or both. The separate numr and dnom features provide numerator and denominator forms. Do not substitute the sups and subs feature names for these mechanisms or promise support for every input sequence without testing it. glyph index glyph number 字符索引 proposed Apple Font Book zh-TW has 字形索引; rebuilt with 字符, the Taiwan professional word for glyph. A glyph index is the number a glyph occupies in the font's own order, counting from zero. Text engines work in indices after the cmap has done its job, and binary tables reference glyphs by index rather than by name. You rarely set one by hand, but you meet it when you inspect a compiled font or debug a lookup that fires on the wrong glyph. The index depends on glyph order, so it changes when the order does. glyph name 字符名稱 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant uses 字符名稱. A glyph name identifies a glyph in an editing project, feature code or a tool's data. Names such as a, a.sc and a.alt can distinguish related drawings. They are separate from Unicode assignments and glyph indices, and need not survive in every exported format. After renaming a glyph, check references in feature code, classes and scripts, including references the editor cannot update automatically. GPOS GPOS do-not-translate GPOS is the OpenType table that holds positioning: kerning, mark attachment, cursive attachment, and any rule that moves a glyph without replacing it. FontLab writes your kerning here, as pairs and as class based positioning, and builds the mark lookups from your anchors. You reach it through feature code rather than by editing the table. A font may also carry a legacy kern table; modern text engines read GPOS and many ignore the other. GSUB GSUB do-not-translate GSUB is the OpenType table containing glyph-substitution lookups. It supports operations such as replacing a glyph with an alternate, forming a ligature or selecting a form from its context. FontLab compiles feature code into these structures. To diagnose a missing substitution, check the glyphs, compiled rules, feature selection, language and shaping order in the target application. ligature joined letters 連字 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont), justfont's blog, Adobe and Apple zh-TW use 連字; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant uses 合字 for the glyph and 連字 in feature names, and FontForge zh_TW's 連體字 is isolated. A ligature is a glyph used to represent a sequence of characters, such as fi. OpenType substitution can replace several glyphs with one ligature glyph. The liga and dlig features distinguish standard and discretionary ligatures. Shaping does not change the underlying text; whether a later document export preserves searchable text also depends on that export and its text mappings. localized forms language-specific variants 在地化形式 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant names the locl feature 在地化形式. Localized forms are glyph variants selected for a text run's language. The OpenType locl feature can provide these substitutions, for example Bulgarian forms of Cyrillic letters. The shaping engine needs the relevant language information, which the application may obtain from a setting or other context. The substitution changes glyph selection, not the underlying characters or their codepoints. lookup procedure 程序 approved User/team procedure fallback. No sufficiently strong established OpenType-specific alternative verified in the reviewed primary sources. Keep the approved contextual Rules panel title. Preserve literal FEA lookup/lookupflag keywords, identifiers and OpenType structure names. Ordinary search senses are separate. A lookup groups substitution or positioning rules of one type in GSUB or GPOS. Features reference lookups, and several features can share one. The shaping engine selects features and may process them in script-specific stages; within a stage, LookupList order matters. Source-code order alone does not describe the complete shaping sequence. Inspect the compiled tables and the target engine when diagnosing ordering problems. mark glyph combining mark glyph 標號字符 proposed Built from 標號 (Glyphs 3 zh-Hant) and 字符. A mark glyph is an accent or other combining mark that attaches to a base glyph through anchors. The GDEF table classes it as a mark so shaping engines position it rather than advancing past it. nonspacing mark zero-width combining mark 非間距標號 proposed Built from 非間距 and 標號; Yin Tzu-Yuan writes 非間距重音符號. A nonspacing mark is the Unicode general category Mn: a combining mark with zero advance, such as a combining acute. It differs from FontLab's nonspacing element, which is a property of an element inside a glyph. oldstyle figures lowercase-style figures 不等高數字 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) lists oldstyle figures as 不等高數字, the pair of 等高數字; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 古典數字 and Apple's 舊式數字 are the alternatives. Oldstyle figures are numerals with varying heights, often including forms with ascenders and descenders. The OpenType onum feature selects them when provided by the font. Figure height and figure width are separate choices: oldstyle figures can be proportional or tabular. Use tabular widths when numerals must align in columns, whether their forms are oldstyle or lining. OpenType class layout glyph group OpenType 類別 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and FontForge zh_TW use 類別 for classes; name protected. An OpenType class is a named group of glyphs that feature code can address at once, written with an at sign before the name. One rule over two classes replaces a page of single rules, and one edit to a class reaches every rule that cites it. You define classes in the Classes panel or in feature code, and you keep their order stable, because a substitution between two classes pairs them by position. Kerning classes are a separate mechanism with the same idea. OpenType feature layout feature OpenType 特性 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan writes OpenType 特性; InDesign's OpenType 功能 rejected with 功能. An OpenType feature identifies typographic behaviour through a four-character tag, such as liga, smcp or ss01. Feature records reference substitution or positioning lookups. In FontLab, you can write feature code and compile it into the font. Whether and when a feature is applied depends on the shaping engine, script, language and application settings; not every feature is a user-controlled switch. OS/2 table OS/2 表 proposed Tag protected, noun translated with 表. The OS/2 table carries the font's metadata for applications: vertical metrics, weight and width classes, embedding permissions, the panose values, and the codepage and Unicode range bits that say what the font covers. You fill it from Font Info rather than by hand, and you check it before release, because a wrong weight class puts a font in the wrong slot in a menu and wrong vertical metrics change line spacing in every browser. Write it with the slash: OS/2. Private Use Area Private Use Area do-not-translate A private-use area is one of three Unicode blocks whose codepoints can receive meanings by private agreement. Different fonts or systems may assign different meanings to the same private-use codepoint. Use a documented agreement when encoding custom symbols there. An alternate glyph reached through a feature does not require its own private-use assignment. single substitution 單一替換 proposed FontForge zh_TW has 單一替代; 替換 is used instead (Glyphs 3 zh-Hant: 以替換方式) so that substitution stays apart from 替代, the word for alternates. A single substitution replaces one glyph with one other glyph, the simplest GSUB lookup type. Small caps, stylistic alternates and localized forms are mostly built from it. small caps small capitals 小型大寫字母 proposed jf 字體口袋書 (justfont) and FontForge zh_TW use 小型大寫字母; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 小字大寫 and InDesign's 小型大寫字 are the alternatives. Small caps are capital shapes drawn at roughly lowercase height, with their own weight and width rather than scaled capitals. Apps apply the smcp feature to put them in place of lowercase letters, and c2sc to put them in place of capitals, so a run set in both features becomes uniform. You draw them as separate glyphs, usually with a dot sc suffix, and write both features. Scaled capitals look thin beside real text, which is the reason to draw them rather than let an app fake them. stylistic set 文體集 proposed Word zh-TW and Apple CoreText zh-TW use 文體集; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 文樣集 and InDesign's 文體組合 are the alternatives. A stylistic set is a numbered group of alternate glyphs a reader can switch on, from ss01 through ss20. Each set holds alternates that belong together: a single storey a with a matching g, a set of flat topped figures. You name each set in the font so an app can show a readable label instead of a number, and you keep one idea per set. A set that mixes unrelated alternates gives a reader nothing they can decide about. tabular figures equal-width figures 等寬數字 proposed Built from 等寬 (jf 字體口袋書 (justfont)); Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 等寬齊高 names tabular lining only and FontForge zh_TW has 定寬數字. Tabular figures all carry the same advance width, so columns of numbers line up whatever digits they contain. Apps apply the tnum feature to put them in place of proportional figures. You draw them as a separate set and give every one the same width, centring the narrow digits inside it. They matter in any table, price list, or running total, and they look loose in prose, which is why a font offers both sets rather than choosing for the reader. Unicode codepoint character code Unicode 碼位 proposed 碼位 is the Chinese Unicode term for a code point, shared with the Simplified decision; not attested in the corpus. FontForge zh_TW's 編碼點 and 字元代碼 rejected. A Unicode codepoint is an integer from U+0000 to U+10FFFF. Not every codepoint has an assigned character. Write it with U+ and at least four hexadecimal digits, as in U+0041 for A. In a font editor, a glyph's Unicode assignment connects it to an encoded character; the exported cmap records the relevant mapping. variation selector variant picker character 變體選擇器 proposed FontForge zh_TW uses 變體選擇器; its 異體字選擇器 covers only the ideographic use. A variation selector is a Unicode character that follows a base character to request a specific glyph form. The pair is a variation sequence, mapped in the cmap format 14 subtable; a default mapping points at the base glyph. writing system 書寫系統 proposed W3C's Chinese layout requirements use 書寫系統; Microsoft zh-TW's 文字系統 is the alternative, and Glyphs' 語系 and Apple's 文字 name the OpenType script. A writing system is the set of characters and rules a language writes with, such as Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic. OpenType calls it a script and identifies it by a four letter tag. Say writing system in prose and script tag for the identifier, so the reader does not confuse it with a Python script.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: English Fallback Chinese (Traditional) Status Note Definition AI file AI file do-not-translate An AI file is an Adobe Illustrator document, and it is the container the Vexy Illustrator plug-ins work inside. It holds paths, strokes, fills, appearances, and the live effects that a plug-in adds. You do not export an AI file from the plug-ins; you work in one. Write it as an AI file or an Illustrator document, never as an ai, and name Adobe Illustrator in full on first mention in the same document. AIP AIP do-not-translate An AIP file is an Adobe Illustrator plug-in binary, and it is how Vexy Linestra and Vexy Vextra reach Illustrator. The filenames close up the product name, VexyLinestra.aip and VexyVextra.aip, while prose keeps the space. You copy the file into the Illustrator plug-ins folder, whose name the operating system may show translated, and restart Illustrator so it loads. Name the file exactly as it ships, since a renamed plug-in does not load. FLREQ FLREQ do-not-translate An FLREQ file is a licence request the application writes when a machine cannot reach the licensing service, and an FLLIC file is the response that activates it. You send the request from the machine that needs the licence, receive the response, and open it there. The pair exists for machines that stay offline, so name both files in a procedure that uses either, and say which machine each step happens on. Fog.net Fog.net do-not-translate Fog.net is Fontographer's project data format, and fognet is the Python module that reads and writes it from a script. A project file carries the extension .fog. You meet the format when you script against a project or move one between machines, rather than in ordinary editing, where the dashboard handles saving. The module name is lowercase, as Python module names are, and it goes in code font wherever it appears in prose. Glyphs file Glyphs file do-not-translate A Glyphs file is the source format of the Glyphs editor, and FontLab reads and writes it so that a project can move between the two. It holds masters, glyphs, metrics, and features in one text file. You use it when a collaborator works in the other editor, and you check the result after the trip, because two editors model masters and components in ways that do not correspond exactly. Write it as a Glyphs file, not as a glyphs. Lines file Lines file do-not-translate A Lines file is the native document of Vexy Lines, holding the source image, the fills applied to it, and the settings that produced the result. You save to it while you work and export vector artwork when you are finished, because the export keeps the result and not the recipe. Write it as a Lines file with a capital L when you name the format, and as the extension in lowercase with a dot when you mean the file suffix. OTF OTF do-not-translate OTF is the usual filename extension for an OpenType font with PostScript outlines. These use cubic curves stored in CFF or CFF2 data. State the outline flavour when it matters: OpenType fonts with TrueType outlines also support OpenType layout features. The .otf extension alone does not establish which features, colour formats or variation capabilities a font contains. SVG SVG do-not-translate SVG is the vector graphics format, and it names two different things in this documentation: a graphic file that a drawing tool exports, and the SVG table inside a colour font. Say which you mean. You export SVG artwork from the Vexy products, and you meet the SVG table when you build a colour font in FontLab. A sentence that says SVG support without saying which one leaves a reader to guess. TTC TTC do-not-translate TTC is the usual filename extension for a TrueType font collection: several fonts stored in one file. Collection members can share tables, reducing duplication where their data is identical. A collection is a packaging format, not an interpolation model. Distinguish its individual fonts from named instances within a variable font. TTF TTF do-not-translate TTF is the usual filename extension for a font with TrueType outlines, which use quadratic curves. An OpenType TTF can contain layout features and variation data. Exporting cubic source outlines to this flavour requires curve conversion, which can change the point structure and approximate the original geometry. Check the exported outlines at the intended sizes. Type 1 Type 1 do-not-translate Type 1 is an older PostScript outline-font format. It remains relevant when opening archived fonts or explaining conversion workflows. Support depends on the application and version, so identify the target when discussing compatibility. Converting a Type 1 font to OpenType does not automatically supply missing Unicode mappings or new layout features. UFO UFO do-not-translate UFO, Unified Font Object, is an open source-font format. UFO 3 stores glyph layers, font information, kerning, groups and optional feature code in a directory package or ZIP archive. It also allows images and application-specific data. Interchange depends on what both applications support; a UFO export does not by itself guarantee that every editor-specific property survives. VFB VFB do-not-translate VFB is the native source format of FontLab Studio 5. FontLab 8 can open and export it, but the format cannot represent every feature of a FontLab 8 project. Use VFC or VFJ for ongoing work in FontLab 8. Name VFB when explaining migration or an exchange workflow that requires the older format, and check the exported result for unsupported data. VFC VFC do-not-translate VFC is FontLab's native binary format, and the one you work in. It holds everything the editor knows: masters, elements, references, anchors, kerning, features, and the project settings that no font format carries. You save to it while you design and export to OTF or TTF when you ship. Write the format in capitals when you name it and in lowercase with a dot when you mean the extension. Its sibling VFJ stores the same content as text. VFJ VFJ do-not-translate VFJ is FontLab's JSON source format. It provides a text representation of a FontLab project for workflows that need readable or scriptable data. Use it as a source format, not an installable font. When exchanging files between FontLab versions or external tools, check that the receiving tool supports the data the project uses. WOFF2 WOFF2 do-not-translate WOFF2 is a compressed font format for web delivery. Its encoding uses font-specific transformations and Brotli compression. Export it for web use and test the resulting font in the target browsers. The size saving depends on the source font and its contents; do not promise a fixed reduction or infer available features from the extension.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: English Fallback Chinese (Traditional) Status Note Definition action 動作 proposed Apple (Final Cut, Motion) and Inkscape zh_TW use 動作 for a named invokable operation; 操作 stays free for the generic word. An action is an operation you can invoke in the application. An action label names the operation; help explains its effect. add 新增 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant (新增錨點, 新增主版), Adobe and Microsoft zh-TW use 新增; Apple's 加入 is the alternative. Add inserts another item into the current collection or selection. Name the item when the surrounding control does not make it clear. alternate 替代 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant feature names and InDesign zh-TW use 替代字 for alternates; Apple's 替用項目 rejected. 替換 is kept for substitution. An alternate is a different glyph form for the same character or purpose. The context determines how you select or substitute that form. anchor cloud attachment point cloud 錨點雲 proposed No attestation; built from 錨點 plus 雲, as the Simplified 锚点云 and German Ankerwolke do. The anchor cloud previews the marks that attach to an anchor by showing them faintly around the glyph in the Glyph window. It checks mark positioning without leaving the base glyph. auto layer recipe-built layer 自動圖層 proposed No attestation; fallback translated from 圖層, as the Simplified 自动图层. An auto layer builds a glyph from a recipe, such as A plus acute, and rebuilds it when the parts change. Turn auto off to edit the glyph by hand. autohint 自動 Hint proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant labels the command 自動 Hint and keeps Hint in Latin script; FontForge zh_TW's 自動渲調 rejected with its coinage 渲調. Autohint is the command to generate hints automatically. Use autohinting when naming the process rather than the command. Brush 筆刷 proposed Glyphs 3 zh-Hant and Adobe zh-TW use 筆刷; 畫筆 is the less common alternative. The Brush tool draws a stroke freehand, and what the stroke becomes differs by product. In FontLab and Fontographer the Brush keeps the path you drew as a centreline and generates the thick outline from it, so the drawing stays editable until you expand it into ordinary contours. In Vexy Lines the Brush paints masks by hand, and a mask decides where a layer's fills can draw rather than being artwork itself. Name the application in any sentence where a reader could take one tool for the other. collapse 收攏 proposed No attestation for this node operation; the everyday verb for gathering things to one spot, as in the Simplified decision. 收合 (fold a panel) and Blender's 塌陷 rejected. Collapse aligns the selected nodes to one point. In the Contour tool it aligns both coordinates; in the Metrics tool only the horizontal one. It moves nodes; it does not merge them. color flag color mark 顏色標記 proposed Fallback color mark translated; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 顏色標籤 rejected because 標籤 is its word for tags, and 標記 is free since mark glyphs are 標號. A color flag is a color you assign to a glyph cell, a kerning pair or a class to mark it for later. Flags are annotations for the designer and are not exported. corner angles 轉角角度 proposed No attestation; descriptive rendering with 轉角, Adobe zh-TW's word for a corner (即時轉角). The angles at contour vertices. These geometric measurements describe how adjacent segments meet at a corner and can be displayed on the canvas. cousins related glyphs alongside 表親 proposed No attestation; house voice. The plain family word for cousins, kept from the Simplified decision; it reads the same in Taiwan. Cousins are related glyphs or other masters that FontLab shows faintly around the current glyph in the Glyph window, so you can compare shapes and spacing while you edit. The name is FontLab's, rendered in each language's house voice. crop 裁切 proposed Apple and Adobe zh-TW use 裁切; 裁剪 is the alternative. Crop trims an image or drawing to a chosen area. The command label names the operation; its context identifies the object being cropped. cubic 三次 proposed Mathematical term (三次貝茲曲線); FontForge zh_TW's 正方體形 and Blender's 立方 are the volume sense. A cubic Bézier segment is a curve defined by two endpoints and two control points. Cubic describes the degree of the curve, not its physical dimensions. current 目前 proposed Standard zh-TW interface word (FontForge zh_TW, GIMP, Apple 目前使用者); 當前 is the mainland word. Current identifies the item or state active at the time of an operation. Name the item, such as the current layer, when the context is ambiguous. cusp 尖點 proposed Mathematical term for a cusp; kept apart from 尖角 (sharp) and from a smooth join. A cusp is a sharp point where a curve changes direction abruptly. Keep it distinct from a smooth join. decompose break into contours 分解 proposed Yin Tzu-Yuan's zh-TW Glyphs scripts use 分解組件 and Glyphs 3 zh-Hant has 字符組合與分解; the Glyphs command label 拆開 is the alternative. Decompose replaces components with copies of their contours, so the glyph no longer follows its source glyphs. Use it before edits that a component cannot carry, or before export to a format without composites. default 預設 proposed Standard zh-TW interface word (Apple, Adobe, Microsoft, Glyphs). A default is the value or choice used when no explicit alternative has been selected. It need not be the currently selected value. demo mode 展示模式 proposed No attestation; standard zh-TW rendering of demo. 演示 is the mainland word. Demo mode is how FontLab runs without a license: everything works except saving, exporting and printing. dialog 對話框 proposed Apple zh-TW, Qt and Krita use 對話框; Microsoft's 對話方塊 is longer. A dialog presents information, settings or a question for a particular interaction. A modal dialog restricts interaction with its parent until it is dismissed; a modeless dialog does not. Use the application's established name and reproduce its button labels exactly. If a procedure opens a dialog, explain the relevant choices and how to apply or cancel them. Dream Up generate shapes 發想 proposed No attestation; house voice. Same idea as the Simplified 畅想 (imagine freely), but 暢想 reads as mainland usage; 發想 is the everyday Taiwan design-studio verb for coming up with ideas. Dream Up is a Fontographer command for generating glyph shapes. Dream Up Font generates a whole font; Mixfont blends existing fonts. Keep these commands distinct and show any confirmed cost before the reader runs an operation. Generated shapes may need further editing. echo text repeated text 重複文字 proposed No attestation; fallback repeated text translated. The Simplified 回显 is a mainland computing term not used in Taiwan. Echo text makes a preview repeat the text of the current window, so the Preview panel or the TrueType hinting preview shows the same string you are editing. Eraser 橡皮擦 proposed The real tool's name, as in Adobe and Apple zh-TW. The Eraser removes or simplifies points on a contour. In FontLab, its modes remove nodes and handles, select points for removal, or simplify a path. In Vexy Vextra, normal Eraser removes covered points; Soft Eraser removes a node only when a replacement curve is close enough to the original. That does not guarantee an identical outline. In Fontographer, Eraser shares a grouped toolbar button with Trowel. Name the application and mode when describing an operation. expand filter bake filter into contours 展開濾鏡 proposed 展開 is Adobe zh-TW's word for baking a live appearance into paths (展開外觀) and FontForge zh_TW's for expanding a stroke; 濾鏡 is the filter word in Glyphs 3 zh-Hant. Expand filter bakes a live element filter, such as Smart Corners, Skin or a boolean Fusion, into plain contours. The filter parameters are no longer editable afterwards. expand stroke bake stroke into contours 展開筆畫 proposed FontForge zh_TW has exactly 展開筆畫; Glyphs 3 zh-Hant's 擴展外框 rejected to keep the 展開 family. Expand stroke converts a stroked centerline, or a brush applied to a contour, into plain filled contours. The live stroke or brush is gone afterwards and the result can be edited node by node. expand transformation bake transformation into contours 展開變形 proposed Same expand family as 展開濾鏡 and 展開筆畫; no attestation for the exact phrase. Expand transformation writes an element's live transformation, such as scaling or rotation, into the node coordinates.
